*etāsāṃ ca samūhaiśca yūthikābhiḥ samanvitam \|*  
*cārukuṃjakuṭīraistaiḥ paṃcāśatkoṭibhirmune \|\| 127 \|\|*

*ratnapradīpadīpaiśca dhūpena surabhīkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgāradravyayuktaiśca vāsitairgaṃdhavāyubhiḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*caṃdanāktaiḥ puṣpatalpairmālājālasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*madhulubdhamadhughrāṇāṃ kalaśabdaiśca śabditam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*ratnālaṃkāraśobhāḍhayairgopīvṛṃdaiśca veṣṭitam \|*  
*paṃcāśatkoṭigopībhī rakṣitaṃ rādhikājñayā \|\| 130 \|\|*

126-130. All round, there were clusters of kalpavrksa besides the creepers of Mallika, Malatl, jasmine and creepers of other fragrant flowers. О sage, there were fifty crores of cottages in which the lamps of gems remained burning, besides there were fragrant essence cosmetics and fragrant breeze, having the scent of sandal-paste. The beds were decorated with flowers and garlands which were surrounded by the black-wasps producing the hissing sound, These cottages were surrounded by beautiful cowherdesses adorned with all the ornaments studded with gems. Thus at the command of Radhika, the place was protected by fifty crores of cowherdesses.

## \|\| 4.131 \|\|

*dvātriṃśatkānanaṃ tatra ramyaṃ ramyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*vṛṃdāvanābhyaṃtaritaṃ nirjanasthānamuttamam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. In that Vmdavana there were thirty-two forests which were quite charming, beautiful and served as ideal secluded places.

## \|\| 4.132-135 \|\|

*supakvamadhurasvāduphalairvṛṃdārakaṃ mune \|*  
*goṣṭhānāṃ ca gavāṃ caiva samūhaiśca samanvitam \|\| 132 \|\|*

*puṣpodyānasahasreṇa puṣpitena sugaṃdhinā \|*  
*madhulubdhamadhughrāṇāṃ \|samūhena samanvitam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*paṃcāśatkoṭigopīnāṃ vilāsaiśca virājitam \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇatulyarūpāṇāṃ sadratnaguṃṭhitairvaraiḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā vṛṃdāvanaṃ ramyaṃ yayurgolokamīśvarāḥ \|*  
*parito vartulākāraṃ koṭiyojanavistṛtam \|\| 135 \|\|*

132-135. О sage, it was filled with best of ripe and delicious fruits beside the cows and the abodes of cows, the blossoming fragrant flowers in thousands gardens in which the black-wasps becoming greedy of the honey, always roamed about. There were fifty crores of cowherds who were as beautiful lord Krishna himself and were adorned with the gem-studded ornaments. Vrindavana was a place of exquisite beauty and enjoying the beauty of natural environment of the place, the gods reached Goloka which was circular in shape and was spread over crores of yojanas.

## \|\| 4.136 \|\|

*ratnaprākārasaṃyuktaṃ caturddhārānvitaṃ mune \|*  
*gopānāṃ ca samūhaiśca dvārapālaiḥ samanvitam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. О sage, it had the boundary walls in which the gems were studded and had four entrance gates guarded by the cowherds as door keeper.

## \|\| 4.137-140 \|\|

*āśramai ratnakhacitairnānābhogasamanvitaiḥ \|*

*bhaktānāṃ gopavṛndānāmāśramaiḥ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*tato'dhikasuvistīrṇaiḥ sadratnagrathitairyutam \|\| 138 \|\|*

*āśramaiḥ pārṣadānāṃ ca tato'dhikavilakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ daśakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*pārṣadapravarāṇāṃ ca śrīkṛṣṇarūpadhāriṇām \|*  
*āśramaiḥ koṭibhiryuktaṃ sadratnena vinirmitaiḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

137-140. The cowherds who always remain-in attendants of lord Krishna had the abodes which were decorated with gems and having various items of pleasures the number of such houses ran into the fifty crores. Besides them, there were a hundred crores of the abodes of the groups of the cowherds, the construction of which was more beautiful then the earlier houses. All of them were studded with the best of gems, such of the abodes which were decorated with the best of gems belonged to the courtiers of the lord and their number was ten crores. The foremost of the courtiers look like lord Krishna himself and they have a crore of beautiful dwelling places built in gems to serve as their residence.

## \|\| 4.141-142 \|\|

*rādhikāśuddhabhaktānāṃ gopīnāmāśramairvaraiḥ \|*  
*sadratnaracitairdravyairdvātriṃśatkoṭibhiryutam \|\| 141 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ ca kikarīṇāṃ ca bhavanaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*maṇiratnādiracitaiḥ śobhitaṃ daśakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

141-142. Such of the cowherdesses who, were immensely devoted to Radhika had thirty-two crores of divine abodes. These were also constructed using the best of gems of very high quality. Their servants also had the abodes built with precious stones which looked quite beautiful and they were crores in number.

## \|\| 4.143-147 \|\|

*śatajanmatapaḥpūtā bhaktā ye bhārate bhuvi \|*  
*haribhaktiparā ye ca karmanirvāṇakārakāḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

*svapne jñāne harerdhyāne viviṣṭamānasā mune \|*  
*rādhākṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti prajapaṃto divāniśam \|\| 144 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ śrīkṛṣṇabhaktānāṃ nivāsaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*sadratnamaṇinirmāṇairnānābhogasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

*puṣpaśayyāpuṣpamālāśvetacāmaraśobhitaiḥ \|*  
*ratnadarpaṇaśobhāḍhyairharinmaṇisaparpitaiḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnakalaśasamūhānvitaśekharaiḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmavastrābhyaṃtaritaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

143-147. О sage, such of the devotees of the lord born on the sacred land of Bharata performed the severe tapas for a number of years and getting devoted to the lord and are relieved of the fetters of performing of deeds end they always recite the name of the lord while sleeping or awakes during the day or the night. For such devotees of lord Krishna, the impressive structures were been built, which are filled with many articles of dally consumption. They had enough of flower beds, flower garlands many of white fly-whisks, mirrors of gems and other jewels. They also had valuable kalasas in large numbers decorating the tops of the houses and the certain were made of fine cloth. The number of such houses also into a hundred crores.

## \|\| 4.148-149 \|\|

*devāstamadbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā kiyaddūraṃ yayurmudā \|*  
*tatrākṣayavaṭaṃ ramyaṃ dadṛśurjagadīśvarāḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*paṃcayojanavistīrṇamūrdhvaṃ taddviguṇaṃ mune \|*  
*sahasraskaṃdhasaṃyuktaśākhāsaṃsthāsamanvitam \|\| 149 \|\|*

148-149. Brahma, Shiva and other gods, roamed about with a delightful mind. They walked up to some distance and came across a beautiful banyan tree which was eternal in nature. That tree was spread into five yojanas and its height was ten yojanas. It had thousands of branches which looked quite charming.

## \|\| 4.150-151 \|\|

*raktapakkaphalākīrṇaṃ śobhitaṃ ratnavedibhiḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasvarūpāṃstanmūle dadṛśurvallabhāñchiśūn \|\| 150 \|\|*

*pītavastraparīdhānānkrīḍāsaktamanoharān \|*  
*candanokṣitasarvāṃgānratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitān \|\| 151 \|\|*

150-151. It had a large number of ripe fruits of red colour besides several pedestals. They saw a number of children resembling Krishna playing under the tree who were clad in yellow lower garment and were playing delightfully with their limbs plastered in the sandal-paste and their body were adorned with gem-studded ornaments.

## \|\| 4.152-158 \|\|

*dadṛśustatra deveśāḥ pārṣadapravarānhareḥ \|*

*siṃdūrākāramaṇibhiḥ parito racitaṃ mune \|*  
*iṃdranīlaiḥ padmarāgairhīrakai rucakaistathā \|\| 153 \|\|*

*nirmitairvedibhiryuktaṃ parito ratnamaṃḍapam \|*  
*caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitam \|\| 154 \|\|*

*dadhipūrṇalājaphalapuṣpadūrvāṃkurānvitam \|*  
*sūkṣmasūtragraṃthiyuktaśrīkhaṃḍapallavānvitam \|\| 155 \|\|*

*raṃbhāstaṃbhasamūhaiśca kuṅkumāktairvirājitam \|*  
*sadratnamaṃḍalaghaṭaiḥ phalaśākhāsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

*siṃdūrakuṃkumāktaiśca gaṃdhacaṃdanacarcitaiḥ \|*  
*bhūṣitaiḥ puṣpamālābhiḥ pādapaiḥ paribhūṣitam \|\| 157 \|\|*

*gopikānāṃ samūhaiśca krīḍāsaktaiśca veṣṭitama \|*  
*bahumūlyena ratnena ratnasopānanirmitān \|\| 158 \|\|*

152-158. The gods found theirs the courtiers of lord Krs па. О sage, at a distance from that place, they came across the royal road which was built with red rubies emitting the lustre of vermilion. In its background there were several pedestals made in gems and jewels. On all the sides of the road, there were gem-studded resting places. There were a sprinkling of the scented water of sandal-paste, aguru, kastUrl and saffron. There were thousands of the trunks of banana trees besides the tender leaves, fried paddy, fruits, flowers, Ourva-grass, fruits, flowers, which were tied in very thin cord which decorated the space in between the trunks of banana trees. The saffron was sprinkled over all of them, the mangala-kalasas made of gems were consecrated at several places. The fruits and branches besides the fresh tender leaves decorated the kalashas. The saffron, fragrance, vermilion and sandal-paste were applied to them. These trees were decorated with the garlands of flowers which added to the grandeur of the royal houses. The cowherdesses in playful mood surrounded the road. Beautiful steps of gems were constructed there.

## \|\| 4.159-167 \|\|

*vahniśaucāṃśukai ramyaiḥ śvetacāmaradarpaṇaiḥ \|*  
*ratnatalpavicitraiśca puṣpamālyairvirājitāna \|\| 159 \|\|*

*ṣoḍaśadvārasaṃyuktāndvārapālaiśca rakṣitān \|*  
*paritaḥ parikhāyuktānratnaprākāraveṣṭitān \|\| 160 \|\|*

*caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitān \|*  
*gṛhānmanoramāndṛṣṭvā te devā gamanotsukāḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*jagmuḥ śīghraṃ kiyaddūraṃ dadṛśuḥ sundaraṃ tataḥ \|*  
*āśramaṃ rādhikāyāśca rāseśvaryāśca nārada \|\| 162 \|\|*

*devādhidevyā gopīnāṃ varāyāścārunirmitam \|*  
*prāṇādhikāyāḥ kṛṣṇasya ramyadravyamanoharam \|\| 163 \|\|*

*sarvānirvacanīyaṃ ca paṃḍitairna nirūpitam \|*  
*sucāruvartulākāraṃ ṣaḍgavyūtipramāṇakam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*śatamaṃdirasaṃyuktaṃ jvalitaṃ ratnatejasā \|*  
*amūlyaratnasārāṇāṃ cayaurviracitaṃ varam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*durlaṃghyābhirgabhīrābhiḥ parikhābhiḥ suśobhitam \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣaiḥ parivṛtaṃ puṣpodyānaśatāṃtaram \|\| 166 \|\|*

*sumūlyaratnakhacitaprākāraiḥ pariveṣṭitam \|*  
*sadratnavedikāyuktairyuktaṃ dvāraiśca saptabhiḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

159-167. In all, there were sixteen entrance gate which were decorated with beautiful fine garments purified by the fire and had the white fly-whisks, mirrors, gem-studded beds and flower garland’s. Several of the gate-keepers guarded the place. There were deep valleys around them and there were surrounded by boundary walls of red colours, after looking at such beautiful places, the gods proceeded further and they walked quite swiftly for some distance and came across the abode of Radha, the goddess of the divine dance. О Narada, the abode of Radha, the primeval goddess of the gods, the best of the cowherdesses and the beloved of Krishna, was built quite beautifully, the use of the divine material in the construction of that abode had added to its elegance. Everything of that place was inexplicable for all. Even the best of the intellectual were unable describe its beauty. That elegant place was built in a circular manner spread over an area of twelve kosas. There were several buildings in it. It had astonishing types of asramas which continued shining with divine gems, it was created using the best of the gems. It had a number of inaccessible and deep valleys. The place was surrounded by the kalpavrksas from all the sides and had a number of pleasure gardens in the same. The asrama was surrounded by the boundary walls built with precious stones, it had seven entrance gates and had elegant pedestals made of gems.

## \|\| 4.168-170 \|\|

*saṃyuktaratnacitraiśca vicitrairvartulaṃ mune \|*  
*pradhānasaptadvārebhyaḥ kramaśaḥ kramaśo mune \|\| 168 \|\|*

*sarvato'pi tatastatra ṣoḍaśadvārasaṃyutam \|*  
*devā ddaṣṭvā ca prākāraṃ sahasradhanurucchritam \|\| 169 \|\|*

*sadratnakṣudrakalaśasamūhaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*pradīptaṃ tejasā ramyaṃ paramaṃ vismayaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

168-170. The doors were studded with astonishing type of gems and also contained several types of paintings. After passing through the seven gates, one had to pass through sixteen other doors. The gods saw, its boundary wall had a height of a thousands bows and had a number of small-kalashas adorning the boundary wall. The sight delighted the gpds immensely.

## \|\| 4.171-178 \|\|

*tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kiyaddūraṃ yayurmudā \|*  
*purato gacchatāṃ teṣāṃ paścādbhūtastadāśramaḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

*gopānāṃ gopikānāṃ ca dadṛśuścāśramānparān \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitāñchatakoṭimitānmune \|\| 172 \|\|*

*darśaṃdarśaṃ ca parito gopānāṃ sarvamāśramam \|*  
*gopikānāṃ cāparaṃ vā ramyaṃ ramyaṃ navaṃnavam \|\| 173 \|\|*

*golokaṃ nikhilaṃ dṛṣṭvā pulakāṃgaṃ yayuḥ surāḥ \|*  
*tadeva vartulākāraṃ ramyaṃ vṛṃdāvanaṃ vanam \|\| 174\|\|*

*dadṛśuḥ śataśṛṃgaṃ ca tadbahirvirajānadīm \|*  
*virajāṃ tāṃ yayurdevā dadṛśuḥ śūnyameva ca \|\| 175 \|\|*

*vāyvādhāraṃ ca golokaṃ sadratnamayamadbhutam \|*  
*īśvarecchāvinirmāṇaṃ rādhikājñānubaṃdhanāt \|\| 176 \|\|*

*yuktaṃ sahasraiḥ sarasāṃ kevalaṃ maṃgalālayam \|*  
*nṛtyaṃ ca dadṛśustatra devāśca sumanoharam \|\| 177 \|\|*

*sutānaṃ cārusaṃgītaṃ rādhākṛṣṇaguṇānvitam \|*  
*śrutvaiva gītapīyūṣaṃ mūrchāmāpuḥ surā mune \|\| 178 \|\|*

171-178. Going round the place delightfully they moved forward for some distance. While doing so, they left the asramas behind, thereafter they came across the abodes of cowherds and cowherdesses which were studded with gems. They were numbering a hundred crores. Thus visualising the abodes of cowherds, cowherdesses, the entire ashramas and new elegant spots-they went round the entire universe. Visual is the Goloka, their bodies were thrilled. They went wound the circular and pleasant Vrindavanas. The mountain with hundred peaks had the river Viraja flowing besides it. After crossing the Viraja, they found everything deserted. The astonishing Goloka was constructed with gems and was floating in the air. It was built at the command of Radhika with the approval of lord Krishna. It was the place of prosperity and had thousands of rivers. О sage, the gods also witness the pleasant dance accompanied with sweet music and the reciting the name of Radha and Shri Krishna. Listening to the songs, the gods were fainted.

## \|\| 4.179-184 \|\|

*kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya te devāḥ kṛṣṇamānasāḥ \|*  
*dadṛśuḥ paramāścaryaṃ sthānesthāne manoharam \|\| 179 \|\|*

*dadṛśurgopikāḥ sarvā nānāveṣavidhāyikāḥ \|*  
*kāścinmṛdaṃgahastāśca kāścidvīṇākarā varāḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

*kāściccāmarahastāśca karatālakarāḥ parāḥ \|*  
*kāścidyaṃtravādyahastā ratnanūpuraśobhitāḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

*sadratnakiṃkiṇījālaśabdena śabditā varāḥ \|*  
*kāścinmastakakuṃbhāśca nṛtyabhedamanorathāḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

*puṃveṣanāyikāḥ kāścitkāścittāsāṃ ca nāyikāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaveṣadharāḥ kāścidrādhāveṣadharāḥ parāḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

*kāścitsaṃyogaviratāḥ kāścidāliṃgane ratāḥ \|*  
*krīḍāsaktāśca tā dṛṣṭvā sasmitā jagadīśvarāḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

179-184. In a moment, they regained consciousness and mentally reciting the name of Krishna, they came across charming scenes at every step. They came across several cowherdesses clad in different type of costumes, some one was playing on double-drums and some one was playing on vlna. Some one held the fly-whisks in her hands, while other sounded the karatala. Some of them were holding musical instruments, while others produced dangling sound with the anklets worn by them. The waist-bands studded with gems worn by some of them, were producing sound which resembled the sounds of bells. Some of them carried pitchers filled with water and were displaying various dance postures. Some of the cowherdesses were clad in male costumes white others served as the spouses; some of them appeared in the form of Krishna while others appeared in the form of Radha, some of them were getting separated per chance while others were embracing each other and still others were engaged in love-sports. Lord Vishnu smiled looking at them.

## \|\| 4.185-187 \|\|

*pragacchaṃtaḥ kiyaddūraṃ dadṛśuścāśramānbahūn \|*  
*rādhāsakhīnāṃ gehāṃśca pradhānānāṃ ca nārada \|\| 185 \|\|*

*rūpeṇaiva guṇenaiva veṣeṇa yauvanena ca \|*  
*saubhāgyenaiva vayasā sadṛśīnāṃ ca tatra vai \|\| 186 \|\|*

*trayastriṃśadvayasyāśca rādhikāyāśca gopikāḥ \|*  
*veṣānirvacanīyāśca tāsāṃ nāmāni ca śṛṇu \|\| 187 \|\|*

185-187. О Narada, after covering some distance they came across several asramas which serves as the dwelling places of the chief female fiends of Radha all of them were equal in beauty, virtues, costumes youthfulness, fortune and age. There were thirty three cowherdesses who we of the same age as Radha was. Their costumes, were beyond description. You listen to their names.

## \|\| 4.188-193 \|\|

*suśīlā ca śaśikalā yamunā mādhavī ratī \|*  
*kadaṃbamālā kuṃtī ca jāhnavī ca svayaṃprabhā \|\| 188 \|\|*

*caṃdramukhī ca sāvitrī gāyatrī sumukhī sukhā \|*  
*padmālayā pārijātā gaurī ca sarvamaṃgalā \|\| 189 \|\|*

*kālikā kamalā durgā bhāratī ca sarasvatī \|*  
*gaṃgā 'mbikā madhumatī caṃpā'parṇā ca suṃdarī \|\| 190 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇapriyā satī caiva naṃdinī naṃdaneti ca \|*  
*etāḥ samānāḥ sadratnaracitā rādhikāpriyāḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

*etāsāṃ samarūpāṇāṃ ratnadhātuvicitritān \|*  
*nānāprakāracitreṇa citritānsumanoharān \|\| 192 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnakalaśasamūhaiḥ śikharojjvalān \|*  
*sadratnaracitāñchubhrānāśramāndadṛśustathā \|\| 193 \|\|*

188-193. Their names were Suslla, Sasikala, Yamuna, Madhavi, Rati, Kadambamala, KuntI, Jahnavl, Svayamprabha, ChandramukhI, Savitri, Gayatri, SumukhI, Sukha, Padmalaya then Parijata, Gauri, Sarvamangala, Kalika, Kamala, Durga, Bharati, Sarasvati, Ganga, Ambika, Madhumatl, Campa, Aparna Sundarl, Krishnapriya, Sati, Nandin! and Nandana. All of them had similar type of beauty and form as compared to Radha. Their auspicious abodes adorned with gems and others metals. Because of different types of paintings they looked quite attractive. Their peaks were adorned with beautiful vases of gems which have divine lustre. They were created from best of gems.

## \|\| 4.194-196 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍādbahirūrdhvaṃ ca nāsti lokastadūrdhvakaḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ śūnyamayaṃ sarvaṃ tadaṃtā sṛṣṭireva ca \|\| 194 \|\|*

*rasātalebhyaḥ saptabhyo nāstyadhaḥ sṛṣṭireva ca \|*  
*tadadhaśca jalaṃ dhvāṃtamagaṃtavyamadṛśyakam \|\| 195 \|\|*

*brahmāṃḍāṃtaṃ tadbahiśca sarvaṃ matto niśāmaya \|\| 196 \|\|*

194-196. Goloka stood beyond the globe and above it, There is no other place above the same. Above that, it is all void there. There happens to be the end of the creation beyond the seven neither worlds, since there is only darkness and water below them and the place is inaccessible and nothing can be seen there. You listen from me the things, which one comes across, up to the globe and beyond it.

## Chapter 5

## \|\| 5.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*golokaṃ nikhilaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāste hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*punarājagmū rādhāyāḥ pradhānadvārameva ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said – Enjoying the view of the Goloka, the gods delightfully again reached the gate of Radhikas palace.

## \|\| 5.2-4 \|\|

*sadratnamaṇinirmāṇaṃ vedikāyugmasaṃyutam \|*  
*haridrākāramaṇinā vajrasaṃmiśritena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnaracitakapāṭena vibhūṣitam \|*  
*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśurvīrabhānumanuttamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca ratnābharaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*pītavastraparīdhānaṃ sadratnamukuṭojjvalam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. It was built with the best of gems two seater pedestals, It was studded with the gems of yellow colour besides jewels and the precious stoned They came across a door-keeper name Virabhanu who was quite graceful. He was seated on a gem-studded lion-throne, adorned with ornaments studded with gems, clad in yellow garment, with a gem-studded crown adoring his head.

## \|\| 5.5-6 \|\|

*iti śrībrahma vaivarte mahāpurāṇe śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṃḍe golokavarṇane śrīkṛṣṇastotrarājapaṭhanaṃ nāma paṃcamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tānuvāca dvārapālo niḥśaṃkaṃ tridaśeśvarān \|*  
*nāhaṃ vinā''jñayā gaṃtuṃ dātuṃ sāṃpratamīśvaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The doors of the palace were painted with beautiful paintings and all the gods narrated to the gate-keepers the cause of their arrival there. On hearing them, the gate-keeper fearlessly spoke to the gods, you I cannot let you in without the permission of the lord.

## \|\| 5.7-8 \|\|

*kiṃkarānpreṣayāmāsa śrīkṛṣṇasthānameva ca \|*  
*hareranujñāṃ saṃprāpya dadau gaṃtuṃ surānmune \|\| 7 \|\|*

*taṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdevā dvitīyaṃ dvāramuttamam \|*  
*tato'dhikaṃ vicitraṃ ca suṃdaraṃ sumanoharam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. О sage, he sent the messengers to lord Krishna and got his permission. Thereafter he allowed the gods to enter. The gods after getting permission, moved forward and came across another door which was equally beautiful having astonishing type of painting drawn over it.

## \|\| 5.9-10 \|\|

*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśuścaṃdrabhānuṃ ca nārada \|*  
*kiśoraṃ śyāmalaṃ cāru svarṇavetradharaṃ varam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*gopānāṃ ca samūhena paṃcalakṣeṇa śobhitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. О Narada, Chandrabhanu was serving there as the gate-keepers who was of tender age, of dark complexion and holding a staff of gold seated on the gem-studded lion-throne. He was adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments and surrounded by five lakhs of cowherds.

## \|\| 5.11 \|\|

*taṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdevāstṛtīyaṃ dvāramuttamam \|*  
*tato'tisundaraṃ citraṃ jvalantaṃ maṇitejasā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Meeting him, the gods reached the third gate which was more beautiful then the previous ones. It had beautiful paintings and the gem-studded in it were issuing lustre.

## \|\| 5.12-16 \|\|

*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśuḥ sūryabhānuṃ ca nārada \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ muralīhastaṃ kiśoraṃ śyāmasundaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

*maṇikuṇḍalayugmena kapolasthalarājitam \|*  
*ratnadaṃḍakaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ preṣyaṃ rādheśayoḥ param \|\| 13 \|\|*

*navalakṣeṇa gopānāṃ veṣṭitaṃ ca nṛpeṃdravat \|*  
*taṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdevāścaturthaṃ dvārameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tebhyo vilakṣaṇaṃ ramyaṃ sudīptaṃ maṇitejasā \|*  
*atyadbhutavicitreṇa bhūṣitaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśurvasubhānuṃ vrajeśvaram \|*  
*kiśoraṃ sundaravaraṃ maṇidaṇḍakaraṃ param \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. О Narada, they found the gate-keeper named Suryabhanu there, who was two-armed and was holding a flute in his hand. He was of tender age, having dark complexions, wearing a couple of kundalas in the ears and had beautiful cheeks. He was holding a staff of gems in his hand, he was the servant of Radhamadhava accompanied by nine lakhs of cowherds and was looking like a great king. Informing him the gods reached the fourth gate which was more beautiful then the earlier three and having the lustre of the gems, it was quite large, astonishing and studded with various types of jewels which were quite pleasant to look at. They came across the gate-keeper named Vasubhanu there, who looked like the lord of Vraja, quite tender in age, beautiful one and held a gem-studded staff in his hand.

## \|\| 5.17-18 \|\|

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*pakvabiṃbādharoṣṭhaṃ ca sasmitaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*taṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdevā pañcamaṃ dvārameva ca \|*  
*vajrabhittisthitaiścitravicitrairjvalitaṃ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. He was seated on a gem-studded lion-throne, adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments, having the lips like the wood-apple fruits. He wore a serene smile on the face and was quite pleasant to look at. Informing him the gods move forward and reached the fifth gate, which was built in the walls of precious stones and had beautiful paintings on the door.

## \|\| 5.19-21 \|\|

*dvārapālaṃ ca dadṛśurdevabhānuṃ ca tatra vai \|*  
*cāru siṃhāsanasthaṃ ca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*mayūrapicchacūḍaṃ ca ratnamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*kadaṃbapuṣpasaṃsaktasadratnakuṇḍalojjvalam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*caṃdanāgarukastūrīkuṅkumadravacarcitam \|*  
*nṛpeṃdravaratulyaṃ ca daśalakṣaprajānvitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. It was guarded by the gate-keepers named Devabhanu who was seated on the gem-studded lion-throne, adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments, wearing a crown of peacock feather adorned with the garland of gems. He wore the beautiful kundalas decorated with the flowers of kadamba. His body was plastered with the paste of sandal, aguru, kastwl and saffron. He, was surrounded by ten lakhs of cowherds and appeared like the lord himself.

## \|\| 5.22-27 \|\|

*taṃ vetrapāṇiṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdevā mudā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*vilakṣaṇaṃ dvāraṣaṭkaṃ citrarājivirājitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vajrabhittiyugmayukte puṣpamālyavibhūṣite \|*  
*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśuḥ śukrabhānuṃ vrajeśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*nānālaṃkāraśobhāḍhyaṃ daśalakṣaprajānvitam \|*  
*śrīkhaṃḍapallavāsaktakapolaṃ kuṇḍalojjvalam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tūrṇaṃ surāstaṃ sabhāṣya yayurdvāraṃ ca saptamam \|*  
*nānāprakāracitraṃ ca ṣaḍbhyaścātivilakṣaṇam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dvāre niyuktaṃ dadṛśū ratnabhānuṃ hareḥ priyam \|*  
*caṃdanokṣitasarvāṃgaṃ puṣpamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣaṇai ramyairmaṇiratnamanoharaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

22-27. Getting permission from him, the gods reached the sixth gate which quite surprising and had several lines of paintings. There were the walls of precious stones all round the place and the garland of lowers were decorating the wall, the gate-keeper was known as Sukrabhanu who was adorned with various types of ornaments and surrounded by ten lakhs of cowherds. He wore the kundalas resembling the tender leaves of sandal-wood. Informing him accordingly, gods moved on to the seventh, gates which was astonishing built and its workmanship was better then all the earlier six gates. The gate was guarded by Ratnabhanu, who was the loving gate-keeper of the lord. All his limbs were plastered with the sandal-paste and was adorned with the garland of flowers and the ornaments of beautiful gems.

## \|\| 5.28-29 \|\|

*gopairdvādaśalakṣaiśca rājeṃdramiva rājitam \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsanasthaṃ ca smerānanasaroruham \|\| 28 \|\|*

*taṃ vetrahastaṃ saṃbhāṣya jagmurdeveśvarā mudā \|*  
*vicitramaṣṭamaṃ dvāraṃ saptabhyo'pi vilakṣaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. He was surrounded by twelve lakhs of cowherds and appeared like a great king seated on the gem-studded lion-throne, wearing a serene smile on the face. Informing the gate-keeper, the god, moved ahead and reached the eight gate which was more astonishing than the earlier seven.

## \|\| 5.30-31 \|\|

*dauvārikaṃ te dadṛśuḥ supārśvaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*sasmitaṃ sundaravaraṃ śrīkhaṇḍatilakojjvalam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bandhujīvādharoṣṭhaṃ ca ratnakuṇḍalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*sarvālaṃkāraśobhāḍhyaṃ ratnadaṇḍadharaṃ varam \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. They came across the gate-keeper known as to Suparsva and who was smiling gracefully. He bore the tilaka on his forehead, had beautiful lips, adored with gem-studded ornament and held the staff of gems.

## \|\| 5.32-36 \|\|

*gopairdvādaśalakṣaiśca kiśoraiśca samanvitam \|*  
*tataḥ śīghraṃ yayurdevā navamaṃ dvāramīpsitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vajrasadratnaracitaṃ caturvedisamanvitam \|*  
*apūrvacitraracitamālajālairvirājitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dvārapālaṃ ca dadṛśuḥ subalaṃ lalitākṛtim \|*  
*nānābhūṣaṇaśobhāḍhyaṃ bhūṣaṇārhaṃ manoharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vajrairdvādaśalakṣaiśca saṃyuktaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*taṃ daṇḍahastaṃ sambhāṣya surā dvārātaraṃ yayuḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*viśiṣṭaṃ daśamaṃ dvāraṃ dṛṣṭvā te vismayaṃ yayuḥ \|*  
*sarvānirvacanīyaṃ cāpyadṛṣṭamaśrutaṃ mune \|\| 36\|\|*

32-36. He was surrounded by twelve lakhs of young cowherds. Speaking to him, the gods moved on and reached the ninth gate which was standing on the four pedestals made of gems and jewels besides various types of garland of flowers decorating it. The gate-keeper named Subala having the charming appearance was standing there, who was adorned with various types of gems and surrounded by twelve lakhs of cowherds, holding a beautiful staff in his hand. With this permissions the gods reached the tenth gate which was specially built. Looking at the gate, the gods were immensely surprised. О sage, the gate was beyond description and unheard of.

## \|\| 5.37-43 \|\|

*dadṛśurdvārapālaṃ ca sudāmānaṃ ca sundaram \|*  
*anivarcanīyarūpaṃ kṛṣṇatulyaṃ manoharam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*gopaviṃśatilakṣāṇāṃ samūhaiḥ parivāritam \|*  
*taṃ daṇḍahastaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva jagmurdvārāṃtaraṃ surāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*dvāramekādaśākhyaṃ ca sucitraṃ mahadadbhutam \|*  
*dvārapālaṃ ca tatrasthaṃ śrīdāmānaṃ vrajeśvaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

*rādhikāputratulyaṃ ca pītavastreṇa bhūṣitam \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitaratnasiṃhāsanasthitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnabhūṣābhirbhūṣitaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*candanāgurukastūrīkuṃkumena virājitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gaṇḍasthalakapolārhasadratnakuṇḍalojjvalam \|*  
*sadratnaśreṣṭharacitavicitramukuṭojjvalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*praphullamālatīmālājālaiḥ sarvāṃgabhūṣitam \|*  
*koṭigopaiḥ parivṛtaṃ rājendrādhikamujjvalam \|\| 43 \|\|*

37-43. The gate was guarded by the cowherd named SudamS having astonishing beauty. He resembled lord Krishna in beauty and was surrounded by twenty lakhs of cowherds, holding a staff in his hand. Meeting him the gods reached the eleventh gate which was also quite astonishing in structure and was guarded by the cowherd named Shridama, as the gate-keepers. He was like the son to Radhika and was clad in yellow garment and adorned with best of valuable gems, seated on a lion-throne which was studded with precious gems. His body was plastered with pleasant sandal-paste, aguru, kasturl and saffron beautiful ear ornaments of gems appeared in his ears. He was also wearing a crown on his head, the garland of blossoming jasmine flower adorned his body and was surrounded by a crores of cowherds.

## \|\| 5.44 \|\|

*taṃ saṃbhāṣya yayurdvāraṃ dvādaśākhyaṃ surā mudā \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitavedikābhiḥ samanvitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Informing him the gods moved on to the twelfth gates, which was built with the pedestals made with beautiful gems.

## \|\| 5.45 \|\|

*sarveṣāṃ durlabhaṃ citramadṛśyamaśrutaṃ mune \|*  
*vajrabhittisthitaṃ citraṃ sundaraṃ sumanoharam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. О sage, the walls were constructed with gems and several paintings were pained on them, which were quite inaccessible in nature, beyond vision and unheard of.

## \|\| 5.46-50 \|\|

*dvāre niyuktā dadṛśurdevā gopāṃganā varāḥ \|*  
*navayauvanasaṃpannā ratnābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pītavastraparīdhānāḥ kabarībhārabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*sugaṃdhimālatīmālā jālaiḥ sarvāṃgabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ratnakaṃkaṇakeyūraratnanūpurabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*ratnakuṃḍalayugmena gaṇḍasthalavirājitāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*candanāguru kastūrīkuṃkumadravacarcitāḥ \|*  
*pīnaśroṇībharānamrā nitaṃbābhārapīḍitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gopīnāṃ śatakoṭīnāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ preṣṭhā harerapi \|*  
*gopīśca koṭiśo dṛṣṭvā surāste vismayaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

46-50. The gods came across the cowherdesses who were deputed there and were quite youthful, adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments clad in yellow lower garment, having beautiful hair on the head and wearing the garland of fragrant jasmine flowers, their bodies were adorned with gem-studded ornaments like armlets, anklets, wristlets and the kuridalas, of gems, their bodies were plastered with sandal-paste, kastUrl, aguru and saffron. They had developed pelvic region as well as the breasts, their number was a hundred crores and were the best in all respect being beloved of lord Krishna. The gods were surprised at their sight.

## \|\| 5.51-53 \|\|

*saṃbhāṣya tā mudā yuktā yayurdvārātaraṃ mune \|*  
*tataśca kramaśo vipra triṣu dvāreṣu tatra vai \|\| 51 \|\|*

*gopāṃganānāṃ śreṣṭhāśca dadṛśuḥ sumanoharāḥ \|*  
*varāṇāṃ ca varā ramyā dhanyā mānyāśca śobhanāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*sarvāḥ saubhāgyayuktāśca rādhikāyāḥ priyāśca tāḥ \|*  
*bhūṣitā bhūṣaṇai ramyaiḥ prodbhinnanavayauvanāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. О sage, getting permission from him, the gods moved forward with a pleasant mind. О Brahmana, thus they came across further these cowherdesses on three more gates, who were the best, beautiful, graceful and were fortunate one and were quite close to Radha. They were adorned with beautiful ornaments and their youthfulness was merging out of their bodies.

## \|\| 5.54-64 \|\|

*evaṃ dvāratrayaṃ dṛṣṭvā svapnā jñānādbhutāśrutam \|*  
*adṛśyamatiramyaṃ cāpyanirūpyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tāstāḥ saṃbhāṣya devāste vismitā yayurīśvarāḥ \|*  
*rādhikābhyaṃtaraṃ dvāraṃ ṣoḍaśākhyaṃ manoharam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sarvāsāṃ ca pradhānaṃ ca gopyaṃ gopāṃganāgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*trayastriṃśadvayasyānāṃ nikarairveṣṭitaṃ mune \|\| 56 \|\|*

*teṣāmanirvacanīyairnānāguṇasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*rūpayauvanasaṃpannai ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ratnakaṃkaṇakeyūratnanūpurabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*sadratnakiṃkiṇījālaimardhyadeśavibhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ratnakuṃḍalayugmena gaṃḍasthalavirājitaiḥ \|*  
*praphullamālatīmālājālairvakṣasthalojjvalaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*śaratpārvaṇapadmānāṃ prabhāṃ muṣṇanmukheṃdubhiḥ \|*  
*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālena veṣṭitaiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*pakvabiṃbādharoṣṭhaiśca smerānanasaroruhaiḥ \|*  
*pakvadāḍimabījābhiḥ śobhitairdaṃtapaṃktibhiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*cārucaṃpakavarṇābhirmadhyasthalakṛśairmune \|*  
*gajamauktikayuktābhirnāsikābhirvirājitaiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*khageṃdracārucaṃcūnāṃ śobhāmuṣṇābhireva ca \|*  
*gajeṃdragaṃḍakaṭhina stanabhārabharānataiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pīnaśroṇibharārtaiśca mukuṃdapadamānasaiḥ \|*  
*nimeṣarahitā devā dvāraṃ ca dadṛśuśca tāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

54-64. Thus all the three gates were seen by the gods like a dream and were quite astonishing unheard of, quite beautiful and could hardly be described by the intellectuals. Looking at them and talking with the beautiful damsels, the gods were surprised and ultimately they reached the sixteenth gate which happened to be the main gate of the inner apartment of Radha, it was the best of all the gate and was guarded by only the cowherdesses. The thirty cowherdesses of the age comparable to that of Radha, were guarding the gates their costumes and ornaments were beyond description. They possessed many good qualities besides beauty, youthfulness and were adorned with gem-studded ornaments including the armlets, anklets and wristlets of gems. Their waist-bands were decorated with the best of small-bells their ears were adorned with beautiful ear-ornaments. The garlands of blossoming jasmine flowers were adorning their breasts. Their faces resembled the full-moon of, the winter seasons the beautiful Parijata flowers were inserted in their hair-do on the heads. They were adorned with various types of ornaments; their lies looked like the ripe wood-apples and wore a serene smile on their faces. Their teeth resembled the ripe pomegranate fruit which added to their beauty. All of them had the beautiful fair-complexion like the campaka flowers. All of them were slander-waisted and their noses were adorned with pearls, Their noses resembled the beak of Garuda and their breasts were stiff like the temples of the elephants, their hips were quite heavy and their mind was attracted towards lord Krishna. For a moment the gods looked at the cowherdesses.

## \|\| 5.65-66 \|\|

*lasadramaṇiratnaiśca vedikāyugmaśobhitam \|*  
*harinmaṇīnāṃ staṃbhānāṃ samūhaiḥ saṃyutaṃ sadā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*siṃdūrākāramaṇibhirmadhyasthalavirājitaiḥ \|*  
*pārijāta prasūnānāṃ mālājālairvibhūṣitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

79-88. О Narada, the house was decorated with crores of invaluable and beautiful kalasas of gems and diamonds decorated with vases of gems and the sweet sound of music was emerging from the same. The vina and other musical instruments were being played upon with the beating or the double drums and their sound was quite pleasant. The songs relating to the glory of Radha and Krishna were being recited. All the gods felt surprised with the book of this astonishing type of houses they listened to the sweet music there and witnessed the best of the dance. All the gods stood there attentively and they felt attracted towards the sound of the music, Thereafter the gods spotted a gem-studded beautiful lion-throne which was as vast as a bow. It looked circular from all the sides. Various types of small vases made in gems were fixed to it. The astonishing types of puppets, the flowers and the artificial forests were painted in the same. О Brahmana, they witnessed an astonishing type of the mass of lustre which resembled the lustre to crores of suns, it was shining like the divine flames and its glory was spread on the height of seven tala trees. The mass of lustre could snatch away the tejas of all and was pervading the entire asramas, it was all-pervading, the seed of all and could dazzle the eyes of all.

## \|\| 5.89-91 \|\|

89-91. At the sight of the blissful one, the eyes of all the gods were filled with tears and hair on this body stood and ends. They could have a glimpse of the success ahead. All of them bowed before the mass of lustre. Thereafter all of them got up and went closer to the mass of lustre and looked at it quite carefully.

## \|\| 5.92-93 \|\|

*dhyātvaivaṃ jagatāṃ dhātā babhūva saṃpuṭāṃjaliḥ \|*

О Narada, while looking at it carefully the hands of Brahma, the creator of the universe were automatically folded, He made Shiva to stand on his right and Dharma to his left and with their mind filled with devotion, all of them started offering prayer to the lord, who is beyond the comprehension of everyone and is the great soul.

## \|\| 5.94 \|\|

*. brahmovāca \|*

94\. Brahma said – I bow in reverence to the form of lustre who happens to be the best, bestower of the boons, the cause of the boons and the cause of all the creatures.

## \|\| 5.95 \|\|

*maṃgalaṃ maṃgalānāṃ ca maṃgalaṃ maṃgalapradam \|*

95\. He is the one who happens to be the prosperity for all the prosperities, bestower of prosperity and the base of all of them. I bow in reverence to the same lustre.

## \|\| 5.96 \|\|

*sthitaṃ sarvatra nirliptamātmarūpaṃ parātparam \|*  
*nirīhamavitarkyaṃ ca tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The one who is all-pervading, uninvolved, the form of Atmana and beyond the comprehension of all, indifferent and the subject of discussion for everyone. I bow in reverence to that lustre.

## \|\| 5.97-98 \|\|

*saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ brahma jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*sākāraṃ ca nirākāraṃ tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 97 \|\|*

*tamanirvacanīyaṃ ca vyaktamavyaktamekakam \|*  
*svecchāmayaṃ sarvarūpaṃ tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. The one who is of visible and invisible Brahman, the form of flame, eternal and ever lasting, having no qualities as well as possessing all the qualities, I bow in reverence to such a type of lustre. The one who is manifesto beyond description and unmanifest, the supreme one, the one who moves at will and is the form of all. I bow in reverence to such a type of lustre.

## \|\| 5.99 \|\|

*guṇatrayavibhāgāya rūpatrayadharaṃ param \|*  
*kalayā te kṛtāḥ sarve kiṃ jānanti śruteḥ param \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. He is the one who takes to three forms because of the three qualities (sattva, rajas and tamas). All the gods have emerged from your rays. You are beyond shruti and therefore no one can be aware of your true form.

## \|\| 5.100 \|\|

*sarvādhāraṃ sarvarūpaṃ sarvabījamabījakam \|*  
*sarvāṃtakamanantaṃ ca tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Therefore the one who is the base of everyone, the form of everyone the cause of everyone's without seed and is the cause of end of everyone and is beyond measures I bow in reverence to the divine lustre like this.

## \|\| 5.101-102 \|\|

*lakṣyaṃ ṣaṅguṇarūpaṃ ca varṇanīyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*

*aśarīraṃ vigrahavadiṃdriyaṃ yadatīṃdriyam \|*  
*yadasākṣi sarvasākṣi tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. You are the from of all the qualities, the only goal, are discussed by the people of wisdom always but how can I describe your invisible form? I bow in reverence to such a form of tejas. You are formless as well as with form, having the organ of senses and without them, you have no witness but you serve as a witness of all. 1 therefore adore the form of tejas.

## \|\| 5.103 \|\|

*gamanārhamapādaṃ yadacakṣuḥ sarvadarśanam \|*  
*hastāsyahīnaṃ yadbhoktṛ tejorūpaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. You move at several places without feet, you can see everything without the eyes and can eat without the hands and the mouth, I bow in reverence to that lustre.

## \|\| 5.104-105 \|\|

*vede nirūpitaṃ vastu santaḥ śaktāśca varṇitum \|*

104-105. The intellectual are unable to truly visualise the form described in the Vedas but even the Vedas as conceived him beyond description. I, therefore, adore the form of that tejas. You are the one who is the lord of everyone and is otherwise also, the one who happens to be the beginning and end of everything, who happens to be the soul of everyone and also behave otherwise, I adore the form of that tejas.

## \|\| 5.106 \|\|

*ahaṃ vidhātā jagato vedānāṃ janakaḥ svayam \|*

106\. I am myself the creator of the universe and the Vedas, the protector of Dharma and the destroyer of the universe therefore there is no one else to offer prayer to you.

## \|\| 5.107-108 \|\|

107-108. Dharma was deputed only to serve you. Shiva was entrusted at your command to serve as a destroyer for the prescribed period and I have become the creators of the universe because of my serving at your lotus-like feet. Because of you I bestow the reward for the deeds. Therefore you happen to be the lord of the devotees like us.

## \|\| 5.109 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍe biṃbasadṛśe bhūtvā viṣayiṇo vayam \|*

109\. We are attracted towards the worldly elements in this universe like the word-apple. Similarly there are innumerable devotees of your sin the other globes.

## \|\| 5.110-111 \|\|

*yathā na saṃkhyā reṇūnāṃ tathā teṣāmaṇīyasām \|*

*ekaikalomavivare brahmāṃḍamekamekakam \|*  
*yasyaiva mahato viṣṇoḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśastavaiva saḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

110-111. Since the particles of dust and atoms can never be counted similarly the number of your devotees cannot be counted but the one who is the creator of everyone's who can be competent enough to offer prayers to him because the Maha-Vishnu one in whose hair-pit a complete globe is enshrined happens to be only the sixteenth part of your rays.

## \|\| 5.112 \|\|

*dhyāyaṃte yoginaḥ sarve tavaitadrūpamīpsitam \|*

112\. All the yogis meditate upon your present, form and with their mind filled with devotion, your devotees always serve at your feet.

## \|\| 5.113-119 \|\|

*kiśoraṃ suṃdarataraṃ yakṣaṃ kamanīyakam \|*

*navīnajaladaśyāmapītāṃbaradharaṃ varam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ muralīhastaṃ sasmitaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 114 \|\|*

*mayūrapicchacūḍaṃ ca mālatījālamaṃḍitam \|*  
*caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumadravacarcitam \|\| 115 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnasārāṇāṃ sārabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitakirīṭamukuṭojjvalam \|\| 116 \|\|*

*śaratpraphullapadmānāṃ prabhāmoṣyāsyacaṃdrakam \|*  
*pakvabiṃbasamānena hyadharoṣṭhena rājitam \|\| 117 \|\|*

*pakvadāḍimabījābhadaṃtapaṃktimanoharam \|*  
*kelīkadaṃbamūle ca sthitaṃ rāsarasonmukham \|\| 118 \|\|*

*gopīvaktrasmitatanuṃ rādhāvakṣaḥsthalasthitam \|*  
*evaṃ vāṃchitarūpaṃ te dṛṣṭuṃ ko vā na cotsukaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

113-119. Therefore, О lord, you appear before us in your tender, beautiful and attractive form, which is like the new clouds and has dark-complexion, clad in yellow lower garment, having two holding a flute in the hand, wearing a smile on the face, quite harming and the best, wearing a peacock father over the head, decorated with garlands of jasmine flowers, having the sandal-paste plastered over all the limbs. The sandal-paste, kastiiri, aguru, and saffron are applied over all the limbs and you are adorned with all the ornaments studded with gem, wearing a kirlt a-mukuta on the head, having the face of the fully blossomed lotus flowers of the winter season and the lips resembling the ripe wood-apples. You are the one having the teeth like the ripe pomegranate seeds, standing under the kadamba tree anxious to perform the divine dance with the cowherdesses, glancing at your smiling face, the one in whose chest Radha always dwells. Who will not be anxious to have a look at such a charming face of yours?

## \|\| 5.120-124 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā viśvasṛṭ praṇanāma punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ stotreṇa tuṣṭāva dharmo'pi śaṃkaraḥ svayam \|\| 120 \|\|*

*nanāma bhūyobhūyaśca sāśrupūrṇavilocanaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhato'pi punaḥ stotraṃ pracakrustridaśeśvarāḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

*vyāptāstatrāśrame sarve śrīkṛṣṇatejasā mune \|*  
*stavarājamimaṃ nityaṃ brahmeśadharmabhiḥ kṛtam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*pūjākāle harerevaṃ bhaktiyuktaśca yaḥ paṭhet \|*  
*sudurlabhāṃ dṛḍhāṃ bhaktiṃ niścalāṃ labhate hareḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

*surāsuramunīṃdrāṇāṃ durlabhaṃ dāsyameva ca \|*

120-124. Thus speaking Brahma the creator of the universe, started bowing before him again and again. Similarly, Shiva and Dharma also offered prayers to him with their eyes filled with tears and bowing before him again and again. The gods also offered their prayer remaining there. О sage, in that ashrama all the gods were influenced with the lustre of lord Krishna, whosoever will recite this stotra of lord Krishna recited by Brahma, Vishnu and Dharma after offering pitja, with devotion daily, he will achieve the inaccessible and deep devotion of the lord.

## \|\| 5.125 \|\|

*ihaiva viṣṇutulyaśca vikhyātaḥ pūjito dhuvam \|*  
*vāksiddhirmaṃtrasiddhiśca bhavettasya suniścitam \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. This is inaccessible to the gods, the demons and the sages and if one gets the slavehood of the lord, all his siddhis including anima and Salokya and all the four types of salvation are achieved by him. He is adored in the universe like Vishnu and becomes famous like him. He attains success in speech as well as mantras.

## \|\| 5.126-127 \|\|

*sarvasaubhāmyasaṃyuktaṃ yaśasā pūritaṃ jagat \|*  
*putraśca vidyā kavitā niścalā kamalā tathā \|\| 126 \|\|*

*patnī pativratā sādhvī suśīlā susthirāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*kīrtiśca cirakālīnā tvaṃte kṛṣṇāṃtike gatiḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

126-127. He achieves all the fortunes sound health and his glory spreads in the universe. He achieves sons, knowledge, poetry and the indestructible riches. The goddess Lakshmi always resides him. He becomes chaste and noble and all his people becomes stable. His glory pervades the universe for a long time and ultimately he achieves the abode of lord Krishna.

## Chapter 6

## \|\| 6.1-5 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*dhyātvā stutvā ca tiṣṭhaṃto devāste tejasaḥ puraḥ \|*  
*dadṛśustejaso madhye śarīraṃ kamanīyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sajalāṃbhodavarṇābhaṃ sasmitaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*paramāhlādakaṃ rūpaṃ trailokyacittamohanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gaṃḍasthalakapolābhyāṃ jvalanmakara kuṇḍalam \|*  
*sadratnanūpurābhyāṃ ca caraṇāṃbhojarājitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vahniśuddhaharidrābhāmūlyavastravirājitam \|*  
*maṇiratneṃdrasārāṇāṃ svecchā kautukanirmitaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣaṇai ramyaistadrūpeṇaiva bhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*vinodamuralīyuktabiṃbādharamanoharam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Narayana said – Standing before the mass of lustre the gods offered there salutations and prayers and soon after that they found a human body inside the lustre which was having the complexion of the clouds filled with water, quite graceful, wearing a serene smile on the face. Immensely charming, blissful, the one who could attract all the three worlds, wearing makara-kundalas in the ears gem-studded anklets worn over the lotus-like feet, pure like the fire and was clad in yellow garment, was adorned with best of ornaments studded with gems and rubles holding a flute, pleased all having the lips like the ripe wood-apples.

## \|\| 6.6 \|\|

*prasannekṣaṇapaśyaṃtaṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram \|*  
*sadratnaguṭikāyuktakavacoraḥsthalojjvalam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He was looking at the gods delightfully and was anxious to do good to his devotees. He had a vast chest which looked like the doors of the box illumining everything.

## \|\| 6.7-10 \|\|

*kaustubhāsaktasadratnapradīptatejasojjvalam \|*  
*tatra tejasi cārvaṃgīṃ dadṛśū rādhikābhidhām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*paśyaṃtaṃ sasmitaṃ kāṃtaṃ paśyaṃtīṃ vakracakṣuṣā \|*  
*muktāpaṃktiviniṃdyaikadaṃtapaṃktivirājitām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyāṃ śaratpaṃkajalocanām \|*  
*śaratpārvaṇacandrābhāviniṃdāsyamanoharām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*baṃdhujīvaprabhāmuṣṭādharauṣṭharu cirānanām \|*  
*raṇanmaṃjīrayugmena pādāṃbujavirājitām \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. The best of kaustubha gem worn by him was illuminating the environment. The gods also found Radha with beautiful figure within the mass of lustre. She was looking with her side-glance with a smile on her face towards his beloved. She had the line of teeth which could put even the jewels to shame. She was pleasantly smiling with grace! her eyes resembled the lotus flowers of winter season, her face had a glory before which the moon of the winter season of no consequence. She looked quite graceful, she had beautiful lips which could steal away the beauty of the flowers at noon. Her mouth was looking charming, she was adorned with the anklets which produced the dangling sound.

## \|\| 6.11-14 \|\|

*maṇīṃdrāṇāṃ prabhāmoṣanakharājivirājitām \|*  
*kuṅakumābhāsamācchādya padādhorāgabhūṣitām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnasārāṇāṃ raśanāśroṇibhūṣitām \|*  
*hutāśanaviśuddhāṃśukāmūlyajvalitojjvalām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mahāmaṇīṃdrasārāṇāṃ kiṅkiṇīmadhyasaṃyutām \|*  
*sadratnahārakeyūrakarakaṃkaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ratneṃdrasāraracitakapolojjvalakuṇḍalām \|*  
*karṇopari maṇīndrāṇāṃ karṇabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. She had beautiful nails which were shining like the gems. The soles of her feet were tainted with saffron and were emitting beautiful shine. She was wearing the waist-band which was made of the best of gems and her pelvic region appeared quite graceful. She had the element of having been clad in the fine and valuable garment purified by fire. Her tinkling ornament was studded with the best of gems. She was also wearing the garland of gems besides the armlets and wristlets. The gem-studded kundalas worn in the ears added to her glory, she had also the par ornaments studded with gems adorning her ears.

## \|\| 6.15 \|\|

*khageṃdracaṃcunāsāgra gajeṃdramauktikānvitām \|*  
*mālatīmālayā vakrakabarībhāraśobhi tām \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Her nose resembled the beak of Garuda and her nose was decorated with the pearls. In her curly hair, the garland of jasmine flowers were decorated.

## \|\| 6.16 \|\|

*mālayā kaustubheṃdrāṇāṃ vakṣaḥsthalasuśobhitām \|*  
*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālojjvalāṃbarām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Her breasts were decorated with the rosaries of the best of diamonds. With the decoration of the garland of Parijdta flowers, her costumes appeared more graceful.

## \|\| 6.17-19 \|\|

*ratnāṃgulīya nikaraiḥ karāṃgulivibhūṣitām \|*  
*divyaśaṃkhavikāraiśca citrarāgavibhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sūkṣmasūtrākṛtai ramyairbhūṣitā śaṃkhabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*sadratnasāraguṭikārājisūtrasuśobhitām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prataptasvarṇavarṇābhāmācchādya cāruvigrahām \|*  
*nitambaśroṇilalitāṃ pīnastananatāṃbarām \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. The fingers of her hands were decorated with the gem-studded finger rings, she also wore the best of the ornaments of the conches which were entwined in the silken cord. By interweaving the gem in the red silken cord it appeared as if they had put themselves to shame. She was clad in spotless garments having the colour of the molten gold. Her body was looking quite charming. She appeared like a figure of elegance from the pelvic region. Because of the stiff breasts, the costume was folded.

## \|\| 6.20 \|\|

*bhūṣitāṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ sauṃdaryeṇa vibhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*vismitāstridaśāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tāmīśvarīṃ varām \|*  
*tuṣṭuvuste surāḥ sarve pūrṇasarvamanorathāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. She was looking beautiful adorned with all the ornaments. All the gods felt surprised having a look at, the goddess. Thinking in their mind that they were successful in their mission, they started eulogising her.

## \|\| 6.21 \|\|

*. brahmovāca \|*  
*tava caraṇasaroje manmanaścaṃcarīko bhramatu satatamīśa premabhaktyā saroje \|*  
*bhuvanavibhavabhogāttāpaśāṃtyauṣadhāyasudṛḍhasu paripakvādehibhakti cadāsyam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Brahma said – О lord, the black-wasps of my mind who always roam about around your lotus-like feet and you bestow your devotion which should enable us to remove the sufferings emerging out of the riches of the universe and provide us; to remove the sufferings emerging out of the riches of the universe and provide us peace and your slavehood.

## \|\| 6.22 \|\|

*. śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*bhavajalanidhimagnambittamīno madīyo bhramati satatamasminghorasaṃsāra kūpe \|*  
*viṣayamativiniṃdyaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārarūpamapanaya tava bhaktiṃ dehi pādāraviṃde \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Shiva said – My mind like the fish is floating in the ocean of the universe. Therefore removing the condemned action of the destruction of the universe and relieving me from the same, you bestow the devotion of your lotus-like feet.

## \|\| 6.23 \|\|

*. dharma uvāca \|*  
*tava nijajanasārddhaṃ saṃgamo me madīśa bhavatu viṣayabaṃdhacchedane tīkṣṇakhaṅgaḥ \|*  
*tava caraṇasaroje sthānadānaikaheturjanuṣi januṣi bhaktiṃ dehi pādāravinde \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Dharma said – О my lord, you bestow me a sharp sword which could destroy the fetters of worldly attractions and enjoy the company of your devotees. It happens to be the only way to serve at your feet. You bestow the devotion of your lotus-like feet in each one of my births.

## \|\| 6.24 \|\|

*ityevaṃ stavanaṃ kṛtvā paripūrṇaikasānasāḥ \|*  
*kāmapūrasya puratastiṣṭhato rādhikāpateḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Thus offering prayers, having their desires fulfilled, all the three of them stood before Krishna, the spouse of Radhika.

## \|\| 6.25 \|\|

*surāṇāṃ stavanaṃ śrutvā tānu vāca kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca vacanaṃ smerānanasaroruhaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. On hearing the prayer of the gods, the compassionate lord Krishna with a smiling face spoke to them, the beneficial and truthful words.

## \|\| 6.26-27 \|\|

*. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*tiṣṭhatāgacchata surā madīyā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śivāśrayāṇāṃ kuśalaṃ praṣṭuṃ yuktaṃ na sāṃpratam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*niściṃtā bhavatātraiva kā ciṃtā vo mayi sthite \|*  
*sthito'haṃ sarvajīveṣu pratyakṣo'haṃ stavena vai \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Lord Krishna said – О gods, you are my people there is no doubt about it. Therefore you come along and have your seats. Such of the people who has takes refuge with lord Shiva, it would not be proper to enquire about their welfare, is such you be rest assured at this place. How can you have any cause of worry when I am there. I pervade all the creatures, but I appear in person only after salutations.

## \|\| 6.28 \|\|

*yuṣmākaṃ yamabhiprāyaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi niścitam \|*  
*śubhāśubhaṃ ca yatkarma kāle khalu bhaviṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I am quite well-aware of the purpose of your arrival here. One gets the reward of good and bad deeds at the appropriate time.

## \|\| 6.29 \|\|

*mahatkṣudraṃ ca yatkarma sarvaṃ kālakṛtaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*sve sve kāle ca taravaḥ phalitāḥ puṣpiṇaḥ sadā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. О god, the big or the small appears, according to the time. The trees blossom according to the time.

## \|\| 6.30-34 \|\|

*paripakvaphalāḥ kāle kāle pakvaphalānvitāḥ \|*  
*sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vipatsaṃpacchokaciṃtāśubhāśubham \|\| 30 \|\|*

*svakarmaphalaniṣṭhaṃ ca sarvakāle'pyupasthitam \|*  
*na hi kasya priyaḥ ko vā vipriyo vā jagattraye \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kāle kāryavaśātsarve bhavaṃtyevāpriyāḥ priyāḥ \|*  
*rājāno manavaḥ pṛthvyāṃ dṛṣṭā yuṣmābhiratra vai \|\| 32 \|\|*

*svakarmaphalapākena sarve kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākamadhunā caiva goloke yatkṣaṇaṃ gatam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāṃ tatkṣaṇenaiva saptamanvataraṃ gatam \|*  
*iṃdrāḥ sapta gatāstatra deveṃdra ścāṣṭamo'dhunā \|\| 34 \|\|*

30-34. At proper time they bear fruits and at proper time they have unripe fruits. The pleasure, pain, misery, wealth, grief, worries, good and bad appear before a person according to the result of his own deeds at suitable times. In fact, there is no one liked or hated in the universe. It happens according to time, that the unliked person is also liked. You have observed the conduct of the people like Manus and the kings. Bearing the results of their own deeds, all of them proceed to the heavenly abodes. The moment you have spent in the Goloka presently, during the same period on the earth seven manvantaras have elapsed, seven Indras have spent their times and currently the eighth Indras is in position.

## \|\| 6.35 \|\|

*kālacakraṃ bhramatyeva madīyaṃ ca divāniśam \|*  
*indrāśca mānavā bhūpāḥ sarve kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. My wheel of time rotates always; therefore even Indra, Manu and kings disappear according to the time.

## \|\| 6.36 \|\|

*kīrtiḥ pṛthvyāṃ puṇyamadya kathāmātrāvaśeṣitam \|*  
*adhunā'pi ca rājāno duṣṭāśca hariniṃdakāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. At present only their glory, virtues, and the stories of their noble deeds are known on earth. Even now there are a number of kings who are wicked and denounce lord Hari.

## \|\| 6.37 \|\|

*babhūvurbahavo bhūmau mahābala parākramāḥ \|*  
*sarve yāsyaṃti rājānaḥ kālāṃtaravaśaṃ dhuvam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. There had been several valorous kings on earth but all of them had ultimate to leave for the heavenly abode.

## \|\| 6.38 \|\|

*upasthito'pi kālo'yaṃ vāto vāti niraṃtaram \|*  
*vahnirdahati sūryaśca tapatyeva mamājñayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The time is present even at the moment. With my command the wind always blows, the fire bums and the sun emits the heat.

## \|\| 6.39 \|\|

*vyādhayaḥ saṃti deheṣu mṛtyuścarati jaṃtuṣu \|*  
*varṣaṃtyete jaladharāḥ sarve devā mamājñayā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О gods, the ailments appear in the bodies at my command, the death is influencing all the creatures and the clouds pour rain at my command.

## \|\| 6.40 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyaniṣṭhā viprāśca taponiṣṭhāstapodhanāḥ \|*  
*bra*  
*hmarṣayo brahmaniṣṭhā yoganiṣṭhāśca yoginaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The Brahmanas are engaged in their respective duties, the ascetics are engaged in tapas, the Brahmarsis are engaged in search of Brahman and yogis are engaged in yogic practices.

## \|\| 6.41 \|\|

*te sarve madbhayādbhītāḥ svakarmadharmatatparāḥ \|*  
*madbhaktāścaiva niḥśaṃkāḥ karmanirmūlakārakāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. All of them are engaged in their respective dharma getting panicky from me, but my devotees who destroy the karmas are quite free.

## \|\| 6.42 \|\|

*devāḥ kālasya kālo'haṃ vidhātā dhātureva ca \|*  
*saṃhārakartuḥ saṃhartā pātuḥ pātā parātparaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. O gods, I am death for the death, the creator for the creator and destroyer of the destroyer, besides being the protector of the protector.

## \|\| 6.43 \|\|

*mamājñayā'yaṃ saṃhartā nāmrā tena haraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ viśvasṛṭ sṛṣṭihetoḥ pātā dharmasya rakṣaṇāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Shiva became destroyer at my command that is why he is called Нага. You are the creator of the universe being the cause of the universe and because you protect them you become the protector of dharma.

## \|\| 6.44 \|\|

*brahmāditṛṇaparyantaṃ sarveṣāmahamīśvaraḥ \|*  
*svakarmaphaladātā'haṃ karmanirmūlakārakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. I happen to be the lord of everyone, starting from Brahma to a straw. I bestow the reward of ones own deeds and uproots the deeds.

## \|\| 6.45 \|\|

*ahaṃ yānsaṃhariṣyāmi kasteṣāmapi rakṣitā \|*  
*yānahaṃ pālayiṣyāmi teṣāṃ haṃtā na ko'pi vā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Who can protect the creatures who are to be killed by me? Who could protect the creatures who are to be destroyed by me.

## \|\| 6.46 \|\|

*sarveṣāmapi saṃhartā sraṣṭā pātā'hameva ca \|*  
*nāhaṃ śaktaśca bhaktānāṃ saṃhāre nityadehinām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I happen to be the creator, the preserver and the destroyer of everyone but I am unable to destroy the devotees who have achieved the eternal body.

## \|\| 6.47 \|\|

*bhaktā mamānugā nityaṃ matpādārcanatatparāḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ bhaktāṃtike śaśvatteṣāṃ rakṣaṇahetava \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The devotees always remain engaged in the adoration of my feet. Therefore, they follow me and I always remain with them for their protection.

## \|\| 6.48 \|\|

*sarve naśyaṃti brahmāṇḍe prabhavaṃti punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*na me bhaktāḥ praṇaśyanti niḥśaṃkāśca nirāpadaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In the universe everything ms destroyed again and again, reemerging at the same time, but my devotees never get destroyed but remain quite hail and hearty and freely roam about in the universe.

## \|\| 6.49 \|\|

*ato vipaścitaḥ sarve dāsyaṃ vāṃchaṃti no varam \|*  
*ye māṃ dāsyaṃ prayācaṃte dhanyāste'nye ca vaṃcitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Therefore all the intellectuals aspire for achieving my slavehood and they do not aspire for any other boon. Graceful are the person who aspire for my slavehood and other people are deprived of it.

## \|\| 6.50 \|\|

*janmamṛtyujarāvyādhi bhayaṃ ca yamayātanā \|*  
*anyeṣāṃ karmiṇāmasti na bhaktānāṃ ca karhicit \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Thus the birth, the death, the old age, ailment, fear and the torture of Yama are meant for other people and not for my devotees.

## \|\| 6.51-54 \|\|

*bhaktā na liptāḥ pāpeṣu puṇyeṣu sarvaka rmiṇaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ dhunomi teṣāṃ ca karmabhogānsuniścitam \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ahaṃ prāṇaśca bhaktānāṃ bhaktāḥ prāṇā mamāpi ca \|*  
*dhyāyaṃte te ca māṃ nityaṃ tānsmarāmi divāniśam \|\| 52 \|\|*

*cakraṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśāraṃ sutīkṣṇakam \|*  
*yattejaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśo'pi nāsti sarveṣu jīviṣu \|\| 53\|\|*

*bhaktāntike tu taccakraṃ dattvā rakṣārthamīpsitam \|*  
*na svāsthyaṃ na ca prītirme yāmi teṣāṃ ca sannidhim \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. Because my devotees are never involved in sinful ways and always engage themselves in noble deeds and as such I surely destroy the result of their deeds, I happen to be the life of the devotees who daily meditate upon me while I myself recite their name daily. The Sudarsana-cakra with sixteenth spokes is very sharp and one-sixteenth of its lustre can destroy the entire universe, I don’t feel satisfied; by giving away the cakra for the protection of my devotees. Therefore I myself remain with them always.

## \|\| 6.55 \|\|

*na me svāsthyaṃ ca vaikuṃṭhe goloke rādhikāṃtike \|*  
*yatra tiṣṭhaṃti bhaktāste tatra tiṣṭhāmyaharniśam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. I don’t feel stable in the Goloka or with Radha as much as I do by remaining with my devotees whenever they stay.

## \|\| 6.56 \|\|

*prāṇebhyaḥ preyasī rādhā sthitorasi divāniśam \|*  
*yūyaṃ prāṇādhikā lakṣmīrna me bhaktātparā priyā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Though Radha is dearer to me than my life and she dwells always on my chest. But you devotees are much dearer for me than Lakshmi.

## \|\| 6.57 \|\|

*bhaktadattaṃ ca yaddravyaṃ bhaktyā 'śnāmi sureśvarāḥ \|*  
*abhaktadattaṃ nāśnāmi dhruvaṃ bhuṃkte baliṃ svayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О lord of the gods, I lovingly accept the offerings made ray devotees with deep sense of devotion but whatever is given by a none-believers to me is not accepted me at all. Such offerings are consumed by Bali himself.

## \|\| 6.58 \|\|

*strīputrasvajanāṃstyaktvā dhyāyaṃte māmaharniśam \|*  
*yuṣmānvihāya tānnityaṃ smarāmyahamaharniśam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The devotees do not care for their wives, sons and others members of the family and spend towards the time only in adoring me. Therefore leaving you all, I always adore such of my devotees.

## \|\| 6.59-60 \|\|

*duṣṭā yadā me bhaktānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāmapi \|*  
*kratūnāṃ devatānāṃ ca hiṃsāṃ kurvaṃti niścitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tathā'ciraṃ te naśyaṃti yathā vahnau tṛṇāni ca \|*  
*na ko'pi rakṣitā teṣāṃ mayi haṃtaryupasthite \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. That is why in case the wicked people troubles my devotees, Brahmanas, cows, yajnas and gods, they get destroyed like the straw which in the fire. Such people cannot be protected by anyone till I am there.

## \|\| 6.61-62 \|\|

*yāsyāmi pṛthivīṃ devā yāta yūyaṃ svamālayam \|*  
*yūyaṃ caivāṃśarūpeṇa śīghraṃ gacchata bhūtalam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ityuktvā jagatāṃ nātho gopānā hūya gopikāḥ \|*  
*uvāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ yatsamayocitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Therefore, О gods, I shall incarnate on earth but all of you should return to your respective abodes. I shall incarnate on earth from my Goloka. Having been thus spoken to the gods, the lord of the universe, called for the cowherds and cowherdesses and talked to them appropriately according to the time.

## \|\| 6.63 \|\|

*gopā gopyaśca śṛṇuta yāta naṃdavrajaṃ param \|*  
*vṛṣabhānugṛhe kṣipraṃ gaccha tvamapi rādhike \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Не said, "О cowherds and cowherdesses listen to me, you go to Vraja on earth and О Radhika, you proceed to the abode of Vrsabhanu."

## \|\| 6.64-66 \|\|

*vṛṣabhānupriyā sādhvī naṃdagopakalāvatī \|*  
*subalasya sutā sā ca kamalāṃśasamudbhavā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*pitṝṇāṃ mānasī kanyā dhanyā mānyā ca yoṣitām \|*  
*purā durvāsasaḥ śāpājjanma tasyā vraje gṛhe \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tasyā gṛhe janma labha śīghraṃ naṃdavrajaṃ vraja \|*  
*tvāmahaṃ bālarūpeṇa gṛhṇāmi kamalānane \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. Vrsabhanu has a loving queen known as the chaste loving queen known as the chaste Kalavati who happened to be the daughter of Subala and was born out of the amsa of Kamala, she was the mind born daughter of the manes and is considered to be quite graceful among the ladies. In earlier times she was born in Vraja with the curse of Durvasa. О louts faced one, you go and take your birth in that house. Therefore, you go to Vraja of Nanda, I shall own you there from my childhood.

## \|\| 6.67 \|\|

*tvaṃ me prāṇādhikā rādhe tava prāṇādhiko'pyaham \|*  
*na kiṃcidāvayorbhinnamekāṃgaṃ sarvadaiva hi \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. О Radha, you are dearer to me than my life even and I am like the same to you. There has been no point of separation or difference between us. Both of us have one and the same form.

## \|\| 6.68 \|\|

*śrutvaivaṃ rādhikā tatra ruroda premavihvalā \|*  
*papau cakṣuścakorābhyāṃ mukhacaṃdraṃ harermune \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O sage, on hearing this, Radhika getting infatuated with love kept on crying and started starring at the face of the lord with her eyes.

## \|\| 6.69 \|\|

*janurlabhata gopāśca gopyaśca pṛthivītale \|*  
*gopānāmuttamānāṃ ca maṃdire maṃdire śubhe \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. О cowherds and cowherdesses, you are also to be born on earth in the divine houses of the cowherds.

## \|\| 6.70-73 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare sarve dadṛśū rathamuttamam \|*  
*maṇiratneṃdrasāreṇa hīrakeṇa vibhūṣitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*śvetacāmaralakṣeṇa śobhitaṃ darpaṇāyutaiḥ \|*  
*sūkṣmakāṣāyavastreṇa vahniśuddhena bhūṣitam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sadratnakalaśānāṃ ca sahasreṇa suśobhitam \|*  
*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālājālairvirājitam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*pārṣadapravaraiyuktaṃ śāta kuṃbhamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*tejaḥsvarūpamatulaṃ śatasūryasamaprabham \|\| 73 \|\|*

70-73. In the meantime all of them found a divine chariot there which was built with precious gems and studded with rubies. It had a lakh of white fly-whisks, ten thousands mirrors, fine clothes, sanctified by fire, having thousands of pitchers built in gems, having large number of garlands of Parijata flowers and had a number of the best of courtiers. It was like gold, auspicious, possessing lustre and had the glory like hundreds of suns.

## \|\| 6.74-76 \|\|

*tatrasthaṃ puruṣaṃ śyāmaṃ sundaraṃ kamanīyakam \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ pītāṃbaraṃ varam \|\| 74 \|\|*

*kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*caṃdanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumadravacarcitam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*caturbhujaṃ smeravaktraṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram \|*  
*maṇiratneṃdrasārāṇāṃ sārabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. In that a human being was seated having dark-complexion, with charming appearance, holding samkha, cakra, gada and padma. He wore yellow lower garments, kirita crown, kundalas and the long garland of forest flowers. His body was plastered with sandal-paste, aguru, kasturl and saffron. He had four arms and had a smiling face and was anxious to shower his grace on his devotees. He was adorned with all the ornaments studded with gems.

## \|\| 6.77-78 \|\|

*devīṃ tadvāmato ramyāṃ śuklavarṇāṃ manoharām \|*  
*ratnālaṃkāraśobhāḍhyāṃ śobhitāṃ pītavāsasā \|\| 77 \|\|*

*śaratpārvaṇacaṃdrāsyāṃ śaratpaṃkajalocanām \|*  
*pakvabiṃbādharoṣṭhīṃ ca smerayu ktāṃ manoharām \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. To his left there appeared a fair complexioned goddess who was adorned with all the ornaments and was clad in the yellow lower garment. She had the face resembling the full moon of tie winter season, the eyes resembling the lotus flower of the winter season, the lips resembling the ripe wood-apple, wearing serene smile on her face and appeared quite elegant.

## \|\| 6.79 \|\|

*veṇuvīṇāgraṃthahastāṃ bhaktānugrahakātarām \|*  
*vidyādhiṣṭhātṛdevīṃ ca jñānarūpāṃ sarasvatīm \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. She was holding vlnax a book and a flute in her hands. She was anxious to shower her grace over the devotees, she happens to be goddess Sarasvati, the all intelligent one and the goddess of learnings.

## \|\| 6.80 \|\|

*aparāṃ dakṣiṇe ramyāṃ śatacaṃdrasamaprabhām \|*

It had the best of jewels and precious stones, the clothes sanctified by fire white fly-whisks and mirrors, having a number of kalasas built in gems, a large number of garland of Parijata flowers and had a thousand wheels. It could move with the speed of the mind and was quite pleasant to look at. The lustre of the mid-day sun or the winter season was of no consequence before the same. It had a large number of rubies and diamonds shining in it. A large number of puppets, flowers, streams, forests, were adding to its astonishing grandeur.

106-113. The gods found Mula-Prakriti in that chariot who was adorned with all the ornaments studded with g. ms and had the complexion resembling the molten gold and the lustre of the diamond. The goddess possessing great lustre had thousands of arms in which different types of attributes were held by her. She wore smile on her face and happened to be quite graceful to her devotees. She wore the best of the kundalas in the ear. She wore anklets which produced dangling sound and were quite beautiful. She had the waist-band of gems decorating the middle part of a body. Her hands were adorned with wristlets and armlets made of the best of gems and a beautiful garland or Mandara flower was falling on her breasts, her pelvic region was well-built and her breasts were well developed; her face resembled the full moon of the winter season. The collyrium was applied in her eyes which resembled the lotuses of the winter season. The sandal-paste, aguru, kasturi were painted in her body. Her lips resembled the lustre of the flowers which blossom during the mid-day; her teeth resembled the luster of gems; she was wearing the blossomed jasmine flowers in the hair and was losing quite graceful.

*pakṣīṃdracaṃcunāsāgragajeṃdramauktikānvitām \|*

117-121. Thereafter, she bowed in reverence to Shiva, Dharma, Ananta and Brahma. Looking at both the gods, all the gods welcomed her with sons. All the gods took their seats in the court which surprised all the cowherds and cowherdesses. Thereafter, lord Krishna spoke to Lakshmi smilingly, "O eternal goddess, you go to the abode of king Bhlsmaka which is filled with various types of gems and you be born there from the womb of VaidarbhI. О chaste lady, I myself reaching the Kundina city shall accept your hand in marriage.

131-134. Thus speaking the lord immediately spoke to Karttikeya, "O best of the gods you reaches the earth from your amsa and he born as a son from the womb of Jambavati. All the gods should go to the earth and be born from their amsa on the land, I shall surely relieve the earth of her burden. Thus speaking, the lord of Radhika was seated on the lion-throne. Thereafter, the gods, goddesses and the cowherdesses also took their seats. In the meantime Brahma stood before the lord with folded hands and started speaking to the lord of the universe in humble tone.

## \|\| 6.135-138 \|\|

*. brahmovāca \|*

135-138. Brahma said – О blissful one, you kindly listen to a request of mine. О lord you give me your command as to who would be lodged and where on earth? The lord always feeds his servants, protects them and redeems them also, such a servant is always called the devotes and he always obeys the command of the lord. You kindly tell me which one of the gods and goddesses would be born as which place on the earth and by which one of the rays of the gods or the goddess? In whose abode would they be born and what will be there names? On hearing the words of Brahma, the lord of the universe replied, "I am going to tell you appropriately the places were each one of them would be lodged."
