154\. О sage, at the time of conjugal pleasure, the hair dishevelled the tilakam; the vermilion and other decorations of the body were disfigured.

## \|\| 15.155 \|\|

*pulakāṅkitasarvāṃṅgī babhūva navasaṃgamāt \|*  
*mūrcchāmavāpa sā rādhā bubudhe na divāniśam \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. At the time of first love-sport the body of Radha became emotional and she fainted. She lost consciousness of day and night.

## \|\| 15.156-157 \|\|

*pratyaṅgenaiva pratyaṅgamaṅgenāṅgaṃ samāśliṣat \|*  
*śṛṅgārāṣṭavidhaṃ kṛṣṇaścakāra kāmaśāstravit \|\| 156 \|\|*

*punastāṃ ca samāśliṣya sasmitāṃ vakralocanām \|*  
*kṣatavikṣatasarvāṅgīṃ nakhadantaiścakāra ha \|\| 157 \|\|*

156-157. Lord Krishna who was well-versed in the love-sport united all the limbs of his body with those of Radha and he enjoyed eight types of sexual pleasure with her. Embracing him she was looking at Krishna with side glance, smilingly and he injured all the limbs of her body with the biting of the teeth.

## \|\| 15.158-160 \|\|

*kaṅkaṇānāṃ kiṅkiṇīnāṃ mañjīrāṇāṃ manoharaḥ \|*  
*babhūva śabdastatraiva śṛṅgārasamarodbhavaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

*punastāṃ ca samākṛṣya śayyāyāṃ ca niveśya ca \|*  
*cakāra rahitāṃ rādhāṃ kabarībandhavāsasā \|\| 159 \|\|*

*nirjane kautukātkṛṣṇaḥ kāmaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*cūḍāveṣāṃśukairhīnaṃ cakāra taṃ ca rādhikā \|\| 160 \|\|*

158-160. At the time of the sexual pleasure the armlets, anklets and wristlets of Radha were creating sweet sounds. Thereafter, in the secluded place Krishna who was well-versed in the art of making love, made Radha to sit on the bed and dishevelled her hair unrobing her at the same time. Radha too behaved similarly.

## \|\| 15.161-165 \|\|

*na kasya kasmāddhāniśca tau dvau kāryaviśāradau \|*  
*jagrāha rādhāhastāttu mādhavo ratnadarpaṇam \|\| 161 \|\|*

*muralīṃ mādhavakarājjagrāha rādhikā balāt \|*  
*cittāpahāraṃ rādhāyāścakāra mādhavo balāt \|\| 162 \|\|*

*jahāra rādhikā rāsānmādhavasyāpi mānasam \|*  
*nivṛtte kāmayuddhe ca sasmitā vakralocanā \|\| 163 \|\|*

*pradadau muralīṃ prītyā śrīkṛṣṇāya mahātmane \|*  
*pradadau darpaṇaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ krīḍākamalamujjvalam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*cakāra kabarīṃ ramyāṃ sindūratilakaṃ dadau \|*  
*vicitrapatrakaṃ veṣaṃ cakāraivaṃvidhaṃ hariḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

161-165. Neither of them was able to cause any harm to either of them because both of them were well-versed in the art of making love. Thereafter, Madhava snatched away the mirror of gems from the hand of Radha and she on her part forcibly snatched the flute from the hand of Krishna. Madhava then forcibly stole away the heart of Radha and Radha also acted similarly. At the end of the sexual play Radha looked at Krishna lovingly and handed over the flute to him. The lord also returned the mirror to Radha after enjoying the love-sport. He then arranged her hair nicely and decorated her forehead with the painting of tilakam and flower leaves. The hair-decoration done by Shri Krishna or Radha was beyond even Vishvakarma to do so, what to speak to her female friends.

## \|\| 15.166-171 \|\|

*viśvakarmā na jānāti sakhīnāmapi kā kathā \|*  
*veṣaṃ vidhātuṃ kṛṣṇasya yadā rādhā samudyatā \|\| 166 \|\|*

*babhūva śiśurūpaṃ ca kaiśoraṃ ca vihāya ca \|*  
*dadarśa bālarūpaṃ taṃ rudantaṃ pīḍitaṃ kṣudhā \|\| 167 \|\|*

*yādṛśaṃ pradadau nando bhītaṃ tādṛśamacyutam \|*  
*viniśvasya ca sā rādhā hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 168 \|\|*

*itastatastaṃ paśyantī śokārtā virahāturā \|*  
*uvāca kṛṣṇamuddiśya kākūktimiti kātarā \|\| 169 \|\|*

*māyāṃ karoṣi māyeśa kiṃkarīṃ kathamīdṛśīm \|*  
*ityevamuktvā sā rādhā papāta ca ruroda ca \|\| 170 \|\|*

*ruroda kṛṣṇastatraiva vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|*  
*kathaṃ rodiṣi rādhe tvaṃ smara kṛṣṇapadāmbujam \|\| 171 \|\|*

166-171. Thereafter Radha got ready to decorate the body of Krishna but he, shedding away the form of boyhood, again became a child. Radha then found that Krishna in child form was feeling hungry. He appeared in the same form in which Nanda had handed him over to her. Radha felt painful and she started running here and there in search of the boy Krishna. She was filled with grief and was feeling upset because of separation from Krishna. She then spoke to Krishna in a disappointing manner and humble tone, "O lord of illusion, why are you indulging in illusion with your own slave girl." Thus speaking Radha fell down and started crying. Krishna also was crying but in the meantime there was a divine voice from the sky saying, О Radha, you remember the lotus-like feet of lord Krishna; why are you crying?

## \|\| 15.172-175 \|\|

*ārāsamaṇḍalaṃ yāvannaktamatrāgamiṣyati \|*  
*kariṣyasi ratiṃ nityaṃ hariṇā sārddhamīpsitām \|\| 172 \|\|*

*chāyāṃ vidhāya svagṛhe svayamāgatya mā ruda \|*  
*kṛtvā kroḍe ca prāṇeśaṃ māyeśaṃ bālarūpiṇam \|\| 173 \|\|*

*tyaja śokaṃ gṛhaṃ gaccha sundarītthaṃ prabodhitā \|*  
*śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ rādhā kṛtvā kroḍe ca bālakam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*dadarśa puṣpodyānaṃ ca vanaṃ sadratnamaṇḍapam \|*  
*tūrṇaṃ vṛndāvanādrādhā jagāma nandamandiram \|\| 175 \|\|*

172-175. From now onwards the lord would come here daily at the time of Rasamandala and you leaving your shadow with him, shall come here daily and enjoy the love-sport. Don't cry. Your lord has turned himself into a child with his illusion; you carry him and go home. Thus the divine voice made Radha understand the reality. On hearing these words, Radha picked up the child in her lap and looked at the flower orchard, the forest and the mandapa made of the best of gems. Thereafter she at once reached the abode of Nanda in Vrindavana.

## \|\| 15.176-177 \|\|

*sā manoyāyinī devī nimiṣārdhena nārada \|*  
*saṃsiktasnigdhamadhurarasanā raktalocanā \|\| 176 \|\|*

*yaśodāyai śiśuṃ dātumudyatā satyuvāca ha \|*  
*gṛhītvaivaṃ śiśuṃ sthūlaṃ rudantaṃ ca kṣudhāturam \|\| 177 \|\|*

176-177. О Narada, Radha who could move with the speed of the mind reached there in a moment, her speech was quite stable and sweet. The eyes were red. Handing over the child to Yashoda, she said, "In Vraja your husband had carried him, but carrying this fat, hungry and crying child, I had been suffering throughout the journey. My wet cloth has stuck to the body of this child. The sky is overcast with clouds. The weather is bad and the ground is getting slippery. The mud has increased. О Yashoda, I am unable to carry his weight any further. О chaste lady, you take back the child from me and pacify him by feeding him at your breasts. I left my home long back and therefore I may go now. О chaste lady, you be happy." Thus speaking and handing over the child to her, she left for her abode.

## \|\| 15.178-183 \|\|

*goṣṭhe tvatsvāminā dattaṃ prāpnomi yātanāṃ pathi \|*  
*saṃsiktaṃ vasanaṃ vatse meghācchanne'tidurdine \|\| 178 \|\|*

*picchile kardamodreke yaśodā voḍhumakṣamā \|*  
*gṛhāṇa bālakaṃ bhadre stanaṃ dattvā prabodhaya \|\| 179 \|\|*

*gṛhaṃ ciraṃ parityaktaṃ yāmi tiṣṭha sukhaṃ sati \|*  
*ityuktvā bālakaṃ dattvā jagāma svagṛhaṃ prati \|\| 180 \|\|*

*yaśodā bālakaṃ nītvā cucumba ca stanaṃ dadau \|*  
*bahirniviṣṭā sā rādhā svagṛhe gṛhakarmaṇi \|\| 181 \|\|*

*nityaṃ naktaṃ ratiṃ tatra cakāra hariṇā saha \|*  
*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ vatsa śrīkṛṣṇacaritaṃ śubham \|\| 182 \|\|*

*sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ puṇyamaparaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 183 \|\|*

178-183. Yashoda took the child in her lap, kissed him and fed him with the milk of her breasts. On the other hand though Radha outwardly looked busy in performing her household jobs during the night she always went to Vrindavana and enjoyed love-sport with Krishna. Thus I have spoken to you about the life of Krishna which is quite auspicious, a bestower of pleasure, moksa and virtues. I have told all this to you. And I now recite the other story.

## Chapter 16

## \|\| 16.1 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*mādhavo bālakaiḥ sārddhamekadā halinā saha \|*  
*bhuktvā pītvā ca krīḍārthaṃ jagāma śrīvanaṃ mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said – Once Krishna, together with Balabhadra and the cowherd boys, went to the forest.

## \|\| 16.2 \|\|

*tatra nānāvidhāṃ krīḍāṃ cakāra madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā tāṃ śiśubhiḥ sārddhaṃ cālayāmāsa godhanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. After taking their food and while playing in the forest, Madhusudana pushed the cows ahead of the cowherds.

## \|\| 16.3-4 \|\|

*yayau madhuvanaṃ tasmācchrīkṛṣṇo godhanaiḥ saha \|*  
*tatra svādu jalaṃ pītvā vane ca sa mahābalaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tatraikadaityo balavāñchvetavarṇo bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*vikṛtākāravadano bakākāraśca śailavat \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Moving along with the cows and the cowherds Shri Krishna reached Madhuvana. The valorous lord consumed the delicious water in the forest and spotted a terrific demon of white complexion, having a deformed face in the form of a skylark, which was as huge as the mountain itself.

## \|\| 16.5 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca gokulaṃ goṣṭhe śiśubhirbalakeśavau \|*  
*yathā hyagastyo vātāpiṃ sarvaṃ jagrāsa līlayā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Finding the cows and the cowherds together with Krishna and Balarama there, he swallowed them the same way as Agastya had swallowed Vatapi in his valley.

## \|\| 16.6 \|\|

*bakagrastaṃ hariṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve devā bhayānvitāḥ \|*  
*cakrurhāheti saṃtrastā dhāvantaḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Finding the lord having been swallowed by the skylark, all the gods felt frightened and cried in panic. They rushed to the scene carrying weapons.

## \|\| 16.7 \|\|

*śakraścikṣepa vajraṃ ca munerasthivinirmitam \|*  
*na mamāra bakastasmātpakṣamekaṃ dadāha ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Indra shot his vajra at it which was built by the bones of the sage Dadhlci. With the strike of vajra the skylark could not be killed, but one of his wings was burnt out.

## \|\| 16.8 \|\|

*nīhārāstraṃ śaśadharaḥ śītārtastena dānavaḥ \|*  
*yamadaṇḍaṃ sūyarputrastena kuṇṭho babhūva ha \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The moon shot the arrow of snow on it which made the demon to suffer from cold. Yama the son of Surya then attacked it with the Yamadaqda which made the skylark motionless.

## \|\| 16.9 \|\|

*vāyavyāstraṃ ca vāyuśca tena sthānāntaraṃ yayau \|*  
*varuṇaśca śilāvṛṣṭiṃ cakāra tena pīḍitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The wind-god issued the wind-arrow which carried the skylark to some other place. Varuna, on the other hand, showered a rain of stones which injured the skylark.

## \|\| 16.10-11 \|\|

*hutāśanaśca vāhnena pakṣāṃścaiva dadāha saḥ \|*  
*kuberasyārdhacandreṇa chinnapādo babhūva ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

*īśānasya ca śūlena babhūva mūrcchito'suraḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayo munayaścaiva kṛṣṇaṃ cakurbhiyā''śiṣam \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The fire-god issued the fire-arrow at the skylark which burnt its wings. Kubera attacked it with the crescent-arrow which severed its legs. The trident of Shiva made the demon unconscious. All the sages and ascetics feeling panic pronounced their blessing on Krishna.

## \|\| 16.12-13 \|\|

*etasminnantare kṛṣṇaḥ prajvalanbrahmatejasā \|*  
*dadāha daityasarvāṅgaṃ bāhyābhyantaramīśvaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ vamanaṃ kṛtvā prāṇāṃstatyāja dānavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. In the meantime Krishna illumining with his divine lustre burnt the demon from within as well as outside which made it vomit out all those who had been swallowed by it and was ultimately killed.

## \|\| 16.14-16 \|\|

*bakaṃ nihatya balavāñchiśubhirgodhanaiḥ saha \|*  
*yayau kelikadambānāṃ kānanaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*etasminnantare tatra vṛṣarūpadharo'suraḥ \|*  
*nāmnā pralambo balavānmahādhūrtaśca śailavat \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śṛṅgābhyāṃ ca hariṃ dhṛtvā bhrāmayāmāsa tatra vai \|*  
*dudruvurbālakāḥ sarve ruruduśca bhayāturāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. Thus lord Kjrsna after having killed Bakasura accompanied with the cowherds and the cows, went to the forest of banana and kadamba trees. At that point of time a huge bull known as Pralambasura arrived there which was extremely wicked and of the size of a mountain. Carrying Krishna on its horns, it started moving him round and round. All the boys felt panicky and started crying but Balabhadra well realising his brother to be an incarnation of the lord, was smiling and was making the boys to understand that there were nothing to worry.

## \|\| 16.17-24 \|\|

*balo jahāsa balavāñjñātvā bhrātaramīśvaram \|*  
*bālakānbodhayāmāsa bhayaṃ kimityuvāca ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tadviṣāṇaṃ gṛhītvā ca svayaṃ śrīmadhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*bhrāmayitvā ca gagane pātayāmāsa bhūtale \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prāṇāṃstatyāja daityendro nipatya ca mahītalam \|*  
*jahasurbālakāḥ sarve nanṛtuśca jagurmudā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*hatvā pralambaṃ śrīkṛṣṇo balena saha satvaram \|*  
*godhanaṃ cārayāmāsa yayau bhāṇḍīramīśvaraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gacchantaṃ mādhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā keśī daityeśvaro balī \|*  
*veṣṭayāmāsa taṃ śīghraṃ khureṇa vilikhanmahīm \|\| 21 \|\|*

*mūrdhni kṛtvā hariṃ tuṣṭo gaganaṃ śatayojanam \|*  
*utpātya bhrāmayāmāsa papāta ca mahītale \|\| 22 \|\|*

*jagrāha sa hariṃ pāpī carvayāmāsa kopataḥ \|*  
*sa bhagnadanto daityaśca vajrāṅgacarvaṇādaho \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇatejasā dagdhaḥ prāṇāṃstatyāja bhūtale \|*  
*svarge dundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭirbabhūva ha \|\| 24 \|\|*

17-24. On the other hand, Madhusiidana himself caught hold of the bull by the horns and moving it round and round in the sky threw it on the ground. With the fall of the bull on the ground the demon was killed. All the boys started laughing looking at the demon. 3rl Krishna after killing Pralambasura rapidly went to BhSndlravana together with Balabhadra. On the way finding Krishna so moving, the valorous demon KesI surrounded him tearing the earth with its hoofs. It carried Kj-sna on its head and flew a hundred yojanas in the sky; the demon moved Krishna round and round and then fell down on to the ground. The wicked demon tried to chew lord Krishna holding him tightly but its effort to chew Krishna with its teeth, all his vajra-like teeth were broken. Thereafter getting burnt with the lustre of lord Krishna it fell down and was killed. The big drums were beaten in heaven and flowers were showered.

## \|\| 16.25-27 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra pārṣadā divyarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*tatrājagmuḥ syandanasthā dvibhujāḥ pītavāsasaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*kirīṭinaḥ kuṇḍalino vanamālāvibhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*vinodamuralīhastāḥ kvaṇanmañjīrarañjitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgā gopaveṣadharā varāḥ \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyā bhaktānugraha kātarāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. In the meantime the divine attendants arrived there with the chariots. All of them were two-armed; they were clad in yellow lower garments, adorned with kirita crown, kundalas and long garlands of forest flowers, each holding playfully a flute in his hands and creating sounds with their movement. They had anklets on their feet, their bodies were plastered with the sandal-paste. They appeared in beautiful form of the cowherds and wore a serene smile on their faces and could bestow their grace on the devotees of the lord.

## \|\| 16.28-30 \|\|

*pradīptaṃ rathamāsthāya ratnasāravinirmitam \|*  
*bhāṇḍīravanamājagmuryatra sannihito hariḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*divyavastraparīdhānā ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*praṇamayya hariṃ stutvā jagmurgolokamuttamam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*muktvā dehaṃ parityajya vaiṣṇavāḥ puruṣāstrayaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya dānavīṃ yoniṃ babhuvuḥ kṛṣṇapārṣadāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. They were mounted on the chariot studded with the best of gems and they arrived in the Bhandlra forest at the place were Krishna was present. They were clad in divine garments and were adorned with gem-studded ornaments. All of them started offering prayers to lord Krishna, after bowing in reverence to him. All of them had been Vaishnavas in the earlier births who had achieved demon-hood as a result of the curse pronounced on them; all of them, therefore, became the attendants of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 16.31 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*ke te ca divyapuruṣā vaiṣṇavā daityarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāva śrutaṃ kiṃ paramādabhutam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Narada said – О virtuous one, you tell me about the Vaishnavas who were turned into demons. "Who were they"? You tell me all this. I am interested in listening to the same.

## \|\| 16.32-33 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu bahmanpravakṣye'hamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*śrutaṃ maheśavadanātsūryaparvaṇi puṣkare \|\| 32 \|\|*

*harerguṇaprasaṅgena kathayāmāsa śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*saṃpṛṣṭo munisaṃghaiśca mayā dharmeṇa brahmaṇā \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Narayana said -O Brahman, in this connection I am going to narrate the story of ancient history which I heard from the mouth of lord Shiva at the time of the solar eclipse in the Puskara region. You please listen to it. Shiva had narrated it to me by describing the qualities of the lord, at the instance of the sage, the god of death, Brahma and myself.

## \|\| 16.34-35 \|\|

*brahmaputra mahābhāga kathāṃ bhuvanapāvanīm \|*  
*kathayāmāsa vistārya sāvadhānaṃ niśāmaya \|\| 34 \|\|*

*gandharveśo gandhavāhaḥ parvate gandhamādane \|*  
*mahāṃstapasvipravaro harisevanatatparaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. О Brahmaputra, О virtuous one, he narrated the story in detail which purifies the universe; the lord of Gandharvas known as Gandhavaha used to live there who had been a great ascetic of the lord.

## \|\| 16.36 \|\|

*putrā babhūvuścatvāro gandharvapravarā mune \|*  
*sasmaruḥ kṛṣṇapādābjaṃ svapne jñāne divāniśam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О sage, he had four Gandharva sons who were always devoted at the lotus-like feet of the lord, while sleeping, awake, during the day or the night.

## \|\| 16.37 \|\|

*te ca durvāsasaḥ śiṣyāḥ śrīkṛṣṇārcanatatparāḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ dattvā ca kamalaṃ saṃpūjya taṃ papurjalam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Becoming the pupils of Durvasa they adored lord Krishna and they sipped the water only after offering the lotus flower at the feet of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 16.38-40 \|\|

*vasudevaḥ suhotraśca sudarśanasupārśvakau \|*  
*catvāro vaiṣṇavaśreṣṭhāstepuste puṣkare tapaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*cirakālaṃ tapastaptvā babhūvuḥ siddhamantriṇaḥ \|*  
*jyeṣṭho durvāsaso yogaṃ saṃprāpya yogināṃ varaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*siddhaścākṛtadāraśca prajvalanbrahmatejasā \|*  
*sadyo dehaṃ parityajya babhūva kṛṣṇapārṣadaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. They were known by the names of Vasudeva, Suhotra, Sudarsana and Suparsvaka. All the four of them started performing tapas in the Puskara region. After performing tapas for a long time, they achieved success in the mantras. The eldest son known as Vasudeva who happened to be the best of the yogis achieved success, as per the advice of Durvasa, in the yogic practices. He did not marry, burning himself with the lustre of the Brahman. He left for his heavenly abode and became an attendant of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 16.41-42 \|\|

*ekadā bhrātaraste ca jagmuścitrasarovaram \|*  
*padmāni kṛṣṇapūjārthamāhartumudaye raveḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*padmānāṃ cayanaṃ kṛtvā gacchato vaiṣṇavānmune \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nibadhya saṃjagmuḥ sarve śaṃkarakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Once all the brothers went to Chitra-sarovara for collecting lotus flowers for offering to the lord, at dawn. О sage, while they were collecting the lotus flowers, the attendants of Shiva caught hold of them and bound them in fetters.

## \|\| 16.43-44 \|\|

*baliṣṭhā durbalāndhṛtvā jagmuḥ śaṃkarasannidhim \|*  
*te sarve śaṃkaraṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇemuḥ śirasā bhuvi \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tānuvāca śivaḥ śīghraṃ prayujyāśiṣamuttamām \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyo bhaktānugrahakātaraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. The powerful attendants of Shiva caught hold of the poor fellows and sent them all to Shiva. At the audience with Shiva they bowed in reverence to him and prostrated before him. Wearing a serene smile on the face and the one who is always compassionate to his devotees, §iva blessed them variously.

## \|\| 16.45-46 \|\|

*śiva uvāca \|*  
*ke yūyaṃ padmahartāraḥ pārvatyāśca sarovare \|*  
*lakṣayakṣai rakṣaṇīyaṃ pārvatīvratahetave \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nityaṃ sahasrakamalaṃ dadāti haraye satī \|*  
*vrate traimāsike bhaktyā patisaubhāgyavarddhane \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Shiva said – "Who are you to steal the lotus flowers from the lake of Parvati? A lakh of Yaks as protect that lake for the successful performance of the vrata of Parvati. She is performing the "three months" vrata for increase in the welfare of her husband and for that purpose she offers a thousand lotus flowers daily with devotions to lord Hari."

## \|\| 16.47 \|\|

*śivasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tamūcurvaiṣṇavā bhiyā \|*  
*puṭāñjaliyutāḥ sarve bhaktinamrātmakandharāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. On hearing the words of Shiva, the Vaishnavas felt panicky and with folded hands bending before him, they said.

## \|\| 16.48-49 \|\|

*gandharvā ūcuḥ \|*  
*vayaṃ gandharvapravarā gandhavāhasutā vibho \|*  
*haraye kamalaṃ dattvā pibāmo jalamīśvara \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vayaṃ na vidmo he nātha pārvatyā rakṣitaṃ saraḥ \|*  
*gṛhāṇa kamalaṃ sarvaṃ yuṣmākaṃ ca phalaṃ kuru \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Gandharvas said – О virtuous one, we are the best of the Gandharvas and the sons of Gandhavaha. О lord, we consumed water only after offering lotus flowers to lord Krishna. О lord, we were not aware of the fact that the tank was protected by Parvati. О Shiva, you kindly accept these lotus flowers and make the vrata a success.

## \|\| 16.50-51 \|\|

*na dāsyāmo'dya kamalaṃ pāsyāmo'dya jalaṃ hara \|*  
*kiṃ vā kathaṃ na pāsyāmastubhyaṃ dattāni tāni ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nityaṃ dhyātvā yatpadābjaṃ padmena pūjayāmahe \|*  
*sākṣāttasmai pradattvā ca padmaṃ pūtā vayaṃ prabho \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. We shall not offer the lotus flowers to the lord today and shall consume water without doing so. Otherwise, when we are offering these flowers to you, then why should we not consume the water. О lord by meditating at his feet we adore him by offering lotus flowers. We have been purified by offering the lotus flowers to you.

## \|\| 16.52-59 \|\|

*ekaṃ brahma hyadvitīyaṃ kva dehaḥ kva ca rūpavān \|*  
*bhaktānugrahato deho rūpabhedaśca māyayā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kiṃ tu gṛhāṇa padmāni tvameva matprabhuḥ prabho \|*  
*yato no mānasaṃ pūrṇaṃ tadrūpaṃ darśayācyuta \|\| 53 \|\|*

*dvibhujaṃ kamanīyaṃ ca kiśoraṃ śyāmasundaram \|*  
*vinodamuralīhastaṃ pītāṃbaradharaṃ param \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ekavaktraṃ dvinayanaṃ candanāgurucarcitam \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyaṃ ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kaustubhena maṇīndreṇa vakṣaḥsthalasamujjvalam \|*  
*mayūrapicchacūḍaṃ ca mālatīmālyabhūṣitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālārājivibhūṣitam \|*  
*koṭikandarṣalāvaṇyalīlādhāmamanoharam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*gopī saṃcaiduśyamānaṃ sasmitairvakralocanaiḥ \|*  
*navayauvanasaṃpananaṃ rādhāvakṣaḥsthalasthitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*brahmādibhiḥ stūyamānaṃ vandyaṃ dhyeyamabhīpsitam \|*  
*svātmārāmaṃ pūrṇakāmaṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram \|\| 59 \|\|*

52-59. Brahman happens to be one and unparalleled. Therefore he has no body or form. He takes to human form only to bestow his grace on the people and he takes to other forms under the influence of illusion. Therefore, О lord, kindly accept these lotus flowers because you happen to be our lord. О Acyuta, the form which pleases our mind, you please appear in the same form, having two arms, of tender age, charming dark complexion and beautiful. Playfully you hold the flute in your hand, clad in yellow lower garment. You should have a single face, two eyes and your body should be plastered with sandal-paste and aguru. The body should be adorned with gem-studded ornament and the kaustubha gem should adorn your bright chest. Your head should be adorned with the peacock feather and the garland of jasmine and Parijata flowers should decorate you. Having the beauty of crores of gods of love, wearing a serene smile on the face and you should be passionately looking at the faces of the cowherdesses. You should be quite young and should occupy the heart of Radha, adored by Brahma and other gods. You should be adorable, desirable, fulfil the desires of all and always anxious to bestow your grace on all.

## \|\| 16.60-63 \|\|

*ityuktvā purataḥ śambhostasthurgandharvapuṅgavāḥ \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇarūpaśravaṇātpulakāḍitavigrahaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*gandharvāṇāṃ vacaḥ śarutvā śivastānityuvāca ha \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇarūpaśravaṇātsāśupūrṇavilocanaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*pūtāṃ kartuṃ ca bhramatha caraṇāmbhojareṇunā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*ahaṃ vāñchāṃ karomyeva śrīkṛṣṇabhaktadarśane \|*  
*samāgamo hi sādhūnāṃ triṣu lokeṣu durlabhaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

60-63. Thus speaking the Gandharvas stood before lord Shiva. On hearing the description of lord Krishna, lord Shiva felt emotional and his hair stood on end. His eyes were filled with tears and he said, "I have come to realise that ydu happen to be the best of Vaishnavas and you are roaming about on the ground in order to purify it with the dust of your feet. I am always anxious to have an audience with the devotees of lord Krishna. It is very difficult to meet the noble people in the three worlds.

## \|\| 16.64-69 \|\|

*pārvatyāśca surāṇāṃ ca sadā yūyaṃ mama priyāḥ \|*  
*ātmanaścātmabhaktebhyo vaiṣṇavāśca priyāśca naḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kintu moghaṃ ca na bhavenmayā yatsvīkṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*tacchrūyatāṃ mahābhāgāḥ pārvatīvratakarmaṇi \|\| 65 \|\|*

*sarasaścaiva padmāni yairhṛtāni vratāntare \|*  
*te tūrṇamāsurīṃ yoniṃ gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*na hi śrīkṛṣṇabhaktānāmaśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit \|*  
*saṃprāpya mānavīṃ yoniṃ golokaṃ yāsyatha dhruvam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yūyaṃ śrīkṛṣṇarūpaṃ ca pratyakṣaṃ draṣṭumutsukāḥ \|*  
*dhruvaṃ drakṣyatha bho vatsā vṛndāraṇye ca bhārate \|\| 68 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ tato mṛtyuṃ saṃprāpya vaiṣṇavottamāḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ syaṃdanamāruhya gamiṣyatha harergṛham \|\| 69 \|\|*

64-69. You are dearer to me always than Parvati and the gods. Though the Vaishnavas are dearer to me than my own devotees, the promise I have already made cannot be otherwise. О virtuous one, you listen to it. I had ordained that during the performing of the vrata by Parvati, whosoever will collect lotus flowers from the lake would be turned into demons. There is no doubt about it. But the devotees of lord Krishna never meet with misfortune; therefore after becoming demons you would go back to the Goloka. You are desirous of having an audience with lord Krishna, О son, in the land of Bharata in the forest of Vrindavana you will meet with Krishna being a Vaishnava and meet with your end and getting mounted on a chariot you will go to the abode of the lord.

## \|\| 16.70-74 \|\|

*adhunā vāñchanīyaṃ ca rūpaṃ draṣṭumihotsukāḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ paśyatetyuktvā darśayāmāsa tacchivaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sāśrunetrāḥ praṇamya sarvarūpiṇam \|*  
*ājagmurdānavīṃ yonimiti te dānaveśvarāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vasudevaḥ purā muktaḥ suhotraśca bakāsuraḥ \|*  
*sudarśanaḥ pralambo'yaṃ svayaṃ keśī supārśvakaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*harasya varadānena dṛṣṭvā rūpamanuttamam \|*  
*mṛtyuṃ saṃprāpya śrīkṛṣṇājjagmuste kṛṣṇamandiram \|\| 73 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ vipra hareścaritamadbhutam \|*  
*bakakeśipralambānāṃ mokṣaṇaṃ mokṣakārakam \|\| 74 \|\|*

70-74. Presently if you are desirous of having a look at your desired form you can do so. Thus speaking lord Shiva made them look at the form of Krishna and looking at the same, the eyes of all the Gandharvas were filled with tears of love. Thereafter, bowing in reverence before the all-pervading lord, the Gandharvas took to the demonic form and became the lords of the demons. Thus Vasudeva had achieved salvation earlier, his brother Suhotra became Bakasura, Sudarsana became Pralamba and Suparsvaka became Kesl. With the boon of lord Shiva all of them had a look at the form of Shri Krishna and met with their end ultimately achieving the abode of Krishna. О dear one, thus I have narrated to you an astonishing story of the lord in which Baka, KesT and Pralamba achieved salvation. This story provides salvation to all. This has been ordained.

## \|\| 16.75-77 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*śrutaṃ sarvaṃ mahābhāga tvatprasādādyadadbhutam \|*  
*adhunā śrotumicchāmi pārvatyā kiṃ kṛtaṃ vratam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*ko vā''rādhyo vratasyāsya kiṃ phalaṃ niyamaśca kaḥ \|*  
*kāni dravyāṇi bhagavanvratopayogikani ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*katikālaṃ vrataṃ kiṃ vā pratiṣṭhāyāṃ nirūpaṇam \|*  
*suvicārya vada vibho śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. Narada said – О virtuous one, I have listened by your grace to whatever had been astonishing. Presently I intend to know the vrata Parvati had to perform and who had been the chief god of the same, what was the reward for the vrata! And what are its regulations? О lord, what are the beautiful materials required for the said vrata? What is the time for it? You kindly also tell me about the performing of the same. О all-pervading one, you think over it carefully and tell me everything since I am getting quite anxious about it.

## \|\| 16.78-81 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*ārādhyo bhagavānkṛṣṇo rādhikāsahito mune \|\| 78 \|\|*

*viṣuve ca samāraṃbhaḥ samāptirdakṣiṇāyane \|*  
*saṃyamya pūrvadivase kṛtvā'vaśyaṃ haviṣyakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*snātvā vaiśākhasaṃkrāntyāṃ saṃkalpya jāhnavītaṭe \|*  
*ghaṭe maṇau śālagrāme jale vā pūjayedvratī \|\| 80 \|\|*

*dhyāyedbhaktyā ca rādheśaṃ saṃpūjya pañca devatāḥ \|*  
*dhyānaṃ ca sāmavedoktaṃ nibodha kathayāmi te \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. Narayana said – О sage, the vrata is to be continued for three months which increases the fortunes of the husband. Lord Krishna together with Radhika are the chief deities for the same. It starts in the first half of the year and is completed in the second half. At the time of the start of the vrata one has to get disciplined and consume the food of havisya and the next day being the first day of Vaishakha one should take a bath in the Ganga and start the vrata on the bank of the Ganga, taking samkalpa (vow). The one performing the vrata should adore the kalasha, the gem, a Shalagrama, a vase of water. After adoring the five gods, one should adore the lord of Radha with devotion. I am telling you the method of the same as prescribed in the Samaveda. You listen to it.

## \|\| 16.82-84 \|\|

*navīnanīradaśyāmaṃ pītakauśeya vāsasam \|*  
*śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyamīṣaddhāsyasamanvitam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*śaratpraphullapadmākṣaṃ mañjulāñchanaraṃjitam \|*  
*mānasaṃ gopikānāṃ ca mohayantaṃ muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*rādhayā dṛśyamānaṃ ca rādhāvakṣaḥsthalasthitam \|*  
*brahmānanteśadharmādyaiḥ stūyamānamahaṃ bhaje \|\| 84 \|\|*

82-84. His complexion is like the fresh clouds, is clad in a yellow lower garment, his face wears a smile and looks like the full moon of the winter season, his eyes are like the fully blossomed lotus of the winter season, in whose eyes the collyrium has been applied. He attracts the minds of the cowherdesses again and again. Radha is looking at him and he resides in the heart of Radha. The gods like Brahma, Ananta, Shiva and Dharma adore him. I meditate upon him.

## \|\| 16.85-87 \|\|

*dhyātvā kṛṣṇaṃ ca dhyānena tamāvāhya vratī mudā \|*  
*dhyāyettadā rādhikāṃ ca dhyānaṃ madhyaṃdineritam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*rādhāṃ rāseśvarīṃ ramyāṃ rāsollāsarasotsukām \|*  
*rāsamaṇḍalamadhyasthāṃ rāsādhiṣṭhātṛdevatām \|\| 86 \|\|*

*rāseśvaroraḥsthalasthāṃ rasikāṃ rasikapriyām \|*  
*rasikapravarāṃ ramyāṃ ramāṃ ca ramaṇotsukām \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. Thus the performer of the vrata should meditate upon Krishna and should delightfully invoke him. Thereafter one should meditate upon Radhika. The said dhyanam is contained in the Madhyandina-shakha. According to this dhyanam, Radha is the chief of Rasa, quite charming, always anxious to perform the Rasallla, always present in Rdsamandala, the chief goddess of the divine dance, residing in the heart of lord Krishna, quite attractive, beloved of Krishna, the best of those performing Rasa, beautiful one and anxious for meeting the beloved.

## \|\| 16.88-93 \|\|

*śaradrājīvarājīnāṃ prabhāmocanalocanām \|*  
*vakrabhrūbhaṅgasaṃyuktāṃ mañjīreṇaiva rañjitām \|\| 88 \|\|*

*śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyāmīṣaddhāsyamanoharām \|*  
*cārucampakavarṇābhāṃ candanena vibhūṣitām \|\| 89 \|\|*

*kastūrībindunā sārdhaṃ siṃdūrabiṃdunā yutām \|*  
*cārupatrāvalīyuktāṃ vahniśuddhāṃśukojjvalām \|\| 90 \|\|*

*sadratnakuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca sukapolasthalojjvalām \|*  
*ratnendrasārahāreṇa vakṣaḥsthalavirājitām \|\| 91 \|\|*

*ratnakaṅkaṇakeyūrakiṅkiṇīratnarañjitām \|*  
*sarveśena stūyamānāṃ sarvabījāṃ bhajāmyaham \|\| 92 \|\|*

*brahmādibhiśca sevyena śrīkṛṣṇotaiva sevitām \|*  
*saraveśena stūyamānāṃ sarvavījāṃ bhajāmyaham \|\| 93 \|\|*

88-93. Her eyes resembled the lotus flowers of the winter season. She had curved eyebrows and was adorned with anklets. Her face resembled the lustre of the moon of the winter season and she wore a pleasant smile on her face; her body had the glory of campaka flowers; her body was decorated with sandal-paste, kastUri, vermilion and other cosmetics. Her cheeks were painted with beautiful leaves. She was clad in garments purified by fire, her gem-studded kundalas illumined her cheeks. The garland of gems decorated her breasts; the anklets, armlets and wristlets besides the waist-band were decorated with gems. The anklets decorate her feet which were studded with gems and created sweet sounds. Lord Krishna who is devoted by Brahma and other gods served her always. All the gods adore her and she happens to be the cause of all. I adore such a type of Radha.

## \|\| 16.94-96 \|\|

*iti dhyātvā ca kṛṣṇena sahitāṃ tāṃ ca pūjayet \|*  
*bhaktyā dattvā pratidinamupacārāṃśca ṣoḍaśa \|\| 94 \|\|*

*pratyekaṃ ca pṛthakkṛtvā sarvaṃ dadyādvratī mudā \|*  
*sahasrakamalaṃ divyaṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ mune \|\| 95 \|\|*

*homaṃ kuryādvratī nityamaṣṭottaraśatāhutīḥ \|*  
*dadyādbhaktyā ca kṛṣṇāya svāhetyuccārya yatnataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. Thus meditating upon Krishna one should adore him. Daily with the devoted mind one should make sixteen types of offering and adore him. The one who performs the vrata should make every offering separately with a delightful mind. He should make a hundred and eight offerings with the divine lotus flowers; he should make his offering in the fire with a devoted mind reciting

## \|\| 16.97-98 \|\|

*rasālasya kadalyāśca hyāmaṃ vā pakvameva ca \|*  
*nityamaṣṭottaraśataṃ dadyādbhaktyā'kṣataiḥ phalam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*nityaṃ ca bhojayedbhaktyā brāhmaṇānāṃ śataṃ mune \|*  
*homaṃ kuryādvratī nityamaṣṭottaraśatāhutīḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. One should make the offering of the unripe or ripe mango or banana fruits a hundred and eight times with devotion. The fruits should be uninjured. О sage, a hundred and eight Brahmana should be served with food daily and the performer of vrata should make a hundred and eight offerings in the fire.

## \|\| 16.99 \|\|

*dadyādbhaktyā ca kṛṣṇāya rādhikāsahitāya ca \|*  
*tilena havanaṃ kuryādājyamiśreṇa nārada \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Those offerings should be made both to Radha and Krishna. О Narada, one should perform homa with the sheshamum seeds mixed with ghee.

## \|\| 16.100 \|\|

*vādyaṃ ca vādayennityaṃ kārayeddharikīrtanam \|*  
*evaṃ māsatrayaṃ kṛtvā pratiṣṭhāṃ tadanantaram \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. The musical instruments should be played upon daily, besides the recitation of the name of Hari. After doing this, for three months, the vrata is completed.

## \|\| 16.101-102 \|\|

*pratiṣṭhādivase tatra vidhānaṃ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*kamalānāṃ ca navatisahasrāṇyakṣatāni ca \|\| 101 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi nava viprendra yatnataḥ \|*  
*bhojayetparamānnāni svādūni miṣṭakāni ca \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. О Narada, I am now speaking out the method for the same; you please listen to it. One should offer ninety thousand uninjured lotus flowers and should serve to nine thousand Brahmans food which should be delicious and sweet.

## \|\| 16.103-108 \|\|

*phalaṃ viṃśādhikaṃ saptaśataṃ navasahasrakam \|*  
*dadyānnānāvidhaṃ dravyaṃ naivedyaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*saṃskṛtāgniṃ ca saṃsthāpya homaṃ kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*navatiṃ ca sahasrāṇi hutvā''jyena tilena ca \|\| 104 \|\|*

*savastraṃ ca sabhojyaṃ ca yajñasūtraphalānvitam \|*  
*gandhapuṣpārcitānbhaktyā dadyānnavatilaḍḍukān \|\| 105 \|\|*

*dadyānnavatikumbhāṃśca śītatoyaprapūritān \|*  
*evaṃvidhaṃ vrataṃ kṛtvā dadyādviprāya dakṣiṇām \|\| 106 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāyāḥ parimitaṃ vedeṣu yannirūpitam \|*  
*vṛṣendrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ ca svarṇaśṛṅgasamanvitam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ vipra kṛtaṃ traimāsikavratam \|*  
*viśiṣṭasaṃtatikaraṃ patisaubhāgyavarddhanam \|\| 108 \|\|*

103-108. One should offer naivedya of nine thousand seven hundred and twenty fruits, several types of beverages besides other eatables; one should perform homa with the sanctified fire making ninety thousand offerings of ghee and sheshamum seeds. Thereafter the costumes, food and fruits, yajnopavita, ninety fragrant sweet balls and ninety pitchers filled with cool water should be given. Thus completing the vrata in this manner, one should offer daksina to the Brahmanas. The quantity of daksina should be the same as has been prescribed in the Vedas. One should give away in charity a hundred bulls whose horns should be coated with gold. О Brahman, thus I have narrated to you the method of performing the three months' vrata which bestows on the husband competent progeny and increases his fortunes.

## \|\| 16.109-111 \|\|

*vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa saubhāgyaṃ śatajanmani \|*  
*satputrajananī sā ca bhavejjanmaśataṃ dhruvam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*kadā'pi na bhavettasyā bhedaśca patiputrayoḥ \|*  
*dāsatulyo bhavetputro bhartā ca svavacaskaraḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*anukṣaṇaṃ bhavedrādhākṛṣṇabhaktiyutā satī \|*  
*bhavedvrataprabhāveṇa prāptajñānaharissmṛtiḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

109-111. With the influence of this vrata one achieves fortune for a hundred births. She produces the best of sons in a hundred births and is never separated from the husband or the son. The son is always obedient like the slave and the husband also listens to her and such a chaste lady always remains engrossed in the devotion of Radha to Krishna. With the influence of this vrata, she always remains full of knowledge and remembers the god always.

## \|\| 16.112 \|\|

*vrataṃ ca sāmavedoktaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvamathāvayoḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ca vratānāṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ śṛṇu vadāmi te \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. In the earlier times this vrata which is prescribed in the Samaveda was performed by us. It is the best of all the vratas and I am going to spell out the names of all of them those who have performed it. You listen to it.

## \|\| 16.113-119 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvasya ca manoḥ śatarūpābhidhā satī \|*  
*tayā kṛtaṃ prathamataḥ kṛtvā'gastyaṃ purohitam \|\| 113 \|\|*

*tadā kṛtaṃ devahūtyā cākūtyā ca kṛtaṃ tadā \|*  
*purohitaṃ pulastyaṃ ca kṛtvā śrutyuktyā mune \|\| 114 \|\|*

*cakāra rohiṇī tattu kratuṃ kṛtvā purohitam \|*  
*ratiścakāra tadbhaktyā gautamastatpurohitaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*akāri tadvrataṃ bhaktyā tārayā gurukāntayā \|*  
*mahāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārā vasiṣṭhastatpurohitaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

*taddṛṣṭvā gurupatnyāśca śakraśacyā kṛtaṃ vratam \|*  
*mahāsambhṛtasambhārastatpurodhā bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*vrataṃ cakāra svāhā ca sarvato'pi vilakṣaṇam \|*  
*atisaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro marīcistatpurohitaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*taddṛṣṭvā pārvatī brahmannuvāca śaṃkaraṃ mudā \|*  
*puṭāñjaliyutā devī bhaktinamrātmakandharā \|\| 119 \|\|*

113-119. SatarOpa the wife of Svayambhuvamanu making the sage Agastya as the chief priest, performed this vrata first of all. Thereafter, both Devahtiti and Aktlti performed this vrata with Pulastya as the priest. О sage, Rohini also performed this vrata with Kratu as the priest. Rati also performed this vrata making Gautama as the priest, with great devotion. Tara the wife of teacher Brihaspati also performed this vrata with devotion, making Vasistha as the chief priest. Thereafter Tara made elaborate arrangements for this vrata and following her IndranI also performed the vrata with great pomp and show, making Brihaspati as the priest. Svaha performed this astonishing vrata collecting immense materials and making sage Marlci as the priest. О Brahman, looking at the same, goddess Parvati stood before Shiva with folded hands and bowing in reverence spoke to him.

## \|\| 16.120-123 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*ājñāṃ kuru jagannātha karomi vratamuttamam \|*  
*āvayoriṣṭadevasya vratānāṃ ca paraṃ vratam \|\| 120 \|\|*

*harerārādhanaṃ nātha sarvamaṃgalakāraṇam \|*  
*iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ śruteḥ pāṭhaṃ tīrthaṃ pṛthvyāḥ pradakṣiṇam \|\| 121 \|\|*

*harerārādhanasyāpi kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*bahirabhyaṃtare yasya harismṛtiranukṣaṇam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*jīvanmuktasya tasyaiva muktirbhavati darśanāt \|*  
*tasya pādābjarajasā sadyaḥ pūtā vasundharā \|\| 123 \|\|*

120-123. Parvati said – О lord of the universe, if you permit me I intend to perform the best of the vratas, which could bestow the welfare on both of us. О lord, the adoration of the lord is the cause of the welfare. Because the performing of the yajnas, charities, reciting the Vedas, visiting the holy places and going round the earth do not weigh even one-sixteenth part of the adoration of the lord. The one who always remembers the lord outwardly and inwardly and who is free from the death, gets redeemed by having a look at such a person. With the dust of his lotus-like feet, the earth gets purified at once.

## \|\| 16.124-128 \|\|

*tasya darśanamātreṇa punāti bhuvanatrayam \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca dharmaśca śeṣastvaṃ ca gaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

*dhyāyaṃdhyāyaṃ yatpadābjaṃ tejasā tatsamo mahān \|*  
*yaśca yaṃ santataṃ dhyāyetsa tamāpnoti niścitam \|\| 125 \|\|*

*guṇena tejasā buddhyā jñānena tatsamo bhavet \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya smaraṇāddhyānāttapasā tasya sevayā \|\| 126 \|\|*

*mayā prāpto hi bhagavānsvāmī vā putra eva ca \|*  
*pralabdhaṃ līlayā sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ manmānasaṃ tadā \|\| 127 \|\|*

*svāmī me tvādṛśaḥ putrau kārttikeyagaṇeśvarau \|*  
*pitā himādriḥ kṛṣṇāṃśo mama kiṃ durlabhaṃ prabho \|\| 128 \|\|*

124-128. At the sight of such a person all the three worlds are purified. By meditating upon whose lotus-like feet, Brahma, Vishnu, Dharma and Shesha and you yourself besides Ganesha had achieved similar glory. The one who adores daily such a person, gets a high place and ultimately he becomes like him in qualities, glory, intelligence and knowledge. By adoring at the feet of lord Krishna, remembering his name, performing dhyanam, tapas and serving him at the same time, I have achieved my husband and son; I have got everything playfully. Therefore my mind is completely satisfied and at peace. О lord, I have been fortunate enough to get a husband like you, sons like Ganesha and Karttikeya and the father Himalaya who happens to be the athsa of Krishna. Therefore, nothing remains to be desired by me now.

## \|\| 16.129 \|\|

*pārvatīvacanaṃ śrutvā suprītaḥ śaṃkaraḥ svayam \|*  
*prahasyovāca madhuraṃ pulakāhdhitavigrahaḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. On hearing the words of Parvati, Shiva was extremely delighted and the hair on his body stood on end. Thereafter he spoke to her smilingly.

## \|\| 16.130-131 \|\|

*mahādeva uvāca \|*  
*mahālakṣmīsvarūpā'si kimasādhyaṃ taveśvari \|*  
*sarvasampatsvarūpā tvamanantaśakti rūpiṇī \|\| 130 \|\|*

*tvaṃ ca yasya gṛhe devi sa caiśvaryasya bhājanam \|*  
*na lakṣmīryadgṛhe tasya jīvanānmaraṇaṃ varam \|\| 131 \|\|*

130-131. Mahadeva said – О goddess, you are the form of Maha-Lakshmi and nothing is beyond you. You are the form of all the riches and the prowess which is beyond measure. О goddess, the house in which you remain is bestowed with all the riches. The house which is devoid of Lakshmi, death is better than life in that house.

## \|\| 16.132-133 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmā ca viṣṇuśca tvayi bhaktyā śubhaprade \|*  
*saṃhāre sṛṣṭikāle ca tvatprasādādvayaṃ kṣamāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

*ko vā himālayaḥ ko'haṃ kau kārttikagaṇeśvarau \|*  
*tvadvihīnā aśaktāśca tvayā ca vayamīśvarāḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

132-133. О auspicious one, myself, Brahma and Vishnu adore you and by your grace we indulge in the creation of the universe, its preservation and destruction.

## \|\| 16.134-141 \|\|

*yuktāḥ pativratāyāśca yāḥ purājñāḥ śrutau śrutāḥ \|*  
*gṛhītvā''jñāmīśvarasya vrataṃ kuru pativrate \|\| 134 \|\|*

*vratametatkṛtaṃ yābhistābhyaḥ kuru vilakṣaṇam \|*  
*sanatkumāro bhagavānvrate te'stu purohitaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

*kamalānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ dāyako'pyaham \|*  
*kuberaṃ dravyakośe ca rakṣakaṃ kuru sundari \|\| 136 \|\|*

*vrate ca dānādhyakṣo'haṃ dhanadātrī ca śrīḥ svayam \|*  
*pāṭhako vahnidevaśca varuṇo jaladāyakaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

*vastūnāṃ vāhakā yakṣāstadadhyakṣaḥ ṣaḍānanaḥ \|*  
*sthānasaṃskāra kartā ca vrate'tra pavanaḥ svayam \|\| 138 \|\|*

*pariveṣṭā svayaṃ śakraścandro'dhiṣṭhāpako vrate \|*  
*sūryaśca dānanirvaktā yogyāyogyaṃ yathocitam \|\| 139 \|\|*

*vratopayuktaṃ yaddravyaṃ dattvā niyamitaṃ priye \|*  
*tato'dhikaṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ haraye dehi sundari \|\| 140 \|\|*

*vrate niyamitānviprānbhojayitvā tato'dhikām \|*  
*asaṃkhyānbrāhmaṇāndevi bhaktyā kuru nimantraṇam \|\| 141 \|\|*

134-141. Himalaya, myself, Karttikeya and Ganesha are all of no consequence, without you. All of us are of no consequence without you and with you we are all powerful. Therefore, О chaste lady, whatever is appropriate for a chaste lady and whatever has been heard in the ancient times havu to be taken as the words of the lord. Therefore accepting the divine voice you perform this vrata. As the ladies who have performed this vrata, you also perform it in a most astonishing manner. In your vrata, Sanatkumara would conduct himself as the chief priest while I will arrange for the lotuses, Brahmanas and other materials. О beautiful one, Kubera would be the treasure, while I myself would be in charge of the charities. Lakshmi herself would provide all the riches. The god of fire would recite the Vedas. Varuna would perform the function of the supply of water and the Yaksas would be responsible for carrying the materials under the leadership of six-headed Karttikeya. The place of yajna would be kept neat and clean by the wind god himself while Indra would serve in the kitchen. Moon would be the chief organiser while Surya would supervise the charities and make appropriate arrangements. О dear one, whatever materials are needed for the performing the vratas, you offer the same in greater quantities to please lord Hari. Whatever is the number of Brahmanas prescribed to be fed in the vrata, you invite much more of them and serve them food.

## \|\| 16.142 \|\|

*samāptidivase svarṇaṃ ratnaṃ muktāṃ pravālakam \|*  
*vratoktāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā sarvaṃ dehi dvijātaye \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. On the concluding day of the vrata, the Brahmanas should be given in charity gold, gems, pearls, coral and other things which have been prescribed in the vrata. These should be given in daksina and the entire riches should be distributed.

## \|\| 16.143-145 \|\|

*ityuktvā śaṃkarastāṃ ca kārayāmāsa tadvratam \|*  
*vrataṃ cakāra sā durgā sarvābhyaśca vilakṣaṇam \|\| 143 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ vipra pārvatyā yadvrataṃ kṛtam \|*  
*ratnaṃ voḍhumaśaktāśca brāhmaṇāḥ pārvatīvrate \|\| 144 \|\|*

*itihāsaḥ śrutaḥ sarvaḥ prakṛtaṃ śṛṇu nārada \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇabālacaritaṃ nūtnaṃ nūtnaṃ pade pade \|\| 145 \|\|*

143-145. Thus speaking Shiva made Parvati to perform the vrata. Thus Durga performed the vrata in an astonishing manner. О dear one, thus have I narrated to you the details of the vrata performed by Parvati. О Narada, the Brahmanas were unable to carry the load of the daksina money given away to them by Parvati. This is what I have heard from history; now I narrate to you further in the context of the story. The childhood plays of lord Krishna would appear to be fresh at every step.

## \|\| 16.146-147 \|\|

*hatvā tāndānavendrāṃśca śiśubhiḥ saha gokule \|*  
*jagāma svagṛhaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kuberabhavanopamam \|\| 146 \|\|*

*sarvebhyo vanavārtā ca proktā ca śiśubhirmudā \|*  
*śrutvaivaṃ vismitāḥ sarve nando bhayamavāpa ha \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. After killing the demons, lord Krishna accompanied by the cowherds returned to his home in Gokula which was a huge mansion like that of Kubera. Reaching home the cowherds narrated the happenings of the forest to every one in Gokula. On listening to these stories the people were surprised while Nanda felt panic.

## \|\| 16.148 \|\|

*ānīya vṛddhāngopāṃśca gopikāḥ sthavirāstathā \|*  
*yuktiṃ cakāra taiḥ sārddhamālocya samayocitām \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. He summoned all the old cowherds and cowherdesses and consulted them. Deciding on the future course of action, Nanda the chief of the cowherds got prepared to leave the place. О sage, at that point of time, he asked all the people to leave Vmdavana.

## \|\| 16.149-153 \|\|

*kṛtvā yuktiṃ ca gopeśastatsthānaṃ tyaktumudyataḥ \|*  
*gantuṃ vṛndāvanaṃ sarvānuvāca tatkṣaṇaṃ mune \|\| 149 \|\|*

*nandājñāṃ ca samākarṇya te sarve gantumudyatāḥ \|*  
*gopāśca gopikāścaiva bālakā bālikāstathā \|\| 150 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇena halinā sārdhaṃ prayayurbālakā mudā \|*  
*saṃgītaṃ ca pragāyanto nānāveṣa samanvitāḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

*veṇupravādakāḥ kecitkecicchṛṅgapravādakāḥ \|*  
*karatālakarāḥ kecidvīṇāhastāśca kecana \|\| 152 \|\|*

*śarayantrakarāḥ kecicchṛṅgahastāśca kecana \|*  
*navapallavakarṇāśca kecidgopālabālakāḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

149-153. Listening to the command of Nanda all the people got ready to depart from there; all the cowherds, cowhferdesses, boys and girls delightfully went to Vrindavana together with Krishna and Balabhadra. All of them were singing taking to many forms, some of them were playing on vlna, some of them were playing on horns. Some of them were playing on karatala while others were playing on flutes; some of them played on the arrow instruments in their hands while others had the horns; some of the cowherds were wearing tender leaves in their ears.

## \|\| 16.154-156 \|\|

*kecinmukulakarṇāśca puṣpakarṇāśca kecana \|*  
*navamālyakarāḥ kecitkecidājānumālinaḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*kecitpallavacūḍāśca puṣpacūḍāśca kecana \|*  
*gopālabālakāḥ sarve viprendra navakoṭayaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

*jagmurgopyo vayasyāśca koṭiśaḥ koṭiśo mudā \|*  
*vṛddhāśca koṭiśastatra bṛhacchroṇyaścalatkucāḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

154-156. Many of them had adorned their ears with flower buds while others had inserted the flowers into them. Some of them were carrying fresh garlands of flowers; some of the boys had worn long garlands of forest flowers, while others had decorated their tufts. О best of the Brahmanas, there were nine crores of cowherd boys and the cowherdesses numbering crores having developed pelvic region and breasts. All the female friends and the old ladies were moving delightfully.

## \|\| 16.157-158 \|\|

*rādhikāsahacāriṇyo bālā gopālikā mune \|*  
*tāḥ suśīlādayo bhavyā nānālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

*divyavastraparīdhānāḥ sasmitāstā yayurmudā \|*  
*kāścidāruhya śibikāṃ rathamāruhya kāścana \|\| 158 \|\|*

157-158. О sage, the female friend of Radhika like Sus'Ila and others were also moving while Radha on the other hand adorned with all the ornaments was clad in divine garment. She was moving wearing a smile on her face. Some of the ladies were moving in palanquins, while others were mounted on the chariots.

## \|\| 16.159-161 \|\|

*rādhā syandanamāruhya śātakaumbhaparicchadam \|*  
*tābhiryuktā yayau devī ratnālaṃkāra bhūṣitā \|\| 159 \|\|*

*yaśodā rohiṇī caiva ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitā \|*  
*yayau syandanamāruhya śātakaumbhaparicchadam \|\| 160 \|\|*

*nandaḥ sunandaḥ śrīdāmā giribhānurvibhākaraḥ \|*  
*vīrabhānuścandrabhānurgajasthāḥ prayayurmudā \|\| 161 \|\|*

159-161. They were all moving together on the chariots adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments and gold equipment. Both Yashoda and Rohini, adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments were travelling in the golden chariots. Nanda, Sunanda, Sridama, Giribhanu, Vibhakara, Virabhanu and Chandrabhanu were mounted on the chariots and were moving pleasantly.

## \|\| 16.162-164 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇabaladevau tau ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitau \|*  
*svarṇa syandanamāsthāya jagmatuḥ parayā mudā \|\| 162 \|\|*

*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśo gopā vṛddhāśca yauvanānvitāḥ \|*  
*aśvasthāśca gajasthāśca rathasthāścaiva kecana \|\| 163 \|\|*

*gopā yayurmudā yuktāścoddhatā nandakiṃkarāḥ \|*  
*vṛṣasthā gardabhasthāśca saṃgītatānatatparāḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

162-164. Both Shri Krishna and Balabhadra adorned with gem-studded ornaments and mounted on the golden chariots were moving on pleasantly. Crores of old and young cowherds mounted on horses, elephants and chariots moved on. The arrogant servants of Nanda mounted on bulls and donkeys playing on musical instruments.

## \|\| 16.165-166 \|\|

*aparā rādhikādāsyastrisaptaśatakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*mudānvitāḥ sasmitāśca svarṇālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

*kāścitsindūrahastāśca kāścitkajjalavāhikāḥ \|*  
*kāścitkandukahastāśca kāścitputtalikākarāḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

165-166. The twenty one million slave-girls of Radha were moving with her delightfully. They had smiling faces and were adorned with golden ornaments. Some of them were holding vermilion, collyrium and even balls, while others were holding puppets.

## \|\| 16.167-175 \|\|

*bhogadravyakarāḥ kāścitkrīḍādravyakarā varāḥ \|*  
*veṣadravyakarāḥ kāścitkāścinmālākarā varāḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

*kāścidvādyakahastāśca prayayurgopikā mudā \|*  
*vahniśuddhāṃśukānāṃ ca vāhikāścaiva kāścana \|\| 168 \|\|*

*candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumadravavāhikāḥ \|*  
*kāścitsaṃgītaniratāḥ kāściccitrakathāratāḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśo ramyāḥ prayayuḥ śibikānvitāḥ \|*  
*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśaścāśvāḥ koṭiśaḥ koṭiśo rathāḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśaścaiva śakaṭā dravyapūritāḥ \|*  
*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśaścaiva vṛṣendrā dravyavāhakāḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

*koṭiśaḥ koṭiśaścaiva daśalakṣāṇi hastinām \|*  
*hastipāṃkuśayuktāni yayurvṛndāvanaṃ vanam \|\| 172 \|\|*

*sarve vṛndāvanaṃ gatvā dṛṣṭvā śūnyagṛhaṃ mune \|*  
*vṛkṣamūle yathāsthānaṃ tasthuḥ sarve yathocitam \|\| 173 \|\|*

*uvāca gopāñchrīkṛṣṇo gṛhāṃśceṣṭatamānvrajāḥ \|*  
*adya saṃtiṣṭhatetyevaṃ śrutvā śrīkṛṣṇabhāṣitam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*kutra santi gṛhāḥ kṛṣṇetyevamūcustu gopakāḥ \|*  
*iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śrīkṛṣṇo vākyamabravīt \|\| 175 \|\|*

167-175. Some of them were carrying cosmetics and materials for decorating the body. Some of them had the material for decorating the costumes while others carried garlands of flowers. Some of them carried the musical instruments and were moving on delightfully. Some of them were clad in the garments purified by fire, while other carried sandal-paste, aguru, kasturl and saffron in their hands. Some of them were engaged in playing music and while others were engaged in reciting astonishing types of story. Thus crores of beautiful cowherdesses moved on in palanquins. There were crores of horses, chariots, bullock-carts filled with several types of materials, crores of bulls carrying the materials, crores of elephants, driven by the elephants, driven by the elephant driver, by means of goads. All of them moved on to Vrindavana. On reaching Vrindavana, they found no dwelling places and as such they had to take shelter under the trees in an appropriate manner. At that point of time lord Krishna pointed out to the places for the stay of the cows as well as the people and said, "You spend the night somehow today." On hearing the words of Krishna all of them said, "O Krishna, where are the houses?" In reply to them Shri Krishna said.

## \|\| 16.176 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*atra sthāne gṛhāḥ santi prasannā devanirmitāḥ \|*  
*devaprītiṃ vinā śaktā nahi draṣṭuṃ ca kecana \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. Shri Krishna said – There are several clean houses built here by the gods but no one can look at them unless the gods are pleased.

## \|\| 16.177-179 \|\|

*adya tiṣṭhata gopālāḥ saṃpūjya vanadevatāḥ \|*  
*prātaryūyaṃ gṛhānramyāndrakṣyathādya dhruvaṃ mudā \|\| 177 \|\|*

*dhūpadīpādinaivedyairbalibhiḥ puṣpacandanaiḥ \|*  
*devīṃ ca vaṭamūlasthāṃ pūjāṃ kuruta caṇḍikām \|\| 178 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā gopāḥ saṃpūjya devatām \|*  
*bhuktvā bhogāndine rātrau tatraiva suṣupurmudā \|\| 179 \|\|*

177-179. Therefore, О cowherds, let us adore the god of forest and live here tonight. In the early morning you will surely find beautiful houses. Therefore, all of you should adore goddess Chandika here offering incense, lamp, naivedya, offerings, flowers and sandal-paste, who is lodged under the banyan tree. On hearing the words of Krishna all the cowherds adored the goddess during the day time and spent the time delightfully there itself.

## Chapter 17

## \|\| 17.1-5 \|\|

*śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*supteṣu vrajanandeṣu naktaṃ vṛndāvane vane \|*  
*sunidrite ca nidreśe mātṛvakṣaḥsthalasthite \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nidritāsu ca gopīṣu ramyatalpasthitāsu ca \|*  
*yūnāṃ ca sukhasaṃyogānuṣaktamānasāsu ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kāsucicchiśuyuktāsu sakhīyuktāsu kāsucit \|*  
*kāsucicchakaṭasthāsu syaṃdanasthāsu kāsucit \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pūrṇendukaumudīyukte svargādapi manohare \|*  
*nānāprakārakusumavāyunā surabhīkṛte \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarvaprāṇini niśceṣṭe muhūrte pañcame gate \|*  
*tatrājagāma bhagavāñchilpināṃ ca gurorguruḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Narayana said – During the night when the people of vraja together with Nanda went to sleep. Krishna also went to sleep in the lap of his mother. When all the young people slept with the cowherds some of whom carried the infants in their laps, some of them slept with the female friends, some of them slept in the carts, some of them in the chariots. From the moon light Vrindavana was looking better than heaven and the cool fragrant breeze started blowing. All the people went to sleep. After the passage of five muhurtas, Vishvakarma the teacher of all the architects reached there.

*bibhraddivyāṃśukaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ratnamālyaṃ manoharam \|*

6-8. He was clad in fine and divine garment, he was wearing a garland of gems and the gem-studded ornament having unprecedented glory, wearing makara-kundalas in the ears, all knowledgeable and appeared quite young, possessing the lustre of the god of love.

*svarṇapātraghaṭādīnāṃ vāhakāścaiva kecana \|*

*golokasya ca sopānaṃ sarveṣāṃ vāñchitapradam \|*  
*catuṣkoṭicatuḥśālaṃ tatraivātimanoharam \|\| 16 \|\|*

9-16. He was accompanied by three crores of architects who carried in their hands many gems and weapons made of iron. The Yaksas of the forest of Kubera who happen to be his servants also arrived there. They were adorned with crystal gems and the ornaments studded with gem. The shoulders of some of them were very broad. Some of them carried heaps of rubies, emeralds, and syamantaka gems. Some of them carried axes in their hands while others carried iron implements. Some of them carried the best of the gems while others carried fly-whisks, mirrors, vases of gold, gold pitchers in heaps. With the best of material available with Vishvakarma, he looked at the same and thought of lord Krishna. He then started the work of constructing the city. It happened to be the best of the city of Bharata and was spread over an area of five yojanas. It was the best of the holy places and was considered to be the most sacred place, liked best by Hari. It could lead the people desirous of salvation to achieve their goal by residing there. Four crores of four-roomed houses were built there as a result of which the entire city looked quite beautiful.

## \|\| 17.17 \|\|

*kapāṭastambhasopānasahitaiḥ prastarairvaraiḥ \|*

17\. It was built in stones with a large number of doors, pillars and steps decorated with puppets, flowers and kalasas at the top of each one of the house, which illumined the area.

## \|\| 17.18 \|\|

*śailajāśmavinirmāṇavedigrāṅgaṇasaṃyutam \|*

18\. There were pedestals made with blocks of stones and the courtyards added to the beauty of the houses there. The city was surrounded by boundary walls made in block of stones. Vishvakarma built the entire city playfully.

## \|\| 17.19-22 \|\|

*yathocitavṛhadadradamāradyasamanvitam \|*

*sopānairgandhasārāṇāṃ stambhaiḥ śaṃkuvinirmitaiḥ \|*

19-22. In each and every house there were big or small doors which wrere appropriately fixed. Vishvakarma had delightfully constructed the houses of the city with crystal gems. The steps were made of sandal-wood and the pillars were without nails; the doors were fixed with chains of steel, vases of silver were fixed on the boundary walls which were strong like vajra as a result of which the entire city was looking quite glorious. After constructing the appropriate types of the houses for the Gopas, Vishvakarma constructed a beautiful house for Vrsabhanu. It was covered with boundary walls and moats all round, which had four gates on all the four sides.

## \|\| 17.23-28 \|\|

*cāruviṃśaccatuḥśālaṃ mahāmaṇivinirmitam \|*

*viśiṣṭena maṇīndreṇa cakārāṭṭālikālayam \|*

23-28. He constructed twenty, four-roomed houses, in the entire complex in which the gems were studded, the paintings were made with gems, the steps were made with various types of pearls which looked quite beautiful, the doors were made of steel and with artificial paintings, the houses of Vrsabhanu looked quite beautiful. Every temple in that complex had the kalasha of gold which kept on shining. A lonely place of that asrama having a beautiful campaka trees, was made for enjoying the love-sports by Kalavati with her husband, was also made by Vishvakarma. It was built with the special types of gems, having nine steps of emerald, the pillars were made of sandal-wood and the doors were quite high. It was indeed an astonishing type of mansion.

## \|\| 17.29 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kalāvatī kā bhagavankasya patnī manoharā \|*  
*yatnato yadgṛhaṃ ramyaṃ nirmame surakāruṇā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Narada said – О lord, who was the attractive Kalavati and who was her husband for whom Vishvakarma constructed the mansion with such great efforts.

## \|\| 17.30-32 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ mānasī kanyā kamalāṃśā kalāvatī \|*  
*sundarī vṛṣabhānasya pativrataparāyaṇā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*yasyāśca tanayā rādhā kṛṣṇaprāṇādhikā priyā \|*

*yasyāśca caraṇāmbhojarajaḥpūtā vasundharā \|*

30-32. Narayana said – О Narada, Kalavati had been born of the amsa of Kamala and was the mind-born daughter of the manes, who was quite chaste and the beloved of Vrsabhanu. She was the mother of Radha, who was dearer to Krishna than his life, emerging out of the half of the body of Krishna, she possessed the lustre equal to that of the lord. The earth was purified with the dust of her feet and the noble people are always desirous of her devotion.

## \|\| 17.33-34 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ mānasīṃ kanyāṃ vraje tiṣṭhankathaṃ mune \|*

33-34. Narada said – О sage, how could the people of Vraja achieve the mind-bom daughter of the manes, so easily; who was Vrsabhanu, the lord of Vraja in earlier times and by what merit could he achieve Radha as his daughter?

## \|\| 17.35 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā maharṣirjñānināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*prahasyovāca prītyā tamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Suta said – On hearing the words of Narada, the sage Narayana who happens to be the best of the learned people smiled and lovingly narrated the ancient story.

36-47. Narayana said – In earlier times Kalavati, Ratnamala and Menaka were known as the mind-

## \|\| 17.48-52 \|\|

*divyaṃ syandanamāruhya kāmukyā saha kāmukaḥ \|*  
*krīḍāṃ cakāra rahasi sthānesthāne manohare \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ramyāyāṃ malayadroṇyāṃ candanāguruvāyunā \|*  
*cārucampakapuṣpāṇāṃ talpe ratisukhāvahe \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mālatīmallikānāṃ ca puṣpodyāne'tipuṣpite \|*  
*puṣpabhadrānadītīre nirjane ketakīvane \|\| 50 \|\|*

*paścimābdhitaṭāntasthakānane jantuvarjite \|*  
*nandane mandaradroṇyāṃ kāverītīraje vane \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śaileśaile suramye ca nadyāṃnadyāṃ nadenade \|*  
*dvīpedvīpe tu rahasi sa reme vāmayā saha \|\| 52 \|\|*

48-52. bom daughters of the manes who were quite inaccessible. Out of them the passionate Ratnamala married Janaka and Menaka accepted Himalaya the lord of the mountain as her husband, the truthful Sita happened to be daughter of Ratnamala who was born without human contact and happened to be the wife of lord Rama. Parvati happened to be the daughter of Menaka who was also born without human contact. She was also the illusion of Hari and quite eternal. She, after performing great tapas for Narayana achieved Shiva as her husoand. Kalavati on the other hand accepted Sunanda who belonged to the race of Manu as her husband. The king considered himself to be quite fortunate since she was born out of the amsa of the Kamala by getting the virtuous Kalavati as his wife. Praising Kalavati he used to think in his mind, "She has an astonishing type of beauty and costumes. How beautiful is she in her tender age! Her limbs are quite tender and beautiful and her face resembles the glory of the full moon of the winter season; her walking pushed to shame the moving of the elephant and the wagtail bird. With her side-glances she can attract the minds of even the great sages, her pelvic region and thighs are well developed and look like the tmnk of banana trees. О sage, both her breasts, were quite stiff and well developed and her buttocks resembled the wheels of the chariot. The hands and the feet were quite red and the lips resembled the ripe wood-apples, the lines of teeth resembled the seed of pomegranate and were quite charming; her eyes resembled the fully blossomed lotus flowers of the winter season. She was adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments." Thus thinking, the king felt infatuated with passion.

## \|\| 17.53 \|\|

*navasaṃgamasaṃyogādbubudhe na divāniśam \|*  
*evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tadgatameva muhūrtavat \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thereafter, the passionate king mounted on the divine chariot together with Kalavati moved on to a charming spot. He enjoyed sex with her, in the charming forest of Malayacala valley, where the trees of sandal, aguru were found in large number and their fragrance was spread everywhere carried by the wind, on the beautiful bed of campaka flowers which made the sexual pleasure quite comfortable, in the groves of jasmine flowers and on the bank of river Pus pabhadra, the secluded forest of KetakI trees, on the western ocean in Bengal, devoid of any creatures, in the valley of Nandanavana in the Mandracala mountain, in the forest of the bank of the Kaverl river. Thus he roamed about in all the charming places, the mountains, the rivers, the rivulets, the islands and all the charming places where he enjoyed himself in her company.

## \|\| 17.54-56 \|\|

*kṛtvā vihāraṃ suciraṃ sa virakto babhūva ha \|*  
*jagāma tapase vindhyaśailaṃ tīrthaṃ tayā saha \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhārate'tipraśasyaṃ ca pulahāśramamuttamam \|*  
*tapastepe nṛpastatra divyavarṣasahasrakam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*mokṣākāṅkṣī niḥspṛhaśca nirāhāraḥ kṛśodaraḥ \|*  
*mūrchāmāpa muniśreṣṭha dhyātvā kṛṣṇapadāmbujam \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Thus in this first sexual encounter they lost awareness of day and night and thus a thousand years elapsed like a moment.

## \|\| 17.57-58 \|\|

*tadgātravyāptavalmīkaṃ sādhvī dūraṃ cakāra sā \|*  
*niśceṣṭitaṃ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā tyaktaṃ prāṇaiśca pañcabhiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*māṃsaśoṇitaraktaṃ tamasthisaṃsaktavigraham \|*  
*uccai ruroda śokārtā nirjane tu kalāvatī \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Having been thus indulged in the sexual behaviour for a long time, the king became fed up with the same and thereafter he went for tapas together with his wife in the hermitage of sage Pulaha located in Vindhyacala in the land of Bharata. Reaching there the king performed severe tapas leaving all the desires, remaining without food for a divine thousand years and his body became lean and thin. О best of the sages, devoting his mind at the lotus-like feet of lord Krishna he fainted.

## \|\| 17.59-66 \|\|

*he nāthanāthetyuccārya kṛtvā vakṣasi mūrchitam \|*  
*vilalāpa mahādīnā pativrataparāyaṇā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā nṛpaṃ nirāhāraṃ kṛśaṃ dhamanisaṃyutam \|*  
*śrutvā ca rodanaṃ tasyāḥ kṛpayā ca kṛpānidhiḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*āvirbabhūva jagatāṃ vidhātā kamalodbhavaḥ \|*  
*kroḍe kṛtvā ca taṃ tūrṇaṃ ruroda bhagavānvibhuḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*brahmā kamaṇḍalujalenāsicya nṛpavigraham \|*  
*jīvaṃ saṃcārayāmāsa brahmajñānena brahmavit \|\| 62 \|\|*

*nṛpendraścetanāṃ prāpya puro dṛṣṭvā prajāpatim \|*  
*praṇanāma ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca kāmasamaprabham \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tamuvāceti saṃtuṣṭo varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam \|*  
*sa vidhervacanaṃ śrutvā vavre nirvāṇamīpsitam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*dayānidhe tvaṃ dayayā varaṃ dātuṃ samudyataḥ \|*  
*prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānsmerānanasaroruhaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*kṛtvānumānaṃ manasi śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukā \|*  
*tamuvāca satī trastā varaṃ dātuṃ samudyatam \|\| 66 \|\|*

59-66. The hole created in the body because of the tapas was removed by his chaste wife. But the chaste wife Kalavati finding her husband lifeless, devoid of the five elements, flesh blood and the remnants of the bones and skin, became grief-stricken and started crying aloud in that secluded forest.

## \|\| 17.67-70 \|\|

*kalāvatyuvāca \|*  
*yadi muktiṃ nṛpendrāya dadāsi kamalodbhava \|*  
*ato'balāyā he brahmankā gatirbhavitā vada \|\| 67 \|\|*

*vinā kāntaṃ ca kāntānāṃ kā śobhā caturānana \|*  
*vrataṃ pativratāyāśca patireva śrutau śrutam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*guruścābhīṣṭadevaśca tapodharmamayaḥ patiḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ ca priyataro na bandhuḥ svāminaḥ paraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*sarvadharmātparā brahmanpatisevā sudurlabhā \|*  
*svāmisevāvihīnāyāḥ sarvaṃ tanniṣphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 70 \|\|*

67-70. Placing the fainted king in her lap she uttered, "O lord". Thereafter the grief-stricken and chaste wife started lamenting. The body of the king had dried up because he took no food and all the veins of his body were quite visible. Finding this, listening to the lamenting of Kalavati, the compassionate Brahma who was born out of the lotus and happened to be the creator of the universe, compassionately reached there. Carrying the king in his lap he also started crying. Thereafter Brahma, who was well aware of the Brahman took out water from his kamandalu and sprinkled it on the body of the king and with his divine knowledge be brought him back to life; getting his senses back the king found Brahma before him and he bowed in reverence to him. Thereafter, Brahma was pleased and he spoke to the king, who was as beautiful as the god of love, "You ask for a boon desired by you." On hearing the words of Brahma, the king said, "O compassionate one, in case you intend to bestow a boon on me with a mind filled with compassion, with your face blossoming like the lotus, then you give me the boon of achieving salvation. Realising the gravity of the situation in her mind, the throat, lips and palate of the queen were dried up. Feeling panicky the chaste lady spoke to Brahma who was about to pronounce his boon for the king.

## \|\| 17.71-73 \|\|

*vrataṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ pūjā japahomādikaṃ ca yat \|*  
*snānaṃ ca sarvatīrtheṣu pṛthivyāśca pradakṣiṇam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*dīkṣā ca sarvayajñeṣu mahādānāni yāni ca \|*  
*paṭhanaṃ sarvavedānāṃ sarvāṇi ca tapāṃsi ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

*vedajñānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhojanaṃ devasevanam \|*  
*etāni svāmisevāyāḥ kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. Kalavati said – О Brahman, born of the lotus, in case you redeem the king then you tell me what shall be the fate of the helpless woman like me? О four-faced one, without the husband, the wife has no glory. It is said in the Vedas that for the chaste ladies the husband happens to be their vratas. He is the only dharma for their tapas besides being the teacher and the supreme god. For all the ladies there is no better relative than the husband. He happens to be dearer to her compared to all other people. О Brahman, the serving of the husband with devotion is considered to be the best of all the dharmas. Such of the women who are deprived of serving their husbands, all their performances become infructuous.

## \|\| 17.74-76 \|\|

*svāmisevāvihīnā yā vadaṃti svāmine kaṭum \|*  
*pataṃti kālasūtre ca yāvaccaṃdradivākarau \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sarpapramāṇāḥ kṛmayo daṃśaṃti ca divāniśam \|*  
*saṃtataṃ viparītaṃ ca kurvaṃti śabdamulbaṇam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*mūtraśleṣmapurīṣāṇāṃ kurvaṃti bhakṣaṇaṃ mudā \|*  
*mukhe tāsāṃ dadatyevamulkāṃ ca yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. The performing of vrata, charities, tapas, puja, recitation, om and other religious practices, besides bathing in the holy places, going round the earth, performing all the yajnas, the great charities, reciting all the ’Vedas, performing tapas, serving food to the Brahmanas, being well-versed in the Vedas and serving the gods, do not compare even one-sixteenth part of the merit of serving the husband.

## \|\| 17.77 \|\|

*bhuktvā bhogaṃ ca narake kṛmiyoniṃ prayāṃti tāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣaṃti janmaśatakaṃ raktamāṃsapurīṣakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Such a woman who, instead of serving her own husband, showers harsh words on him, falls in the kalasutra hell and remains there till the time of the sun and the moon. There the insects as big as snakes bite them day and night and also create frightening sounds. There they have to consume urine and refuse. The messengers of Yama insert the burning rods into the mouth of such women.

## \|\| 17.78-79 \|\|

*śrutvāhaṃ viduṣāṃ vaktrādvedavākyeṣu niścitam \|*  
*jānāmi kiṃcidabalā tvaṃ vedajanako vibhuḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*gurorguruśca viduṣāṃ yogināṃ jñānināṃ tathā \|*

150\. Vishvakarma the best of the architects went to the abode of Vrsabhanu and then went to some other place with his workers.

## \|\| 17.151-156 \|\|

*kṛtvā'numānaṃ buddhyā ca sarvato'pi vilakṣaṇam \|*  
*parikhābhirgabhīrābhiścaturbhiḥ saṃyutaṃ varam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*durlaṅghyābhirvairibhiśca khanitābhiśca prastaraiḥ \|*  
*puṣyodyānaiḥ puṣpitābhiḥ pārāvāreṣu puṣpitaiḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*cāru campakavṛkṣaiśca puṣpitaiḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*parito vāsitābhiśca sugandhivāyunā mune \|\| 153 \|\|*

*āmrairguḍālaiḥ panasaiḥ kharjūrairnārikelakaiḥ \|*  
*dāḍimaiḥ śrīphalairbhṛṅgairjambīrairnāgaraṅgakaiḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*tuṅgairāmrātakairjambusamūhaiśca phalānvitaiḥ \|*  
*kadalīnāṃ ketakīnāṃ kadambānāṃ kadambakaiḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

*sarvataḥ śobhitābhiśca phalaistaiḥ puṣpitairaho \|*  
*krīḍārhābhirnigūḍhābhirvāñchitābhiśca sarvadā \|\| 156 \|\|*

151-156. Vishvakarma who is well-versed in the tattvas mentally thought of constructing a vast building for the use of Nanda and he started the work accordingly.

## \|\| 17.157 \|\|

*parikhānāṃ rahaḥ sthāne cakāra mārgamuttamam \|*  
*durgamaṃ paravargāṇāṃ svānāṃ ca sugamaṃ sadā \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Thinking from his mind he built the abode for Nanda in an unprecedented manner which was surrounded by the high boundary walls and deep moats. It was inaccessible to the enemies and was built of stone. On both the banks of the river there were flower gardens, as a result of which it looked like a flower orchard. On the banks of the river, the campaka flowers were blossoming. The air which blew in the area touching the fragrant flowers, carried the fragrance everywhere. The trees grown on the banks included mango, betel-nut, jack-fruits, palms, coconut, pomegranate, wood-apple, cardamom, lemon, orange, mango, silk-fruit, banana, kevade, kadamba and several other trees blossoming with flowers. The place was surrounded by the moats on all the sides. Since it was always covered with the trees it was best suited for water-sport and therefore desired by all.

## \|\| 17.158 \|\|

*saṃketena maṇistambhaiśchāditaiḥ svalpapāthasā \|*  
*stambhasīmākṛtamaho na saṃkīrṇaṃ na vistṛtam \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. For entry into these moats a beautiful pathway was constructed which was always inaccessible to the enemies, but was easily accessible to the known people.

## \|\| 17.159-160 \|\|

*parikhoparibhāge ca prākāraṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*dhanuḥśatapramāṇaṃ ca cakārātisamucchritam \|\| 159 \|\|*

*prastarasya pramāṇaṃ ca pañcaviṃśatihastakam \|*  
*sindūrākāramaṇibhirnirmitaṃ cātisundaram \|\| 160 \|\|*

159-160. The boundary of the road was indicated by signs of pillars studded with gems, having enough water. These pillars were indicative of the boundary, which were neither too big nor too small.

## \|\| 17.161-162 \|\|

*bāhye dvābhyāṃ ca saṃyuktamantare saptabhistathā \|*  
*dvārbhiśca sanniruddhābhirmaṇisārakapāṭakaiḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*harinmaṇīnāṃ kalaśaiścitrayuktairvirājitam \|*  
*maṇisāravikāraiśca kapāṭaiśca suśobhitam \|\| 162 \|\|*

161-162. On the upper portion of the complex, there was a beautiful boundary wall which was as high as a hundred bows and each boulder studded in the wall was as high as twenty five feet each and was built with red precious stone, looking quite beautiful.

## \|\| 17.163 \|\|

*svarṇasāravinirmāṇakalaśojjvalaśekharam \|*  
*mandālayaṃ vinirmāya vrabhrāma nagaraṃ punaḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. There were two gates outside the same and inside there were seven of them with doors which were studded with the best of gems.

## \|\| 17.164 \|\|

*rājamārgāśca vividhānsa ca cārūṃścakāra ha \|*  
*raktabhānuvikāraiśca vedībhiśca supattanaiḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. The top of the palace of Nanda was built with pitchers of gold which were always shining. By constructing this palace Vishvakarma started roaming about in the city.

## \|\| 17.165 \|\|

*pārāvāre ca parito nibandhāṃśca manoharān \|*  
*vāṇijyārhaiśca vaṇijāṃ parito maṇimaṇḍapaiḥ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. He constructed several types of beautiful kingsway, besides the pedestal made of red precious stones and the roads decorated with beautiful sign boards.

## \|\| 17.166-167 \|\|

*sarvato dakṣiṇe vāme jvaladbhiśca virājitān \|*  
*tato vṛndāvanaṃ gatvā nirmame rāsamaṇḍalam \|\| 166 \|\|*

*sundaraṃ maṇḍalākāraṃ maṇiprākārasaṃyutam \|*  
*parito yojanāyāmaṃ maṇivedibhiranvitam \|\| 167 \|\|*

166-167. They were built quite strong which added to their beauty. The kingsway was provided with mandapas of gems which could be used by the business community.

## \|\| 17.168 \|\|

*maṇisāravikāraiśca maṇḍapairnavakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgārārhaiśca citrāḍhyai ratitalpasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

168\. Getting illumined themselves the mandapas also illuminated the kingsway. Thereafter Vishvakarma constructed a circular Rasamandala in Vrindavana surrounded by a high boundary wall which was spread by a yojana from all sides. A number of pedestals were constructed and decorated with gems at several places.

## \|\| 17.169 \|\|

*nānājātiprasūnānāṃ vāyunā surabhīkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*ratnapradīpasaṃyuktaiḥ suvarṇakalaśojjvalaiḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Nine crores of maridapas were added to the beauty of Rasamandala which were studded with the best of precious stones; it had enough of cosmetics, beautiful paintings and beds for enjoying the love-sports.

## \|\| 17.170 \|\|

*puṣpodyānaiḥ puṣpitaiśca sarobhiśca suśobhitam \|*  
*rāsasthalaṃ vinirmāya jagāmānyatsthalaṃ puraḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. The cool breeze which carried the fragrance of numerous flowers of different types filled the mandapas with the fragrance, the lamps made of diamonds were lighted in the same. The gulden pitchers enhanced its lustre.

## \|\| 17.171-172 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ parituṣṭo babhūva ha \|*  
*vṛndāvanābhyantare ca sthānesthāne sunirjane \|\| 171 \|\|*

*kṛtvā parimitaṃ buddhyā manasālocya yatnataḥ \|*  
*vilakṣaṇāni ramyāṇi tatra triṃśadvanāni ca \|\| 172 \|\|*

171-172. Vishvakarma after constructing the Rasamandala duly filled with the flowers, gardens and lakes, went to some other place.

## \|\| 17.173-175 \|\|

*rādhāmādhavayoreva krīḍārthaṃ ca vinirmame \|*  
*tato madhuvanābhyāśe nirjane'timanohare \|\| 173 \|\|*

*vaṭamūlasamīpe ca sarasaḥ paścime taṭe \|*  
*campakodyānapūrvāyāṃ ketakīvanamadhyataḥ \|\| 174 \|\|*

*punastayośca krīḍārthaṃ cakāra ratnamaṇḍapam \|*  
*caturbhirvedikābhiśca parītamatisundaram \|\| 175 \|\|*

173-175. Finding the charming Vrindavana so beautiful, he was immensely delighted and he set up beautiful gardens of astonishing type in Vrindavana which were scattered at several places and were created thoughtfully.

## \|\| 17.176-181 \|\|

*sadratnasāraracitai rājitaṃ tūlikāśataiḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnaracitairnānācitreṇa citritaiḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

*kapāṭairnavabhiryuktaṃ navadvārairmanoharaiḥ \|*  
*ratneṃdracittrakalaśaiḥ kṛtrimaiśca trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

*paritaḥ parito bhittyāmūrdhvaṃ ca pariśobhitam \|*  
*mahāmaṇīndravikṛtairārohairnavabhirvṛtam \|\| 178 \|\|*

*sadratnasāraracitakalaśojjvalaśekharam \|*  
*patākātoraṇairyuktaṃ śobhitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

*sarvataḥ purato dīptamamūlyaratna darpaṇaiḥ \|*
