38\. one, you forgive me for my failing, you have purchased me by you tapas, therefore you be compassionate on me. You are eternal and happen to be the seed of Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesha.

## \|\| 37.39 \|\|

*liṅgopari ca yaddattaṃ tadevāgrāhyamīśvara \|*  
*supavitraṃ bhavettasya viṣṇornaivedyamiśritam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. You are all virtuous, the invisible prowess of the lord of the universe, the form of all the prowess and you are always my companion.

## \|\| 37.40 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sā devī dehaṃ tyaktuṃ samudyatā \|*  
*trasto harastatpurataḥ stutvā ca svīcakāra ha \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. О dear one, you are visible as well as invisible, eternal and move at will, you are present in my heart because of the grace of the virtuous lord Krishna.

## \|\| 37.41-42 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*sthirā bhava mahādevi caṇḍike jagadaṃbike \|*  
*mamāparādhamakhilaṃ kṣantumarhasi sundari \|\| 41 \|\|*

*māṃ bhṛtyaṃ tapasā krītaṃ kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari \|*  
*brahmaviṣṇumaheśānāṃ bījabhūte sanātani \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. O lord, only such of the naivedya which will be offered to Shivalinga will be unsuitable for consumption and in case your naivedya is mixed with the naivedya of Vishnu it will become extremely auspicious.

## \|\| 37.43 \|\|

*aho golokanāthastha guṇātītasya nirguṇe \|*  
*sarvaśaktisvarūpe ca sadaiva sahacāriṇi \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Thus speaking the goddess got ready to end her life. Thereafter, the terrified Shiva accepted her words praising her at the same time.

## \|\| 37.44 \|\|

*sākāre ca nirākāre nitye svecchāmaye priye \|*  
*kṛpayā tadvibhoreva mama vakṣasi sāṃpratam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Shiva said – О great goddess, О Chandika, О mother of the universe, be composed, О beautiful

## \|\| 37.45-46 \|\|

*sarvabījasvarūpe ca mahāmāye manohare \|*  
*sarvasiddhiprade devi muktide kṛṣṇabhaktide \|\| 45 \|\|*

*icchaiva śrīhareḥ sākṣānnāhaṃ dātumapi kṣamaḥ \|*  
*tadā dehaṃ parityajya nirguṇaṃ vraja nirguṇe \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. You are the form of all the seeds, Mahamaya, quite a pleasant one, the one who bestows all the siddhis and salvation beside the devotion of lord Krishna. This was the desire of lord Krishna himself because of which I did not give you his naivedya. О invisible one, you realise this reason carefully and only than end your life and get merged in the invisible one.

## \|\| 37.47 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā puratastasthau ca candraśekharaḥ \|*  
*babhūva suprasannā sā praṇanāma haraṃ param \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus speaking lord Shiva having the crescent on his head stood before her. Thereafter the goddess got immensely pleased and offered her salutation to Shiva.

## \|\| 37.48 \|\|

*ityevaṃ pārvatīstotraṃ śaṅkareṇa kṛtaṃ purā \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhedvipadā grastaḥ sa bhayādeva mucyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Thus this stotra of Parvati was created by Shiva in ancient times. The one who is entangled in controversies recites this stotra he is relieved of all the dangers.

## \|\| 37.49 \|\|

*mitrabhedo bhaved dūraṃ tatsaṃmprītirbhavetpurā \|*  
*pārvatī parituṣṭā ca na tyajettasya mandiram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. All his bickering with friends would disappear and the earlier friendship would be restored. The goddess Parvati would never desert him.

## \|\| 37.50 \|\|

*. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*śrutvā pratijñāṃ nāthasya parituṣṭā babhūva sā \|*  
*jagāma svarṇadīṃ tūrṇaṃ snānārthaṃ śaṃkarājñayā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Shri Krishna said – Listening to the words of her husband, Parvati felt satisfied and with the permission of lord Shiva, she went to the bank of the Ganga for taking a bath.

## \|\| 37.51 \|\|

*snātvā saṃpūjya bhaktyā ca suramiṣṭaṃ ca nirguṇam \|*  
*cakāra prastutaṃ śīghraṃ miṣṭānnaṃ vyañjanāni ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. After taking a bath, she with her mind filled with devotion adored lord Shiva who is eternal end thereafter at once prepared sweets and other eatables.

## \|\| 37.52 \|\|

*śivaḥ snātvā ca saṃpūjya brahmajyotiḥ sanātanam \|*  
*tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā māmeva hṛdayasthitam \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. On the other hand Shiva also after taking bath adored the eternal flame of Brahman and with his mind filled with devotion he started praising her.

## \|\| 37.53 \|\|

*gatvā sarvamahaṃ bhuktvā tasmai dattvā'bhivāñchitam \|*  
*naivedyaṃ pārvatī lebhe tava mūlaṃ samāgatā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I than went to them and bestowed the desired reward for them. Parvati than took refuge under your feet and accepted your naivedya.

## \|\| 37.54 \|\|

*bhuktvā'vaśeṣaṃ sā devī saha bhartrā mudā'nvitā \|*  
*tuṣṭāva śaṅkaraṃ bhaktyā praṇanāma muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Thereafter Parvati with Shiva consuming the 'left-over' with delight praised me again and again.

## \|\| 37.55 \|\|

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ sureśvari \|*  
*abhiśaptaṃ śaṅkarasya nirmālyaṃ yena hetunā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. О chief of the goddesses thus I have narrated to you everything whatever was asked by you and the reason for which the 'left-over' of Shiva was cursed.

## Chapter 38

## \|\| 38.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*darpabhaṅgaḥ śruto devi śaṅkarasya jagadguroḥ \|*  
*adhunā śrūyatāṃ matto durgādarpavimocanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Shri Krishna said – You have listened to the episode of the shattering of the pride of Shiva. Now you listen from me to the episode of the shattering of the pride of Durga.

## \|\| 38.2 \|\|

*tejasā sarvadevānāmāvirbhūya jagatprasūḥ \|*  
*dadhāra kāminīrūpaṃ kamanīyaṃ manoharam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The goddess who emerged out of the lustre of all the gods took to the form of Mohini once.

## \|\| 38.3 \|\|

*nihatya dānavendrāṃśca rarakṣa devatākulam \|*  
*lebhe janma tato devī jaṭhare dakṣayoṣitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By killing the great demons she protected the gods. Thereafter she was born out of the womb of the wife of Daksha.

## \|\| 38.4 \|\|

*pinākapāṇiṃ jagrāha sā devī surasādhanam \|*  
*śaśvatparamabhaktyā ca siṣeve svāminaṃ satī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. She then accepted Shiva the holder of bow who always performed the tasks of gods as her husband. Sati continued to serve her husband with devotion.

## \|\| 38.5 \|\|

*dakṣeṇa sārddhaṃ devena babhūva śivaśatrutā \|*  
*nirarthakaṃ daivayogātpurā vai surasaṃsadi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. At once by a turn of destiny, in the assembly of the gods, Daksha became uselessly inimical to Shiva.

## \|\| 38.6 \|\|

*dakṣaścakāra yajñaṃ ca tata āgatya kopataḥ \|*  
*sarvānvijñāpayāmāsa tatraiva śaṃkaraṃ vinā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After returning from the assembly Daksha organised a yctjna in which all the gods except Shiva were invited.

## \|\| 38.7 \|\|

*sastrīkā devatāḥ sarvā ājagmurdakṣamandiram \|*  
*sagaṇaḥ śaṅkaraḥ kopānnājagāmābhimānataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All the gods went to the abode of Daksha with their spouses but Shiva together with his attendants did not attend the yajna because of anger and pride.

## \|\| 38.8 \|\|

*satī patiṃ ca mohena bodhayāmāsa yatnataḥ \|*  
*na taṃ cālayituṃ śaktā babhūva cañcalā svayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Sati tried to convince shiva of participating in the yajna due to the illusion, but she could not persuade him to go there. Thereafter she herself went there.

## \|\| 38.9-10 \|\|

*ājagāma piturgehaṃ darpāttasya vinā''jñayā \|*  
*tasya śāpena tasyāśca darpabhaṅgo babhūva ha \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na hi saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ cakre vāṅmātreṇa pitā ca tām \|*  
*śrutvā ca nindāṃ bhartuśca dehaṃ tatyāja mānataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. She went to the place of Daksha of her own sweet will without the permission of Shiva and the pride of Sati was shattered because of the curse. On her arrival in the hose of her father. Daksha did not welcome her. He did not welcome her even with of a few words. Then hearing the denouncement of her husband, she ended her life there.

## \|\| 38.11 \|\|

*evaṃ priye nigaditaṃ satīdarpavimocanam \|*  
*tasyā janmāntaraṃ nityaṃ darpabhaṅgaśca śrūyatām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О my beloved thus the pride of Sati, was shattered by me. How I tell you the story as to how her pride after having been born as Parvati was shattered. You listen to me.

## \|\| 38.12 \|\|

*lebhe janma satī śīghraṃ jaṭhare śailayoṣitaḥ \|*  
*śivastasyāścitābhasma cāsthi jagrāha bhaktitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After ending her life as Sati, she was born from the womb of Mena, the wife of Himavan. Shiva on the other hand infatuated with the love of Sati plastered the ashes of her pyre on his body.

## \|\| 38.13 \|\|

*cakāra mālāmasthnāṃ ca bhasmanā tanulepanam \|*  
*smāraṃsmāraṃ satīṃ premṇā bhrāmaṃbhrāmaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He made a garland of her bones and wore it round his neck. The ashes of her body served as a decoration of the body of Shiva. He reciting the name of Sati started roaming about everywhere.

## \|\| 38.14 \|\|

*suṣāva menā tāṃ devīmatīva sumanoharām \|*  
*sṛṣṭau vidhātustasyāśca hyupamā nāsti kutra ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. On the other hand, Mena gave birth to a beautiful goddess, the comparison of whom could not be found in the creation of Brahma.

## \|\| 38.15-19 \|\|

*guṇaprūrmuṇānsarvāsarvarūpānvibhari sā \|*  
*sarvāśca devapalyastatkalāṃ nārhanti sodasim \|\| 15 \|\|*

*babhūva varddhamānā sā śukle candrakalā yathā \|*  
*atīva yauvanasthā ca śailagehe dinedine \|\| 16 \|\|*

*babhūvākāśavāṇī ca tāṃ saṃbodhya jagatprasūm \|*  
*śive śivaṃ ca tapasā kaṭhoreṇa labheti ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vineśvaraṃ na tapasā prāptā hi garbhasambhavam \|*  
*prahasya tasthau śrutveti sā ca yauvanagarvitā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mama janmāntarīyaṃ ca bhasmāsthi ca bibharti yaḥ \|*  
*sa māṃ prauḍhāṃ kathaṃ dṛṣṭvā na gṛhṇātyatra janmani \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. She was the mother of all the virtues and possessed all the virtues in her. All the spouses of the gods could not be compared even to the one sixteenth part of her beauty. As the moon goes on increasing in the bright fortnight similarly the goddess started growing in the house of Himalaya day by day. When she achieved the youthful age, there was a divine voice from the sky with spoke addressing her, "O Shiva you achieve Shiva by performing great tapas because without performing tapas it would be difficult for you to achieve him and to conceived from him". On hearing the divine voice, Parvati was filled with pride of her youthfulness laughed and then kept quiet. She started thinking within herself that the one who has applied ashes of her body on his is body and is also adorning his body with the garland her my bones why should he not accept me on her becoming an adult.

## \|\| 38.20 \|\|

*yo vidagdhaśca brahmāṇḍaṃ babhrāma mama śokataḥ \|*  
*sa kathaṃ māṃ na gṛhṇāti dṛṣṭvā paramasundarīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The one who in spite of being so intelligent went on roaming about the universe because of the grief stricken-heart why should he not own her, because she is so beautiful at present.

## \|\| 38.21 \|\|

*dakṣayajñaṃ yo babhañja mama hetoḥ kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*sa kathaṃ māṃ na gṛhṇāti patnīṃ janmanijanmani \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The compassionate one who destroyed the yajna of Daksha for her sake, why should he not accept her as his wife who has always been adoring her in various births.

## \|\| 38.22 \|\|

*yā yasya patnī yo yasyā bhartā prāktanataḥ purā \|*  
*kuto viśve tayorbhedo niṣeko nānyathā bhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The one who was the husband and the one who was the wife in earlier births how can there be a difference on earth. No one could change the destiny.

## \|\| 38.23 \|\|

*sarvarūpaguṇādhāraṃ matvā svamatimānataḥ \|*  
*na cakāra tapaḥ sādhvī na vijñāya tamīśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Having been with pride because of her beauty and virtues, Parvati did not performed tapes not did she consider Shiva as a lord.

## \|\| 38.24 \|\|

*sundarīṣu ca sarvāsu matto nāstyeva sundarī \|*  
*hṛdīti matvā garveṇa na cakāra tapaḥ śivā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. She thought, “There was no other lady comparable to me in beauty". Thus thinking she did not performed tapas.

## \|\| 38.25-26 \|\|

*rūpayauvanaveṣāṇāṃ pumāngrāhī svayoṣitām \|*  
*śivo macchrutimātreṇa māṃ gṛhṇāti vinā tapaḥ \|\| 25\|\|*

*hṛdīti matvā girijā tasthau himagirergṛhe \|*  
*śaśvatsahacarīmadhye krīḍonmattā divāniśam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. She thought that every body likes to have a damsel who is youthful, beautiful and clad in beautiful garments. Therefore Shiva would surely accept her as his wife when she performs tapas. Thus thinking, Giraja remaining in the abode of her father Himavan, spent her time with her female friends and did not go for tapas.

## \|\| 38.27 \|\|

*etasminnantare tūrṇaṃ dūtaḥ śailendrasaṃsadi \|*  
*uvācāgatya madhuraṃ tatpuraḥ saṃpuṭāñjaliḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. In the meantime messengers arrived in the assembly of the lord of mountains and spoke in sweet voice.

## \|\| 38.28 \|\|

*dūta uvāca \|*  
*uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha śailendra gacchākṣayavaṭāntikam \|*  
*ājagāma mahādevaḥ sagaṇo vṛṣavāhanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The messengers said – О lord of the mountain, you get up and move towards the eternal banyan tree. Lord Shiva mounted on the bull is staying there under the tree with his attendants.

## \|\| 38.29-31 \|\|

*madhuparkādikaṃ dattvā bhaktinamrātmakandharaḥ \|*  
*pūjanaṃ kuru śailendraṃ devendraṃ tamatīndriyam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*siddhisvarūpaṃ siddheśaṃ yogīndrāṇāṃ gurorgurum \|*  
*mṛtyuñjayaṃ kālakālaṃ brahmajyotiḥ sanātanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*paramātmasvarūpaṃ ca saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ vibhum \|*  
*bhaktadhyānārthamamalaṃ dadhānaṃ dehamīśvaram \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. You go there and adore lord Shiva with devotion. He is the one who has controlled the organs of senses and you offer madhuparka to him. He is the form of siddhis, the lord of siddhis the teacher of yogis, the one who has overcome the death, is the death for the time, has divine lustre, is eternal, the form of great soul, possesses all the virtues and is without virtues also, is all-pervading and has taken to a spotless form of Maheshvara for the sake of his meditating devotees.

## \|\| 38.32 \|\|

*śailo dūtavacaḥ śrutvā samuttasthau mudā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*madhuparkādikaṃ nītvā jagāma śaṅkarāntikam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. On listening to the words of the messengers, the lord of the mountain was delighted and he reached Shiva carrying madhuparka with him.

## \|\| 38.33 \|\|

*devī dūtavacaḥ śrutvā prasannavadanekṣaṇā \|*  
*hṛdīti mene maddhetorājagāma maheśvaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. On hearing the words of the messenger, the eyes of goddess Parvati felt delighted. She thought in her mind that the lord had arrived there for her sake only.

## \|\| 38.34 \|\|

*cakāra veṣamatulaṃ dadhāra vastramuttamam \|*  
*ratnendrasārālaṃkārānratnamālāṃ manoharām \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. She clad herself in beautiful garments and then adorned herself with the best of gem-studded ornaments and the garland of diamonds.

## \|\| 38.35-37 \|\|

*pārijātaprasūnānāṃ mālāṃ candanasaṃyutām \|*  
*cakāra śaṅkarārthaṃ ca matvā mālāṃ manoharām \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthā sā dadarśa darpaṇe mukham \|*  
*kastūrībindunā sārddhaṃ sindūrabindubhūṣitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ārakta netrayugalaṃ nirmalāñjanasaṃyutam \|*  
*śaranmadhyāhnamamalaṃ yathālipaṃktiveṣṭitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. She then prepared a garland of Parijata flowers and soaked it with sandal-paste for the sake of Shiva. Finding herself to be extremely charming she sat on the lion throne and looked at her face in the mirror which was adorned with a spot of kasturl and vermilion. Her eyes appeared like the lotus flowers of the winter season surrounded by the black-wasps creating a hissing sound.

## \|\| 38.38 \|\|

*sukomalauṣṭhayugulaṃ tāmbūlarāgasaṃyutam \|*  
*atīva sundaraṃ ramyapakvabiṃbaphalaṃ yathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Both her lips were quite soft and had the redness resulting in the chewing of the betel. They were quite beautiful and looked like the ripe wood-apples.

## \|\| 38.39 \|\|

*ratnakuṃḍaladīptyā ca gaṃḍasthalavirājitam \|*  
*sūryodayena jvalitaṃ sumeruśikharaṃ yathā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. As the peacock on Sumeru mountain starts dancing at dawn, similarly the gem-studded kuridalas were adorning her ears.

## \|\| 38.40 \|\|

*atyanirvacanīyaṃ ca dantapaṃktimanoharam \|*  
*yathā muktāsamūhaṃ ca sajalaṃ jaladāgame \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The beauty of the line of her teeth was beyond description and looked like the jewels during the rainy season.

## \|\| 38.41 \|\|

*gajamuktāsamāyuktaṃ sucārunāsikottamam \|*  
*suśobhitaṃ yathā meruṃ svarṇadījaladhārayā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Her nose appeared beautiful like the falling of Ganga from the Meru mountain and a beautiful gem adorned it.

## \|\| 38.42 \|\|

*mālatīmālyasaṃyuktakabarībhārasaṃyutam \|*  
*bakapaṃktisuśobhāḍhyaṃ navīnaṃ jaladaṃ yathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. As the new cloud looks beautiful with the line of sky-larks, similarly the garland of jasmine flowers adorned her hair-do.

## \|\| 38.43 \|\|

*taptakāñcana varṇābhaṃ cāruvakṣaḥsthalojjvalam \|*  
*ratnendrasārahārāktaṃ kastūrīkuṅkumānvitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The garlands were made of gems and her breast which was painted with the paste of kastUrl and saffron looked quite dazzling.

## \|\| 38.44 \|\|

*cārucampakavarṇābhaṃ stanayugmaṃ manoharam \|*  
*badarīphalatulyaṃ ca cārupatrakaśobhitam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Her nipples which were beautifully painted looked like the jujubi fruits.

## \|\| 38.45 \|\|

*madhyaṃ manoharaṃ kṣīṇaṃ nimnanābhisthalojjvalam \|*  
*atīva sundaraṃ ramyamudaraṃ vartulākṛti \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. she was thin-waisted and looked quite charming. Her navel was deep and shining, the belly was roundish and looked quite beautiful.

## \|\| 38.46 \|\|

*rambhāstaṃbhaviniṃdyaikamūruyugmaṃ manoharam \|*  
*kāmālayaṃ sukaṭhinaṃ nigūḍhamaṃśukena ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Her thighs resembled the trunks of banana tree and were quite pleasant and thick clad in fine clothes.

## \|\| 38.47 \|\|

*sthalapadmaprabhāmuṣṭapadayugmaṃ manoharam \|*  
*ratnapāśakasaṃyuktaṃ siddhālaktakabhūṣitam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Her feet were quite soft, beautiful and could steal the lustre of the lotus flowers and were adorned with anklets and the red paint appeared on the soles of the feet.

## \|\| 38.48 \|\|

*dadhataṃ ratnamañjīraṃ rājahaṃsānukāri ca \|*  
*ratnendrasārābharaṇaṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Her anklets created the sound like the sweet notes issued by the geese. Vishvakarma had made her ornaments with the best of gems.

## \|\| 38.49 \|\|

*karaṃ sukomalataraṃ sundaraṃ kanakaprabham \|*  
*ratnakaṅkaṇakeyūraśaṃkhabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. They were issuing the lustre of gold and her hands looked quite beautiful. She was adorned with beautiful armlets and wristlets besides the ornaments of conch.

## \|\| 38.50 \|\|

*bibhratsadratnamukuraṃ līlākamalamujjvalam \|*  
*ratnāṅgulīyamatulaṃ dadhataṃ sumanoharam \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. She held in her hand an attractive mirror of gems and had the finger rings studded with rubies-which was issuing the lustre like the red lotus flower.

## \|\| 38.51 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā svarūpamatulaṃ dadhyau śaṅkaramīśvaram \|*  
*viśiṣya manasā śaśvadbhartuścaraṇapaṅkajam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Witnessing such a beauty for herself, she devoted her mind to Shiva. She especially meditated upon him to achieve him as her husband.

## \|\| 38.52 \|\|

*pitaraṃ mātaraṃ bandhuṃ sādhvīvargaṃ sahodaram \|*  
*antare sā na sasmāra kiṃcideva śivaṃ vinā \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. At that point of time she did not think of her father, mother, brother, female friends and other relatives.

## \|\| 38.53 \|\|

*atha śaileśvarastatra dadarśa candraśekharam \|*  
*svarṇadīpulinādramyādutpatantaṃ ca sasmitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Himalaya on the other hand reaching before Shiva looked at him. He was smiling when he reached the bank of the charming Ganga.

## \|\| 38.54-57 \|\|

*dadhataṃ saṃskṛtāṃ mālāṃ japantaṃ mama nāmakam \|*  
*taptasvarṇaprabhājuṣṭajaṭārāśi virājitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhasthaṃ śūlapāṇiṃ sarvabhūṣaṇarājitam \|*  
*nāgayajñopavītaṃ ca sarpabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ vyāghracarmadharaṃ param \|*  
*vibhūtibhūṣitāṅgaṃ tamasthimālaṃ digambaram \|\| 56 \|\|*

*pañcavaktraṃ trinayanaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham \|*  
*dadarśa rudrānparito jvalato brahmatejasā \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. Holding a rosary he was reciting my name and his head was adorned with matted locks of hair having the complexion of molten gold. He was mounted on a bull, holding a trident in his hand. The Nagas served as his yajnopavlta and the lustre of the limbs of bodies resembled the crystal. He was clad in tiger skin and wearing the garland of bones; with ashes all on his body, he looked graceful. He had no garments on his person, was five-faced having three eyes in each one of them, all his limbs emitted the lustre of crores of suns. Himavan found the eleven Rudras surrounding him who were illumining with divine lustre.

## \|\| 38.58-62 \|\|

*śivavāme mahākālaṃ dakṣiṇe nandikeśvaram \|*  
*bhūtapretapiśācāṃśca kūṣmāṇḍānbrahmarākṣasān \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vetālānkṣetrapālāṃśca bhairavānbhīmavikramān \|*  
*sanakaṃ ca sanandaṃ ca kumāraṃ ca sanātanam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*jaigīṣavyaṃ devalaṃ ca kāṇādaṃ gautamaṃ tathā \|*  
*pippalādaṃ kaṇakhanaṃ voḍhuṃ pañcaśikhaṃ kaṭham \|\| 60 \|\|*

*jājaliṃ karakhaṃ karṇaṃ lomaśaṃ sūryavarcasam \|*  
*kātyāyanaṃ pāṇiniṃ ca śaṃkhaṃ durvāsasaṃ tataḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śātātapaṃ pāribhadramaṣṭāvakraṃ marudbhavam \|*  
*etānpurogamānnatvā praṇanāma śivaṃ giriḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

58-62. Mahakala was lodged to the left of Shiva while Nandikeshvara was standing to his right, the Pretas, goblins, Pishacas, Kusmanda, Brahmaraks asas, Velalas, Ksetra-palas the valorous Bhairavas, Sanaka, Sananda, Sanatkumara, Sanatana, Jaiglsavya, Devala, Kanada, Gautama, Pippalada, Kanakhana, Vodhu, Pancasikha, Kat ha, Jajali, Karakha, Kama, Lomasa, Suryavarca, Katyayana, Panini, Durvasa, Satatapa, Paribhadra, Astavakra and Maradbhava were standing before him. Himalaya offered his salutation to then.

## \|\| 38.63-64 \|\|

*mūrdhnā nipatya bhūmau sa daṇḍavatsaṃpuṭāñjaliḥ \|*  
*atho analpayā bhaktyā dhṛtvā taccaraṇāmbujam \|*  
*nanāma cāśrunetraḥ sa pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*dharmadattena stotreṇa tuṣṭāva parameśvaram \|*  
*tuṣṭe brāhme dine'tīte puṣkare sūryaparvaṇi \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Then prostrating on the ground he stood before him with folded hands. Thereafter, touching his feet he started washing them with her tears. At that point of time he felt overwhelmed with emotions and the tears started flowing from his eyes. He thereafter started offering prayer to Shiva with the stotra given to him by Dharma. The stotra was handed down by Brahma to Dharma at the time of the solar eclipse.

## \|\| 38.65-66 \|\|

*himālaya uvāca \|*  
*tvaṃ brahmā sṛṣṭikartā ca tvaṃ viṣṇuḥ paripālakaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*tvaṃ śivaḥ śivado'nantaḥ sarvasaṃhārakārakaḥ \|*  
*tvamīśvaro guṇātīto jyotīrūpaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Himalaya said – You are the creator, known as Brahma, the preserver like Vishnu and bestower of welfare as Shiva and also the destroyer of the universe; you are the lord beyond qualities, the form of eternal flame, eternal, nature, lord of Prakfli, beyond Prakriti and the nature.

## \|\| 38.67 \|\|

*prakṛtaḥ prakṛtīśaśca prākṛtaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nānārūpavidhātā tvaṃ bhaktānāṃ dhyānahetave \|*  
*yeṣu rūpeṣu yatprītistattadrūpaṃ bibharṣi ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. You take to many forms and the devotees meditate upon you. Whosoever adores you in whichever form, you take to that form.

## \|\| 38.68 \|\|

*sūryastvaṃ sṛṣṭijanaka ādhāraḥ sarvatejasām \|*  
*somastvaṃ sasyapātā ca satataṃ śītaraśminā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. You are like the sun who creates the universe; you are the base of a 4 the lustres and also serve the crops in the form of cool rays of the moon.

## \|\| 38.69-72 \|\|

*vāyustvaṃ varuṇastvaṃ ca tvamagniḥ sarvadāhakaḥ \|*  
*indrastvaṃ devarājaśca kālo mṛtyuryamastathā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*mṛtyuñjayo mṛtyumṛtyuḥ kālakālo yamāntakaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*vedastvaṃ vedakartā ca vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|*  
*viduṣāṃ janakastvaṃ ca vidvāṃśca viduṣāṃ guruḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*mantrastvaṃ hi japastvaṃ hi tapastvaṃ tatphalapradaḥ \|*  
*vāk tvaṃ vāgadhidevī tvaṃ tatkartā tadguruḥ svayam \|\| 72 \|\|*

69-72. You represent the wind, Varuna, fire, the destroyer of all, Indra the lord of gods, Kala, the death, Yama, the one who has over-powered the death, for the god of death, kala for the time, death for Yama you are the Vedas, the creator of the Vedas, well-versed in the Vedic and post-Vedic literature, the creator of intellectual; you are a great intellectual yourself, the teacher of intellectuals, mantra, recitation, tapas and you bestow the reward for the same. You are the speech the goddess of speech besides being her creator and the teacher, the seed of Sarasvati is quite astonishing, therefore who can offer prayer to you?

## \|\| 38.73 \|\|

*aho sarasvatībījaṃ kastvāṃ stotumiheśvaraḥ \|*  
*ityevamuktvā śailendrastasthau dhṛtvā padāmbujam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Thus speaking Himalaya fell at his feet and then stood there. Shiva then descended from the bull. Addressing Himavan he sat there.

## \|\| 38.74 \|\|

*tatrovāsa tamābodhya cāvaruhya vṛṣācchivaḥ \|*  
*stotrametanmahāpuṇyaṃ trisandhyaṃ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The one who recites this stotra thrice a day, is relieved of all the cures and makes one to cross over the ocean of universe fearlessly.

## \|\| 38.75-78 \|\|

*mucyate sarvapāpebhyo bhayebhyaśca bhavārṇave \|*  
*aputro labhate putraṃ māsamekaṃ paṭhedyadi \|\| 75 \|\|*

*bhāryāhīno labhedbhāryāṃ suśīlāṃ sumanoharām \|*  
*cirakālagataṃ vastu labhate sahasā dhruvam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*rājyabhraṣṭo labhedrājyaṃ śaṃkarasya prasādataḥ \|*  
*kārāgāre śmaśāne ca śatrugraste'tisaṃkaṭe \|\| 77 \|\|*

*gabhīre'tijalākīrṇe bhagnapote viṣādane \|*  
*raṇamadhye mahābhīte hiṃsrajantusamanvite \|\| 78 \|\|*

75-78. One who recites the same for a month gets a son if he has no son, the one having no wife get a chaste wife besides the riches suddenly which he had lost long back. By the grace of Shiva, the dethroned king gets back his kingdom, when a person is in dangers like the prison, cremation ground, danger from enemies, in the flames of fire, breaking of the boat and getting surrounded by the wild animals one is relieved of all these dangers.

7-11. He looked like the passion for the passionate women and bestower of sons to the chaste women, Maha-Vishnu for Vaishnavas, SadaShiva for Saivas, the form of sakti for those who believed in Sakti, the form of sun who believes in the sum worship, the death for wicked people, preserver for the noble people, death for the time and destruction for all the types of destruction's. His tiger skin was turned into charming garments. The ashes were turned into sandal-paste, the snakes were turned into beautiful garlands the kalakuta-poison was turned into kasturl and the beautiful matted locks of hair were turned into tuft. The crescent on the head was turned into sandal-paste and the stream of Ganga was turned into a beautiful garland of jasmine flowers, the garland of bones was turned into a garland of diamonds and the flowers of wood apple trees were turned into campaka flowers.

12-15. In place of five faces only one face could be seen which had only two eyes. The face had the lustre of the full moon of the winter season and was glittering. His lips could put to shame the lustre of the mid-day and his lips added to the beauty of his face. The bull Nandi was burnt into the white moon and the goblins were turned into dancers. О goddess, everything of Shiva was changed at that moment. Finding Shiva in that form, Mena felt pleased. Some of the damsels got infatuated with passion while looking at Shiva and started staring at him. While some of them fainted with the excessive passions.

23-25. They said, "Durga is quite virtuous and her birth in the land of Bharata is quite auspicious because she is going to be wedded to Shiva. Himalaya also adored Shiva and bowing in reverence to him went back to his abode. Thereafter Himalaya in consultation with Mena in a secluded place deputed Parvati to Shiva.

27-33. Finding the peaceful Shiva with a smiling face, she went round him seven times and smilingly offered her salutation to him. Shiva at that point of time blessing her said, "0 beautiful one, you achieve an extremely loveable, virtuous, eternal, the best of intellectuals and the beautiful person as your husband. О auspicious one, you would always remain virtuous and filled with fortunes concerning the husband. О chaste damsel, your son would be as virtuous as Ыйгауапа himself, О mother of the universe, you will be adored always in the world, you will be best of all the ladies in the three worlds. О beautiful one, you have offered salutation to me after going round seven times, therefore I feel satisfied with you for seven births. You will reap the reward for the same, the one who adores the holy places, the husband, the family god, the teacher, the mantra and the medicine with whatever idea in mind, he achieves success in the same way. Thus speaking Shiva the lord of the yogis went into meditation seated on the skin of the tiger.

She then offered to him the lion-throne studded with gems and made by Vishvakarma. Then she offered him naivedya in the bronze vase. Than she offered arghya with the water of Ganga. She also offered the sandal-paste, kastiiri and saffron which were filled with fragrance. Thereafter she adorned his neck which looked beautiful with, spot of the poison, with the garland of jasmine flowers.

37-40. She adored him with devotion and showered flowers on him. Thereafter she offered nectar and sweet honey in vases of gold. She lighted hundreds of lamps around him. Burning fragrant incense around him, she offered him the costumes which were difficult to get in the three worlds beside a yajnopavlta of gold and fragrant cool water for drinking. She offered him the ornaments made of the best of gem, Kamadhenu cow with her horn adorned with plates of gold, articles for use in taking a bath, water from the sacred places and charming betels.

41\. Thus she performed sixteen types of puja of Shiva and bowed in reverence to him again and again. This became her daily routine. She used to offer puja to Shiva daily with devotion and then returned to the abode of her parents.

## \|\| 39.42-43 \|\|

*śuśrāvāpsarasāṃ vaktrāddevīmindro maheśvaraḥ \|*

42-43. Indra the god of gods heard about the news from the mouth of the apsaras and he also got attracted towards Parvati. He started dancing in ecstasy. Indra at once siunmoned the god of love by sending a messenger to him. Kamadeva, on his part, arrived in Amaravati, the kingdom of Indra.

## \|\| 39.44-48 \|\|

*tūrṇaṃ prasthāpayāmāsa taṃ ca yatra śivaḥ śivā \|*

*prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānyatra śaktiyutaḥ śivaḥ \|*  
*gatvā dadarśa madanaḥ śivāyuktaṃ śivaṃ vibhum \|\| 45 \|\|*

*śāntaṃ trailokyakāntaṃ ca prasannavadanekṣaṇam \|*

*cikṣepāstraṃ durnivāryamamoghaṃ śaṃkare mudā \|*

44-48. He deputed the god of love at once to the place of Shiva and Parvati. Kamadeva arrived with his five arrows at the place where both Shiva and Parvati were present. The god of love on arriving there found both Shiva and Parvati together. Shiva was quite peaceful being the lord of the three worlds having delightful face and the eyes, the god of love remaining in the sky took the bow in his hand and shot an infallible arrow delightfully at Shiva but the infallible weapon became infructuous when it came into contact with Shiva like the sky which remains infallible. Similarly the attack of Kama on Shiva was infructuous. At this the god of love was terribly afraid.

## \|\| 39.49-50 \|\|

*cakampe purataḥ sthitvā dṛṣṭvā mṛtyuṃjayaṃ vibhum \|*

*āyayurdevatāḥ sarvāḥ śaṃbhukopena vepitāḥ \|*

49-50. Finding Shiva who had overpowered death, Kama the god of love, started trembling and getting terrified started reciting the name of Indra and other gods. All the gods were terrified at the anger of Shiva and felt panicky and arrived there and started praising Shiva reciting the stotras.

## \|\| 39.51-53 \|\|

*kopāginimudigarantaṃ taṃ kapālalocanādaho \|*

*jajvālordhvaśikho dīptaḥ pralayāgniśikhopamaḥ \|*  
*utpatya gagane ghūrṇannipatya dharaṇītale \|\| 52 \|\|*

*bhrāmaṃbhrāmaṃ ca paritaḥ papāta madanopari \|*  
*babhūva bhasmasātkāmaḥ kṣaṇena harakopataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Nandi got you have so adoring. The fire flame emerged from Shiva's third eye on the forehead, the fire-flames that emerge from the forehead of aiva went on higher. Those fire-flames looked like the fire of-dissolution and started roaming about in the sky and then descended on the earth and searching in all the directions spotted Kamadeva and fell on him with the rage of Shiva. The god of love was reduced to ashes in a moment.

## \|\| 39.54 \|\|

*viṣaṇṇā devatāḥ sarvā natavaktrā ca pārvatī \|*  
*vilalāpa bahutaraṃ harasya purato ratiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. At the sight of this the minds of the gods were filled with grief, who cast their heads downwards. Thereafter, Rati the spouse of the god of love appeared before Shiva and started lamenting.

## \|\| 39.55-57 \|\|

*tuṣṭuvurdevatāḥ sarvāḥ kampitāścandraśekharam \|*  
*ratimūcuḥ surāḥ sarve ruruduśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kiṃcidbhasma gṛhītvā ca rakṣa mātarbhayaṃ tyaja \|*  
*vayaṃ taṃ jīvayiṣyāmo labhiṣyasi priyaṃ punaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*harakopāpanayane suprasanne dine tathā \|*

55-57. Thereafter the terrified gods also offered prayer to Shiva. Crying again and again the gods spoke to Rati, "O mother you take out some dust of the body of the god of love and keep it safe, shed away the fear we shall somehow bring back the god of love to life and you will again get back your beloved. When the anger of Shiva is subsided and he gets pleased, only then this could be possible. At that point of time, finding Rati so lamenting Parvati fainted.

## \|\| 39.58 \|\|

*atīndriyaṃ guṇātītaṃ tuṣṭāva candraśekharam \|*  
*rudantīṃ pārvatīṃ tyaktvā svasthānaṃ prayayau śivaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thereafter she started the virtuous Shiva who had controlled all his senses. Leaving Parvati so crying Shiva went to his abode.

## \|\| 39.59 \|\|

*sadyo babhūva tatraiva pārvatīdarpamokṣaṇam \|*  
*rūpayauvanayorgarvaṃ tatyāja śailakanyakā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. At that point of time the pride of Parvati was shattered. Thereafter the daughter of the mountain disowned the pride for her youthfulness and beauty.

## \|\| 39.60-64 \|\|

*mukhaṃ darśayituṃ lajjā tadbabhūva sakhīgaṇe \|*  
*surāśca ratimāśvāsya sarve jagmuḥ svamandiram \|\| 60 \|\|*

*praṇamya daṇḍavadrudraṃ śokādudvignamānasāḥ \|*  
*stutvā ruditvā śokena bhayena kāmakāminī \|\| 61 \|\|*

*koparaktekṣaṇaṃ rudraṃ rādhike svālayaṃ yayau \|*  
*na jagāma piturgehaṃ pārvatī sā tu lajjayā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*svālibhirvāryamāṇā'pi jagāma tapase vanam \|*  
*prajagmuḥ sahacāriṇyastatpaścācchokavihvalāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*mātṛbhirvāryamāṇā sā svarṇadītīrajaṃ vanam \|*  
*suciraṃ ca tapastaptvā sā saṃprāpa trilocanam \|\| 64 \|\|*

60-64. At that point of time she became shy in showing her face to her female friends. Thereafter, all the gods reassuring Rati and prostrating before Shiva getting upset with their mind filled with grief they left for their respective abodes. О Radha, thereafter, Rati the wife of Kamadeva with her mind filled with grief and terror went on crying and with her eyes getting red like blood she offered prayer to Shiva and then left for her abode. But Parvati feeling ashamed never went back to the abode of her father but disregarding the advice of her parents and the female friends, she went to the forest. Thereafter her female friends with their minds filled with grief, went to their respective abodes. Disregarding the words of her mother, she want to the bank of Ganga and started performing tapas there, in order to achieve the three-eyed Shiva as her husband.

## \|\| 39.65 \|\|

*ratiḥ saṃprāpa madanaṃ śaṃkarasya vareṇa ca \|*

65\. After the tapas Parvati achieved Shiva and Rati also with the boon of Shiva got back Kamadeva. О Radha, thus I have spoken to you about the episode of the shattering of the pride of Parvati. "Which is quite secretive. What more do you want to listen from me.

## Chapter 40

## \|\| 40.1-2 \|\|

*śrīrādhikovāca \|*  
*aho vicitraṃ caritamapūrvaṃ kiṃ śrutaṃ vibho \|*  
*sundaraṃ śrutipīyūṣaṃ nigūḍhaṃ jñānakāraṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1-2. Radhika said – О virtuous one, I have been able to listen to the unprecedented and astonishing story which serves like nectar for the ears and is quite deep and bestows knowledge. О lord, whatever have I heard has neither been told in brief nor in detail. But now I intend to listen to it in detail you tell me.

## \|\| 40.3-4 \|\|

*kiṃ kiṃ tapaḥ kaṭhoraṃ ca cakāra pārvatī svayam \|*

*ratiḥ kena prakāreṇa jīvayāmāsa manmatham \|*

3-4. What type of hard tapas was performed by Parvati and what type of boons did she achieve together with lord Maheshvara? How did Rati get the god of love back to life? О lord Krishna, you kindly define the marriage of Shiva and Parvati.

## \|\| 40.5 \|\|

*tayo rahasi saṃbhogaṃ pāpināṃ pāpamocanam \|*  
*kathyatāṃ karuṇāsindho duḥkhināṃ duḥkhamocanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О ocean of compassion, you describe to me about their union in seclusion, which removes from the sinners of all the sins and the grief of all the grief-stricken people.

## \|\| 40.6-7 \|\|

*dampatīvirahoktiśca karṇajvālā ca yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ kṛṣṇa punaḥ saṃmelanaṃ tayoḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*agnijvālā viṣajvālā kṣamā soḍhuṃ ca yoṣitaḥ \|*  
*dampatīvirahajvālā na śrotuṃ ca kṣaṇaṃ kṣamā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. О Krishna, the words of a woman separated from the husband serve as a fire flame for the women. Therefore I am quite anxious to know about the reunion of Shiva and Parvati. The women can wear the flames of fire and the flames of the poison but they are unable to bear even for a moment the flames of separation.

## \|\| 40.8 \|\|

*rādhikāvacanaṃ śrutvā vismitaścakitānanaḥ \|*  
*vistīrṇaṃ vaktumārebhe hṛdayena vidūyatā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. On hearing the words of Radhika, Krishna was surprised and his face gave an appearance of astonishment. Thereafter he started speaking with his mind overpowered with passion.

## \|\| 40.9-10 \|\|

*dampatīvirahoktiṃ ca yāṃ rādhā śrotumakṣamā \|*  
*vicchede śatavarṣīye kimasyā bhavitā mama \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ mānase kṛtvā māyeśo māyayā'nvitaḥ \|*  
*kṛpāsindhuśca kṛpayā kathāṃ kathitumudyataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Radha who was unable to listen to the separation of the story of the couple, what shall be her position at the time of her separation from the lord for a hundred years? Thus thinking in her mind, the lord of illusion who is all filled with Maya and is the ocean of mercy, started narrating the story.

## \|\| 40.11-12 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*prāṇādhike rādhike tvaṃ śrūyatāṃ prāṇavallabhe \|*  
*prāṇādhidevi prāṇeśi prāṇādhāre manohare \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vaṭamūlādgate rudre pārvatī tapase yayau \|*  
*punaḥ punaḥ svamātrā ca pitrā ca vinivāritā \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Shri Krishna said – О beloved of my life, О Radhika, you are dearer to me than my life, now you listen to me. О beloved, you are the goddess of my life, the support of my life, О pleasant one, when lord Rudra left the place where he was lodged under the banyan tree then Parvati also started performing several tapas in spite of the objection by her parents.

## \|\| 40.13 \|\|

*gatvā sā svarṇadītīraṃ snātvā triṣavaṇaṃ mudā \|*  
*saṃdeśe ca mayā dattaṃ jajāpa taṃ manuṃ mudā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Reaching the bank of Ganga she took a bath thrice a day and started reciting the mantra given by me.

## \|\| 40.14-16 \|\|

*varṣamekaṃ ca saṃpūrṇamanāhārā svabhaktitaḥ \|*  
*taptvā tapaḥ kaṭhoraṃ ca cakāra jagadambikā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*grīṣme ca parito vahniṃ prajvalantaṃ divāniśam \|*  
*kṛtvā pratasthau tanmadhye saṃtataṃ japatī manum \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śaśvatsmaśāne varṣāsu kṛtvā yogāsanaṃ śivā \|*  
*śilāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsiktā babhūva jaladhārayā \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. With her devotion, the mother of the universe performed tapas for one year without consuming anything, She used to raise fire around her during the summer season and always remained inside it throughout day and night, reciting the mantra. In the rainy season she seated herself in the yogasana posture in the cremation grounds and continued to stare at the stone of lord Shiva getting drenched with the rain water.

## \|\| 40.17-18 \|\|

*śīte jalāntare śaśvatpratasthau bhaktipūrvakam \|*  
*anāhārā śaradraudranīhārāsu diśāsu ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*evaṃ kṛtvā paraṃ varṣamaprāpya śaṃkaraṃ satī \|*  
*śucā kṛtvā'gnikuṇḍaṃ ca praveṣṭuṃ sā samudyatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. In the winter season she used to enter the cold water and even during the nights of terrific cold during which the snow used to fall she remained without food and performed the hard tapas with devotion. Thus after performing such a hard tapas for one year, Shiva did not appear before her and at that point of time in utter disgust she prepared herself to enter in to the flames of fire-altar.

## \|\| 40.19-21 \|\|

*tāmagnikuṇḍaṃ viśatīṃ tapasā'tikṛśāṃ satīm \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā śivaḥ kṛpāsindhuḥ kṛpayā tāṃ jagāma ha \|\| 19 \|\|*

*atīva vāmano bālo viprarūpī svatejasā \|*  
*prajvalanmanasā hṛṣṭo daṇḍī chatrī jaṭādharaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śuklayajñopavītī ca śuklavāsāśca sasmitaḥ \|*  
*śvetābjabījamālāṃ ca bibhrattilakamujjvalam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Finding Parvati who had grown very weak because of performing tapas was entering into the fire-altar, Shiva, the ocean of mercy, at once reached before her in the form of a dwarf Brahmana boy. Shiva was delighted in his heart. He had the matted lock of hair on the head and was holding a danda and chatra. He was clad in white garment, white yajhopavlta wearing the garland of white lotus flowers and the white sandal-paste was applied on his forehead. He was serenely smiling.

## \|\| 40.22-23 \|\|

*nirjane bālakaṃ dṛṣṭvā snigdhā sāpi jagāda ha \|*  
*tattejasā'tipracchannā tatyāja ca tapaḥ svayam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ko bhavāniti papraccha taṃ śiśuṃ purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*manasā'liṅganaṃ kartumicchantī paramādaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Finding the boy in lonely place the mind of Parvati was filled with love. Getting influenced with his lustre, she discarding tapas spoke to the boy, “Who are you?” Parvati intended to embrace the boy lovingly.

## \|\| 40.24 \|\|

*śrutvā śailasutā praśnaṃ prahasya parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*uvācātīva madhuraṃ karṇapīyūṣamīśvarīm \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing the question of the daughter of the mountain, Shiva the lord of the universe laughed and then spoke the words which entered the ears of Parvati like nectar.

## \|\| 40.25 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*icchāgāmī baṭurahaṃ tapasvī viprabālakaḥ \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kāntā'tikāntāre tapaścarasi sundari \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Shiva said – I am a Brahmana boy and am an ascetic roaming about at will. О beautiful one, who are you and why are you performing tapas in this lonely forest, in spite of your being so beautiful.

## \|\| 40.26 \|\|

*vada kasya kule jātā kasya kanyā ca kā'bhidhā \|*  
*tapasaḥ phaladātrī tvaṃ kasmāddhetostapastava \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In whose race have you been bom? Who is your father? What is your name? You being yourself the one who bestows the reward of tapas, why are you performing tapas yourself?

## \|\| 40.27 \|\|

*aho vā tapasāṃ rāśiḥ svayaṃ mūrtimatī satī \|*  
*tapo vā lokaśikṣārthaṃ karoṣi kamalekṣaṇe \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О lotus eyed one, you are the actual form of tapas. Surely this tapas of yours is meant for educating the universe.

## \|\| 40.28 \|\|

*svayaṃ tejaḥsvarūpā vā mūlaprakṛtirīśvarī \|*  
*vidhāya bhaktadhyānārthaṃ vigrahaṃ bhārate januḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are yourself the ball of lustre, besides being Mula-Prakriti and Tsvarl and you have taken to this form for the sake of the devotees in the land of Bharata.

## \|\| 40.29-31 \|\|

*kiṃ vā triloke lakṣmīstvaṃ saṃpadrūpā sanātanī \|*  
*rakṣāṃ vidhātuṃ jagatāmāgatā dhāturantike \|\| 29 \|\|*

*kiṃ vāmbikā tvaṃ devānāṃ svayaṃ mūrtimatī satī \|*  
*sāvitrī bhārate janma svecchayā labdhumāgatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*rāgādhiṣṭhātṛdevī vā svayaṃ sākṣātsarasvatī \|*  
*sarvavidyāḥ prakaṭituṃ svecchayā janma bhārate \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Otherwise you are the eternal Lakshmi, the goddess of riches in the three worlds, you have reached before Brahma for the protection of the three worlds or are you the mother of the gods or Sati or Savitri who takes to human births with her own will. Or otherwise are you the great goddess of music known as goddess Sarasvati from whom all types of knowledge emerged. You have been born on earth with your own sweet will.

## \|\| 40.32 \|\|

*etāsu madhye kā vā tvaṃ nāhaṃ tarkitumīśvaraḥ \|*  
*yā sā bhavati kalyāṇi parituṣṭā ca māṃ bhava \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Out of these goddesses, whom do you represent. I am unable to visualise the same. О goddess of welfare, whatever I have asked you, be pleased with me.

## \|\| 40.33-34 \|\|

*sati tvayi prasannāyāṃ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ \|*  
*pativratāyāṃ tuṣṭāyāṃ tuṣṭo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tuṣṭe nārāyaṇe deve śaśvattuṣṭaṃ jagattrayam \|*  
*tarumūleṣu sikteṣu śākhāḥ siktā yathā priye \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. O Sati, if you remain happy, the lord also becomes happy and when a chaste lady is pleased the lord Narayana himself gets pleased. О dear one, with the pleasing of lord Narayana, all the three worlds similarly get pleased, since with the pouring of water at the roots of the trees, the branches sprout.

## \|\| 40.35 \|\|

*śiśostadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya parameśvarī \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ cāru karṇapīyūṣamīśvarī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On hearing the words of the boy, the great goddess smiled for a moment and spoke the words which were pleasing like the pouring of nectar in the ears.

## \|\| 40.36 \|\|

*pārvatyuvāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ vedaprasūrlakṣmīrvāgadhiṣṭhātṛdevatā \|*  
*janma me bhārate varṣe sāmprataṃ śailakanyakā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Parvati said – I am neither Savitri the creator of the Vedas, nor Lakshmi or the goddess of speech. I am pleasantly born in the land of Bharata and am the daughter of the king of mountains.

## \|\| 40.37 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ janma dakṣagehe satī śaṃkarakāminī \|*  
*yogena tyaktadehā'haṃ tātabhartṛvinindayā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In my earlier birth, I had been born in the house of Daksha and happened to be the wife of Shiva named Sati. When my father denounced my husband I ended my life with the use of yogic practices.

## \|\| 40.38 \|\|

*atra janmani puṇyena samprāpte śaṃkare dvija \|*  
*māṃ tyaktvā bhasmasātkṛtvā manmathaṃ sa jagāma ha \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О Brahmana, in this birth also because of my earlier deeds I achieved Shiva but he, reducing the god of love to ashes disowned me and left the place.

## \|\| 40.39 \|\|

*prayāte śaṃkare tāpādvrīḍayā'haṃ piturgṛhāt \|*  
*āgamattapase cittaṃ mamedaṃ svarṇadītaṭe \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. With the departure of Shiva I was filled with mental agony and shame. I therefore left my parents and arrived here at the bank of the Ganga.

## \|\| 40.40 \|\|

*tapaḥ kṛtvā kaṭhoraṃ ca suciraṃ prāṇavallabham \|*  
*aprāpyāgniṃ praveṣṭuṃ ca tvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā kṣaṇaṃ sthitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I performed severe tapas for long but in spite of that I have not been able to achieve Shiva. I am thus going to enter the flames of the fire-altar. But finding you here I have stopped for a moment.

## \|\| 40.41 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ praviśāmyagnau pralayāgniśikhopame \|*  
*kṛtvā svakāmanāṃ vipra haraprāptimanīṣitam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О Brahmana now you go, I am going to enter this fire of dissolution which is burning in flames, in order to achieve Shiva by entering it.

## \|\| 40.42 \|\|

*yatra yatra janurlabdhvā labhiṣyāmi śivaṃ param \|*  
*prāṇādhikaṃ priyaṃ kāntaṃ vibhuṃ janmani janmani \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In future I would achieve Shiva always who is dearer to me than my life, he is my only lord.

## \|\| 40.43 \|\|

*sarvā hi svapriyaṃ labdhuṃ labhanti janma vāñchitam \|*  
*tajjanma patilābhārthaṃ sarvāsāṃ ca śrutau śrutam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. All women are born in human form in order to achieve their beloved. Their birth is only meant for achieving a noble husband.

## \|\| 40.44 \|\|

*prāktanīyo hi yo bhartā sa tāsāṃ pratijanmani \|*  
*yā strī yeṣāṃ suniyatā sā teṣāṃ janmajanmani \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The women generally achieve the same husband whom they had in their earlier births. Whatever woman is destined for one, she achieves the same in every birth.

## \|\| 40.45 \|\|

*taddehamiha na prāpya kṛtvā ghorataraṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā'gnikuṇḍe kāmyaṃ ca labhiṣyāmi paratra tam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Therefore, in case I do not achieve my husband after performing several tapas during this birth. I shall offer this body in the fire-altar. With the desire of having Shiva as my husband in my mind if I enter the fire, I am sure to achieve him in the next birth.

## \|\| 40.46-47 \|\|

*ityuktvā pārvatī tatra tatpuraḥ praviveśa ha \|*  
*niṣidhyamānā purato brāhmaṇena punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vahnipraveśaṃ kurvantyāḥ pārvatyāḥ parameśvari \|*  
*babhūva tapasā sadyo vahniścandanavaddhruvam \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Thus speaking Parvati, in spite of dissuading her by the Brahmana boy, from entering into the fire, she entered the fire-altar. But the fire became cool like the sandal-paste.

## \|\| 40.48 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ tadantare sthitvā cotpatantīṃ śivāṃ śivaḥ \|*  
*punaḥ prapaccha sahasā vṛndāvanavinodini \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О Radha, you enjoy the divine play in Vrindavana, remaining there in the fire for a moment, she came Out end suddenly Shiva asked.

## \|\| 40.49-50 \|\|

*śrīmahādeva uvāca \|*  
*aho tapaste kiṃ bhadre na buddhaṃ kiṃcideva hi \|*  
*na dagdho vahninā deho na ca prāpto manīṣitaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*śivaṃ kalyāṇarūpaṃ ca bhartāraṃ kartumicchasi \|*  
*avigrahaṃ patiṃ kṛtvā kiṃ vā te vāñchitaṃ bhavet \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Shiva said – О noble damsel, what is your tapas? I am unable to understand it. Neither your body could be burnt out in the fire nor could you get the husband of your choice. You intend to achieve Shiva, the form of welfare, as your husband but he is invisible. By achieving an invisible husband, what purpose of yours would be served?

## \|\| 40.51 \|\|

*saṃhartāraṃ ca bhartāraṃ yadīcchasi śucismite \|*  
*kāntamicchati kā vā strī sarvasaṃhārakāraṇam \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О damsel, with a pious smile, in case you want to make the one who is the destroyer of all as your husband, then you tell me which one of the women would like to have a destroyer of all as her husband.

## \|\| 40.52 \|\|

*mokṣaṃ vāñchasi ceddevi kṛtvā kāntaṃ svarūpiṇam \|*  
*sarvamuktipradā tvaṃ ca tapasyā viphalā tava \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. О goddess, in case by achieving him as your husband, you want to achieve moksa then for that purpose your tapas is of no use, because you yourself bestow salvation to everyone.

## \|\| 40.53 \|\|

*śivaśca maṅgale mokṣe saṃhartā na ca dṛśyate \|*  
*śivaśabdasya cānyo'rtho na hi vede nirūpitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. The meaning of the word Shiva is welfare or prosperity, besides salvation and destruction, there is no other meaning for the word Shiva. No other meaning has been given to the word Shiva even in the Vedas.

## \|\| 40.54 \|\|

*taṃ ca saṃhārakartāraṃ yadi vāñchasi sundari \|*  
*labhiṣyase rataṃ rudraṃ sarvalokabhayaṃkaram \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. O beautiful one, in case you are attractive towards the destroyer of all, then you will find yourself attracted towards the one who happens to be the terrific Rudra.

## \|\| 40.55-56 \|\|

*na bhaviṣyati mokṣaste svābhīṣṭaṃ devasevanam \|*  
*harismṛtiramoghā ca sarvamaṃgaladā sadā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śīghraṃ piturgṛhaṃ gaccha tatra drakṣyasi śaṃkaram \|*  
*mamāśiṣā svatapasāṃ phalena ca sudurlabham \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. You would therefore neither achieve moksa nor the desired husband. Reciting of the name of Hari never goes infructuous. The said name always bestowed welfare. Now you should at once go back to your father's house, with my blessing and as a reward of your tapas, you would achieve Shiva who is beyond the reach of all, there itself.

## \|\| 40.57 \|\|

*ityuktvā pārvatīṃ viprastatraivāntaradhīyata \|*  
*durgā yayau piturgehaṃ mahādeveti vādinī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Thus speaking, the Brahmana disappeared from there and Parvati reciting the name of Mahadeva went back to her parents, house.

## \|\| 40.58 \|\|

*pārvatyāgamanaṃ śrutvā menakā ca himālayaḥ \|*  
*divyaṃ yānaṃ puraskṛtya prayayau harṣavihvalaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Hearing about the arrival of Parvati both Mena and Himalaya were filled with delight and they moved towards the path, mounted on a divine plane.

## \|\| 40.59-60 \|\|

*saṃsthāpya maṃgalaghaṭānrājavartmani rādhike \|*  
*candanāgurukastūrīphalaśākhāsamanvitān \|\| 59 \|\|*

*paṭṭasūtrasannibaddharasālapallavānvitaiḥ \|*  
*paritaḥ parito rambhāstambhavṛndasamanvite \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. О Radhika, the royal road was sprinkled with sandal-paste, aguru, kasturi and decorated with fruits, branches and pitchers of welfare and further decorated with banners and flags beside the mango-leaves, tied in cords. The trunks of banana trees were also placed here and there for the purpose of decoration.

## \|\| 40.61 \|\|

*patiputravatīyoṣitsamūhairdīpahastakaiḥ \|*  
*pūrṇairlājādhānyadūrvāphalapuṣpasamanvitaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Some of the damsels whose sons and husbands were alive, holding lamps, fried paddy, Durva-grass, food and flowers in their hands moved forward to welcome Parvati.

## \|\| 40.62 \|\|

*supuṇyairbrāhmaṇaiścāpi munibhirbrahmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*naṭībhirnartakībhiśca gajendraiḥ pariśobhite \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On both sides of the road the noble Brahmanas, the sages, the Brahmacafis, the dancers and the elephants stood in attendance looking graceful.

## \|\| 40.63-64 \|\|

*purohitaiśca saṃyuktaiḥ kurvadbhirmaṅgaladhvanim \|*  
*sucārumālatīmālāhastaiḥ śastaiḥ praśaṃsitaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*nānāprakāravādyaiśca śaṃkhadhvanisunāditaiḥ \|*  
*sindūrareṇubhiścārucandanadravapaṅkilam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. The family priests holding garlands of jasmine flowers in their hands collectively recited the welfare sound. At that point of time various types of musical instrument were sounded, besides the blowing of conches. The vermilion and sandal-paste were mixed with water and it was sprinkled on the roads.

## \|\| 40.65 \|\|

*praviśya nagaraṃ durgā dadarśa pitarau puraḥ \|*  
*suprasannau pradhāvantau harṣāśrupulakānvitau \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. At the time of entering into the city, Durga came across her parents who were fully delighted and rushed towards her with the tears of joy flowing from their eyes.

## \|\| 40.66 \|\|

*prasannavadanā devī cālibhiḥ praṇanāma tau \|*  
*saṃyujyāthāśiṣaṃ tau ca cakratustāṃ ca vakṣasi \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The delightful goddess accompanied by her female friends offered salutation to her parents. Both of them collectively blessed her and embraced her.

## \|\| 40.67 \|\|

*he vatse vatsetyuccārya rudantau premavihvalau \|*  
*tadā tāṃ ca rathe kṛtvā jagmaturnijamandiram \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. They spoke, "О Daughter." Overwhelmed with love, they started sobbing. Then the made Durga to mount on the chariot and moved towards their home.

## \|\| 40.68 \|\|

*striyo nirmaṃcchanaṃ cakrurviprā yuyujurāśiṣam \|*  
*brāhmaṇebhyaśca bandibhyaḥ parvatendro dhanaṃ dadau \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. All the ladies welcomed Durga and the Brahmanas pronounced their blessing on her. The riches were distributed among the bards and the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 40.69 \|\|

*maṅgalaṃ kārayāmāsa pāṭhayāmāsa chāndasam \|*  
*evaṃ svakanyayā sārddhaṃ tasthatustau svamandire \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They performed the welfare ceremony and also arranged for the recitation of the Vedas. Then they lived in the palaces with the girl.

## \|\| 40.70-71 \|\|

*sukhena vasatau tau hi harṣanirbharamānasau \|*  
*ekadā ca tapaḥ kartuṃ jagāma svarṇadīṃ giriḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*menakākanyayā sārddhamuvāsa prāṅgaṇe mudā \|*  
*etasminnantare bhikṣurnartakaśca sugāyanaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. Filled with pleasure and spending time pleasantly, the king of the mountains once went to the bank of the Ganga for perfonning tapas. Mena was seated in the palace court-yard with Parvati. In the meantime a beggar arrived there who happened to be a dancer besides being a singer.

## \|\| 40.72 \|\|

*sahasaika ājagāma menakāsannidhiṃ mudā \|*  
*śṛṅgavādyaṃ vāmahaste ḍamaruṃ dakṣiṇe tathā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He pleasantly reached before Mena. He had a musical instrument of the horn in the left hand and a damaru in the right hand.

## \|\| 40.73 \|\|

*kṛtvā vibhūtigātro'tivṛddho'tīva jarāturaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhakantho raktavāsāḥ sukaṇṭho'timanoharaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He had applied ashes on his body. He looked pretty old and suffering from old age. He was clad in red garments and was carrying a bundle on his back. He had a beautiful neck and looked quite charming.

## \|\| 40.74-75 \|\|

*jagau mama guṇākhyānaṃ kṛtvā nṛtyaṃ manoharam \|*  
*vādayāmāsa śṛṅgaṃ ca kṣaṇaṃ ḍamarukaṃ tathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*ājagmurnāgarā bālā bālikā harṣavihvalāḥ \|*  
*vṛddhā yuvāno yuvatīsamūho vṛddhayoṣitaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. He while dancing recited my glory. Sometimes he blew the horn and sometimes he played on the damarii. Hearing that music and the songs all the boys, girl, old and young men and women besides the old ladies arrived there delightfully.

## \|\| 40.76 \|\|

*śrutvā tu sundaraṃ gītaṃ sutānasvarasaṃyutam \|*  
*sahasā mumuhuḥ sarve tena mūrcchāmavāpnuvan \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Listening to the charming song of the beggar which was in the sweet and the best tone, all the people were suddenly overpowered with illusion and they also fainted.

## \|\| 40.77 \|\|

*mūrchāṃ saṃprāpa sā durgā dadarśa hṛdi śaṅkaram \|*  
*triśūlapaṭṭiśakaraṃ vyāghracarmadharaṃ param \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Durga also fainted and she started visualising the form of Shiva who held a trident and pattisa in his hand and was clad in tiger skin.

## \|\| 40.78-83 \|\|

*vibhūtibhūṣaṇaṃ ramyamasthimālāṃ sunirmalām \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyaṃ suprasannaṃ trilocanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*mālāhastaṃ paṃcavaktraṃ nāgayajñopavītakam \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇvityuktavantaṃ sundaraṃ candraśekharam \|\| 79 \|\|*

*hṛdayasthaṃ haraṃ dṛṣṭvā manasā taṃ nanāma sā \|*  
*varaṃ vavre mānase sā tvaṃ patirme bhaveti ca \|\| 80 \|\|*

*evaṃ dattvā śivastasya cāntardhānaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*na dṛṣṭvā hṛdi taṃ durgā saṃprāpya cetanāṃ punaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*dadarśa cakṣurunmīlya bhikṣukaṃ gāyakaṃ puraḥ \|*  
*nṛtyasaṃgītataḥ sā tu bhikṣukasya ca menakā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*dātuṃ yayau sā ratnāni svarṇapātrasthitāni ca \|*  
*bhikṣāṃ yayāce bhikṣustāṃ durgāṃ nānyāṃ gṛhītavān \|\| 83 \|\|*

78-83. All his limbs were plastered with the ashes. He had a charming face and was wearing round his neck a garland of spotless bones. He wore a serene smile on his face, his appearance was indicative of his inner pleasure. He had five faces, each one of which had three eyes. He held a rosary in his hand, wore a yajnopavlta of serpent on his shoulder and a crescent crown on the forehead; he looked quite beautiful. He spoke to Parvati to ask for a boon. She bowed in reverence to lord Shiva mentally in her heart had asked for the boon, "You be my husband". Shiva said, "Be it so" and then he disappeared. Finding Shiva having disappeared from her heart, Durga regained her consciousness. When she opened her eyes she found the beggar singing there. Mena getting delighted with the song, dance and music of Shiva, went to him carrying the gold coins and gem in a plate in order to offer him but the beggar insisted on getting Durga alone as the offering and nothing else.

## \|\| 40.84 \|\|

*punaśca nartanaṃ kartumudyataḥ kautukena ca \|*  
*menā tadvacanaṃ śrutvā cukopa vismayaṃ yayau \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. When he again got ready to start his dance, Mena got enraged at his words and she was also surprised.

## \|\| 40.85-86 \|\|

*bhikṣukaṃ bhartsayāmāsa bahiḥ kartumuvāca tam \|*  
*patnī trilokanāthasya śivasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*yāñcāmimāṃ prakurvantaṃ dūraṃ kuru subhāṣiṇam \|*  
*etasminnantare taptvā giriḥ svālayamāyayau \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. She denounced the beggar and asked her people to turn him out saying, "Durga has to be the wife of Shiva who is the lord of the three worlds. The degraded beggar who is desirous of her should be turned out".

## \|\| 40.87-88 \|\|

*dadarśa purato bhikṣuṃ prāṅgaṇasthaṃ manoharam \|*  
*kṛtvā nārāyaṇārcāṃ ca gaṅgātīre manohare \|\| 87 \|\|*

*tanpūrtidhyānaviśleṣaśokādudvinamānasaḥ \|*  
*śratvā menāmukhādvātaṃ jahāsa ca cukopa saḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. At that point of time Himalaya the king of the mountain arrived home after performing tapas and, reaching the courtyard, he found the beggar there. He was meditating upon Narayana at the pleasant bank of the river Ganga but he was somehow disturbed in his meditation as a result of which his mind was upset. On hearing about the news from the mouth or Mena, he smiled and was enraged as well.

## \|\| 40.89 \|\|

*ājñāṃ cakāra svacaraṃ bahiḥ kartuṃ ca bhikṣukam \|*  
*ākāśāmiva duḥsparśaṃ prajvalantaṃ svatejasā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. He then commanded his messengers to turn out the beggar from that place. But It was difficult even to touch the beggar, like the sky. He was illumining with his lustre.

## \|\| 40.90-98 \|\|

*na śaśāka bahiḥ kartuṃ samīpaṃ gantumakṣamaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa bhikṣukaṃ śailaḥ kṣaṇaṃ cārucaturbhujam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ param \|*  
*suveṣaṃ sundaraśyāmamīṣaddhāsyaṃ manoharam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram \|*  
*yadyatpuṣpaṃ pradattaṃ ca pūjākāle gadābhṛte \|\| 92 \|\|*

*gātre śirasi tatsarvaṃ bhikṣukasya dadarśa ha \|*  
*dhūpaḥ pradīpo yo datto naivedyaṃ vā manoharam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*dadarśa śailastatsarvaṃ bhikṣukasya puraḥ sthitam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa dvibhujaṃ vinodamuralīkaram \|\| 94 \|\|*

*gopaveṣaṃ kiśoraṃ ca sasmitaṃ śyāmasundaram \|*  
*mayūrapicchacūḍaṃ ca ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa svacchaṃ ca śaṃkaraṃ caṃdraśekharam \|\| 96 \|\|*

*triśūlapaṭṭiśakaraṃ vyāghracarmāmbaraṃ param \|*  
*vibhūtigātramamalamasthimālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*nāgayajñopavītaṃ ca taptasvarṇajaṭādharam \|*  
*ḍamaruśṛṃgahastaṃ ca supraśastaṃ manoharam \|\| 98 \|\|*

90-98. Nobody could turn him out since no one could approach near him. Himavan then visualised in a moment that the beggar has taken to a beautiful form with four arms, having the kirita-сгсшп on his head, kundalas in his ears and was clad in the yellow lower garment. He had dark complexion which attracted the minds very much. His face had serene smile spread over it. All his limbs were plastered with sandal-paste and was getting anxious to bestow his grace on his devotees, all the flowers which Himavan had offered while performing the puja of Gadadhara, were all seen present on the body of the beggar. He also found the incense, the lamp and the pleasant naivedya which was offered by the lord of the mountain to lord Vishnu was also present there around him before the beggar, in the second moment. The same beggar took to the two-armed form. Holding a beautiful flute in his hand, he was is the form of a cowherd, in tender age, with a smiling face and a peacock feather fixed on his head. Adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments and the limbs pasted with the fragrant sandalwood-paste he was wearing the long garland of forest flowers. He appeared like Shri Krishna having the dark-complexioned body. He then found him again in the spotless form of Shiva, holding a trident and pattisha in his hand, clad in tiger skin having applied ashes on the body, wearing a garland of bones and the complexion of gold. He held a damaru and horn in his hands. He had an extremely pleasant appearance.

## \|\| 40.99-102 \|\|

*prajapantaṃ harernāma śvetābjabījamālayā \|*  
*īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyaṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram \|\| 99 \|\|*

*svatejasā prajvalantaṃ pañcavaktraṃ trilocanam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa jagatāṃ sraṣṭāraṃ ca caturmukham \|\| 100 \|\|*

*japantaṃ śrīharernāma svacchasphaṭikamālayā \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ sūrya svarūpaṃ ca dadarśa triguṇātmakam \|\| 101 \|\|*

*dadarśa tamatīvraṃ tu jvalantaṃ brahmatejasā \|*  
*kṣaṇamagnisvarūpaṃ ca jvalantamatitejasā \|\| 102 \|\|*

99-102. Holding a rosary of white lotuses, he was reciting the name of Hari and wearing a smile on his face, he appeared anxious and bestowed grace on his devotees. He had five faces, having three eyes on each one of them which had a dazzling lustre. In the next moment he found the beggar in the form of the four armed Brahma, the creator of the universe who was holding a white rosary and reciting the name of Hari. The next moment he found him in Trigunatmaka-swya, with the divine tejas illumining the universe. In the next moment he found him again in the form of the fire emitting immense fire flames.

## \|\| 40.103-105 \|\|

*kṣaṇamāhlādajanakaṃ candrarūpaṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ tejaḥsvarūpaṃ ca nirākāraṃ nirañjanam \|\| 103 \|\|*

*nirliptaṃ ca nirīhaṃ ca paramātmasvarūpiṇam \|*  
*evaṃ svecchāmayaṃ dṛṣṭvā nānārūpadharaṃ param \|\| 104 \|\|*

*harṣāśrupulakaḥ śailo daṇḍavatpraṇanāma tam \|*  
*bhaktyā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. The next moment he found him in the form of a moon who delighted all. In the next moment he found him in the form of tejas invisible, spotless, unattached and in the form of the great soul. Thus finding the beggar appearing in several forms, the eyes of Himalaya were filled with tears of joy. He felt overwhelmed. Finding the beggar taking to so many forms he then prostrated before him and with his mind filled with devotion, he went round him offering his salutations to him again and again.

## \|\| 40.106-108 \|\|

*samutpatya harṣayukto dadarśa punareva tam \|*  
*vāstavaṃ bhikṣukaṃ dṛṣṭvā śailendro viṣṇumāyayā \|\| 106 \|\|*

*visasmāra ca tatsarvaṃ nānārūpadharaṃ param \|*  
*bhikṣāṃ yayāce bhikṣustaṃ bhikṣāsthālīsvapārśvakam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*raktāmbaraḥ śṛṅgavādyavicitraḍamaruḥ kare \|*  
*ādātumutsuko durgāṃ nānyāṃ bhikṣuḥ kadācana \|\| 108 \|\|*

106-108. Thereafter jumping with delight, the king of the mountain, when the again looked at the beggar, he found that he was the beggar in reality. This was visualised by him, with the illusion of Vishnu. The king of the mountain forgot about everything about his taking to various forms. On the other hand the beggar demanded of alms from him, carrying the begging bowl with him. He was clad in red garments holding a horn and a typical type of damaru, he was only anxious to receive Durga as charity and nothing else.

## \|\| 40.109-111 \|\|

*na svīcakāra śailendro mohito viṣṇumāyayā \|*  
*bhikṣuḥ kiṃcinna jagrāha tatraivāntaradhīyata \|\| 109 \|\|*

*tadā babhūva jñānaṃ ca menakāśailayoḥ priye \|*  
*aho dṛṣṭo jagannātha āvābhyāṃ svapnavaddine \|\| 110\|\|*

*āvāṃ śivau vañcayitvā svasthānaṃ gatavānvibhuḥ \|*  
*tayorbhaktiṃ śive dṛṣṭvā sarve devāśca cintitāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

109-111. But influenced with the illusion of lord Vishnu, the king of the mountain did not accept his request. The beggar on his part refused to accept anything else and disappeared from the scene. О dear one, after the departure of the beggar both Mena and Himavan came to realise that Shiva the lord of the universe before them like a demon during the day but had disappeared finding them so much devoted towards Shiva. The gods then felt worried.

## \|\| 40.112-115 \|\|

*cakruḥ śakrādayo yuktiṃ sumero rakṣaṇe bharāt \|*  
*ekāntabhaktyā śailaścetkanyāṃ tasmai pradāsyati \|\| 112 \|\|*

*dhruvaṃ nirvāṇatāṃ sadyaḥ saṃprāpnotyeva bhārate \|*  
*anantaratnādhāraścetpṛthvī tyaktvā prayāsyati \|\| 113 \|\|*

*ratnagarbhābhidhā bhūmermithyaiva bhavitā dhruvam \|*  
*sthāvaratvaṃ parityajya divyarūpaṃ vidhāya saḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*kanyāṃ śūlabhṛte dattvā viṣṇulokaṃ gamiṣyati \|*  
*nārāyaṇasya sārūpyaṃ bhaviṣyatyeva līlayā \|\| 115 \|\|*

112-115. Then they started to device ways and means for the protection of Sumeru because of its weight. They started talking among themselves that in case Himalaya with his utmost devotion would offer his daughter to Shiva then he would surely achieve nirvana as well as moksa. In case Himalaya which is the abode of several gems, disappeared from the land of Bharata then the name of the earth as Ratnagarbha possessing the gems or in her womb Vasundhara would become false. Because by offering his daughter to Shiva, he discarding his pleasant form would achieve the divine form and then Himalaya would achieve Vishnuloka. Reaching there, he would achieve the SarUpya moksa of lord Vishnu without any effort.

## \|\| 40.116 \|\|

*saṃprāpya pārṣadatvaṃ ca haridāso bhaviṣyati \|*  
*daśavāpīsamā kanyā dīyate brāhmaṇāya tām \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Thereafter they would achieve the place of a courtier and then would become slaves of lord Vishnu. By offering a daughter to a Brahmana, one achieved merit of constructing ten step wells.

## \|\| 40.117-122 \|\|

*vedajñāya pavitrāya cāpratigrahaśāline \|*  
*saṃdhyāyajñavedapāṭhakāriṇe satyavādine \|\| 117 \|\|*

*asyai pradattā kanyā ca daśavāpīphalapradā \|*  
*trisaṃdhyākāriṇe satyavādine gṛhaśāline \|\| 118 \|\|*

*vedajñāya suviprāya dattvā suphaladāyinī \|*  
*paradāragṛhītāya yājakāya dvijātaye \|\| 119 \|\|*

*śaṭhāya saṃdhyāhīnāya vāpyaikaphaladā sutā \|*  
*sarvasaṃdhyāsvagāyatrīvihīnāya śaṭhāya ca \|\| 120\|\|*

*vaiśyodbhavāya dattā yā vāpyarddhaphaladā smṛtā \|*  
*pāpine śūdrajātāya viprakṣatrodbhavāya ca \|\| 121 \|\|*

*dattvā cāṇḍālatulyāya kanyā sā narakapradā \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktāya viduṣe viprāya satyavādine \|\| 122 \|\|*

117-122. In case the daughter is given to such a person who is well-versed in the Vedas, having the noble character the one who does not accept charity, who performs always sandhya, yajna and the reciting of the Vedas regularly, the one who is truthful, the father achieves the merit of digging ten step wells. The one who gives away his daughter to a Brahmana who performs the sandhya, thrice a day, is truthful, householder, well-versed in the Vedas and gives away his daughter to such a person. By performing charity he becomes successful, the one who accepts charity is devoid of performing of sandhya and is a fool, the giver gets half the merit. The Brahmana, who accepts the wife of others, the one who performed yajna the wicked is devoid of the performing of sandhya and in case a daughter is given to him one achieved the merit of the digging of a single step-well. In case, a daughter is given to a Brahmana who is deprived of the sandhya of three types and the Gayatri mantra, is wicked and is born of a Vaisya, the donor gets the merit of constructing half a step-well. A Brahmana who is a sinner, born of Shudra women or the one who is born of Brahmana and Kshatriya or the one who is like Chandala and if a girl given to him, the donor falls into the hell.

## \|\| 40.123-126 \|\|

*jitendriyāya dattā yā viṃśadvāpīphalapradā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭi varṣasahasrāṇi divyarūpaṃ vidhāya ca \|\| 123 \|\|*

*evaṃbhūtāya dattā cenmodate viṣṇumaṃdire \|*  
*dattvā kanyāṃ suśīlāṃ ca harāya haraye'tha vā \|\| 124 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇasvarūpaṃ ca bhavedeva śrutau śrutam \|*  
*viṣṇubhakto yadā kanyāṃ dadāti viṣṇuprītaye \|\| 125 \|\|*

*sa labheddharidāsyaṃ ca dhruvaṃ viprodbhavāya ca \|*  
*ityālocya surāḥ sarve kṛtvā ca mantraṇāṃ priye \|\| 126 \|\|*

123-126. If a girl is given to a Brahmana who is devoted to Vishnu, is intelligent, truthful and the one who has controlled all his senses, the donor earns the merit of constmcting twenty step wells. He then takes to the divine form for sixty thousand years and the donor enjoys all the pleasures in the abode of Vishnu. By giving away the daughter to Vishnu or Shiva, the donor achieves the form of Narayana. This has been ordained in the Vedas. When a devotee of Vishnu offer a daughter in marriage to a Brahmana for the pleasure of Vis nu, he surely achieves the slavehood of lord Vis nu.

## \|\| 40.127-128 \|\|

*guruṃ prasthāpituṃ jagmurhimālayagṛhaṃ prati \|*  
*gatvā praṇamya ca guruṃ sarve cakrurnivedanam \|\| 127 \|\|*

*himālayagṛhaṃ gatvā kuru nindāṃ ca śūlinaḥ \|*  
*pinākinaṃ vinā durgā varaṃ nānyaṃ variṣyati \|\| 128 \|\|*

127-128. О beloved, thus thinking all the gods consulted among themselves and intended depute Brihaspati to the abode of Himalaya they went to Brihaspati to depute him for the purpose. All the gods went to Brihaspati and offering their salutation to him said,

## \|\| 40.129 \|\|

*anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā phalaṃ tūrṇaṃ labhiṣyati \|*  
*kālena yātu śailendraścedānīṃ bhuvi tiṣṭhatu \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. "You go to the place of Himavan and denounce Shiva because except Shiva, Durga is not going to marry anyone else.

## \|\| 40.130-132 \|\|

*anantaratnādhāraṃ ca tvameva rakṣa bhārate \|*  
*devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pradadau karṇayoḥ karau \|\| 130\|\|*

*na svīcakāra svaguruḥ smarannārāyaṇeti ca \|*  
*uvāca devavargāṃśca saṃbhartsya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

*vedavedāntavijñātā mahābhakto harau hare \|*  
*bṛhaspatiruvāca \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ madvacaḥ satyaṃ he devāḥ svārthasādhakāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

130-132. In that case, Himavan would give away his daughter to Shiva unmindfully and if he does so he would achieve the complete merit of giving away the daughter in charity. In due course of time, the lord of the mountains could be free and achieve salvation but presently he has to remain on earth, you go and arrange for the stay of Himalaya permanently on the land of Bharata. Listening to the words of the gods, Brihaspati touched his ears with both the hands declining the offer and, reciting the name of Narayana, he refused to oblige them. Brihaspati who was quite well-versed in the Vedas besides being the devotee of Vishnu and Shiva denounced the gods repeatedly and said.

## \|\| 40.133-138 \|\|

*nītisāraṃ ca vedoktaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham \|*  
*harakeśavayorbhaktaṃ ye ca nindanti pāpinaḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

*bhūdevānbrāhmaṇāṃścaiva svaguruṃ ca pativratāḥ \|*  
*patibhikṣubrahmacārisṛṣṭibījānsurāṃstathā \|\| 134 \|\|*

*pacyante kālasūtre te yāvaccandradivākarau \|*  
*śleṣmamūtrapurīṣeṣu śerate te divāniśam \|\| 135 \|\|*

*bhakṣitāḥ kīṭanikaraiḥ śabdaṃ kurvaṃti kātarāḥ \|*  
*ye nindanti ca brahmāṇaṃ sraṣṭāraṃ jagatāṃ gurum \|\| 136 \|\|*

*śivaṃ surāṇāṃ pravaraṃ durgāṃ lakṣmīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*gītāṃ ca tulasīṃ gaṅgāṃ vedāṃśca vedamātaram \|\| 137 \|\|*

*vrataṃ tapasyāṃ pūjāṃ ca mantraṃ maṃtrapradaṃ gurum \|*  
*te pacyante'ndhakūpe vai cāyuṣo'rdhaṃ vidheraho \|\| 138 \|\|*

133-138. Brihaspati said – О selfish gods, a you listen to my truthful words which are a gist of polity, according to the Vedas and would result in pleasure. Such of the sinners who denounce Shiva or Vishnu or their devotees, the Brahmanas on earth, their own teacher, the chaste ladies, the noble husbands, the beggars. Brahmacaris and the gods who happen to be the seed of the universe, they fall into the kalasUtra hell and remain there till the land of the world. They have to consume there vomit refuse and urine daily. They are bitten by the crores of insects daily which makes them cry aloud. Those who denounce the creator of the universe and teacher of Brahma, Shiva, the best of the gods, Durga, Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Gita, Tulasi, Ganga, Vedas, Savitri, Vratas, Tapas, Adoration, Mantra and the Guru who give the mantra, they fall into the andhakupa hell and remain there till the life of Brahma.

## \|\| 40.139-142 \|\|

*bhakṣitāḥ sarpasaṃghaiśca śabdaṃ kurvanti saṃtatam \|*  
*ye nindanti hṛṣīkeśaṃ devasāmyaṃ vidhāya ca \|\| 139 \|\|*

*viṣṇubhaktipradaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ ca śruteḥ param \|*  
*rādhā tadaṅgajā gopī brāhmaṇāṃśca sadārcitān \|\| 140\|\|*

*te pacyante'vaṭe devā vidhāturāyuṣā samam \|*  
*adhomukhā ūrdhvajaṅghāḥ sarpasaṃghaiśca veṣṭitāḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

*bhakṣitā vikṛtākāraiḥ kīṭaiḥ sarpasamākṛtaiḥ \|*  
*atīva kātarā bhītāḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti saṃtatam \|\| 142 \|\|*

139-142. Groups of snakes eat them up, as a result of which they cry aloud always. Such of the people who compare lord Madhusudana with other gods and also denounce him such of the people who find fault with the Puranas which bestow the devotion of Vishnu or whatever is treated to be the Vedas and find fault with them, denounce Radha and the cowherdesses who actually are her forms denounce adorable Brahmanas, even they have to fall into the hell till the life of Brahma. They are hanged with their heads placed upside down and the legs are raised up. The serpents with different deformities and other insects like the serpents bite all their limbs and they getting terrified cry aloud.

## \|\| 40.143 \|\|

*śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇi dhruvaṃ bhakṣanti kṣobhitāḥ \|*  
*ulkāṃ dadati ruṣṭāśca tanmukhe yamakiṃkarāḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. They have to consume the vomit, urine and refuse and have to face the unkind messengers of Yama who place burning rods in their mouths.

## \|\| 40.144 \|\|

*trisandhyaṃ tarjanaṃ kṛtvā kurvanti daṇḍatāḍanam \|*  
*kurvanti mūtrapānaṃ ca prahāraistṛṣitānbhiyā \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. They torture them thrice a day beating them with rods and when they feel thirsty, they have to consume only urine.

## \|\| 40.145 \|\|

*tadā kalpāntare sraṣṭuṃ sṛṣṭiṃ ca prathame punaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhavetpratīkāra ityāha kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. In the other kalpas their sins are pardoned. This has been ordained by Brahma.

## \|\| 40.146 \|\|

*kṛtvā hi śivanindāṃ ca yāsyanti narakaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*imamevopakāraṃ ca kartumicchatha putrakāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. By denouncing Shiva, all the gods would be thrown into the hell. О sons, is it not good whatever you want to do.

## \|\| 40.147 \|\|

*brahmaṇā prerito dakṣo dattvā śūlabhṛte sutām \|*  
*na pāpaṃ paramaiśvaryaṃ saṃprāpa haranindakaḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. With the inspiration of Brahma, Daksha gave away his daughter to Shiva. Because of this he could not earn a sin even after denouncing him. On the other hand he achieved all the fortunes.

## \|\| 40.148 \|\|

*anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā turyapuṇyaṃ lalābha saḥ \|*  
*aho vihāya sārūpyaṃ tucchaṃ svargaṃ lalābha saḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. Of course it happened to be like this that he achieved only one fourth of the merit because he gave away his daughter to Shiva unwillingly, therefore he could not achieve salvation but could achieve only heaven.

## \|\| 40.149-150 \|\|

*kaścinmadhye ca yuṣmākaṃ gatvā śailagṛhaṃ surāḥ \|*  
*saṃpādayatu svamataṃ śailendrasya prayatnataḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

*anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā sukhaṃ tiṣṭhatu bhārate \|*  
*tasmai bhaktyā sutāṃ dattvā mokṣaṃ prāpsyati niścitam \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. О gods, someone from you should go to the house of the king of mountains and with considerable efforts you should act according to wisdom. By offering his daughter in marriage to Shiva unwillingly, Himalaya can remain in Bharata but in case he offers his daughter with devotion then he would surely achieve the merit and the moksa.

## \|\| 40.151-153 \|\|

*paścātsaptarṣayaḥ sarve gṛhītvā tāmarundhatīm \|*  
*dhruvaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ gatvā bodhayiṣyanti parvatam \|\| 151 \|\|*

*vinā pinākinaṃ durgā varaṃ nānyaṃ variṣyati \|*  
*anicchayā sutāṃ tasmai pradāsyati sutājñayā \|\| 152 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ devā gacchantu mandiram \|*  
*ityuktvā vākpatiḥ śīghraṃ tapase svarṇadīṃ gataḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

151-153. Thereafter, developing discard Saptarsis together with Arundhatl will go to the abode of Himalaya and try to convince him. Durga on the other hand, would never accept anyone else as her husband without Shiva. In that case at the insistence of his daughter, Himalaya would surely gave away in marriage his daughter to Shiva. Thus I have spoken everything to you. All other gods should revert to their respective abodes. Thus speaking Brihaspati left for the bank of the Ganga for performing tapas.

## Chapter 41

## \|\| 41.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*tadā devāḥ samālocya jagmuste brahmaṇo'ntikam \|*
