*brahmāṇḍeṣu ca sarveṣu maryādā sthāpitā mayā \|*  
*tayā karma prakurvanti munayaśca surā narāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. In all the Brahmandas I have prescribed the decorum by which the sages, the gods and the humans perform the actions.

## \|\| 69.85-86 \|\|

*sudāmaśāpādvicchedaḥ śatavarṣamanīpsitaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyatyeva daṃpatyorāvayoreva sundari \|\| 85 \|\|*

*bhedo jāgaraṇe'syāśca mayā saha sumadhyame \|*  
*saṃśleṣaḥ saṃtataṃ svapne madvareṇa bhaviṣyati \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. O beautiful one, we are going to face separation for a hundred years because of the curse of Sudama though it is not desired by either of us, but О slender waisted, one because of my boon, she will get separated from me only when she is awake but when in sleep she would always be united with me.

## \|\| 69.87 \|\|

*ādhyātmikī mayā dattā śokacchedo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*rādhāṃ bodhaya bhadraṃ te yāsyāmi nandamandiram \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. I have already bestowed on her the divine knowledge as a result of which the grief would disappear. Therefore, you wake up Radha, you will meet with all the welfare. I shall now go to the abode of Nanda.

## \|\| 69.88 \|\|

*ityuktvā jagatāṃ nātho yayau nandālayaṃ prati \|*  
*rādhikāṃ bodhayāmāsurālisaṃghāśca nārada \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. О Narada, thus speaking lord Krishna went to the abode of Nanda and the group of cowherdesses woke up Radha.

## \|\| 69.89 \|\|

*gatvā gṛhaṃ ca pitaraṃ nanāma mātaraṃ tathā \|*  
*cakāra mātā kroḍe ca navanītaṃ ca nūtanam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Reaching home Krishna offered his salutation to his parents; thereafter the mother took Krishna in his lap and offered him the fresh butter.

## \|\| 69.90 \|\|

*mātṛdattaṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ cakhāda śītalaṃ jalam \|*  
*uvāsa tatra jagatāṃ nātho mātṛsamīpataḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The mother then offered him the cool water and the betel, consuming which Shri Krishna dwelt in this house of the mother.

## \|\| 69.91 \|\|

*sarvairgopasamūhaiśca sevitaḥ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*mālyacandanatāmbūlaṃ te ca tasmai dadurmudā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. All the Gopas offered him delightfully the garlands, sandal-paste and the betels, serving him with the white fly-whisks.

## Chapter 70

## \|\| 70.1-7 \|\|

*atha saptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca athākrūraḥ svaśaraṇaṃ gatvā kaṃsena preṣitaḥ \|*  
*cakāra śayanaṃ talpe bhuktvā mīṣṭānnamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sakarpūraṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ cakhāda vāsitaṃ jalam \|*  
*jagāma nidrāṃ sukhataḥ sukhasaṃbhogamātrataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tato dadarśa susvapnaṃ purāṇaśrutisaṃmatam \|*  
*niśāvaśeṣasamaye bādhādiparivarjitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*arogī baddhakeśaśca vastrayugmasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*sutalpaśāyī susnigdhaścintāśokavivarjitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kiśoravayasaṃ śyāmaṃ dvibhujaṃ muralīdharam \|*  
*pītavastraparīdhānaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ mālatīmālyaśobhitam \|*  
*bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣaṇārhaṃ ca sadratnamaṇibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mayūrapicchacūḍaṃ ca sasmitaṃ padmalocanam \|*  
*evaṃbhūtaṃ dvicaśiśuṃ dadarśa prathamaṃ mune \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Narayana said – Thereafter Akrura who was dispatched by Karhsa, went to his abode and took food including sweets mixed with camphor, scented betel and fragrant water and comfortably slept on the bed. Towards the end of the night, he witnessed a dream which was described in the Vedas and the Puranas. He found that the Brahmana boy who was quite healthy, his hair tied in a knot, clad in two garments was sleeping on the bed. He had a beautiful complexion and his face was devoid of any worry or grief. He was in tender age, having a dark complexion and two hands, holding a flute in hand, clad in pltambara, adorned with a garland of forest flowers, having the body plastered with sandal-paste, wearing the garland of jasmine flowers, adorned with the best of the ornaments studded with gems, having peacock feathers on his head, wearing a serene smile on the face and having the eyes like lotus flowers. О sage, he witnessed that beautiful boy in his dream for the first time.

## \|\| 70.8-9 \|\|

*tato dadarśa rucirāṃ patiputravatīṃ satīm \|*  
*pītavastraparīdhānāṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jvalatpradīpahastāṃ ca śukladhānyakarāṃ varām \|*  
*śaraccandranibhāsyāṃ ca sasmitāṃ varadāṃ śubhāma \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Thereafter he saw a chaste lady whose husband and son were alive. She was clad in yellow garments adorned with the ornament of gems, holding a burning lamp in one hand and white paddy in the other. She had beautiful limbs and the face was like that of the beautiful moon of the winter season. She was wearing a serene smile on her face and was anxious to shower a boon.

## \|\| 70.10 \|\|

*tato dadarśa vipraṃ ca prakurvantaṃ śubhāśiṣam \|*  
*śvetapadmagataṃ haṃsaṃ turagaṃ ca sarovaram \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereafter pronouncing a blessing she looked at the Brahmana together with the goose on the white lotus besides a horse and a pool.

## \|\| 70.11 \|\|

*dadarśa citritaṃ cāru phalitaṃ puṣpitaṃ śubham \|*  
*āmranimbanārikelagurvarkakadalītarum \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He also witnessed trees blossoming with flowers and fruits, beautiful and auspicious trees of mango, neem, coconut, a huge sun-tree and a plantain tree.

## \|\| 70.12 \|\|

*daśantaṃ śvetasarpaṃ ca svātmānaṃ parvatasthitam \|*  
*vṛkṣasthaṃ ca gajasthaṃ ca taristhaṃ turagasthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He found himself having been bitten by a white serpent and also found himself seated on a mountain, a tree, an elephant, as a boat and himself mounted on the horse.

## \|\| 70.13-15 \|\|

*vīṇāṃ vāditavantaṃ ca bhuktavantaṃ ca pāyasam \|*  
*dadhikṣīrayutānnaṃ ca padmapatrasthamīpsitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṛmiviṭsahitāṅgaṃ ca rudantaṃ mohitaṃ tadā \|*  
*śukladhānyapuṣpakaraṃ kṣaṇaṃ candanacarcitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prāsādasthaṃ samudrasthamātmānaṃ ca salohitam \|*  
*chinnabhinnaṃ kṣatāṅgaṃ ca medapūyasamanvitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Thereafter he found himself playing vlna and consuming milk with rice, -food with curd and milk placed on the lotus leaves. He witnessed that his limbs had become dirty because of insects and dirt. He then found himself crying infatuated with illusion, then carrying the flowers and white paddy in his hands. In a moment his body was plastered with sandal-paste, in a moment he found himself seated on a roof, in the ocean filled with blood, with his wounded limbs and filled himself with blood and puss.

## \|\| 70.16-19 \|\|

*tato dadarśa rajataṃ maṇiṃ śubhraṃ ca kāñcanam \|*  
*suktāmāṇikyaratnaṃ ca pūrṇakumbhajalaṃ śubham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*surabhiṃ ca savatsāṃ ca vṛṣabhendraṃ mayūrakam \|*  
*śukaṃ ca sārasaṃ haṃsaṃ cillaṃ khañjanameva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tāmbūlaṃ puṣpamālyaṃ ca jvaladagniṃ surārcanam \|*  
*pārvatīpratimāṃ kṛṣṇapratimāṃ śivaliṅgakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*viprabālāṃ ca bālaṃ ca supakvaphalitāṃ kṛṣim \|*  
*devasthalīṃ ca rājendraṃ siṃhaṃ vyāghraṃ guruṃ suram \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. He then found the silver, the gems, gold, finger rings, jewels, gems, welfare pitcher filled with water, cow with calves, the big bull, the peacock, parrot, crane, kite, wagtail bird, betel, garland of flowers, fire in flames, adoration of gods, the image of Parvati and of Krishna, Shivalinga, Brahmana's daughter, a child, the ripened crops, the temple, the king, the lion, the tiger, the teacher and the gods.

## \|\| 70.20 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā svapnaṃ samuttasthau cakārā''hnikamīpsitam \|*  
*uddhavaṃ kathayāmāsa sarvaṃ vṛttāntameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Thus after witnessing the dream he performed his daily routine and then narrated the entire dream to Uddhava.

## \|\| 70.21-28 \|\|

*uddhavājñāṃ samādāya kṛtvā gurusurārcanam \|*  
*yātrāṃ cakāra śrīkṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā manasi nārada \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dadarśa vartmanyevaṃ ca maṅgalārhaṃ śubhapradam \|*  
*vāñchāphalapradaṃ ramyaṃ puro maṅgalasūcakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vāme śaivaṃ śivāṃ pūrṇakumbhaṃ nakulacāṣakam \|*  
*patiputravatīṃ sādhvīṃ divyābharaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śuklapuṣpaṃ ca mālyaṃ ca dhānyaṃ ca khañjanaṃ śubham \|*  
*dakṣiṇe jvaladagriṃ ca vipraṃ ca vṛṣabhaṃ gajam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vatsaprayuktāṃ dheruṃ ca śvetāśvaṃ rājahaṃsakam \|*  
*veśyāṃ ca puṣpamālāṃ ca patākāṃ dadhi pāyasam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*maṇiṃ suvarṇa racataṃ muktāmāṇikyamīpsitam \|*  
*madyaṃ māṃkaṃ candanaṃ ca mādhvīkaṃ ghṛtamuttamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇaśāraṃ phalaṃ lājāḥ siddhānnaṃ darpaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*vicitritaṃ vimānaṃ ca sudīptāṃ pratimāṃ tathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śuklotpalaṃ padmavanaṃ śaṅkhacillaṃ ca kīrakam \|*  
*mārjāraṃ parvataṃ meghaṃ mayūraṃ śukasārasam \|\| 28 \|\|*

21-28. О Narada, getting permission from Uddhava, adorning his teacher and the gods, with his mind set at the feet of lord Krishna, he travelled to the abode of Krishna. At the time of tlie start of his journey, he met with various auspicious symbols which bestowed welfare. He found the he-jackal and she-jackal on his left, a vase filled with water, the mangoos, Nllakantha bird, a beautiful chaste woman adorned with divine ornaments whose husband and son were alive, white flowers, garland of flowers, fried paddy, a wagtail bird. On the right side he met with the burning fire fames, a Brahmana, a bull, an elephant, a cow with calf, a white horse, a goose, a garland of flower, the flag, gem, gold, silver, pearls, ruby, wine, flesh, sandal, wine of Bassia latifolia trees, ghee, black deer skin, fruit, fried paddy, mirror, painted plane, beautiful image, a white lotus flower, a forest of lotus flowers, Samkha, kite, cat, mountain, clouds, peacock, parrot and crane.

## \|\| 70.29-30 \|\|

*śaṅkhakokilavādyānāṃ dhvaniṃ śuśrāva maṅgalam \|*  
*vicitrakṛṣṇasaṃgītaṃ hariśabdaṃ jayadhvanim \|\| 29 \|\|*

*evaṃbhūtaṃ śubhaṃ dṛṣṭavā śrutvā prahṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*praviveśa hariṃ smṛtvā puṇyaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ vanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Thereafter he met with snake, cuckoo, welfare sound of the musical instruments, recital of the music of Krishna, reciting of the name of Hari and sound of victory. Thus witnessing the auspicious symbols and hearing of auspicious sound, Akrura delightfully remembered the name of the lord and entered Vmdavana.

## \|\| 70.31-33 \|\|

*dadarśa purato ramyaṃ rāsamaṇḍalamīpsitam \|*  
*candanāgurukastūrīpuṣpacandanavāyunā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*vāsitaṃ maṅgalaghaṭai rambhāstamabhairvirājitam \|*  
*āmrapallavasaṃghaiśca paṭṭasūtravicitritaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śobhitaiḥ paritaḥ śaśvatpadmarāgavinirmitam \|*  
*śobhitaṃ śobhanārhaṃ ca trikoṭiratnamandiraiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. He found there the desirable Rasamandala which was quite pleasant and was decorated with sandal-paste, aguru, kasturl, flowers and where the fragrant cool breeze was blowing. It had several welfare pitchers, trunks of banana tree, tender leaves of the mango trees tied to a cord and spread everywhere. The place was decorated with several gems and three crores of beautiful diamonds, studded in the temple and a hundred crores of charming kunja-cottages. Looking at the divine dance he walked in Vmdavana up to a distance.

## \|\| 70.34-38 \|\|

*ramyaiḥ kuñjakuṭīraiśca rājitaṃ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*rāsaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ dṛṣṭvā kiyaddūraṃ yayau ca saḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dadarśa purato ramyaṃ nandavrajamanuttamam \|*  
*paraṃ vekuṇṭhasaṃkāśaṃ vaikuṇṭha nilayaṃ śubham \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ratnasopānasaṃyuktaṃ ratnastambhairvirājitam \|*  
*nānācitravicitrāḍhyaṃ sadratnavalayānvitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*khacitaṃ maṇisāreṇa racitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*dvāri dṛṣṭena mārgeṇa rājadvāraṃ viveśa saḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*patākāratnajālāḍhyaṃ suktāmāṇikyabhūṣitam \|*  
*ratnadarpaṇaśobhāḍhyaṃ ratnacitravicitritam \|\| 38 \|\|*

34-38. Thereafter he came across the beautiful and charming Vraja of Nanda. It was quite charming like Vaikuntha, having many beautiful houses and steps besides the pillars which were decorated with various types of creepers and gems; it was built by Vishvakarma, using the best of gems. By the visible road he entered the royal gate, having a number of banners and decorated with a large number of gems. It was decorated with pearls and rubies beside the mirrors made of the gems; if had a number of marigala kalashas made of gems.

## \|\| 70.39-42 \|\|

*ratnavithīviracitaṃ maṅgalaṃ maṅgarairghaṭaiḥ \|*  
*akrūrāgamanaṃ śrutvā sāṅlādo nanda eva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sahito rāmakṛṣṇābhyāṃ jagāmānuvrajāya vai \|*  
*vṛṣabhānvādibhiryuktaḥ kṛtvā veśyāṃ puraḥsaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pūrṇakumbhaṃ gajendraṃ ca kṛtvā'gre śukladhānyakam \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṃ gāṃ madhuparkaṃ ca pādyaṃ ratnāsanādikam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gṛhītvā sādaraḥ śāntaḥ sasmito vinatasthā \|*  
*ānandayukto nandaśca sagaṇaḥ sahabālakaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

39-42. When Nanda came to know about the arrival of Akriira he was immensely delighted. Accompanied by Balarama and Krishna, he went to welcome him. Vrsabhanu and other cowherds and dancers were moving ahead. Placing the pitchers filled with water and the elephant to the fore besides black cow, they could with them madhuparka, padya, the asanas of gems. Nanda went to him with a delightful and humble face. The boys and the servants then saw the virtuous Akrura there. He was immediately embraced and all the cowherds offered their salutation to him bowing their heads on the feat of Akrura who blessed them all.

## \|\| 70.43-45 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā'krūraṃ mahābhāgaṃ tūrṇamāliṅganaṃ dadau \|*  
*praṇemuḥ śiramā sarvai gopā jagṛhurāśiṣam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*parasparaṃ ca saṃyogo babhūva guṇatrānmune \|*  
*kroḍe cakārākrūraśca kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ krameṇa ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

*cucumba gaṇḍayugule pulakāñyitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*sāśrunetro'tisāhlādaḥ kṛtārthaḥ siddhavāñchitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. О sage, thus all the people were united together. Akrura lifted up Krishna and Balarama in his lap and was overwhelmed with emotion, feeling blissful and tears started flowing from his eyes. He felt gratified and since he was successful in his mission he kissed their tender cheeks.

## \|\| 70.46-47 \|\|

*dadarśa kṛṣṇaṃ dvibhujaṃ kṣaṇaṃ śyāmalasundaram \|*  
*pītavastraparīdhānaṃ mālatīmālyabhūṣitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*candanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ paraṃ vaṃśīdharaṃ varam \|*  
*stutaṃ brahmeśaśeṣādyairmunīndraiḥ sanakādibhiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. At that point of time, he found Krishna having two arms clad in yellow garment, adorned with the jasmine flowers with the sandal-paste having been applied on his limbs, holding a flute in his hand. Brahma, Shiva, Shesha and other gods including the sages like Sanaka and others were offering prayers to him. The girls of the cowherds v/ere staring at him continuously.

## \|\| 70.48-49 \|\|

*vīkṣitaṃ gopakanyābhiḥ paribūrṇatamaṃ vibhum \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa kroḍasthaṃ sasmitaṃ ca caturbhujam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*lakṣmīṃsarasvatīyuktaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|*  
*sunandanandakumudaiḥ pārṣadaiḥ parisevitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The next moment he found the lord in the lap of Akrura with four arms wearing a smile on his face surrounded by Lakshmi and Sarasvati, adorned with the garland of forest flowers and flanked by the courtiers like Sunanda, Nanda and Kumuda. Many of the devotees and siddhas were serving him.

## \|\| 70.50-51 \|\|

*sevitaṃ siddhasaṃghaiśca bhaktinamraiḥ parātparam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ dadarśa devaṃ taṃ pañcavaktraṃ trilocanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ nāgarājairvirājitam \|*  
*digambaraṃ paraṃ brahma bhasmāṅgaṃ ca jaṭāyutam \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. In the next moment they found him with five faces, three eyes, having the complexion of spotless crystal gems, adorned with Nagas, without robes, like eternal Brahma and with the ashes applied on his body. He had the matted locks of hair on his head and was holding a rosary in his hand like a yogi.

## \|\| 70.52 \|\|

*japamālākaraṃ dhyānaniṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ca yoginam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ caturmukhaṃ dhyānaniṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ manīṣiṇām \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. In the next moment they found him in the form of Brahma who was engaged in meditation.

## \|\| 70.53 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ dharmasvarūpaṃ ca śeṣarupaṃ kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇam \|*  
*kṣaṇaṃ bhāskararūpaṃ ca jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. In another moment, he was found in the form of Dharma and in another moment he was found in the form of Shesha, in another moment he was found in the form of eternal flame or the sun.

## \|\| 70.54 \|\|

*kṣaṇaṃ paramaśobhāḍhyaṃ koṭikandarpaninditam \|*  
*kāminīkamanīyaṃ ca kāmukaṃ kāmasaṃyutam \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Again he was found in extremely graceful form, which put the lustre of the moon to shame crores of beautiful gods of love. He was loved by innumerable damsels, quite passionate and filled with passion. Finding such a type of boy, Akrura embraced him.

## \|\| 70.55-56 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtaṃ śiśuṃ dṛṣṭvā sthāpayāmāsa vakṣasi \|*  
*ratnamiṃhāsane ramye nandadatte ca nārada \|\| 55 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ bhaktyā pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya śirasā bhūmau tuṣṭāva puruṣottamam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. О Narada, then Akrura placed the boy on the gem-studded lion-throne, offered to him by Nanda and with his mind filled with devotion, he went round the lord and then offered his salutation to him placing his head on the ground.

## \|\| 70.57-60 \|\|

*akrūra uvāca namaḥ kāraṇarūpāya paramātmasvarūpiṇe sarveṣāmapi viśvānāmīśvarāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*parāya prakṛterīśa parātparatarāya ca \|\| 57 \|\|*

*nirguṇāya nirīhāya nīrūpāya svarūpiṇe \|*  
*sarvadevasvarūpāya sarvadeveśvarāya ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

*sarvadevādhidevāya viśvādibhūtarūpiṇe \|*  
*asaṃśyeṣu ca viśveṣu brahmaviṣṇuśivātmaka \|\| 59 \|\|*

*svarūpāyā''dibījāya tadīśaviśvarūpiṇe \|*  
*namo gopāṅganeśāya gaṇeśeśvararūpiṇe \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. Akrura said – You are the form of cause, form of the lord I offer my salutation to you. You are the lord of all the globes and I offer my salutation to you, the one who is beyond Prakriti and also the lord, is without qualities, unattached, without form, with form, the form of all the gods, the lord of all the gods, the only supreme god of all the gods, the beginning of the universe, Brahma in innumerable globes beside being Vishnu and Shiva, you are the seed of all the form. You are the lord of the universe, the lord of the cowherdesses and lord of all the Gangs, I offer my salutation to you.

## \|\| 70.61-64 \|\|

*namaḥ suragaṇeśāya rādheśāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*rādhāramaṇarūpāya rādhārūpadharāya ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

*rādhārādhyāya rādhāyāḥ prāṇādhikatarāya ca \|*  
*rādhāsādhyāya rādhādhidevapriyatamāya ca \|\| 62 \|\|*

*rādhāprāṇādhidevāya viśvarūpāya te namaḥ \|*  
*vedastutātmavedajñarūpiṇe sarvavedine \|\| 63 \|\|*

*vaidādhiṣṭhātṛdevāya vedabījāya te namaḥ \|*  
*yasya lomasu viśvāni cāsaṃkhyāni ca nityaśaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. You are the lord of all the gods I offer my salutation to you. You are the lord of Radha, I offer my salutation to you. You are husband of Radha I offer my salutation to you. I offer my salutation to the one who takes to the form of Radha, you are adorable by Radha, you are dearer to Radha than her life, you are adored by Radha. You are the only god of Radha and her beloved, the life of Radha, salutation to you. You are the one who is adored by the Vedas, you are all knowledgeable and the sole god of the Vedas being the seed of the Vedas. I offer my salutation to you, in the hair pits of whom always innumerable globes are enshrined, I offer my salutation to him.

## \|\| 70.65-66 \|\|

*mahadviṣṇorīśvarāya viśveśāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ prakṛtirūpāya prākṛtāya namoo \|\| 65 \|\|*

*prakṛtīśvararūpāya pradhānapurūṣāya ca \|*  
*ityevaṃ stavanaṃ kṛtvā mūrcchāmāpa sabhātale \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. I offer my salutation to you again and again to Maha-Vishnu, Isvara and the lord of the universe, you are yourself, the form of Prakriti, the form of Isvari, the foremost among the humans, I offer my salutation again and again. Thus offering prayer Akriira fainted in the court of Nanda.

## \|\| 70.67-70 \|\|

*papāta sahasā bhūmau punarīśaṃ dadarśa saḥ \|*  
*bahiḥsthaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ ca paramātmānamīśvaram \|\| 67 \|\|*

*paritaḥ śyāmarūpaṃ ca viśvasthaṃ viśvameva ca \|*  
*akrūraṃ mūrcchitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nandaḥ sādarapūrvakam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsane ramye vāsayāmāsa nārada \|*  
*papraccha sarvavṛttāntaṃ kiṃsviddṛṣṭamiti tvayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*iti śībrahmo śrikṛṣṇajanmakho utto nāradanāo gopīviṣayo nāma saptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

67-70. He suddenly fell down on the ground. He again saw that the lord who was standing outside was also in his heart, was the soul of all, being Isvara, was found in dark complexion, all round, was established in the universe and the from of the universe. О Narada, finding Akrura having fainted, Nanda lifted him up and seated him honourably on the gem-studded lion-throne. He then enquired of him about the news and also said, "What is there being visible." Thereafter he served him with delicious sweet food and enquired about his welfare again and again. Akrura on his part conveyed the news of Kamsa to him.

## \|\| 70.71-74 \|\|

*svapitrormokṣaṇārthaṃ ca gamanaṃ rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*ityakrūrakṛtaṃ stotraṃ yaḥ paṭhetsusamāhitaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*aputro labhate putramabhāryoṃ labhate priyam \|*  
*adhano dhanamāpnoti nirbhūmirurvarāṃ mahīm \|\| 72 \|\|*

*hataprajaḥ prajālābhaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ cāpratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*yaśaḥ prāpnoti vipulamayaśasvī ca līlayā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*atha suṣvāpa samaye paraṃ saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*ramye campakatalpe ca kṛṣṇaṃ kṛtvā svavakṣasi \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. He also advised him to send Krishna and Balarama to Mathura for getting their parents released from the bondage. Thus whosoever recites the stotras composed by Akrura, with devotion, he would get a son if he has a none, a wife if he has no wife, riches if he has no riches, land if he has no land, the one having lost children would get children, a disgraced person would be graceful and inglorious person would achieve immense glory. Thereafter he slept on the bed of campaka flowers.

## \|\| 70.75-78 \|\|

*prātaruthāya sahasā kṛtvā''ṅnikamanuttamam \|*  
*svarathe sthāpayāmāsa rāmaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ jagatpatim \|\| 75 \|\|*

*gavyaṃ pañcaprakāraṃ ca nānādravyaṃ sudulrabham \|*  
*vṛṣabhānaṃ ca nandaṃ ca sunandaṃ candabhānakam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*nānāprakāraṃ vādyaṃ ca mṛdaṅgamurajādikam \|*  
*paṭahaṃ paṇavaṃ caiva ḍhakkāṃ duṃdubhimānakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*sajjāṃ saṃnahanīṃ kāsyapaṭṭamardalamaṇḍavīm \|*  
*vādayāmāsa sānandaṃ nandagopo vrajeśvaraḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

75-78. Thereafter getting up early in the morning he completed his daily routine and made Balarama and Krishna to take their seats in the chariot. He carried five types of eatables like milk, curd, ghee, butter and butter milk with him and other valuable eatables. Accompanied by Vrsabhanu, Nanda, Sunanda and Chandrabhanu, they got ready for the journey. Nanda the lord of Vraja made several of the musical instruments to be sounded including double drums, drums, panavas, damarii, big drums and several other musical instruments.

## \|\| 70.79-80 \|\|

*śrutvā vādyaṃ ca gopyaśca gamanaṃ rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ rathasthaṃ tamāyayuḥ kopapīḍitāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇena vāritāḥ sarvāḥ preritā rādhāyā dvijaḥ \|*  
*babhañjurīśvararathaṃ pādāghātena līlayā \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Listening to the sound of musical instruments and coming to know of the departure of Balarama and Krishna to Mathura, the cowherdesses were extremely enraged and they arrived there finding Krishna having mounted on the chariot. О Brahman, thereafter, inspired by Radha the cowherdesses in anger, in spite of dissuading lord Krishna not to do so, broke the royal chariot with their kicks.

## \|\| 70.81-82 \|\|

*tatra sarveṣu gopeśa hāhākāraṃ kṛteṣu ca \|*  
*prayayurbalavatyaśca kṛṣṇaṃ kṛtvā svavakṣasi \|\| 81 \|\|*

*kācitkrūraṃ tamakrūraṃ bhartsayāmāsa kopataḥ \|*  
*kāścidvaddhvā ca vastreṇa cākūraṃ prayayustataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. All the cowherds cried in panic but the powerful cowherdesses embraced Krishna and took him away. Some of them called Akrura in anger to be quite cruel and denounced him. Some of them bound Akrtira with clothes.

## \|\| 70.83-84 \|\|

*kācittaṃ tāḍayāmāsa kaṅkaṇena kareṇa ca \|*  
*tadvastraṃ hārayāmāsa kṛtvā vivasanaṃ mune \|\| 83 \|\|*

*kṣatavikṣatasarvāṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā'krūraṃ ca mādhavaḥ \|*  
*jagāma rādhānikaṭaṃ bodhayāmāsa tāṃ punaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. О sage, some of the cowherdesses removed the costumes of Akrura and tried to break his armlets with their hands. Thereafter, Madhava found Akrtira having been so injured he went to Radha and tried to convince her.

## \|\| 70.85-90 \|\|

*ādhyātmikena yogena vinayena ca sādaram \|*  
*akrūraṃ bodhayāmāsa vodhayāmāsa tāṃ punaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*ākāśātpatitaṃ divyaṃ santraprasthāpitaṃ ratham \|*  
*vicitravastrasaṃyuktaṃ dadarśa purato hariḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*khacitaṃ maṇirājena racitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mātṛbhavanamājagāma jagatpatiḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*bhuktvā pītvā sukhaṃ suptvā bhagavānsahabāndhavaḥ \|*  
*tasthau munīndradevendrabrahmeśaśeṣavanditaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*muṣupurgoṃpikāḥ sarvāḥ paraṃ saṃhṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*puṣpatalpe ca ramye ca rādhayā saha nārada \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sarve cā''nandayuktāśca janā gokulavāsinaḥ \|*  
*kecidgopāśca nanṛtuḥ kecitsaṃgītatatparāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

85-90. The lord then humbly enlightened her about the divine yoga and also to Akrtira. Again for convincing Radha, Krishna went to her. In the meantime, they found a divine chariot moving in the sky which was decorated with beautiful costumes besides the gems and was built by Vishvakarma. At the sight of the chariot, the lord of the universe went to the palace of his mother. He took his food together with all his relatives and slept there. Then the lord was surrounded by the sages Indra, Brahma, Shiva, Shesha and other ascetics. О Narada, thereafter Radha together with the cowherdesses also slept on the flower bed. All the people of Gokula were filled with delight, some of them started dancing and some of them were singing.

## Chapter 71

## \|\| 71.1-5 \|\|

*athaikasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca rādhikāyāṃ ca suptāyāṃ suptāsu gopikāsu \|*  
*puṣpacandanatalpe ca vāyunā surabhīkṛte \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaprahare'tīte niśāyāṃ ca śubhe kṣaṇe \|*  
*śubhacandrarkṣayoge cāmṛtayogasamanvite \|\| 2 \|\|*

*saumyasvāmiyute lagne saumyagrahavilokite \|*  
*pāpagrahasamāsaktaduṣṭadoṣādivarjite \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yaśodāṃ bodhayāmāsa kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|*  
*vandhūnāśvāsayāmāsa samutthāya hariḥ svayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vādyaṃ niṣedhayāmāsa rādhikābhayabhītavat \|*  
*svatantro viśvakartā ca pātā bhartā svatantravat \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Narayana said – With the fragrant wind blowing Radhika was sleeping on the bed of flowers and sandal-paste. After the three fourths of the night was over, Krishna woke up Yashoda to perform the welfare ceremony in the auspicious moment when the moon and the constellations were in a favourable position, lagna was auspicious and the unfavourable planets which had no bad no effect. Lord Hari himself got up and assured his relatives. Getting afraid of Radhika he stopped the playing of the musical instruments. The one who is independent and creator of the universe besides being the protector and maintains the entire universe, was found afraid of Radha.

## \|\| 71.6-10 \|\|

*prakṣālya pādayugalaṃ dhṛtavā dhaute ca vāsasī \|*  
*uvāsa saṃskṛte sthāne vilipte candanādinā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*phalapallavasaṃyuktaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ candanādibhiḥ \|*  
*vāme kṛtvā pūrṇakumbhaṃ vahniṃ vipraṃ svadakṣiṇe \|\| 7 \|\|*

*patiputravatīṃ dīpaṃ darpaṇaṃ puratastathā \|*  
*dūrvākāṇḍaṃ ca susnigdhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhānyaṃ sitaṃ śubham \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gurudattaṃ guhītvā ca pradadhau mastakopari \|*  
*dhṛtaṃ dadarśa mādhvīkaṃ rajataṃ kāñcanaṃ dadhi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*candanaṃ lepanaṃ kṛtvā puṣpamālāṃ gale dadau \|*  
*guruvargaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ca vandayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. He washed his feet and was clad in two garments. Thereafter the spotless paste was applied on his body. A pitcher filled with water was placed to his left which was filled with fruits and tender leaves and was painted with sandal-paste, aguru and Brahmanas were placed to the right. In the forefront a chaste woman having the son and the husband alive was placed ahead carving the mirror and the burning lamp. The DUrva grass given by the teacher, beautiful flowers, the auspicious white paddy were placed on the bead, ghee, beverages, silver, gold and curd were shown to him, plastering his neck with sandal-paste, he was made to wear the garland of flowers. Thereafter, Krishna was made to adore his teachers as well as the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 71.11-12 \|\|

*śaṅkhadhvaniṃ vedapāṭhaṃ saṃgītaṃ maṅgalāṣṭakam \|*  
*vipraśīrvacanaṃ ramyaṃ śuśrāva paramādaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dhyātvā maṅgalarūpaṃ ca sarvatra maṅgalapradam \|*  
*cikṣepa dakṣiṇāṃ pādaṃ sundaraṃ svātmavigraham \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Thereafter conches were blown and the Vedas were recited with music and the verses showering welfare were also recited by the Brahmanas. Devoting the mind to the form or the one who bestows welfare, he lifted up his right foot to move forward.

## \|\| 71.13-18 \|\|

*vidhṛtya nāsikāvāmabhāgaṃ madhyamayā vibhuḥ \|*  
*visṛjya vāyuṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ nāsādakṣiṇarandhrataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tato yayau nandanando nandasya prāṅgaṇaṃ varam \|*  
*sānandaḥ paramānando nityānandaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nityo'nityo nityabīcasvarūpo nityavigrahaḥ \|*  
*nityāṅgabhūto nityeśo nityakṛtyaviśāradaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nityanūtanarūpaśca nityanūtanayauvanaḥ \|*  
*nityanūtanaveṣaśca vayasā nityanūtanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nityanūtanasaṃbhāṣo yatprema nityanūtanam \|*  
*nityanūtanasaṃprāptiḥ saubhāgyaṃ nityanūtanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sudhārasaparaṃ miṣṭaṃ yatvākyaṃ nityanūtanam \|*  
*nityanūtanabhaktaṃ ca yatpadaṃ nityanūtanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. The lord then pressing his nose with middle fmger stopped breathing for a while from the left side, he them released the breath from the right side. Thereafter, he went to the best of the court-yard of Nanda. The lord was delightful, blissful, always engrossed in bliss, eternal, the eternal form, the eternal form of the seed, appearing in human form always, the lord of all, always engaged in welfare deeds, taking to new form always and always appearing youthful in garments and speaking always new words, his love is always achieved by internal efforts. His words are sweeter then the nectar and always look new; his feet are always eternal and fresh and his adoration is always new and eternal.

## \|\| 71.22-23 \|\|

*tatra tasthau svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sahākrūraḥ sabāndhavaḥ \|*  
*yaśodayā samāśliṣṭo vāmapārśvena māyayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nandenā''nandayuktenā''śliṣṭo dakṣiṇapārśvataḥ \|*  
*saṃbhāṣito bāndhavaiśca pitrā mātrā ca cumbitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Thus the lord of illusion who always is combined with the illusion standing in that courtyard got ready to depart for the journey. In the courtyard, which was decorated with the trunks of banana trees, with tender flower leaves tied with the silken cord and the gems which were made by Vishvakarma and painted with kastCirl, saffron and sandal-paste. Lord Krishna together with Akrnra and other relatives made preparation for their departure. At that point of time Yashoda stood on the left and Nanda on the right and embraced Krishna, kissing his cheeks. The relatives also extended their love for Krishna.

## Chapter 72

## \|\| 72.1-9 \|\|

*atha dvisaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca atha kṛṣṇo guruṃ natvā nirgamya śibirānmune \|*  
*āruhya svargayānaṃ ca śubhāṃ madhupurīṃ yayau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viveśa mathurāṃ ramyāṃ sahākrūragaṇaiḥ samam \|*  
*nirjitya śakranagarī śobhāyuktāṃ manoharām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ratnaśreṣṭhena khacitāṃ racitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*amūlyaratnakalaśo rājitaiśca virājanām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*rājamargaśatairiṣṭairvaiṣṭitāṃ rucirairvaraiḥ \|*  
*candrākāraiścandrasārairmaṇimiḥ parisaṃskṛtaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vicitrairmaṇisāraiśca vīthīśatavinirmitaiḥ \|*  
*śobhitairvaṇijaiḥ śreṣṭhaiḥ puṇyavastusamanvitaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sarovarasahasraiśca paritaḥ pariśobhitam \|*  
*śudhdhasphaṭisaṃkāśaiḥ padmarāgavirājitaiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ratnālaṃkārabhūṣāḍhyaiḥ śobhitāṃ padminīgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*syirayauvanasaṃyuktairnimeṣarahitaiḥ paraiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śākṣarairūrdhvavadanaiḥ kṛṣṇadarśanalālasaiḥ \|*  
*bhrūbhaṅgalīlālolaiśca śaśvaccañcalalocanaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śaśvatkāmasamāyuktaiḥ pīnaśroṇipayodhareḥ \|*  
*komalāṅgairmadhyakūpai ratirāsaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

1-9. Narayana said – О sage, lord Krishna bowing in reverence to his teacher moved out of the camp and mounted the chariot that had arrived from heaven and moved towards the city of Mathura. He entered in the beautiful city of Mathura together with Akrnra and other attendants. The city of Mathura was more beautiful than Amaravati, was quite charming, shining and studded with gems. It was constructed by Vishvakarma and was invaluable, extremely beautiful, decorated with gem-studded pitchers, having hundreds of royal roads which were decorated with the best of gems and diamonds like the moon on all sides. It had many lanes which were numberless and was filled with many auspicious things, the best of the business people and thousands of lakes so abundantly found in the city. The damsels of the city were adorned with the best of the costumes and the ornaments studded with gems. The beautiful damsels were quite youthful and were raising their heads with the desire of having a look at the lotus-like face of lord Krishna. They were looking at him with unstable eyes, their eye-brows were moving and roving. They were always feeling passionate, with the stiff pelvic region and the breasts, soft limbs, beautiful slender-waist and were well-versed in the love-sport.

## \|\| 72.10-14 \|\|

*ratnanirmāṇayānānāṃ koṭibhiḥ pariśobhitām \|*  
*bhūṣaṇairbhūṣitābhiśca citretābhiśca citrakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nānāprakāraśrīyuktāṃ puṣpodyānatrikoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*nānāpuṣpaiḥ puṣpitābhiryuktābhirmadhusūdanaiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mādhuryamadhusaṃyuktairmadhulubdhairmudā'nvitaiḥ \|*  
*mādhvīkamadhumattaiśca yuktairmaṃdhukarīcayaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nānāprakāradurgeśca durgamyāṃ vairiṇāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|*  
*raṇitāṃ raṇakaiḥ śāścadrakṣāśāstraviśāradaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*trikoṭṭyāṭṭālikābhiśca saṃyuktāṃ sumanoharām \|*  
*racitāṃ kila sadratnairvicitrairviśvakarmaṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

10-14. The city of Amaravati had crores of vehicles studded with gems which were decorated with various types of ornaments and painted with paintings, variously decorated and were lodged in three crores of gardens. There were different types of fragrant flowers, in which the black wasps, greedy for the honey, were roaming about over the Bassia Latifolia trees attracting a large number of bees as well. The city had several types of forts which were invincible for the enemies and were filled by those well-versed in the scriptures on the military. Having a large number of valorous soldiers lodged in three crores of mansions, the city was quite pleasant and was built by Vishvakarma with the best of gents.

## \|\| 72.15-17 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtāṃ ca mathurāṃ dṛṣṭvā kamalalocanaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa pathi kubjāṃ tāṃ vṛddhāmatiyarādurām \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yāntoṃ daṇḍasahāyena cātinamrāṃ namadvalīm \|*  
*rūkṣitāṃ vikṛtākārāṃ bibhratīṃ candanadravam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kastūrīkuṅkumāktaṃ ca sparśamātreṇa nārada \|*  
*sugandhimakarandena gandhāḍhyaṃ sumanoharam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Looking at such a type of the city of Mathura, the lotus-eyed lord was moving ahead. In the meantime he met with Kubja (hunch back) who was quite old and was moving with the help of a staff, bending forward considerably. She was quite dry and was deformed and was carrying kastiirl and saffron in her hands. О Narada, with her touch the sandal-paste and the flowers had become more fragrant.

## \|\| 72.18-20 \|\|

*sādṛṣṭvā sasmitā vṛddhā śrīkāntaṃ śāntamīśvaram \|*  
*śrīyuktaṃ śrīnivāsaṃ taṃ śrībījaṃ śrīniketanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*praṇamya sahasā mūdharnā bhaktinamrā puṭāñjaliḥ \|*  
*pradadau candanaṃ tasya gātreśyāmalasundare \|\| 19 \|\|*

*gātreṣu tadgaṇānāṃ ca svarṇapātrakarā varā \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ praṇanāma punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The old women looked at lord Krishna with a delightful mind, who was peaceful, full of lustre, abode of Lakshmi, lord of Shri and the abode of Sri. The hunch-back suddenly folded her hands bowing in devotion. Bowing in devotion, lowering her head, she applied sandal-paste over the body of the lord and also on the attendants surrounding him. Holding the golden vase filled with sandal-paste, the old woman circumambulated lord Krishna and offered her salutation to him again and again.

## \|\| 72.21-32 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇadṛṣṭimātreṇa śrīyuktā sā babhūva ha \|*  
*sahasā śrīsamā ramyā rūpeṇa yauvanena ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vahiśuddhāṃśuvasanā ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*yathā dvādaśavarṣoyā kanyā dhanyā manoharā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bimboṣṭhī sasmitā śyāmā taptakāñcanasaṃnibhā \|*  
*suśroṇī sudatī bilvaphalatulyapayodharā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnanirmāṇahārasāravirājitā \|*  
*gajendrarājagamanā ratnamañjīrarañjitā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*bibhratī kabarībhāraṃ mālatīmālyaveṣṭitam \|*  
*rakṣitaṃ vāmabhāgena ruciraṃ vartulākṛtim \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sindūrabinduṃ dadhatoṃ dāḍimīkusumākṛtim \|*  
*kastūrī bindumupari sārdha candanabindubhiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rannadarpaṇāhastā ca praśastā ratikarmasu \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇaṃ varayāmāsa lolalocanakoṇataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śrīvāsastāṃ samāśvasya yayau sthānāntaraṃ param \|*  
*kṛtārtharūpā sā prītyā yayau padmayathā''layam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sa dadarśa svabhavanaṃ yayā padyālayālayam \|*  
*ratnaśayyāviracitaṃ sadratnasāranirmitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ratnapradīparājībhī rājitābhiśca rājitam \|*  
*ratnadarpaṇarājaiśca rājitaṃ paritastataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sindūravastratāmbūlaṃ ścetacāmaramālyakam \|*  
*bibhratībhiśca dāsībhirveṣṭitaṃ dāsasaṃghakaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatra gatvā ca bhuktvā ca miṣṭānnaṃ paramaṃ mudā \|*  
*suṣvāpa ratnaparyaṅke sā dāsībhiśca sevitā \|\| 32 \|\|*

21-32. Thereafter at the sight of lord Krishna, the old woman was filled with grace achieving youthfulness, beauty and a well-buib body. Suddenly she appeared like beautiful and charming like Lakshmi who was clad gem-studded in beautiful garments. Sanctified by fire and was adorned with several types of gem-studded ornaments having a youthful age of twelve years. She was quite pleasant and her lips appeared like ripe wood-apples. She was wearing a serene smile on her face, having a complexion like that of molten gold, beautiful pelvic region and teeth, the breasts like the fruit of wood-apple, wearing a garland of beautiful gems, walking slowly like an elephant adorned with the anklets of gems and the hair was well arranged in a knot which was adorned with a garland of jasmine flowers. The knot was filled towards the left in a roundish manner. The hunch-back had applied a spot of kastiirl on the forehead and above that there appeared a spot of sandal-paste. She was also adorned with a spot of vermilion like the flower of a pomegranate fruit. She was holding a mirror of gems in her hand. She was well-versed in the love-sport. She, looking with side-glances accepted lord Krishna as her husband. The lord, on his part, also assured her and left for another place, getting gratified, Kubja also delightfully went back to her abode like Lakshmi. She looked at her palace which had been turned like that of Lakshmi having the bed of gems and studded with the best of diamonds. A line of gems was inlaid in the same, the mirrors of gems were displayed on all sides which added to the grandeur. The red garments, betel, white fly-whisks and garland were held by the attendants appearing in large numbers in her abode. Reaching there delightfully, she consumed the sweet food and rested herself on the beautiful bed served by a number of female attendants. Then she went to sleep.

## \|\| 72.33-36 \|\|

*sakarpūraṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ kastūrīkuṅkumānvitam \|*  
*candanaṃ sthāpayāmāsa svatalpe haraye satī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mālatīmālyayugalaṃ karpūrādisuvāsitam \|*  
*śītalaṃ salilaṃ svādu miṣṭānnaṃ svasamīpataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*karmaṇā manasā vācā cintayantī hareḥ padam \|*  
*harerāgamanaṃ cāpi mukhacandraṃ manoharam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*jagatkṛṣṇamayaṃ śaśvatpaśyantī kāmukī mune \|*  
*koṭikandarpalīlābhaṃ kāmasaktaṃ ca kāmukam \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. Thereafter the chaste lady placed on her bed the betel, camphor, kastiirl saffron and sandal-paste and nearby she placed the garland of jasmine flowers. She also arranged the cool drinking water, scented with camphor and also arranged for delicious sweets. Thereafter she physically, mentally and by actions devoted her mind at the feet of the lord. О sage, visualising about the arrival of lord Krishna and devoting her mind to his lotus-like face, tha passionate women looked at the universe in the form of Krishna who was all passionate and filled with passion, moving a delightful mind.

## \|\| 72.37-38 \|\|

*tato tadarśa śrīkṛṣṇo mālākāraṃ manoharam \|*  
*mālāsamūhaṃ bibhrantaṃ gacchantaṃ rājamandiram \|\| 37 \|\|*

*so'pi dṛṣṭvā ca śrīkāntaṃ praṇamya śiraśā bhuvi \|*  
*dadau mālyasamūhaṃ ca kṛṣṇāya paramātmane \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Thereafter lord Krishna looked at the gardener who was carrying the flower garlands in the royal paiace. The gardener looking at the lord bowed in reverence over the ground and offered all the garlands to lord Krishna.

## \|\| 72.39-40 \|\|

*kṛṣṇastasmai varaṃ dattavā svadāsyamatidurlabham \|*  
*mālyaṃ gṛhītvā prayayau rājamārge varaṃ varaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tato dadarśa rajakaṃ bibhrataṃ vastrapuñjakam \|*  
*ahaṃkṛtibaliṣṭhaṃ ca satataṃ yovanodvatam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The lord on his part bestowed his inaccessible slavehood on the gardener and moved forward along the royal road. He then found a washerman carrying a heap of clothes who was quite strong, youthful and proud.

## \|\| 72.41 \|\|

*vastraṃ yayāce taṃ kṛṣṇo vinayena mahāmune \|*  
*sa tasmai na dadau vastraṃ tamuvāca ca niṣṭhuram \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О sage, the lord humbly begged from him some clothes. The washerman, however, did not part with the clothes and on the other hand spoke some very harsh words.

## \|\| 72.42 \|\|

*gorakṣakāṇāṃ tvadyogyaṃ vastrametatsudurlabham \|*  
*rājayogyaṃ ca he mūḍha he gopajanavallabha \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The washerman said – О foolish one, О lord of the cowherds, the costumes are not meant for cowherds like you because they are meant for the king.

## \|\| 72.43-44 \|\|

*gṛhītvā gopakanyāśca kanyālolupa lampaṭa \|*  
*yadvihāraḥ kṛtastatra vṛndāraṇye'pyarājake \|\| 43 \|\|*

*na cātra tādṛśaṃ karma rājñaḥ kaṃsasya vartmaṃni \|*  
*vidyamāno'tra rājendraḥ śāstā duṣṭasya tatkṣaṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. You are greedy for girls and you are extremely wicked, the way in which you have behaved with the cowherd girl in Vmdavana, you cannot behave like that in the region of Kamsa, because the king who punishes the wicked is available here.

## \|\| 72.45-46 \|\|

*rajakasya vacaḥ śrutvā jahāsa madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*jahāsa baladevaśca sākrūro gopavargakaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*taṃ nihatya capeṭena jagrāha vastrapuñjakam \|*  
*vastraṃ saṃdhārayāmāsa śrīkṛṣṇaḥ sagaṇastathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. On hearing the words of the washerman, Madhusudana laughed with Baladeva and together with all the cowherds. Thereafter lord Krishna, administered a slap on the face of the washerman and snatched away all the costumes and wore them all with all the cowherds.

## \|\| 72.47-48 \|\|

*ratnayānena gonokaṃ pārṣaderveṣṭitena ca \|*  
*yayau rajakarājaśca dhṛtvā divyakalevaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

*śaśvadyauvanayuktaṃ ca jarāmṛtyuharaṃ varam \|*  
*pītavastrasamāyuktaṃ sasmitaṃ śyāmasundaram \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The chief of the washerman surrounded by his courtiers mounted a plane and turning to a divine form left for Goloka, having everlasting youthfulness, devoid of death and old age and the best. They were clad in yellow garments, wearing a serene smile on the faces and looked like Krishna.

## \|\| 72.49-52 \|\|

*babhūva so'pi goloke pārṣadeṣu ca pārṣadaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasyā''gamanaṃ tatra sasmāra satataṃ vaśī \|\| 49 \|\|*

*astaṃ gato dinakaro'pyakrūraḥ svagṛhaṃ yayau \|*  
*kṛṣṇasyānumatiṃ prāpya kṛṣṇo'pi kasyacidgṛham \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vaiṣṇavasya kuvindasya tasminnastadhanasya ca \|*  
*sānando nandasahito baladevādibhiryutaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*sa bhaktaḥ pūjayāmāsa praṇamya śrīniketanam \|*  
*tasmai dadau svadāsyaṃ ca varaṃ brahmādidurlabham \|\| 52 \|\|*

49-52. The self-disciplined washerman reached Goloka and was turned into an attendant of the lord and started waiting there for the return of Krishna. At sun-set AkrOra also went to his abode with the permission of lord Krishna and Nanda. Baladeva, accompanied by Krishna, went to a Vais nava Kuvinda who was very poor. The devoted Kuvinda bowed at the feet of the lord and adored him. The lord felt delighted and bestowed on him his slavehood which is beyond the reach of the gods like Brahma and others.

## \|\| 72.53-54 \|\|

*paryaṅke suṣupuḥ sarve bhuktvā miṣṭānnasuttamam \|*  
*nidrāṃ ca lebhe sā kubjā nidreśo'piyayau mudā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*gatvā dadarśa kubjāṃ tāṃ ratnatalpe ca nidritām \|*  
*dāsīgaṇaiḥ parivṛtāṃ sundarīṃ kamalāmiva \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. After consuming the best of the sweets, all the people slept on the beds. At that point of time the lord left for the abode of Kubja who was sleeping on the bed. Reaching there he looked at Kubja who lying on the gem-studded bed and appeared like Lakshmi, served by the female attendants on all sides,

## \|\| 72.55-58 \|\|

*bodhayāmāsa tāṃ kṛṣṇo na dāsīsvapi nidritāḥ \|*  
*tāmuvāca jagannātho jagannāthapriyāṃ satīm \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śrībhagavānuvāca tyaja nidrāṃ mahābhāge śṛṅgāraṃ dehi sundari \|*  
*purā śūrpaṇakhā tvaṃ ca bhaginīṃ rāvaṇasya ca \|\| 56 \|\|*

*rāmajanmani maddhetostvayā kānte tapaḥ kṛtam \|*  
*tapaḥprabhāvānmāṃ kāntaṃ bhaja śrīkṛṣṇajanmani \|\| 57 \|\|*

*adhunā sukhasaṃyogaṃ kṛtvā gaccha mamā''layam \|*  
*sudurlabhaṃ ca golokaṃ jarāsṛtyuharaṃ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. Instead of waking all the attendants of Kubja, lord woke her up alone and spoke to the chaste lady. Lord Krishna said, "O virtuous one, О beautiful one, wake up and let me enjoy the love-sport with you because in earlier birth you happened to be Surpanakha, the sister of Ravana. О damsel, during my incarnation as Rama you had performed the tapas for me. Influenced by those tapas I have taken to this form and have come to you as your beloved. Therefore, you serve me. Presently you enjoy all the pleasures with me and then proceed on to Goloka which destroys birth and death.

## \|\| 72.59-60 \|\|

*ityukatvā śrīnivāsaśca kṛtvātāmeva vakṣasi \|*  
*nagnāṃ cakāra śṛṅgāraṃ cumbanaṃ cāpi kāmukīm \|\| 59 \|\|*

*sa sasmitā ca śrīkṛṣṇaṃ navasaṃgamalajjitā \|*  
*cucumba gaṇḍe kroḍe taṃ cakāra kamalā yathā \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Thus speaking lord Krishna embraced her and unrobing her, enjoyed her passionate advances. With a serene smile on her face, the passionate damsel felt shy at the first union but implanted a kiss on the lord. The lord took her in his lap like Lakshmi.

## \|\| 72.61-62 \|\|

*suraterviratirnāsti daṃpatī ratipaṇḍitau \|*  
*nānāprakārasurataṃ babhūva tatra nārada \|\| 61 \|\|*

*stanaśroṇiyugaṃ tasyā vikṣataṃ ca cakāra ha \|*  
*bhagavānnakharaistīkṣṇairdaśanairadharaṃ varam \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. O Narada, the lord was well-versed in the art of making love and both of them did not rest during the physical union and they enjoyed the love-sport in various ways. Lord Krishna scratched her breasts and the pelvic region with the nails and also sucked her nectar-like lips.

## \|\| 72.63-64 \|\|

*niśāvasānasamaye vīryādhānaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*sukhasaṃbhogabhogena mūrcchāmāpa ca sundarī \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tatrā''jagāmatāṃ tandrā kṛṣṇavakṣaḥsthalasthitām \|*  
*bubudhe na divārātraṃ svarga martya jalaṃ sthalam \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. At the end of the night the lord implanted the semen in her womb after which the beautiful damsel fainted. In the lap of lord Krishna she lost the consciousness about day and night, heaven or earth, water or earth.

## \|\| 72.65-68 \|\|

*suprabhātā ca rajanī babhūva rajanīpatiḥ \|*  
*patyurvyatikrameṇaiva lajjayeva malīmasaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*athājagāma golokādratho ratnavinirmitaḥ \|*  
*jagāma tena taṃ lokaṃ dhṛtvā divyakalevaram \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vahniśuddhāṃ śukādhānaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam \|*  
*prataptakāñcanābhāsaṃ nityaṃ janmādivarjitam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*sā babhūva ca tatraiva gopī candramukhī mune \|*  
*gopyaḥ katividhāstasyā babhūvuḥ paricārikāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

65-68. Thus the time of day-break arrived and it appeared that moon had become dirty getting enraged with the husband. Thereafter the plane from Goloka arrived and she attaining the divine form went to Goloka. She was clad in the divine garments sanctified by Agni and adorned with the gem-studded ornament. She was having the complexion of molten gold becoming eternal and devoid of birth and death. О sage, she was known in the Goloka as the cowherdess Chandramukhi and several types of cowherdesses became her attendants.

## \|\| 72.69-72 \|\|

*bhagavānapi tatraiva kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā svamandiram \|*  
*jagāma yatra nandaśca sānando nandanandanaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*atha kaṃso niśāyāṃ ca nidrāyāṃ bhayavihvalaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa duḥkhaduḥsvapnamātmano mṛtyusūcakam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dadarśa sūryaṃ bhūmisthaṃ catuḥkhaṇḍaṃ nabhaścyutam \|*  
*daśakhaṇḍe candrabimbaṃ bhūmisthaṃ khāccyutaṃ mune \|\| 71 \|\|*

*puruṣānvikṛtākārānrajjuhastāndigambarān \|*  
*vidhavāṃ śūdrapatnīṃ ca nagnāṃ ca cchinnanāsikām \|\| 72 \|\|*

69-72. The lord also remaining there for a while went back to the palace where Nanda was staying delightfully. Kamsa on the other hand was enjoying a sound sleep in the night when he felt terrified and started witnessing frightening dreams. О sage, he saw the sun had fallen from the sky breaking into four pieces on earth and the moon also after falling from the sky had broken into ten pieces. A.terrific unrobed man holding a terrific noose in his hand and besides, there also appeared a widow the wife of a Siidra, who was also unrobed and had her nose cut off.

## \|\| 72.73-82 \|\|

*hasantīṃ cūrṇatilakāṃ śvetakṛṣṇoccamūrdhajām \|*  
*khaḍgakharparahastāṃ ca lolajihvāṃ ca bibhratīm \|\| 73 \|\|*

*ruṇḍamālāsamāyuktāṃ gardabhaṃ mahiṣaṃ vṛṣam \|*  
*bhallūkaṃ sūkaraṃ kākaṃ gṛdhraṃ kahkaṃ ca vānaram \|\| 74 \|\|*

*virajaṃ kukkuraṃ nakraṃ śṛgālaṃ bhasmapuñjakam \|*  
*asthirāśiṃ tālaphalaṃ keśaṃ kārpāsamulbaṇam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*nirvāṇāṅgāramilkāṃ ca śavaṃ sartyaṃ citāśritam \|*  
*kulālatailakārāṇāṃ cakraṃ vakraṃ kapardakam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śmaśānaṃ dagdhakāṣṭhaṃ ca śuṣkakāṣṭhaṃ kuṇaṃ tṛṇām \|*  
*gacchantaṃ ca kabandhaṃ ca nadantaṃ mṛtamastakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*dagdhasthānaṃ bhasmayutaṃ taḍāgaṃ jalavarjitam \|*  
*dagdhamatsyaṃ ca lohaṃ ca nirvāṇadagdhakānanam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*galatkuṣṭhaṃ ca vṛṣalaṃ nagnaṃ ca suktasūrdhacam \|*  
*atīva rūpaṭaṃ vipraṃ ca śapantaṃ gurumīdṛśām \|\| 79 \|\|*

*atīvaruṣṭaṃ bhikṣuṃ ca yoginaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ naram \|*  
*evaṃ dṛṣṭvā samutthāya kathayāmāsa mātaram \|\| 80 \|\|*

*pitaraṃ bhrātaraṃ patnīṃ rudatīṃ premavihvalam \|*  
*mañcakānkārayāmasa sthāpayāmāsa hastinam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*mallasainyaṃ ca yoddhāraṃ kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|*  
*sabhāṃ ca kārayāmāsa puṇyaṃ svastyayanaṃ śivam \|\| 82 \|\|*

73-82. She was smiling and was using the line of ashes as tilakam, her white and black hair was turned upwards; she was holding a sword in one hand and a skull cup in the other, her tongue was protruding and was moving. She wore a garland of skulls round her neck. Similarly he also saw a donkey, a he-buffalo, a pig, a bear, a crow, a vulture, a white kite, a monkey, a white dog, a crocodile, a jackal, a heap of ashes, a heap of bones, a fruit of tala tree, hair, cotton, coal, burning wood, a dead body over the burning fire, the wheel of the potter, the oil mill, the cremation ground, burnt wood, dry wood, kusa-grass, straw, the moving headless body of a human, a crying dead body, the dry pool filled with ashes, the burnt fish, iron, the burnt out forest, Shudra suffering from leprosy, a naked Brahmana having dishevelled hair pronouncing a horrible curse in anger, an enraged mendicant, an ascetic and a Vaishnava. Thus witnessing a horrible dream he got up and spoke to his parents, brothers and the wife who was crying, infatuated with love. Thereafter he got the stage prepared and an elephant was made to stand there. He arranged for a terrific army of wrestlers. To start the welfare ceremony, he summoned the assembly and performed auspicious and welfare deeds reciting the welfare mantras. He cautioned his family priest.

## \|\| 72.83-84 \|\|

*yatnena yojayāmāsa yoge yuktaṃ purohitam \|*  
*uvāsa mañcake ramye dhṛtvā khaḍgaṃ vilakṣaṇam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*raṇe niyojayāmāsa yoddhāraṃ yuddhakovidam \|*  
*vāsayāmāsa rājendrānbrāhmaṇāṃśca munīśvarān \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Holding an astonishing sword in his hand, he seated himself on the stage and deputed the very strong warriors on duty. He made the kings, Brahmanas, the mendicant, the relatives, people and the warrior to sit on the stage.

## \|\| 72.85-86 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāśca suhṛdvargāndharmiṣṭhānraṇakovidān \|*  
*athā''jagama govindo rāmeṇa saha nārada \|\| 85 \|\|*

*maheśasya dhanurmadhyaṃ babhañja tatra līlayā \|*  
*śabdena tasya mathurā badhirā ca babhūva ha \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. О Narada, thereafter lord Krishna together with Balarama arrived there and playfully picked up the bow of Shiva. A thundering sound was created with the breaking of the bow. The entire city looked like having become deaf; looking at this Kamsa was immensely disturbed but lord Krishna, the son of Devaki, was immensely delighted.

## \|\| 72.87-88 \|\|

*viṣādaṃ prāpa kaṃsaśca mudaṃ ca devakīsutaḥ \|*  
*upasthitaḥ sabhāmaddhe gajaṃ mallaṃ nihatya ca \|*  
*yogī dadarśa taṃ devaṃ paramātmānamīśvaram \|\| 87 \|\|*

*yathā hṛtpadmamadhyasthaṃ tādṛśaṃ bahireva ca \|*  
*rājendrarūpaṃ rājānaḥ śāstāraṃ daṇḍadhāriṇā m \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. Killing the elephant and the wrestler he entered the assembly. At that point of time, all the ascetics with their delightful mind were looking at the lord. The gods were looking at the lord with a delightful mind, while the kings on the other hand, looked at him in the form of a great lord who was the ruler of the kings.

## \|\| 72.89-90 \|\|

*pitā mātā dugdhamukhaṃ stanāndhaṃ bālakaṃ yathā \|*  
*kāminyaḥ koṭikandarpalīlālāvapyadhāriṇam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*kaṃsaśca kālapuruṣaṃ vairiṇaṃ tasya bāndhavāḥ \|*  
*mallā mṛtyupradaṃ caiva prāṇatulyaṃ ca yādavāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. The parents looked at them like an infant, while the damsels looked at them like the beautiful god of love. Kamsa on the other hand looked at Krishna and Balarama as his own enemies as well as the enemies of his relatives. The wrestler looked at them like the god of death and all the Yadavas looked at them like their own lives.

## \|\| 72.91-92 \|\|

*namaskṛtya munīnviprānpitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum \|*  
*jagāma mañcakāmyāśaṃ haste kṛtvā sudarśanam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭāvā bhaktaṃ bhaktabandhuḥ kṛpayā ca kṛpānidhiḥ \|*  
*ākṛṣya mañcakātkaṃkaṃ jaghāna līlayā mune \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. Lord Krishna holding the Sudarshana-cakra in his hand bowed in reverence to the sage, the Brahmanas, his parents and the teacher and moved towards the stage and reached close to Kariisa. О sage, the all merciful lord who is attached to his devotees and bestowing his grace on the devotees dragged Kamsa from the platform and killed him without much difficulty.

## \|\| 72.93-94 \|\|

*rājā dadarśa viśvaṃ ca sarvaṃ kṛṣṇamayaṃ param \|*  
*purato ratnayānaṃ ca hīrakāhārabhūṣitam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*yayau viṣṇupadaṃ sphīto dibyarūpaṃ vidhāya ca \|*  
*tejo viveśa paramaṃ kṛṣṇapādāmbuje mune \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. At the time of the death, Kamsa looked at the entire universe like Krishna and also found, the arrival of the plane studded with gems. О sage, taking to the divine form, he mounted on the plane and went to Vishnuloka and his lustre was merged into the lotus-like feet of lord Krishna.

## \|\| 72.95-105 \|\|

*nivṛtya tasya satkāraṃ brāhmaṇemyo dharaṃ dadau \|*  
*dadau rājyaṃ rājachatramugrasenāya dhīmate \|\| 95 \|\|*

*sa babhūva nṛpendraśca candravaṃśasamudbhavaḥ \|*  
*vilalāpa kaṃsamātā patnīvargaśca tatpitā \|\| 96 \|\|*

*bāndhavā mātṛvargaśca bhaginī bhrātṛkāminī \|*  
*darśanaṃ dehi rājendra samuttiṣṭha nṛpāsane \|\| 97 \|\|*

*rājyaṃ rakṣa dhanaṃ rakṣa bāndhavaṃ balameva ca \|*  
*kva yāsi bāndhavānhitvā tvamanāthānmahābala \|\| 98 \|\|*

*brahmādistambaparyantamasaṃkhyaṃ viśvameva ca \|*  
*sarvaṃ carācarādhāraṃ yaḥ sṛjatyeva līlayā \|\| 99 \|\|*

*brahmeśaśeṣadharmāśca dineśaśca gaṇeśvaraḥ \|*  
*munīndravargo devendro dhyāyate yamaharniśam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*vedāḥ stupanti yaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ stauti bhītā sarasvatī \|*  
*stauti yaṃ prakṛtirhṛṣṭā prākṛtaṃ prakṛteḥ param \|\| 101 \|\|*

*svecchāmayaṃ nirīhaṃ ca nirguṇaṃ ca nirañjanam \|*  
*parātparataraṃ brahma paramātmānamīśvaram \|\| 102 \|\|*

*nityaṃ jyotiḥsvarūpaṃ ca bhaktānugrahavigraham \|*  
*nityānandaṃ ca nityaṃ ca nityamakṣaravigraham \|\| 103 \|\|*

*so'vatīrṇoṃ hi bhagavānbhārāvataraṇāya ca \|*  
*gopālabālaveṣaśca māyeśo māyayā prabhuḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*sa yaṃ hanti ca sarveśo rakṣitā tasya kaḥ pumān \|*  
*sa yaṃ rakṣati sarvātmā tasya hantā na ko'pi ca \|\| 105 \|\|*

95-105. Thus after killing Kamsa he distributed riches to Brahmanas and bestowed the kingship to the intelligent Ugrasena who was born in the lunar race. On the other hand the mother of Kamsa, his wives, the father, the brothers, the mother, the sisters and the wives or brothers started lamenting. They cried "O Rajendra, you appear before us, get up and occupy the royal lion-throne and mle over the country protecting the riches and the relatives besides the army. О valorous person, where have you gone leaving us like orphans, the people said. The one who could create and preserve all the creatures from Brahma to the least blade of grass playfully and who is adored by Brahma, Shesha, Shiva, Dharma, Stirya, Ganesha, Ganga, the group of sages and the gods continuously during day and night, the same lord Krishna is adored in the Vedas. Sarasavti recites his name feeling panicky while Prakriti offers prayers to him delightfully. He is beyond Prakriti and in the form of eternal Brahma and is adored by all. He moves at will unattached, without qualities, without blemish, beyond everyone, eternal Brahma, the great soul, the great lord, eternal, the form of eternal flame, the one who takes to a definite form for the sake of his devotees, always blissful, eternal and imperishable, the same lord, under the influence of illusion and in order to relieve the earth of her burden, has incarnated on earth together with the cowherds. He is the lord of illusion. He is lord of all and in case he kills someone, no one on earth can protect him. The one who is protected by the eternal soul, who on earth can kill him?

## \|\| 72.106 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā sarvaśca virarāma mahāmune \|*  
*brāhmaṇānbhojayāmāsa tebhyaḥ sarvaṃ dhanaṃ dadau \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. О sage, all the people thus spoke among themselves and then kept quiet. Thereafter they served the Brahmanas with food and distributed riches to them.

## \|\| 72.107-108 \|\|

*bhagavānapi sarvātmā jagāma piturantikam \|*  
*chittavā ca lohanigaḍaṃ tayormokṣaṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*nanāma daṇḍavadbhamau mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tathā \|*  
*tuṣṭāva bhakttayā deveśo bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. On the other hand lord Krishna who happens to be the soul of all went to his parents and he cut off the falters of iron and freed them. He prostrated before his parents and humbly offered prayers to them.

## \|\| 72.109-110 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca pitaraṃ mātaraṃ vidyāmantradaṃ gurumeva ca \|*  
*yo na puṣṇāti puruṣo yāvajjīvaṃ ca so'śuciḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmapi pūjyānāṃ pitā vandyo mahān guruḥ \|*  
*pituḥ śataguṇairmātā garbhadhāraṇapoṣaṇāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Shri Krishna said – The one who does not maintain his father, mother, the teacher who bestows knowledge, the teacher who bestows mantra, such a person always remains impure throughout the world because, of all the people in the world the father is quite adorable besides the teacher and the mother who carries a child in her womb. The parents who bring up the child are therefore adorable a hundred times more.

## \|\| 72.111-115 \|\|

*mātā ca pṛthivīrūpā sarvebhyaśca hiraiṣiṇī \|*  
*nāsti mātuḥ paro bandhuḥ sarveṣāṃ jagatītale \|\| 111 \|\|*

*vidyāmantrapradaḥ katyaṃ mātuḥ paratano guruḥ \|*  
*na hi tasmātparaḥ kau'pi vandyaḥ pūjyaśca vedataḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*ityevamuktvā śrīkṛṣṇo balabhadro nanāma ca \|*  
*mātā cakāratau kroḍe pitā ca sādaraṃ mune \|\| 113 \|\|*

*miṣṭānnaṃ paramaṃ tau ca bhojayāmāsa brāhmaṇān \|*  
*nandaśca bhojayāmāsa gopālānparamādaram \|\| 114 \|\|*

*maṅgale kārayāmāsa bhojayābhāsa brāhmaṇān \|*  
*vasurvasusamūhaṃ ca brāhmaṇebhyo dadau mudā \|\| 115 \|\|*

111-115. Because they bestow welfare, of all those who bestow welfare to all are also treated as the mother. Therefore, there is no other relative closer than the mother in the universe but the teacher who bestows knowledge is more glorious than the mother because, according to the Vedas, there is no one else more adorable than him. О sage, thus speaking lord Krishna and Balarama offered their salutation to them. Thereafter the parents also embraced their children and were served with sweet food. Vasudeva getting delighted performed the welfare ceremonies and serving the Brahmanas with food, distributed wealth among them.

## Chapter 73

## \|\| 73.1-2 \|\|

*atha trisaptatitamodhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca atha kṛṣṇaśca sānandaṃ nandaṃ taṃ pitaraṃ balaḥ \|*  
*bodhayāmāsa śokārtaṃ divyairādhyātmikādibhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*uccai rudantaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ putraviccedakātaram \|*  
*dattvā tasmai maṇiśreṣṭhamityuvāca jagatpatiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Narayana said – Lord Krishna imparted spiritual knowledge to Panda who was suffering from the grief of separation of the son and feeling helpless was crying aloud, getting fainted. Thereafter, the lord of the universe offered him the best of gems and said.

## \|\| 73.3-4 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca nibodha nanda sānandaṃ tyaja śokaṃ mudaṃ labha \|*  
*jñānaṃ gṛhāṇa maddattaṃ yaddataṃ brahmaṇe purā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadyaddattaṃ ca śoṣāya gaṇeśāyeśvarāya ca \|*  
*dineśāya munīśāya yogīśāya ca puṣkare \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Krishna said – О Nanda, shed away the grief and feel delighted and blissful, hearing my words. I am imparting divine knowledge to you which you kindly receive. The divine knowledge was imparted by me in earlier times at Puskara-ksetra to Brahma, Shesha, Ganesha, Shiva, Surya, the ascetics and the great yogis.

## \|\| 73.5 \|\|

*kaḥkasya putraḥ kastātaḥ kā mātā kasyacitkutaḥ \|*  
*āyānti yānti saṃsāraṃ paraṃ svakṛtakarmaṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The people continue to come and go in this universe according to the result of their actions. Therefore who is the father of whom and who is the son of whom?

## \|\| 73.6-8 \|\|

*karmānusārājjantuśca jāyate sthānabhedataḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā ko'pi jantuśca yogīndrāṇāṃ nṛpastriyām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dvijāpatnyāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ vaiśyāyāṃ śūdrayoniṣu \|*  
*tiryagyoniṣu kaścicca kaścitpaśvādiyoniṣu \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mamaiva māyayā sarve sānandā viṣayeṣu ca \|*  
*dehatyāme viṣaṇṇāśca vicchede bāndhavasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Everyone takes birth at a particular place according to his karmas. Someone takes birth with the great yogis, someone with the queen, some with Brahmana woman, someone with Ks atriyas, Vaisyas and Shudra women. Thus someone is born as a bird, someone as an animal. Influenced by my illusion, all the people feel delight in the various types of worldly pleasures and feel painful at heart with the departure of their relatives.

## \|\| 73.9 \|\|

*prajābhūmidhanādīnāṃ vicchedo maraṇādhikaḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ bhavati mūḍhaśca na ca vidvāñchucā yutaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. For them the loss of their sons and daughter, the land and the riches is more painful than even death. Because of this, these foolish people suffer form grief but the intelligent never do so.

## \|\| 73.10 \|\|

*madbhakto bhaktiyuktaśca madyājī vijitendriyaḥ \|*  
*manmantropāsakaścaiva matsevānirataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. My devotees who is filled with my devotion is self-disciplined and adores by the reciting of the mantras and because of his being always devoted to me, he always remains.spotless and without blemish.

## \|\| 73.11-12 \|\|

*madbhayādvāti vāto'yaṃ ravirbhāti ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*bhāti candro mahendraśca kālabhede ca varṣati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vahnirvahati mṛtyuśca caratyeva hi jantuṣu \|*  
*bibharti vṛkṣaḥ kālena puṣpāpi ca phalāni ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Feeling panicky from me the wind blows, the sun rises and illumines the universe, the moon rises with all the rays and Indra pours timely rains, the fire bums, the death takes sway the lives of the people, the trees blossom timely with flowers and fruits.

## \|\| 73.13-14 \|\|

*nirādhāraśca vāyuśca vāyvādhāraśca kaccipaḥ \|*  
*śeṣaśca kacchapādhāraḥ śeṣādhāraśca parvataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tadādhārāśca pātālāḥ sapta eva hi paṅktitaḥ \|*  
*niścalaṃ ca jalaṃ tasmājjalasthā ca vasuṃdharā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The wind has no base but it carries the tortoise, the tortoise carries Shesha and Shesha carries the mountains, the seven nether worlds stand in a line. The waters of the nether worlds are quite static and the earth is floating on the water.

## \|\| 73.15-18 \|\|

*saptasvarga dharādhāraṃ jyotiścakaṃ grahāśrayam \|*  
*nirādhāraśca vaikuṇṭho brahmāṇḍemyaḥ paro varaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tatparaścāpi golokaḥ pañcāśatko ṭiyojanāt \|*  
*ūrdhva nirāśrayaścāpi ratnasāravinirmitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saptadvāraḥ saptasāraḥ parikhāsaptasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*lakṣaprākārayuktaśca nadyā virajayā yutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*veṣṭito ratnaśailena śataśṛṅgeṇa cāruṇā \|*  
*yojanāyutamānaṃ ca yasyaikaṃ śṛṅgamujjvalam \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. The heaven and other seven lokas are based on earth, the Jyotis'cakra and the constellation stand on the bases of the planets but the Vaikuntha stands with out any base and is beyond the globe. Goloka is situated at a distance of fifty crores of yojanas beyond that, which is floating. The Goloka having no base is built with the best of gems having seven gates, having seven substances, seven moats and lakhs of boundary walls. A river named Viraja flows there. Goloka is surrounded by the mountains of hundred peaks covered with gems, a single peak of which spreads over an area of ten thousand yojanas and is filled with lustre.

## \|\| 73.19-20 \|\|

*śatakoṭiyojanaśca śaila ucchrita eva ca \|*  
*dairdhyaṃ tasya śataguṇaṃ prasthaṃ ca lakṣayojanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*yojanāyutavistīrṇastatraiva rāsamaṇḍalaḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇo vartulaścandrabimbavatu \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. That mountain is spread over an area of a hundred yojanas and is more than hundred times in length and a lakh of yojanas in width. A Rasamandala is spread over ten thousand yojanas in Goloka which is built with invaluable gems and is circular like the lunar disc.

## \|\| 73.21-32 \|\|

*pārijātavanenaiva puṣpitena ca vevṭitaḥ \|*  
*kalpavṛkṣasahasreṇa puṣpodyānaśatena ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nānāvidhaiḥ puṣpavṛkṣaiḥ puṣpitena ca cāruṇā \|*  
*trikoṭiratnabhavano gopīlakṣaiśca rakṣitaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ratnapradīpayuktaśca ratnatalpasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*nānābhogasamāyukto sadhuvāpīśatairvṛtaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pīyūṣavāpīyuktaśca kāmabhogasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*golokagṛhasaṃkhyānavarṇane vā viśāradaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*na ko'pi veda vidvānvā vedavidvānvrajeśvaraḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇabhavanānāṃ trikoṭibhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śobhitaṃ sundaraṃ ramyaṃ rādhāśiviramuttamam \|*  
*amūlyaratnakalaśairujjvalaṃ ratnadarpaṇaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*asūlyaratnastamabhānāṃ rājibhiśca virājitam \|*  
*nānācitravicitraiśca citritaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*māṇikyamuktāsaṃsaktaṃ hīrāvārasamanvitam \|*  
*ratnapradīpasaṃsaktaṃ ratnasopānasundaram \|\| 28 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnapatraiśca talparājivirājitam \|*  
*amūlyaratnacitraiśca tribhiścitravicitritaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tisṛbhiḥ parikhābhiśca tribhirdvāraiśca durgamaiḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ ṣoḍaśakakṣābhiḥ pratidvāreṣu vā'ntaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*gopīṣoḍaśalakṣaiśca saṃniyuktairitastataḥ \|*  
*vahniśuddhāṃśukādhānai ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*taptakāñcanavarṇābhaiḥ śatacandrasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*rādhikāriṃkarīvargairyuktamabhyantaraṃ varam \|\| 32 \|\|*

21-32. It is surrounded by the blossoming Parijata flowers a thousand kalpavrksa and a hundred flower orchards in which several types of flowers are blossoming. There are three crores of gem-studded houses, a lakh of cowherdesses who reside there well guarded, the lamps are made of gems, the beds are made of gems and several types of eatables are stored there. It has a hundred step-wells of honey. Similarly there are several step-wells filled with nectar and are also filled with several types of cosmetics and other articles required during love-sport. О lord of Vraja, thus I am narrating to you the number of the buildings of Goloka which are unknown even to the best of intellectuals. It has three crores of palaces which are studded with gems beside the charming and beautiful Bhavana of Radha. This palace of Radha is decorated with invaluable pitchers of gems and the mirrors of gems which illumine. There are lines of gem-studded pillars, has a large number of white fly whisks which are quite astonishing. The handles of the fly-whisks were decorated with the best of gems and rubies. The lamps of gems illumined the area. The steps are decorated with gems and the vases are also made of gems. The beds are also decorated with lines of gems and painted with three types of paintings with three moats. There are difficult entrance gates, there are sixteen apartments. At the gates of these apartments, sixteen lakhs of cowherdesses are deputed to guard them who are clad in the best of garments sanctified by fire and adorned with the best of gem-studded ornaments. They have the complexion of molten gold and illumine like hundreds of moons. The attendants of Radhika are lodged there.

## \|\| 73.33-42 \|\|

*amūlyaratnanirmāṇapraṅgaṇaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*amūlyaratnastambhānāṃ samūraiśca suśobhitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ratnamaṅgalakumbhaiśca phalapallavasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*saṃyutaṃ ratnavedībhirmuktā yuktābhirīpsitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnamukuraiḥ śobhitaṃ sundarairaho \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇaṃ bhavanānāṃ varaṃ gṛham \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthā ca gopīlakṣaiśca sevitā \|*  
*koṭipūrṇenduśobhāḍhyā śvetacampakasaṃnibhā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*amūlyaratnanirmāṇabhūṣaṇaiśca vibhūṣitā \|*  
*amūlyaratnavasanā bibhratī ratnadarpaṇam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ratnapadmaṃ ca ruciraṃ savyadakṣiṇahastataḥ \|*  
*dāḍimbakusumākāraṃ sindūraṃ sumanoharam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*suśobhitaṃ sṛgamadairiṣṭaiścandanabindubhiḥ \|*  
*dadhatī kabarībhāraṃ mālatīmalyamaṇḍitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*racitaṃ vāmabhagena munīndrāṇāṃ manoharam \|*  
*evaṃbhūtaṃ (tā) tatra rādhā gopībhiḥ parisevitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śvetacāmarahastābhistattulyābhiśca sarvataḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇairbhūṣitābhiśca bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*matprāṇādhiṣṭhātṛdevī devīnāṃ pravarā varā \|*  
*sudāmnaḥ sā ca śāpena vṛṣabhānasutā'dhunā \|\| 42 \|\|*

33-42. The court-yard of that palace is inlaid with beautiful gems, which is decorated with the best of the pillars studded with gems, the tree, the leaves and the fruits besides the welfare pitchers made of gems and the pedestals made with rubies. They have innumerable beautiful mirrors made of gems. Thus the palace is decorated with invaluable gems and happen to be the best of all the palaces on which Radhika is seated attended by a lakh of cowherdesses. She illumines like crores of full moons, having a complexion of white campaka flowers, adorned with all the beautiful ornaments and is clad in gem-studded costumes, holding in her hands a mirror and a beautiful lotus of gems; she applies a spot of vermilion of the size of the flowers of pomegranate and also spots of kasturl and sandal-wood. She wears round her neck the garland of jasmine flowers and her hair is tied in a knot. The knot is tilted towards the left which attracts even the sages. Thus Radha is served by the cowherd esses all round. All the cowherdesses carry in their hands white fly-whisks and are adorned with the best of gem-studded ornaments. Radha happens to be the best of the goddesses of my life. She is currently reborn as the daughter of Vrsabhanu, because of the curse of Sudama.

## \|\| 73.43-46 \|\|

*śatābdiko hi vicchedo bhaviṣyati mayā saha \|*  
*tena bhārāvataraṇaṃ kariṣyasi bhuvaḥ pitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tadā yāsyāmi golokaṃ tayā sārdhaṃ suniścatam \|*  
*tvayā yaśodayā cā'pi gobairgopībhireva ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhānena tatpatnyā kalāvatyā ca bāndhavaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ ca nandaṃ sānandaṃ yaśodāṃ kathayiṣyasi \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tyaja śokraṃ mahābhāga vrajaiḥ sārdhaṃ vrajaṃ vraja \|*  
*ahamātmā ca sākṣī ca nirliptaḥ sarvajīviṣu \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. О father, I have to be separated from her for a hundred years during which period, I shall relieve the earth of her burden and thereafter I shall proceed to Goloka. This is certain. You yourself, Yashoda, all the cowherds and cowherdesses, Vrsabhanu his wife Kalavati and all other relatives will proceed with me. О Nanda, you convey all this to Yashoda also. Therefore, О virtuous one, now you shed away the grief and move to Vraja. I happen to be the soul of all, the witness of all, pervade in all, but still I remain uninvolved.

## \|\| 73.47-50 \|\|

*jīvo matpratibimbaśca ityevaṃ sarvasaṃmatam \|*  
*prakṛtirmadvikārā ca sā'pyahaṃ prakṛtiḥ svayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*yathā dugdhe ca dhāvalyaṃ na taryorbhaida eva ca \|*  
*yathā jale tathā śaityaṃ yathā vahnau ca dāhikā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yathā''kāśe tathā śabdo bhūmau gandho yathā nṛpa \|*  
*yathā śobhā ca candre ca yathā dinakare prabhā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*yathā dīvastathā''tmāhaṃ tathaiva rādhayā saha \|*  
*tyaja tvaṃ gopikābuddhiṃ rādhāyāṃ mayi putratām \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. Soul is my reflection, this is admitted by all, Prakriti is my deformed form and I alone happen to be the form of Prakriti. О king, as the whiteness cannot be separated from milk and the coolness of the water cannot be separated from it, the instinct of burning cannot be separated from fire, the sound cannot be separated from the sky, the fragrance cannot be separated from the earth, the lustre cannot be separated from the sun or the moon, the soul cannot be separated from the great soul since there is no difference between them. Similarly Radha and myself are inseparable. Therefore you shed away the feeling of being a cowherdess in Radha and myself being a son to you.

## \|\| 73.51-52 \|\|

*ahaṃ sarvasya prabhāvaḥ sā ca prakṛtinīśvarī \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ nanda sānandaṃ madvibhūtiṃ sukhāvahām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*purā yā kathitā tāta brahmaṇe vyaktajanmane \|*  
*kṛṣṇo'haṃ devatānāṃ ca goloke dvibhujaḥ svayam \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. О Nanda, both of us, myself and Radha who represent Prakriti or the cause of everything. Therefore I am going to reveal to you my pleasant grandeur. You kindly listen to me. О father, in the earlier times, I have displayed the same grandeur to Brahma. In the earlier times I happened to be Krishna among the gods who appears in Goloka with two arms.

## \|\| 73.53-60 \|\|

*caturbhujo'haṃ vaikuṇṭhe śivaloke śivaḥ svayam \|*  
*brahmaloke ca brahmā'haṃ sūyastejasvināmaham \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pavitrāṇāmahaṃ vahnirjalameva draveṣu ca \|*  
*indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi samīraḥ śīghragāminām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*yamo'haṃ daṇḍakarta ṇāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham \|*  
*akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi sāmnāṃ ca sāma eva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

*indraścaturdaśendreṣu kubero dhanināmaham \|*  
*īśāno'haṃ dimīśānāṃ vyāpakānāṃ nabhastathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sarvāntarātmā jīveṣu brāhmaṇaścā''śrameṣu ca \|*  
*dhanānāṃ ca ratnamahamamūlyaṃ sarvadurlabham \|\| 57 \|\|*

*taijasānāṃ suvarṇo'haṃ maṇīnāṃ kaustubhaḥ svayam \|*  
*vaiṣṇavānāṃ kumāro'haṃ yogīndrāṇāṃ gaṇeśvaraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*puṣpāṇāṃ pārijāto'haṃ tīrthānāṃ puṣkaraḥ svayam \|*  
*śālagrāmastathā'rcyānāṃ patrāṇāṃ tulasīti ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

*senāpatīnāṃ skando'haṃ lakṣmaṇo'haṃ dhanuṣmatām \|*  
*rājendrāṇāṃ ca rāmo'haṃ nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī \|\| 60 \|\|*

53-60. Similarly in Vaikuntha I reside as Vishnu having four arms, in Shivaloka I reside as Shiva, in Brahmaloka reside as Brahma. Among those having the lustre, I represent the sun, Agni in all the auspicious things, water in all the things which flow, the mind among the organs of senses, Vayu among these moving with speed, Yama among those who provide punishment, Kala among those which cannot be counted, in the letters Samaveda in the Vedas, Indra among the fourteen Indras, Kubera among the rich people, Isana among the Dikpalas, sky among those who are all-pervading, the soul among the creatures and Brahmana among the varnas. In the riches I happen to be the best of gems, gold in the glittering articles, the kaustubha gem among the gems, Sanatkumara among the Vais navas, Ganapati among the Yogmdras, Parijata among the flowers, Puskara among the holy places, Shalagrama among those who are unthinkable, Tulasi leaf among the leaves, Skanda among the army commanders, Laksmana among the archers, Rama among the great kings and the moon among the constellation.

61-70. I happen to be the MargasTrsa among the months, the spring season among the seasons, Sunday among the days, EMdas'i among the tithis, the earth among those who passionately bear everything, mother among all the relatives. Amrta (nectar) among the consumable, ghee among the articles produced from the milk of the cow, kalpavrksa among the trees, Kamadhenu among the cows, Ganga among the rivers which removes the sins of all, the speech among the intellectuals, the pranava among the mantras, the form of seed among the vidyds, the paddy among the crops, plpala among the trees, the one who bestows the mantra among the teachers, Kashyapa among the Prajapati, Garuda among the birds, Ananta among the snakes, the king among the people, Bhrigu among the Brahmarsis, Narada among the sages of the gods, Janaka among the royal sages, Sukra among the great sages, Chitraratha among the Gandharvas, Kapila among the siddhas, Brihaspati among the wise people, Sukra among the poets, Saturn among the planets, Vishvakarma among the architects, lion among the wild animals, Nandlsvara among the bulls, Airavata among the elephants, Gayatri among the metres, Vedas among the scriptures, Varuna among the aquatics, UrvasI among the apsaras, Jalasagara among the waters.

*mātṛkāsu śāntirahaṃ ratiśca sundarīṣu ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*dharmo'haṃ sākṣiṇāṃ madhye saṃdhyā ca vāsareṣu ca \|*  
*deveṣvahaṃ ca māhendo rākṣaseṣu vibhīṣaṇaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*kālāgnirudro rudrāṇāṃ saṃhāro bhairaveṣu ca \|*

*svāyaṃbhuvo manūnāṃ ca munīnāṃ vyāsadevakaḥ \|*

71-80. Sumeru among the mountains, Himalaya among the stores of gems, Durga among the Prakritis, Lakshmi among the goddesses, Satarupa among the women, Radhika of all my beloved's, Savitri among the chaste woman, Prahlada among the daityas, Bali among the valorous people, the sage Narayana among the intellectuals, Hanuman among the monkeys, Arjuna among the Pandavas, Manasa among the daughters of the serpents, Drona among the Vasus, Bharata among the varsas, Kamadeva among the passionate people, Rambha among the passionate women, Goloka among the lakes, which is the best of all. Similarly I happen to be Santi among the matrkas, Rati among the beautiful women, Dharma among the witnesses, Sandhya among the Vasaras, Mahendra among the gods, Vibhlsana among the demons, Kalagni-rudra among the Rudras, Samhara among the Bhairavas, Pancajanya among the conches, forehead among the limbs, Bhagavata among the Puranas, Mahabharata among the history books, Kapila among the Pancaratras, Svayambhuva among the Manus, Vyasadeva among the Munis, Svadha among the spouse and the manes, Svaha among the beloved's of Agni.

## \|\| 73.81-100 \|\|

*yajñānāṃ nājasūyo'haṃ yajñapatnīṣu dakṣiṇā \|*
