*karoti śaśvannyakkāraṃ mahendrasyāmarāvatīm \|*  
*nivasa tvaṃ sudharmāyāṃ māhendre ca kṣaṇe nṛpa \|\| 62 \|\|*

*jambudvīpasthitā bhūpā rājendramaṇḍaleśvarāḥ \|*  
*karaṃ dāsyanti tubhayaṃ ca mahendrāya surā yathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*bhūyājjitaḥ kuberaśca dhanena dhanasaṃpadā \|*  
*tejasā bhāskaraścāpi mahendraḥ saṃpadaḥ tathā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*devā jitā raṇenaiva puṇyena munayo jitāḥ \|*  
*tapasvinaśya tapasā vratīnaśca vratena ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ugrasenasamo rājā na bhūto na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*sabhāyāṃ yasya bhagavānbaladevo mahābalaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*viśvaṃ ca yasya śirasāṃ sahasrāṇaṃ nareśvara \|*  
*ekasmiñśirasi nyastaṃ śūrpe ca sarṣapo yathā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*na hyanantasamo devo balena balavattaraḥ \|*  
*yadguṇānāṃ ca nāstyantastenānantaṃ jagurbudhāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

61-68. You go to the royal palace together with Brahma, gods and the sages beside the Yadavas and reside there. This city of Dvaraka puts Amaravati, the city of Indra to shame. О king, you enter the divine assembly named Sudharma in the auspicious time of Mahendra. The people of Jambudvipa, the great kings, the courtiers and others would give you the taxes as the gods give to Indra. You conquer Kubera in riches, the sun in the lustre, Indra in fortunes, the gods in the battle, the sages in sacredness and the mendicants in tapas besides with vratas, you would excel the vratas (performers). There has been no king like Ugrasena nor would there any such king be in future. In his court the extremely valorous Balarama is present over one of whose thousand heads, the entire globe is lodged like the sheshamum seed in a windowing basket. There is no one else more valorous than Baladeva and there is no end to his virtues. This is the reason the people have given him the name of Ananta.

## \|\| 104.69-78 \|\|

*vasavo'ṣṭau mahābhāgā rudrāśca śaṃkaraṃ vinā \|*  
*balino dvādaśādityā mahendraśca suraiḥ samaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*na samarthā dhruvaṃ jetumugrasenaṃ nṛpeśvaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā prasannavadano nṛpaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*prayayau yādavaiḥ sārdha mahendrabhavanātparam \|*  
*svālayaṃ dvārakāmadhye jvalantaṃ maṇitejasā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sahasraidvaripālaiśca śūlibhirdaṇḍahastakaiḥ \|*  
*niyuktai rakṣitaṃ dvāraṃ dadarśa mānaveśvaraḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*abhyantare ca śibiraṃ dvārebhyaḥ ṣaḍbhya eva ca \|*  
*mandirāṇāṃ ca śatakai ratnānāṃ paribhūṣaṇam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*koṭiṃ mattagajendrāṇāṃ dadarśa gajamandire \|*  
*caturyugaṃ gajaughaṃ gajānāṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*mahābalāṃśca turagānsūryāśvaṃ ca hasanti ye \|*  
*gajendrarājaṃ sarveṣāṃ vāhanānāmapīśvaram \|\| 75 \|\|*

*hasatyairāvataṃ śaśvanmahendrasya ca nārada \|*  
*atyuccairuccaiḥśravamāṃ dadarśa koṭimīpsitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*kharāṇāṃ daśakoṭiṃ ca pādātaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*nirmāṇaṃ ratnasārāṇāṃ tathānāṃ pañcalakṣakam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*pañcalakṣaṃ sārathīnāṃ tatrāśvaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*aśvavāṭaṃ tatsamaṃ ca sudharmāṃ ca sabhāmapi \|\| 78 \|\|*

69-78. The eight Vasus, Rudras, without Shiva, the valorous twelve Adityas and Indra together with all the gods would not be able to over-power Ugrasena. On hearing the words of Krishna, the king started together with all Yadavas. He found his palace in the middle of Dvaraka shining with gems on the gates of which thousands of gods were deputed holding the staff and the trident in their hands. The camp was inside the six gates. There were palaces inlaid with hundreds of precious stones. The king found a crore of intoxicated elephants in the elephant-stable. The number of ordinary elephants ran to four crores. He found very strong horses in the horse-stable, the number of which was six times more than the elephants who could gallop with the speed of with the horse of the sun. О Narada, the herd of those elephants was superior than all the vehicles of Indra and were jeering at Airavata. The king then came across the horses of very high breed of Uccaisarva. Thereafter there were ten crores of donkeys and the number of foot soldiers was six times more than the same, there were five lakhs of chariots built with the best of gems and an equal number of charioteers. The number of horses was six times more then the cavalry men. The king also witnesses the assembly named Sudharma.

## \|\| 104.79-82 \|\|

*dadarśāmyantare ramye devaughamunisaṃyutām \|*  
*vahniśuddhāśukai ramyairbhūṣitāṃ raktakambalaiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanai ramyairbhūṣitāṃ raktapiṅgalaiḥ \|*  
*amūlyaratnanirmāṇavīthīnāṃ tejasojjvalām \|\| 80 \|\|*

*veṣṭitāṃ ca mahābhītaiḥ kiṃkaraiḥ śatakoṭibhiḥ \|*  
*praviveśa sabhāṃ ramyāṃ śrutvā śaṅkhadhvaniṃ śubham \|\| 81 \|\|*

*vādyaṃ ca duṃdubhīnāṃ ca munīnāṃ vedamantrakam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā nṛpaṃ samuttasthau vegena sabalo hariḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

79-82. The assembly which was quite charming to look at, accommodated the gods and the sages. The assembly was issuing lustre like the fire. It had enough of silken clothes of red and yellow colours, besides the lion thrones. It was decorated with the lines of invaluable gems and was surrounded by a hundred crores of disciplined soldiers. At the time of entering into beautiful assembly hall, the conches were blown and drums were beaten. The sages recited the Vedic hymns. Finding the kings arrival, Krishna and Balarama got up from their seats.

## \|\| 104.83-87 \|\|

*brahmā maheśvaraścaiva śeṣaśca devapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*samuttasthuḥ surāḥ sarve munayaśca mahāvratāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*rājendrāścāpi siddhendrā vasudevapurogamāḥ \|*  
*ratnasiṃhāsane ramye cograseno mahābalaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*samuvāsa mahendrasya munīnāmājñayā hareḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ ca gurūṇāṃ ca gargasyāpi tathaiva ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*saptatīrthodakenaiva pūrṇakumbhena nārada \|*  
*jakāra vedamantraiśca nṛpasyāpyabhiṣecanam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*tasmai vastrayugaṃ dattaṃ vahniśuddhaṃ manoharam \|*  
*varuṇena purā dattaṃ kṛṣṇāya paramātmane \|\| 87 \|\|*

83-87. Brahma, Shiva, Shesha, the ascetics, the best of the gods also stood up. All the kings and the siddhas together with Vasudeva also stood up. Thereafter valorous Ugrasena with the permission of Indra, the sages, lord Krishna, the gods and the teacher, also took his seat. О Narada, the coronation of the king was completed with the reciting of the hymns from the Vedas and pouring water from the seven holy places. The king was then offered the two divine garments sanctified by fire which were presented by Varuna to Krishna.

## \|\| 104.88-90 \|\|

*mālyaṃ ca pārijātānāṃ candanaṃ ratnabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*ratnacchatraṃ dadau tasmai baladevo mahābalaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*brahmā kamaṇḍaluṃ caiva śūlaṃ cāpi maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pārvatī ratnamālyaṃ ca hāraṃ ca mālatī satī \|\| 89 \|\|*

*anye devāśca munayo rājendrāḥ siddhapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*yautakaṃ ca dadau tasmai krameṇa ca pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 90 \|\|*

88-90. The valorous Baladeva presented him the chatra of gems, Brahma presented a kamandalu, Shiva the trident, Parvati a garland of gems, the chaste Malatl presented him a garland of flowers. Thereafter several other gods, the sages, the best of the kings and the siddhas also gave their presents to him.

## \|\| 104.91 \|\|

*vasudevo dadau tasmai śubhadaṃ śvetacāmaram \|*  
*pavanena purā dattaṃ kṛṣṇāya paramātmane \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Vasudeva presented him with an auspicious white-fly-whisks, which was presented to Krishna by Vasudeva.

## \|\| 104.92 \|\|

*nando dadau ca surabhiṃ kāmadhenuṃ ca pūjitām \|*  
*yaśodā devakī tasmai ratnaśreṣṭhaṃ dadau mudā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Nanda presented him a Kamadhenu cow. Yashoda and Devaki delightfully gifted him the best of gems.

## \|\| 104.93-99 \|\|

*saptabhiḥ kiṃkaraiścāpi saivitaḥ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*dadhāra cchatramakrūro bhaktyā caivā''jñayā hareḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

*ratnasihāsane ramye dadarśa ratnadarpaṇam \|*  
*atīva puṇyāvāpyaṃ ca hariṇāṃ ca puraskṛtaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*cakruḥ stutiṃ ca bhaṭṭāśca bhiṅukā brāhmaṇāstathā \|*  
*daduḥ śubhāśiṣaṃ tasmai devāśca munayastathā \|\| 95 \|\|*

*brahmaṇemyo dadau rājā ratnakoṭiṃ ca bhaktataḥ \|*  
*bhaṭṭabhyo ratnaśatakaṃ bhikṣukemyastathaiva ca \|\| 96 \|\|*

*abhiṣicya nṛpendraṃ ca devāṃśca munipuṃgavān \|*  
*saṃpūjya brāhmaṇāṃścāpi bhaṭṭānbhikṣuṃ dvijaṃ gurum \|\| 97 \|\|*

*svālayaṃ ca yayuḥ sarve yādavāśca mudā'nvitāḥ \|*  
*ye ye hareḥ pārṣadāśca te sarve svālayaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*prabhāte cā''yayuḥ sarve sudharmā ca sabhāṃ hareḥ \|*  
*namaskṛtya nṛpendraṃ ca coṣuḥ sarve ca saṃsadi \|\| 99 \|\|*

93-99. The seven attendants started serving him moving the white fly-whisks, Akrura with the permission of Shri Krishna held chatra on the head of the king. The king while seated on the gem-studded lion throne looked at the mirror which could be achieved by performing several good deeds. Thereafter, Shri Krishna offered a present. The Bhdta then started praising the king while the Brahmanas, the gods and the sages showered their blessings on him. The king distributed with great devotion, crores of diamonds, together with the bhatas and the beggars, all the people of the race of Yadu after attending the coronation of the king adored the gods. The sages, BrShmana, the bhatas, the beggars and the teachers went back to their respective abodes. All the attendants of Krishna also went back to their respective abodes. The next morning all of them came to attend the court named Sudharma. In the assembly they bowed before the king and took their seats.

## Chapter 105

## \|\| 105.1-2 \|\|

*atha pañcādhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca atha vaidarbharājendro mahābalaparākram \|*  
*vidarbhadeśe puṇyāśca satyaśīlaśca bhīṣmakaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*rājā nārāyaṇāṃśaśca dātā ca sarvasaṃpadām \|*  
*dharmiṣṭhasca garīyāṃśca variṣṭhaśṭāpi pūjitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Narayana said – The king Bhismaka was possessing immense prowess and was quite noble and truthful king of Vidarbha country. He was born of the arhsha of Vishnu and was the bestower of all riches, quite religious, the best and was quite adorable.

## \|\| 105.3-5 \|\|

*tasya kanyā mahālakṣmī rukmiṇī yoṣitāṃ varā \|*  
*atīva sundarī ramyā ramā rāmāsu pūjitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*navayauvanasaṃpannā ratnābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*taptakāñcanavarṇābhā tejasojjvalitā satī \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śuddhasattvasvarūpā sā satyaśīlā pativratā \|*  
*śāntā dāntā nitāntā cāpyanantaguṇaśālinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. He had a daughter named Rukmini who had the form of Maha-Lakshmi. She was the best of the damsels, extremely beautiful, charming, quite passionate, adored by the damsels, quite youthful, adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments, having the complexion of molten gold, illumining, chaste, the form of auspicious tattva truthful, pious, peaceful, well disciplined and possessed all the qualities.

## \|\| 105.6-7 \|\|

*indrāṇī varuṇānī ca candranārī ca rohiṇī \|*  
*kuberapatnī sūryastrī svāhā śāntā kalāvatī \|\| 6 \|\|*

*anyāsu ramaṇīyāsu śreṣṭhā ca sumanoharā \|*  
*rukmiṇyā bhīṣmakanyāyāḥ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The goddesses like IndranI, VarunanI, the spouse of moon Rohini, the spouse of Kubera, Svaha the spouse of Surya, Santa, Kalavati and all other beautiful woman did not compare to even one-sixteenth part of Rukmini the daughter of Bhismaka.

## \|\| 105.8-10 \|\|

*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājarājendro vālakrīḍāratāṃ parām \|*  
*bālāṃ suśobhāṃ kurvantīṃ yathā'bhreṣu vidhoḥ kalām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śaratpūrṇenduśobhāḍhyāṃ śaratkamalalocanām \|*  
*vivāhayogyāṃ yuvatīṃ lajjānamrānanāṃ śubham \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sahasā cintito dharmo dharmaśīlaśca suvrataḥ \|*  
*sutāṃ papraccha putrāṃśca brāhmaṇāṃśca purohitān \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The king Bhismaka witnessed his daughter engaged in sport like the ray of the moon with the other girls, she possessed the lustre of the full moon of the winter season, her eyes were like the lotus flower of the winter season. She became youthful and fit for marriage. She was filled with shyness, humility and was quite chaste. Having a look at her the religious king who performed all the best of the vratas felt worried. He then consulted his daughter, the sons and the family priest.

## \|\| 105.11 \|\|

*kaṃ vṛṇomi sutārdha ca varāhaṃ pravaraṃ varam \|*  
*muniputraṃ devaputraṃ rājendrasutamīpsitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Bhismaka said – I would like to have a suitable groom for my daughter. Whom should I select, whether, he should be a prince or the son of great king?

## \|\| 105.12-14 \|\|

*vivāhayogyā kanyā me vardhamānā manoharā \|*  
*śīghraṃ paśya varaṃ yāgyaṃ navayauvanasaṃsthitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dharmaśīlaṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ nārāyaṇaparāyaṇam \|*  
*mahākulaprasūtaṃ ca sarvatraiva pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śāntaṃ dāntaṃ kṣamāśīla guṇinaṃ cirajīvinam \|*  
*mahākulaprasūtaṃ ca sarvatraiva pratiṣṭhitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. My growing daughter has achieved the age of puberty, therefore a groom for her should be searched immediately. Such a groom should be quite young, the religious minded, truthful, devoted to Vishnu, well-versed in the Vedas and post-Vedic literature, an, intelligent one, beautiful, pious, peaceful, large hearted should believe in forgiveness, all virtuous, having long life and the one having been born in the high race and well-known everywhere.

## \|\| 105.15 \|\|

*karoṣi rājaputraṃ cedraṇaśāstraviśāradam \|*  
*mahārathaṃ pratāpārhaṃ raṇamūrdhni ca susthiram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In case a prince is selected then he should be well-versed in the treatises on welfare, a great charioteer, glorious and the one who should be able to face the war courageously.

## \|\| 105.16-18 \|\|

*karoṣi devaputraṃ ceddevaṃ guṇayutaṃ tathā \|*  
*karoṣi muniputraṃ ceccaturvedaviśāradam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vāvadūkaṃ vicārajñaṃ siddhānteṣu nitāntakam \|*  
*nṛpendravacanaṃ śrutvā tamuvāca muneḥ sutaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*gotamasya śatānando vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ \|*  
*āptaḥ pravaktā vijñaśca dharmī kulapurohitaḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ sarvatattvajño niṣṇātaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. In case the son of the god is selected then he should be all virtuous. In case the son of an ascetic is selected then he should be well-versed in all the four Vedas, the best orator, a deep thinker and should be the one following all the principles. On listening to the words of the king, Satananda, the son of Gautama who was well-versed in the Vedas and never spoke anything otherwise, the best of orators, well-read, quite a religious one, the family priest and the one who know all the tattvas on earth and was quite efficient in performing all the deeds, spoke to the king.

## \|\| 105.19 \|\|

*śatānanda uvāca rājendra tvaṃ ca dharmajño dharmaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*pṛrvākhyānaṃ ca vedoktaṃ kathayāmi niśāmaya \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Satananda said – О king, you are well-versed in all the religious practices and the religious scriptures, I am going to narrate to you and old story of the Vedas which you kindly listen.

## \|\| 105.20-22 \|\|

*bhuvo bhārāvataraṇe svayaṃ nārāyaṇo bhuvi \|*  
*vasudevasutaḥ śrīmānparibūrṇatamaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vidhātuśca vidhātā ca brahmeśaśeṣavanditaḥ \|*  
*jyotiḥsvarūpaḥ paramo bhaktānugrahavigrahaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*paramātmā ca sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ prakṛteḥ paraḥ \|*  
*nirliptaśca nirīhaptaśca sākṣī ca sarvakarmaṇām \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Narayana himself has incarnated on earth in order to relieve her of the burden. О lord, the son of Vasudeva complete in all respect, is the creator of Brahma, adored by Shiva, Ananta and others, the form of eternal flame, the best of all, the one who takes to human form for the sake of his devotees, the soul of all the creatures, beyond Prakriti, unattached, uninvolved and the witness of all the deeds.

## \|\| 105.23-24 \|\|

*rājendra tasmai kanyāṃ ca paripūrṇatamāya ca \|*  
*dattvā yāsyasi golokaṃ pitṝṇāṃ śatakaiḥ saha \|\| 23 \|\|*

*labha sārūpyamuktiṃ ca kanyā dattvāṃ paratra ca \|*  
*ihaiva sarvapūjyaśca bhava viśvagurorguruḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. О best of the kings, by offering your daughter to him you would go to Goloka together with hundreds of your ancestors. By giving away the daughter to him, you would achieve moksa after death, enjoying all the pleasures on earth.

## \|\| 105.25 \|\|

*sarvasvaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā mahālakṣmīṃ ca rukmiṇīm \|*  
*samarpaṇaṃ kuruvibho kuruṣva janmakhaṇḍanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. You give away Rukmini, the form of Maha-Lakshmi to him with the best of offering. О virtuous one, by doing so you will never have to be reborn on earth.

## \|\| 105.26-28 \|\|

*vidhātā nikhito rājansaṃbandhaḥ sarvasaṃmataḥ \|*  
*dvārakānagare kṛṣṇaṃ śīghraṃ prasthāpaya dvijam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kṛtvā śubhakṣaṇaṃ tūrṇa sarveṣāmapi saṃmatam \|*  
*ānīya paramātmānaṃ bhaktānugrahavigraham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dhyānānurodhahetuṃ ca nityadehamanuttamam \|*  
*dṛṣṭimātrātkuru nṛpa svajanmakarmakhaṇḍanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. О king, this relationship has already been ordained by Brahma, therefore, you send a Brahmana to Dvaraka to meet Krishna in this connection quite expeditiously. After consulting all, settling, about the auspicious time, you call for Krishna the supreme soul, who has taken to human form in order to grace his devotees. О king, at the mere sight of Krishna, the deeds of the human being performed during the past birth get destroyed.

## \|\| 105.29-39 \|\|

*yaṃ na jānanti catvāro vedāḥ saṃtaśca devatāḥ \|*  
*siddhendrāśca munīndrāśca devā brahmādayastathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*dhyāyante dhyānapūtāśca yogino na vidanti yam \|*  
*sarasvatī jaḍībhūtā vedāḥ śāstrāṇiyāni ca \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sahasravaktraḥ śeṣaśca pañcavaktraḥ sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*caturmukho jagaddhātā kumāraḥ kārtikastathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ṛṣayo munayaścaiva bhaktāḥ paramavaiṣṇavāḥ \|*  
*akṣamāḥ stavane yasya dhyānāsādhyaśca yoginām \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bālako'haṃ mahārāja tadguṇaṃ kathayāmi kim \|*  
*śatānandavacaḥ śrutvā praphullavadano nṛpaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*āniṅganaṃ dadau tasmai samutthāya javena ca \|*  
*nānāratnaṃ muvarṇa ca vastraṃ ca ratnabhūṣaṇam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dadau tasmai pradānaṃ ca prasādasumukho nṛpaḥ \|*  
*gajendra turagaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rathaṃ ca maṇinirmitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ratnasihāsanaṃ ramyaṃ dhanaṃ ca vipulaṃ tathā \|*  
*bhūmiṃ ca sarvasasyāḍhyāṃ śaśvadvṛṣṭikarīṃ śubhām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*akṛṣṭasādhyāṃ pūjyāṃ ca grāmaṃ sarvapraśaṃsitam \|*  
*etasminnantare rukmiścukopa nṛpanandanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kampito'dharmayuktaśca raktāsyo raktalocanaḥ \|*  
*uvāca pitaraṃ vripraṃ sabhāyāmasthirastadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*utyāya tiṣṭhanpurataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca sabhāsadām \|\| 39 \|\|*

29-39. The supreme soul who is adored by all the Vedas, the sages, the gods, the siddhas, the mendicant and Brahma do not know him truly, the one who is adored by the great yogis with deep meditation but are unable to achieve him. By reciting whose glory even Sarasvati becomes dumb. Even the Vedas, scriptures, Shesha with hundred hoods, Shiva with five face, Brahma with four faces, Karttikeya with six faces, the sages, devotees and the Vaishnavas are unable to recite his glory and are unable to achieve him. He is beyond the yogis and the siddhas. О king, what can I speak about his qualities, being merely a boy? On hearing the words of Satananda, the face of the king became delightful, he stood up with force and embraced the Brahmana. The king then with the delightful mind presented him with elephants, horses, the best of chariot studded with gems, the charming lion throne, enough of riches and the -land which produced several types of cereals remained wet with the rain water and producer enough of cereals when ploughed. He therefore gave away in charities several villages with cultivative lands. In the meantime, RukmT the son of the king felt enraged since he was quite irreligious, he started trembling, his face and eyes became red. Becoming unstable, he stood before all the members present there and spoke to his father as well as the Brahmana.

## \|\| 105.40 \|\|

*rukmiruvāca śrṛṇu rājendra vacanaṃ hitaṃ tathayaṃ praśaṃsitam \|*  
*tyaja vākyaṃ bhikṣukāṇāṃ lobhināṃ krodhināmaho \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. RukmT said – О great king, you listen to my beneficial, truthful and praise-worthy words, you should not care for the words of the beggar, the greedy and the people filled with anger.

## \|\| 105.41-42 \|\|

*nartakānāṃ ca vaiśyānāṃ bhaṭṭānāmarthināmapi \|*  
*kāyasthānāṃ ca bhikṣūṇāmasatyaṃ vacanaṃ sadā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ghaṭakānāṃ nāṭakānāṃ strīlubdhānā ca kāminām \|*  
*daridrāṇāṃ ca mūrkhāṇāṃ stutipūrva vacaḥ sadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Because the words of the dancers, the Vaishyas, bards, the beggars, kayasthas and the beggars are always full of falsehood. The words of messengers, a actors, lustful, passionate, pauper and the foolish are always filled with sycophancy.

## \|\| 105.43 \|\|

*nihatya kālayavanaṃ rājendraṃ dūrato bhiyā \|*  
*uvāyena mahābāho labdhaṃ kṛṣṇena taddhanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О valorous one, the terrified Krishna deceitfully took away the riches of Kalayavana and than killed him.

## \|\| 105.44 \|\|

*dvārakāyā dhanī kṛṣṇo yavanasya dhanena ca \|*  
*jarāsaṃdhabhayenaiva samudrābhyantare gṛhī \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Krishna is known as the wealthy person in Dvaraka. He has built his house in the sea-bed, getting terrified from Jarasandha.

## \|\| 105.45 \|\|

*jarāsaṃdhaśataṃ caiva kṣaṇenaiva ca līlayā \|*  
*kṣamo'haṃ hantumekākī rājñaścānyasya kā kathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I am myself competent enough to kill hundreds of Jarasandhas playfully in a moment, what to speak of others kings.

## \|\| 105.46 \|\|

*durvāsasaśca śiṣyo'haṃ raṇaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*dhruvaṃ bhīṣmaka tenaiva viśvaṃ saṃhartumīśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. I am the pupil of Durvasa and am well-versed in the welfare. О Bhlsmaka, I am therefore quite competent enough to kill the entire universe in a movement.

## \|\| 105.47 \|\|

*matsamaḥ parśurāmaśca śiśupālaśca matsamaḥ \|*  
*sakhā ca balavāñchūraḥ svargaṃ jetuṃ sa ca kṣamaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Only Parashurama and my friend Sis'upala could be equated with my prowess. Both of them are competent enough to conquer the heaven.

## \|\| 105.48-53 \|\|

*mahendraṃ sagaṇaṃ jetumahamīśaḥ kṣaṇena ca \|*  
*jitvā yuddhe jarāsaṃdhaṃ durbalaṃ yoginaṃ nṛpa \|\| 48 \|\|*

*ahaṃkārayutaḥ kṛṣṇo pīraṃ svaṃ manyate dhiyā \|*  
*yadyāyāsyati madgrāmaṃ vivāhaṃ kartumīpsitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*dhruvaṃ prasthāpayiṣyāmi kṣaṇena yamamandiram \|*  
*aho nandasya vaiśyasya tasmai gorakṣakāya ca \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sākṣājjārāya gopīnāṃ gopālocchiṣṭabhojine \|*  
*karoṣi kanyāsvīkāraṃ devayogyāṃ ca rukmiṇīm \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dātumicchasi vākyena bhiṅukasya dvijasya ca \|*  
*rājendra buddhihīno'si vacanādvadga(durba) lasya ca \|\| 52 \|\|*

*mā rājaputro māśūro ma kulīnaśca mā śuciḥ \|*  
*mā dātā mā dhanāḍhyaśca mā yogyo mā jitendriyaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

48-53. I am competent enough to over-power Indra in a movement with his entire army. О king, by conquering Jarasandha in the battle-fields Krishna has become arrogant and considers himself quite valorous by means of his own intelligence. In case he passes through my village for the purpose of marriage then I will surely dispatch him to the abode of Yama. You intend to give away Rukmini in marriage at the instance of the beggar Brahmana, to Krishna the son of Nanda the cowherd, who got his cows grazed by him, he is the one who is the lover of the cowherdesses and used to eat the left-over of the cowherds. О great king, you are devoid of wisdom because you want to act on the advise of a weal person. Krishna is neither a prince nor a valorous one or born in a spotless family. He is neither auspicious nor the giver of charity, nor a rich person or well disciplined.

## \|\| 105.54 \|\|

*kanyāṃ dehi suputrāya śiśupālāya bhūmipa \|*  
*balena rudratuṣṭāya rājendratanayāya ca \|\| 54\|\|*

54\. О king, you give your daughter to Sisupala who is born of good family who had satisfied Shiva with his prowess and is the son of great king.

## \|\| 105.55 \|\|

*nimantraṇaṃ kuru nṛpa nānādeśabhavānnṛpān \|*  
*bāndhavāṃśca munīndrāṃśca patradvārā tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. You immediately send imitation letters to all the kings in several countries besides the relatives and the sages.

## \|\| 105.56-63 \|\|

*aṅgaṃ kaliṅgaṃ magadhaṃ saurāṣṭraṃ valkalaṃ varam \|*  
*rāṭaṃ varendraṃ vaṅgaṃ ca gurjaraṭiṃ ca paṭheram \|\| 56 \|\|*

*mahārāṣṭraṃ virāṭaṃ ca mudgalaṃ ca muraṅgakam \|*  
*bhallakaṃ gallakaṃ kharva durgaṃ prasthāpaya dvijam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*ghṛtakulyāsahasraṃ ca madhukulyāsahasrakam \|*  
*dadhikulyāsahasraṃ ca dugdhakulyāsahasrakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tailakulyāpañcaśataṃ guḍakulyādvilakṣakam \|*  
*śarkarāṇāṃ rāśiśataṃ miṣṭānnānāṃ caturguṇam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yavagodhūmacūrṇānāṃ piṣṭarāśiśataṃ śatam \|*  
*pṛthukānāṃ rāśilakṣamannānāṃ ca caturguṇam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*gavāṃ lakṣaṃ chedanaṃ ca hariṇānāṃ dvilakṣakam \|*  
*caturlakṣaṃ śaśānāṃ ca kūrmāṇāṃ ca tathā kuru \|\| 61 \|\|*

*daśalakṣaṃ chāgalānāṃ bheṭānāṃ taccaturguṇam \|*  
*parvaṇi grāmadevyai ca baliṃ dehi ca bhaktitaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ pakvamāṃsaṃ ca bhojanārtha ca kāraya \|*  
*paripūrṇa vyañjanānāṃ sāmagrīṃ kuru bhūmipa \|\| 63 \|\|*

56-63. You despatched the letters of invitation to Angadesa, Kalinga country, Magadha, Saurastra, Valkala, Ratadesa, the best of Vangadesha, Virat, Mudgala, Murangaka, Bhallaka, Gallaka, Kharvadesa and Durgadesa, by sending Brahmana there. You should arrange for a thousand canals of ghee, a thousand canals of honey, a thousand of curd and a thousand of milk besides five hundred canals of oil, two lake canals of GUI, five hundred heaps of sugar, two thousand heaps of sweet and hundred heaps of the wheat-flour, four lakes heaps of boiled paddy, the four lake heaps of cereals, a lake of rabies and an equal number of tortoise, ten lakes of he-goats and four times the number of sheep, the sacrifice should be offered to the village goddess with devotion, the cooked meat of the animal should be got ready. The vegetables should also be collected in large number.

## \|\| 105.64-68 \|\|

*atha śrutvā ca tadvākyaṃ rājendraḥ sapurohitaḥ \|*  
*cakāra mantraṇāṃ tūrṇa nirjane mantriṇā saha \|\| 64 \|\|*

*dvijaṃ prasthāpayāmāsa dvārakāṃ yogyamīpsitam \|*  
*kṛtvā ca śubhalagnaṃ ca sarveṣāmabhivāñchitam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*rājā saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro babhūva satvaraṃ mṛdā \|*  
*nimantraṇaṃ ca sarvatra cakāra ca sutājñayā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*vipraḥ sudharmāṃ saṃprāpya nṛpairdevaiśca veṣṭitām \|*  
*pradadī patrikāṃ bhadrāmugrasenāya bhūbhṛte \|\| 67 \|\|*

*praphullavadano rājā śrutvā patraṃ sumaṅgalam \|*  
*suvarṇānāṃ sahasraṃ ca brāhmaṇebhyo dadau mudā \|\| 68 \|\|*

64-68. After listening to the words of Rukml, the king consulted in secrecy the family priest, he than sent a competent Brahmana to Dvaraka and keeping in view the auspicious time, the king arranged for the festivities, as desired by his son the king despatched invitation letters to several places. The Brahmana presented the welfare letter to the king who was seated in the assembly of the kings and gods, named Sudharma. Coming to know about the welfare letter, the face of the king was delighted. He delightfully gave away to the Brahmanas a thousand gold coins.

## \|\| 105.69-74 \|\|

*duṃdubhiṃ vādayāmāsa dvārakāyāṃ ca sarvataḥ \|*  
*devānmunīnnṛpāṃścaiva jñātivargāśca bāndhavān \|\| 69 \|\|*

*bhaṭṭāṃśca bhikṣukāṃścaiva bhojayāmāsa sādaram \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇasya sṛveṣaṃ ca kārayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*atīva ramyamatulaṃ treṣu lokeṣu dulrabham \|*  
*yātrāṃ ca kārayāmāsa jagatāṃ pravaraṃ varam \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vedamantreṇa ramyeṇa māhendre sumanohare \|*  
*ādau brahmā rathasthaśca sāvitryā sahito yayau \|\| 72 \|\|*

*rathasyaśca mahāhṛṣṭo bhavānyā ca bhavaḥ svayam \|*  
*śeṣaścāpi dineśaśca gaṇeśaścāpi kārtikaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*mahendraścatathā candro varuṇaḥ pavanastathā \|*  
*kuberaśca yamo vahnirīśāno'pi yayau mudā \|\| 74 \|\|*

69-74. The big drams were beaten in the whole of Dvaraka, the gods, the sages, the kings, the relatives, the bards, the beggars were served with food with devotion. Shri Krishna was clad in the best of garments which were quite channing and incomparable in the three worlds. Thereafter the marriage procession was taken but to be the best is the three worlds. During the marriage procession the hymns from the Vedas were recited, starting in the Mahendra-yoga. Brahma together with Savitri were mounted on a chariots and moved ahead of all. The delightful Shiva with Parvati also moved on the chariot, followed by Ananta, Shesha, Surya, Ganesha, Karttikeya, Indra,

## \|\| 105.75 \|\|

*devānāṃ ca trikoṭyaśca munīnāṃ ṣaṣṭikoṭayaḥ \|*  
*rājendrāṇāṃ trilakṣaṃ ca śvetacchatraṃ trilakṣakam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The three crores of gods, six crores of the sages, six lakhs of king and three lakhs of white chatras were carried in the procession.

## \|\| 105.76 \|\|

*ugraseno babhau rājā nakṣatreṣu yathā śaśī \|*  
*yayau prasannavadanaḥ kuṇḍinābhimukho balī \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. In the meantime the king appeared glorious like the moon among the constellations. The valorous king delightfully moved towards Kundinapura.

## \|\| 105.77-79 \|\|

*ratnanirmāṇayānena baladevo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*vasudevaścoddhavaśca nando'krūraśca sātyakiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*gopālā yādavendrāśca candravaṃśyāśca te yayuḥ \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭrasutāḥ sarve duryodhanapulogamāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhirastathā bhīmaḥ phālguno nakulastathā \|*  
*sahadevaśca yānaiśca prayayuḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. The valorous Baladeva was mounted on a gem-studded vehicle. Then Vasudeva, Uddhava, Nanda, Akrara, Satyaki, the cowherds, the king Yadavas, the king of the lunar race, Duryodhana and others besides Dhrtarastra also moved on. Then Yudhisthira, Bhlma, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva moved on delightfully in a vehicle.

## \|\| 105.80-81 \|\|

*bhīṣmo droṇaśca karṇaścāpyaśvatthāmā mahābalaḥ \|*  
*kṛpācāryaśca śakuniḥ śalyaścaprayayau mudā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*bhaṭānāṃ ca trikoṭyaśca viprāṇāṃ śatakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*saṃnyāsināṃ sahasraṃ ca yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Bhlsma, Drona, Kama, valorous Asvatthama, Kipacarya, Sakuni and Salya moved on delightfully, three crores of warriors, hundreds crores of Brahmanas, a thousand ascetics, yogis and Brahmacdris also moved on with the procession.

## \|\| 105.82-86 \|\|

*dvisahasraṃ jitakrodhāścāvadhūtāstathaiva ca \|*  
*utpalānāṃ sahasraṃ ca sahasraṃ puṣpakāriṇām \|\| 82 \|\|*

*nānāśirpakarāścaiva vicitraṃ citrameva ca \|*  
*lakṣaṃ ca vādyabhāṇḍānāṃ nartakānāṃ ca lakṣakam \|\| 83 \|\|*

*gandharvāṇāṃ gāyakānāṃ lakṣameva tu nārada \|*  
*tatra kalpe bhaktyeva gandharvaścopabarhaṇaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*pañcāśatkāminībhiśca tvameva teṣu madhyagaḥ \|*  
*vidyādharīṇāṃ lakṣaṃ ca lakṣamapsarasāṃ tathā \|\| 85 \|\|*

*kinnarāṇāṃ trilakṣaṃ cagandharvāṇāṃ trilakṣakam \|\| 86 \|\|*

82-86. Two thousand sages who had controlled their anger, the Avadhutas also moved on together with a thousand carriers of the lotus flowers and a thousand carriers of the other flowers also moved on. Many of the artisans who could create beautiful paintings also moved on. The processions had a lakh of musical instruments as lakh of Gandharva and the singers. О Narada, during that of the time you were born as Gandharva named Upabarhana moving with fifty. damsels. The procession also included a lakh of Vidyadharls, a lakh of apsaras, a lakh of Kinnaras and three lakh of Gandharvas

## Chapter 106

## \|\| 106.1-3 \|\|

*atha paḍadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥnārāyaṇa uvāca etasminnantare nājā kakudmī ca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*varārthaṃ kanyakāyāśca brahmalokātsamāgataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pradadau revatīṃ kanyāṃ śaśvatsusthirayauvanām \|*  
*amūlyaratnabhūṣāḍhyā triṣu lokeṣu durlabhām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*balāya baladevāya saṃpradānena kautukāt \|*  
*vayo yasyā gataṃ satye yugānāṃ saptaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Narayana said – In the meantime the valorous king, Kakudmi arrived from Brahmaloka in search for a suitable groom for his daughter. He gave away in marriage his daughter named Revati who possessed beauty unequal in the three worlds, adorned with all the ornaments, having quite a youthful body to Baladeva quite playfully. She was born in Satyayuga and had seen twenty seven yugas.

## \|\| 106.4-7 \|\|

*dattvā kanyāṃ vidhānena munidevendrasaṃsadi \|*  
*gajendrāṇāṃ trilakṣaṃ ca jāmātre yautukaṃ dadau \|\| 4 \|\|*

*daśalakṣaṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ rathānāṃ lakṣameva ca \|*  
*ratnālaṃkārayuktānāṃ dāsīnāṃ cāpi lakṣakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*maṇilakṣaṃ ratnalakṣaṃ svarṇakoṭiṃ ca sādaram \|*  
*vahniśuddhāṃśukaṃ ramyaṃ muktāmāṇikyahīrakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dattavā kanyāṃ ca rājendo balāya balaśāline \|*  
*ratnendrasārayānena taiḥ sārdha kuṇḍinaṃ yayau \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. He gave away his daughter in marriage to Balarama in the presence of the sages, gods and Indra and also gave away three lakhs of elephant in dowry. The dowry included ten lakhs of horses, a lakh of chariots, a lakh of slave-girls adorned with the gem-studded ornaments, a lakh of diamonds, a lakh of gems, a crores of gold coins, beautiful costumes sanctified by fire, the jewels, rubies and other diamonds. The king Kakudmi handing on his daughter Revati in marriage to Balarama mounted on a gem-studded chariot and went back to Kundinapura.

## \|\| 106.8-9 \|\|

*athāntare ca nirbandhe sāṅge maṅgalakarmaṇi \|*  
*revatīṃ veśayāmāsa yoṣitāṃ kamalākalām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*devakī rohiṇī caiva yaśodā nandagehinī \|*  
*aditiśca ditiḥ śāntirjayaṃ kṛtvā ca mandiram \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. After the completion of the marriage, Devaki, Rohini, Yashoda, Aditi, Diti entered the house together with Revati who was born out of the amsa of Lakshmi.

## \|\| 106.10 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānbhojayāmāsa dadau tebhyo dhanaṃ mudā \|*  
*maṅgalaṃ kārayāmāsa vasudevasya vallabhā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Devaki the spouse of Vasudeva served the Brahmanas with food and the riches, performing the welfare ceremony.

## \|\| 106.11 \|\|

*atha devāśca munayo rājendraḥ kaṭakaiḥ saha \|*  
*saṃprāpurlīlāmātreṇa kuṇḍinaṃ nagaraṃ mudā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereafter the gods, the sages, the king with their armies delightfully reached the city of Kundinapura.

## \|\| 106.12-14 \|\|

*dadṛśurnagaraṃ sarve hyatīva sumanoharam \|*  
*saptabhiḥpariśābhiśca gabhīrābhiśca veṣṭitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prākāraiḥ saptabhiryuktaṃ dvārāṇāṃ śatakaistathā \|*  
*nānāratnaiśca maṇibhirnirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nagarasya bahirdvāraṃ dadṛśurvarayātriṇaḥ \|*  
*rakṣitaṃ rakṣakaiḥ sārdha caturbhiśca mahārathaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The four warriors guarding the gate included Rukml, Sisupala, valorous Dantavaktra and Salva who was well-versed in the warfare as well as illusion, the prince Rukmi was anxious for a war holding all the weapons. He was enraged finding the army of Krishna and then hearing at the gods and the sages, he spoke aloud harsh words, which were echoed in the sky.

## \|\| 106.15-17 \|\|

*rukmiśca śiśupālaśca dantavaktro mahābalī \|*  
*śālvo māyāvināṃ śreṣṭho yuddhaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nānāśāsratraistathā'śtraiśca rathasthaśca raṇonmukhaḥ \|*  
*vilokya kṛṣṇasainyaṃ ca cukopa nṛpanandanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*uvāca niṣṭhuraṃ vākyaṃ śrutitīkṣmaṃ suduṣkaram \|*  
*upahāsya munīndrāṃśca devāṃśca munipuṃgavān \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Rukml said – The deeds performed at a time or the moves of the destiny cannot be stopped by anyone otherwise what to speak in the assembly of the gods.

## \|\| 106.18 \|\|

*rukmiruvāca aho kālakṛtaṃ karma daivaṃ ca kena vāryate \|*  
*kiṃvā'haṃ kathayiṣyāmi devendrāṇāṃ ca saṃsadi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In order to marry RukminT, the beautiful damsel who is suitable for the gods, a cowherds son of Nanda is arriving with the sages.

## \|\| 106.19 \|\|

*grahītuṃ rukmiṇīṃ kanyāṃ devayogyāṃ manoharām \|*  
*āyāti devairmunibhirnandasya paśurakṣakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The cowherds is the lover of the cowherdesses and consumes always the left-over of the cowherds, his caste is unknown nor does he know anything about the food or the love-making.

## \|\| 106.20 \|\|

*sākṣājjāraśca gopīnāṃ gopocchiṣṭānnabhojanaḥ \|*  
*jāteśca nirmayo nāsti bhakṣyamaithunayostathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Everybody found the city to be quite beautiful which was surrounded by seven deep moats and seven boundary walls with hundred gates. Vishvakarma had built the outer gate of the city with various gems and jewels which was witnessed by all the people of the marriage party. The gate was guarded by four great warriors.

## \|\| 106.21 \|\|

*kiṃ nu rājendraputraśca kiṃ nu vā muniputrakaḥ \|*  
*vasudevaḥ kṣatriyaśca bhakṣaṇaṃ vaiśyamandire \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He is neither the son of a king nor a sage, he was born of Vasudeva, Kshatriya and was brought up by a Vaishya.

## \|\| 106.22 \|\|

*śiśukāle ca strīhatyā kṛtā'nena durātmanā \|*  
*kubjā mṛtā ca saṃbhogādvāsasā rajako mṛtaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The wicked person killed a woman during his childhood. By enjoying the conjugal pleasures With him Kubja died, together with the washerman.

## \|\| 106.23 \|\|

*rājendrasya vadhe duṣṭo brahmahatyāṃ labheddhruvam \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ ca dharmiṣṭhaḥ sadyaḥ kaṃso nipātitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By killing a king one earns Brahmahatya and this Krishna killed the religious king Kamsa in Mathura.

## \|\| 106.24 \|\|

*śālva uvāca yaduktaṃ rukmiṇā devāḥ kimasatyaṃ ca tatra vai \|*  
*ko vā'yaṃ rukmiṇībhartā nandasya paśurakṣakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Salva said – О god. there is nothing untrue in whatever has been spoken by Rukmi, how can the cowherd of Nanda become the husband of Rukmini.

## \|\| 106.25 \|\|

*śiśupāla uvāca aho bhuvi kimāścarya devā brahmādayastathā \|*  
*munīndrā brahmaṇaḥ putrāścā''yayurmānavājñayā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Sis'upala said – what more surprise could be there in the universe that Brahma and other gods; and the sons to Brahma have arrived here at the command of a human being.

## \|\| 106.26-27 \|\|

*dantavaktra uvāca saṃtataṃ brāhmaṇā lubdhā devāśca bhaktavatsalāḥ \|*  
*āyayurbrahmaputrāśca nandaputrājñayā katham \|\| 26 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ ca vacanaṃ śrutvā cukopa devasaṃdhakaḥ \|*  
*munirājendrasaṃghaśca lāṅgalītyādayastathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Dantavaktra said – A Brahmana is always greedy and the gods are always graceful to the devotees but why have the sons of Brahma arrived here at the command of the son of Nanda? On hearing the words of these people, all the gods, the sages and the kings besides Balarama were enraged.

## Chapter 107

## \|\| 107.1 \|\|

*atha saptādhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca atha kopapītaśca baladevo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*halena rukmiyānaṃ ca babhañja munipuṃgava \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narayana said – О sage thereafter, the valorous Baladeva broke the chariot of Rukml with the plough.

## \|\| 107.2-3 \|\|

*ghoṭakānsārathiṃ caiva nihatya jagatīpatiḥ \|*  
*bhumiṣṭhaṃ cāpi pāpiṣṭhaṃ rukmiṃ hantuṃ jagāma saḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rukmī ca śarajālena vārayāmāsa līlayā \|*  
*nāgāstraṃ yojayāmāsa baddhuṃ halinamīśvaram \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The valorous Baladeva who happened to be the lord of the universe after breaking to pieces, the chariot and the horses besides the charioteer of Rukml, rushed towards him in order to kill him. Rukml on his part prevented the advance of Balarama by shooting a number of arrows and thought of capturing Balarama with the use of Nagastra.

## \|\| 107.4-5 \|\|

*nāgāstraṃ gāruḍenaiva saṃjahāra halī svayam \|*  
*jagrāha kopādrukmī ca paraṃ pāśupataṃ mune \|\| 4 \|\|*

*avyarthaṃ vairimarda ca śatasūryasamaprabham \|*  
*abhito halinā rukmī jṛmbhaṇāstreṇa jṛmbhitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Balabhadra himself shot Garudastra in order to destroy the Nagastra. О sage, in rage Rukml took out the Pasupata weapon on which could not be infructuous, destroyed the enemies and was illustrious like hundreds of suns. But Baladeva surrounded RukmT with Jrmbhastra and he started having a deep sigh.

## \|\| 107.6-7 \|\|

*bhūmiṣṭhaḥ sthāṇumadrukmī nidrāstreṇaiva nidritaḥ \|*  
*śālvastaṃ nidritaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatabāṇānmumoca tam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śailavṛṣṭiṃ śilāvṛṣṭiṃ jalavṛṣṭiṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*jvaladaṅgāravṛṣṭiṃ ca śaravṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ha \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Rukml was than over-powered with sleep and fell down on earth. Salva on the other hand finding him sleepy, shot a hundred arrows at Baladeva, showered mountains and rocks besides water and fire-flames.

## \|\| 107.8 \|\|

*balāccāstreṇa sarvāṇi vārayāmāsa lāṅgalī \|*  
*halena tadrathaṃ cūrṇa cakāra raṇamadhyataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. But Balarama on his part neutralised all of them with the use of his weapon and with the striking of the plough, he reduced the chariot of Salva into pieces.

## \|\| 107.9-10 \|\|

*ghoṭakānsārathiṃ caiva jaghāna caiva līlayā \|*  
*kopādbalena taṃ hantuṃ vāgbabhūvāśarīriṇī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tyaja śālvaṃ kṛṣṇavadhyaṃ tava kiṃ pauruṣaṃ raṇe \|*  
*yasya mūrdhni ca brahmāṇḍaṃ śūrpe ca sarṣape yathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. He killed his horses and the chariot also play fully, he then rushed towards him with the intention of killing him. But there was a divine voice from the sky, saying, "You forgive Salva because he is to be killed by Krishna alone. Who can described your prowess in the battle-field on whose head the entire globe rests like a seed of sheshamum in a winnowing basket.".

## \|\| 107.11-13 \|\|

*tacchrutvā baladevaśca halena tasya mastakam \|*  
*cakāra cūrṇa vyathitaḥ papāta raṇamūrdhani \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śālvasya patanaṃ dṛṣṭvā śiśupālo mahābalī \|*  
*cakāra śaravṛṣṭiṃ ca jalavṛṣṭiṃ yathā bhuvi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*halī tasya rathaṃ cūrṇa cakāra lāṅgalena ca \|*  
*ardhacandreṇa tadvāṇānvārayāmāsa līlayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. On hearing this, Baladeva struck him on the head with his plough as a result of which he fell in the battle-field. Finding that Salva had fallen, Sisupala showered his arrows like the showering of the water on the ground. Balarama on his part reduced his chariots into pieces.

## \|\| 107.14 \|\|

*taṃ hantuṃ śaṃkaraḥ sākṣānniṣedhaṃ ca cakāra tam \|*  
*kṛṣṇavadhyaṃ tyaja bala pārṣadapravaraṃ haraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Shiva himself stopped Balarama from killing him saying, "O Balabhadra, don't kill Sisupala, the best of the courtier of Vishnu because he is destined to be killed by Krishna himself.".

## \|\| 107.15 \|\|

*dantavaktrasya dantaṃ ca babhañja sa halena ca \|*  
*supravṛttasya yuddhena te sarve jahasuśca tam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Balarama broke the teeth of Dantavaktra with the striking of the plough because he was jeering at all the people.

## \|\| 107.16 \|\|

*balasya vikramaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve vīrāḥ palāyitāḥ \|*  
*cakruḥ praveśanaṃ sarve kuṇḍinaṃ varayātrikāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Witnessing the prowess of Balarama, all the warriors fled away. Thereafter the marriage party entered Kundinapura.

## \|\| 107.17 \|\|

*etasminnantare tatra śatānando mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*koṭibhirmunibhiḥ sārdhamājagāma hareḥ puraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. In the meantime the great sage Satananda arrived before Krishna together with crores of sages.

## \|\| 107.18-19 \|\|

*puraṃ praveśayāmāsa śatadvāraṃ ca durgamam \|*  
*agamyaṃ cāpi śatrūṇāṃ mitrāṇā ca sukhapradam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devakanyā nāgakanyā rājakanyāstathaiva ca \|*  
*munikanyā varaṃ draṣṭuṃ sasmitāśca samāyayuḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Не made the marriage party enter the inaccessible gate of the city which was inaccessible for the enemies but was quite pleasant for the friends. All the daughters of the gods, the Nagas, the sages and the princesses arrived there to have a look at the groom.

## \|\| 107.20-30 \|\|

*dadṛśuryoṣitaḥ sarvā nimeṣarahitena ca \|*  
*prasannaṃ kārayāmāsa sasmitaścandraśekharaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ratnendrasāranirmāṇarathasthaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ paramātmānaṃ bhaktānugrahavigraham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*navīnajaladaśyāmaṃ śobhitaṃ pītavāsasā \|*  
*yandanokṣitasarvāṅgaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ratnakeyūravalayaratnamālākulojjvalam \|*  
*ratnakuṇḍalayugmena gaṇḍasthalavirācitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ratnendrasāranirmāṇakvaṇanmañjīrarañjitam \|*  
*sasmitaṃ muralīhastaṃ paśyantaṃ ratnadarpaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saptabhiḥ pārṣadairgopaiḥ sevitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ \|*  
*navayauvanasaṃpannaṃ śaratkamalalocanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śaratpūrṇendutulyāsyaṃ bhaktānugrahakārakam \|*  
*koṭikandarpasaundaryaṃ satyaṃ nityaṃ sanātanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tīrthapūtaṃ kīrtipūtaṃ brahmeśaśeṣavanditam \|*  
*paramhnādakaṃ rūpaṃ kauṭicandrasamaprabham \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dhyānāsādhyaṃ durārādhyaṃ paramaṃ prakṛteḥ param \|*  
*dūrvayā paṭṭasūtraṃ ca ratnendrasāradarpaṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dadhānaṃ kartṛkāsārdha kadalyāḥ sphuṭamañjarīm \|*  
*cūḍāṃ trivikramākārāṃ mālatīmālyabhūṣitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*puṣpaṃ nārīpradattaṃ ca mukuṭaṃ mastakojajvavalam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā varaṃ yuvatyaśca mūrcchā saṃprāpurīśvaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

20-30. Shiva smilingly delighted Krishna and all the damsels stared Krishna, who was adorned with the best of the gem-studded ornaments, was the lord of all, was graceful to the devotees and took to human form to grace them, having the complexion of new clouds, clad in yellow garments, whose body was plastered with the sandal-paste adorned with the long garland of forest flowers, wearing the armlets, wristlets and; garland of gems. His ears were adorned with a pair of ear-ornaments which decorated his temples, He worn anklets which produced dangling sound, having a smiling face, holding a flute in his hand, looking at the mirrors of gems, served by the white fly-whisks by the seven cowherd attendants, having been a youthful body, the eyes resembling the lotus flowers of the winter season, the face resembling the full moon of the winter season, the one, who was graceful on his devotees, was beautiful like crores of the gods of love, the one who was eternal and spotless like the holy place, sanctified with his glory and adored by Brahma, Shiva and Shesha, having a delightful mind and lustre of crores of moons, the one who could not be achieved even by meditation, could be adored at the time of misery, the one who is beyond Prakriti, who is having the complexion of Durvd-grass holding the mirror made of gems and the silken cord, having the beauty of the blossoming banana tree, having the form of Trivikrama, adorned with the garland of jasmine flowers, holding flowers presented by a damsels. His head was adorned with a crown. Looking at such a fortunate groom, the ladies felt unconscious.

## \|\| 107.31-34 \|\|

*rukmiṇījīvanaṃ dhanyaṃ ślādhyamityūcurīpsitam \|*  
*jāmātaraṃ sā dadarśa rājñī bhīṣmakakāminī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*nimeṣarahitā tuṣṭā prasannavadanekṣaṇā \|*  
*rājā prasannavadanaḥ sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*samāgatya surānviprānbhūpāṃśca praṇanāma saḥ \|*  
*dadau yogyāśramaṃ tebhyo bhakṣyapūrṇa sudhopamam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*divāniśaṃ cāpyuvāca dīyatāṃ dīyatāmiti \|*  
*sukhaṃ nināya rajanīṃ devaiśca bāndhavaiḥ saha \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. They started saying, "The life of Rukmini is quite graceful, praise-worthy and desirable." The queen of Bhlsmaka stared at her son-in-law continuously and felt extremely satisfied; his face and eyes were filled with delight. The king with a delightful face arrived with his courtiers and priest and bowed before the gods, the Brahmanas and the kings offered them the appropriate seats; at the place filled with enough of food-stuffs; the demand of giving echoed through out the day and night. Vasudeva spent the night there with the gods and the relatives.

## \|\| 107.35-37 \|\|

*vasudevaḥ prabhāte ca prātaḥkṛtyaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*snātvā saṃdhyādikaṃ kṛtvā dhṛtvā dhaute ca vāsasī \|\| 35 \|\|*

*cakāra vedamantreṇa śubhādhivāsanaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*saṃpūjya mātṛkāḥ sarvāḥ sākṣācca sarvadevatāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pradāya vasudhārāṃ ca vṛddhiśrāddhādikaṃ tathā \|*  
*prāhmaṇānbhojayāmāsa devāṃśca bāndhavāṃstathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. The next morning he freed himself from all the daily routines, took a bath, performed sandhya and clad himself in two garments. He than reciting the Vedic hymns invoked Vishnu, the Matrkasa and adored all the gods performing the Nandisraddha. Thereafter he served food to the Brahmanas and his relatives.

## \|\| 107.38-42 \|\|

*vādyaṃ ca vādayāmāsa kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|*  
*suveṣaṃ kārayāmāsa varasyāpi praśaṃsitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*sajjaṃ ca kārayāmāsa narayānaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*evaṃ rājā bhīṣmakaśca vivāhārhaṃ ca maṅgalam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*purohitairvedamantraiḥ sarva karma cakāra saḥ \|*  
*maṇiratnaṃ dhanaṃ cāpi muktāmāṇikyahīrakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*bhakṣyadravyaṃ ca vastraṃ cāpyupahāramanuttamam \|*  
*bhaṭṭemyo brāhmaṇebhyo'pi bhikṣukebhyo dadau mudā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*vādyaṃ ca vādayāmāsa kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|*  
*suveṣaṃ kārayāmāsa rukmiṇyāśca manoharam \|\| 42 \|\|*

38-42. The musical instrument were played upon performing the welfare ceremonies. The groom was clad in the best of gannents. A beautiful palanquin was arranged. Similarly king Bhls maka also performed all the festivities through the priest with the reciting of the Vedic hymns, distributing to the Brahmanas and the beggars, the diamonds, riches, jewels, rubies, eatables, beside the beautiful garments. The musical instruments were sounded and all the welfare ceremonies were perfonned, Rukmini was also adorned with the best of ornaments and was clad in the best of costumes.

## \|\| 107.43-46 \|\|

*rājñībhirmunipatnībhirvidhānaṃ ca yathocitam \|*  
*tataḥ śubhe kṣaṇe prāpte māhendre paramodaye \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vivāhocitalagne ca lagnādhipatisaṃyute \|*  
*sadgrahekṣaṇaśuddhe cāpyasatāṃ dṛṣṭivarjite \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śubhakṣaṇe subharkṣe ca viśuddhe candratārayoḥ \|*  
*vedhadoṣādirahite śalākādivivarjite \|\| 45 \|\|*

*daṃpatyoḥ śarmayogye ca pariṇāmasukhaprade \|*  
*evaṃbhūte ca samaye bhīṣmakaprāṅgaṇaṃ hariḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. All the ceremonies were perfonned by the queens and the wives of the sages. Thereafter at the auspicious moment of Mahendra-yoga, when the lord was associated with lagna and was under the influence of the best of the planets the marriage was performed at the auspicious time when constellations the moon and the stars looked quite auspicious having no blemish. The marriage ceremony of the couple was performed in the welfare yoga. At that point of time, Shri Krishna arrived in the court yard of Bhismaka.

## \|\| 107.47-54 \|\|

*ājagāma suraiḥ sārdha suniviprapurohitaiḥ \|*  
*jñātibhirbāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ pitrā mātrānṛpaistathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*gopālakaiḥ pārṣadaiśca vayasyaiśca manoharaiḥ \|*  
*bhaṭṭaiśca gaṇakairjyotiḥ śāstrajñānaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vādyairnānāvidhaiścaiva nartakairgāyanaistathā \|*  
*nānāśilpakaraiścaiva mālākāraistathā'paraiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vidyādharyapsarobhiśca kinnarībhiśca satvaram \|*  
*sthalaṃ ca daduśurdevā munayaśca nṛpeśvarāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sarve samāgatā ye ca vivāhadarśanotsukāḥ \|*  
*rambhāstambhasahasraiśca paṭṭasūtrapariṣkṛtaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*cambakānāṃ candanānāṃ rasālānāṃ ca pallavaiḥ \|*  
*mālyairnānāvidhaiścaiva pītaraktasitānvitaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*parito maṅgalaghaṭaiḥ phalapallavasaṃyutaiḥ \|*  
*kastūrīcandanāktaiśca kuṅkumena virājitaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*parṇairlājaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpairdūrvābhirupaśobhitaiḥ \|*  
*munibhirbrāhmaṇaiścaiva rājendrairapi veṣṭitam \|\| 54 \|\|*

47-54. Не was accompanied by the gods, the sages, the Brahmanas, the priests close relatives, the parent's, the kings, cowherds, courtiers, friends, bards and the astrologers well-versed in the science of astrology. There were several people playing on the musical instruments besides dancers singers, artisans, the gardeners the Vidyadharis, apsaras and the kinnaris and others The gods, the sages, the kings who had arrived to witness the marriage looked at the place of the marriage delightfully which had thousand of the trunks of the banana trees tied with the silken cords. There were innumerable garlands of campaka flowers, the tender leaves of the sandal-wood and mango trees besides several types of garlands of red, yellow and white flowers. There were a large number of Ghdta-pallavas decorating the place which were painted with kasturi, sandal-paste, saffron, leaves, fried paddy, fruits, flowers and Durva-grass. The place was surrounded by the Brahmanas and the kings.

## \|\| 107.55-65 \|\|

*ratnendrasāranirmāṇavedīyuktaṃ manoharam \|*  
*carcitaṃ candanasnigdhaiḥ kastūrīkuṅkumānvitaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sugandhiśītamandaiśca pavanaiḥ surabhīkṛtam \|*  
*ratnānāṃ ca sahasraiśca jvalitaṃ jvaladīptakaiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*nānāprakāradhūpaiśca gandhadravyaiḥ suvāsatam \|*  
*citrairvicitrairvividhaiḥ śilpināṃpuṇyakāriṇām \|\| 57 \|\|*

*paritaḥ paritaścaiva śobhanārhaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ \|*  
*gandharvāṇāṃ ca saṃgītaimadhuraṃrmadhurīkṛtam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*vidyādharīṇāṃnṛtyaiśca nartakīnāṃ ca śilpinām \|*  
*tatra niśceṣṭacitraiśca janarājivirājitam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*guptadvārairgavākṣaiśca yuvatībhiśca vīkṣitam \|*  
*maṅgalena ghaṭenaiva vidhuṣā ca purodhasā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*kuśahastena bhūpena dānena dānavastunā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca prāṅgaṇaṃ rājño devā brahmādayastathā \|\| 61 \|\|*

*avaruhya rathāttūṇaṃ tiṣṭanti prāṅgaṇe mudā \|*  
*rājendrā dānavendrāśca sunayaḥ sanakādayaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇaścāpi bhagavānpārṣadapravaraiḥ saha \|*  
*tāndṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya javena bhīṣmakastathā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*mūrghnā vavande devāśca munondrāṃśca nṛpāṃstathā \|*  
*ratnasihāsaneṣveva suramyeṣu pṛthavapṛthak \|\| 64 \|\|*

*kramato vāsayāmāsa saṃpūjya sādareṇa ca \|*  
*rājā tuṣṭāva bhaktyā ca tānsarvānbhaktipūrvakam vasudevaṃ vāsudevaṃ sāśrunetraḥ puṭāñjaliḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

55-65. There was the goddess of the best of gem. The place was filled with the sandals-paste, kasturl and saffron, issuing fragrance. The cool fragrant wind was blowing, thousands of lamps made of gems were burning there, the burning of several types of the incense and other scented materials were issuing fragrant; the auspicious architects had made various types of attractive paintings all around. The Gandharvas were engaged in beautiful music, the Vidyadhari and the dancers were dancing, the place was decorated with several of the paintings created by the artisans which attracted the people. The damsels were peeping through the windows and the secret gates. The king was holding kusa-grass in his hand besides the pitcher of welfare. The learned priest was also present there. Brahma and other gods looked at the court-yard of the king. All of them delightfully descended from the chariots and entered the court-yard of the king. The kings, the demons, Sanaka and other sages arrived there. Lord Krishna was also present there with his courtiers. Finding all the people there. BhTsmaka at once got up and offered his salutation to the gods, the sages, the kings, bowing his head. He then offered Individual gem-studded lion-throne to everyone for taking their seats. The king respectively adored all, offerings prayers to each one of them with devotion. He then started Vasudeva and Devaki getting emotional with his eyes filled with tears.

## \|\| 107.66 \|\|

*bhīṣmaka uvāca adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam \|*  
*babhūva janmakoṭīnāṃ karmamūlanikṛntanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Bhlsmaka said – My life has met with success today and has been beautified; the fruit of crores of my birth has emerged.

## \|\| 107.67-68 \|\|

*svayaṃ vidhātā jagatāṃ pradātā sarvasaṃpadām \|*  
*svapre yatpādapadmaṃ ca draṣṭuṃ naiva kṣamaḥ prabho \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tapasāṃ pharadātā ca saṃsraṣṭā prāṅgaṇe mama \|*  
*svātmārāmeṣu pūrṇeṣu śubhapraśnamanīpsitam \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. The one who is the creator of the universe and is the bestower of all the riches, whose lotus-like feet are difficult to be seen eve in dream, the one who bestows the reward for the tapas is the creator, the same lord is now present in my court-yard. It is not proper to enquire about the welfare from the one who roams himself into his own soul.

## \|\| 107.69-70 \|\|

*yogīndrairapi siddhendraiḥ surendraiśca munīndrakaiḥ \|*  
*dhyānādṛṣṭaśca yo devaḥ sa śivaḥ prāṅgaṇe mama \|\| 69 \|\|*

*kālasya kālo bhagavānmṛtyormṛtyuśca yaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*mṛtyuṃjayaśca sarveśonarāṇāṃ dṛṣṭigocaraḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. He is the one who is adored by the yogis, the siddhas, the gods and the ascetics but is inaccessible to them, the same Shiva have arrived in my court-yard. The lord who happens to be the killer of the time, death for the god of the death, the one who has conquered the death and is the lord of death, the same lord is presently visible to all.

## \|\| 107.71 \|\|

*yasyamūrdhnāṃ sahasreṣu mūrdhni viśvaṃ carācaram \|*  
*nāstyantaḥ sarvavedeṣu so'yaṃ ca mama prāṅgaṇe \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. The one who carries the earth over one of his thousand heads and the one who is beyond description in the Vedas, the same, lord is present in my court-yard.

## \|\| 107.72-73 \|\|

*sarvakāmapraṇeyo hi sarvāgre yasya pūjanam \|*  
*śreṣṭho devagaṇānāṃ ca sa gaṇeśo mamāṅgaṇe \|\| 72 \|\|*

*munīnāṃ vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca pravaro jñānināṃ guruḥ \|*  
*sanatkumāro bhagavāsmatayakaṣaḥ prāṅgaṇe mama \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The one who is lovingly visible in all the desire, the one who is adored first of all and the one who is the best of all the gods, the same Ganesha is present in my court-yard. The one who is the best of the sages and the Vaishnavas, besides being the teacher of the intellectuals, the same Sanatkumara is present in my court-yard.

## \|\| 107.74 \|\|

*brahmaputrāśca pautrāśca prapautrāścāpi vaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*te sarve madagṛhe'dyaiva jvalanto brahmatejasā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The sons, grandsons, great grandsons and other descendants of Brahma are illumining with divine lustre. All of them have, presently arrived in my house.

## \|\| 107.75-77 \|\|

*aho kalpāntaparyantaṃ tīrthībhūto mamā''śramaḥ \|*  
*yeṣāṃ pādodakaistīrtha viśuddhaṃ tadgṛhe mama \|\| 75 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni tāni tīrthāni sāgare \|*  
*sāgare yāni tīrthāni viprapādeṣu tāni ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*viprapādodakaklinnā yāvattiṣṭhati medinī \|*  
*tāvatpuṣkarapatreṣu pibanti pitaro jalam \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. My house has been turned into the holy place like the one at the end of the kalpa, with the water of whose feet, the holy places get sanctified, he is also available here. All the holy places of the earth and the ocean are lodged in the feet of the Brahmanas; the earth remains wet with the water from the feet of the Brahmanas. The ancestors sip the water from the leaves of the lotus flowers. They are all present in my house.

## \|\| 107.78-79 \|\|

*viprapādodakaṃ bhuktvā dattvā viprāya dakṣiṇām \|*  
*srānānāṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ phalamāpnoti niścitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*nikṛntanaṃ ca vipadāṃ vyādhinirmulakāraṇam \|*  
*sukhadaṃ śubhadaṃ sāraṃ viprapādodakaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. By consuming the water with which the feet of the Brahmanas are washed, by giving them the daksina, one achieve the merit of taking bath in all the holy places. The water of the feet of the Brahmanas removes all the misfortunes, the ailments and bestows pleasure and removes pain.

## \|\| 107.80-82 \|\|

*na gaṅgāsadṛśaṃ tīrtha na devo mādhavātparaḥ \|*  
*sanatkumārā dbhakto na na hi kalpatarostaruḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*na puṣpaṃ pārijātācca na vrataṃ harivāsarāt \|*  
*pūjane na hi pūjyaṃ ca na patraṃ tulasīparam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*na devī prakṛteścāpi nā''dhāraḥ pavanātparaḥ \|*  
*na hi sthūlo mahāviṣṇorna sūkṣmaṃ paramāṇutaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-82. There is no place holier than Ganga; there is no god greater then Hari, there is no devotee greater than Sanatkumara, there is no tree greater than kalpavrksa; there is no flower better than Parijata; there is no vrata greater than Harivasara, there is no goddess greater than Prakriti. There is no base greater than the wind, there is nothing more solid than Maha-Vishnu and nothing is smaller than the atom.

## \|\| 107.83 \|\|

*na brāhmaṇātparaḥ pūto nā''śramaśca na tīryakam \|*  
*na devo na paraḥ ko'pi cetyāha kamalodbhavaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There is no dsrama more sanctified than Brahmana, nor the holy place. Even the gods do not compare with them. This has been ordained by Brahma.

## \|\| 107.84-85 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ prakṛteśca paraḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dhyānāsādhyo durārādhyo yogināmapi niścitam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*nirguṇaśca nirākāro bhaktānugrahavigrahaḥ \|*  
*sa eva cakṣuṣo nṝṇāṃ sākṣāddevaśca madgṛhe \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. The lord who is beyond Brahma, Vishnu, Shesha or Prakriti; the god who is inaccessible through meditation and could be achieved with great devotion and meditation. He is beyond quality invisible and takes to human form in order to bestow his grace on the devotees; all these gods are presently available in my house.

## \|\| 107.86 \|\|

*devairbrahmeśaśeṣaiśca dhyātaṃ yatpādapaṅkajam \|*  
*dhaneśena gaṇeśena dineśenāpi durlabham \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. His inaccessible lotus-like feet are adored by Brahma, Shiva, Ananta, Kubera, Ganesha and Surya.

## \|\| 107.87 \|\|

*ityuktvā bhīṣmakaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ samānīya svayaṃ puraḥ \|*  
*tuṣṭāva sāmavedoktastotreṇa parameśvaram \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Thus speaking Bhlsmaka himself came and stood before Krishna and praised him with the reciting of the stotra from Samaveda.

## \|\| 107.88 \|\|

*bhīṣmaka uvāca sarvāntarātmā sarveṣāṃ sākṣī nirlipta eva ca \|*  
*karmiṇāṃ karmaṇāmeva kāraṇānāṃ ca kāraṇam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Bhlsmaka said – You are the inner soul of everyone, the witness of all, unattached, the cause of the deeds and the cause of all the causes.

## \|\| 107.89 \|\|

*kecidvadanti tvāmekaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*kecicca paramātmānaṃ jīvo yatpratibimbakaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O Narada, thus praising the king sipped water and remembered lord Vishnu. Thereafter he offered water at the feet of the lord which are daily washed Lakshmi. He then offered Diirva-grass, flowers and water together with arghya, madhuparka and sugar. He applied fragrant, sandal-paste on all the limbs.

## \|\| 107.90 \|\|

*kecitprākṛtikaṃ jīvaṃ sagṛṇaṃ bhrāntabuddhayaḥ \|*  
*kecinnityaśarīraṃ ca buddhā (dhā) śca sūkṣmabuddhayaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The garland of Parijdta flowers which was given to him by Indra, who offered by him to the lord adorning his neck.

## \|\| 107.91 \|\|

*jyotirabhyantare nityaṃ deharūpaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*kasmāttejaḥ prabhavati sākāramīśvaraṃ vinā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The beautiful ornament of gems offered to the king by Kubera, was offered with devotions by the king to the lord.

## \|\| 107.92-93 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā sa cā''cāntaḥ smaranviṣṇuṃ ca nārada \|*  
*pādyaṃ padmārcite pādapadme cāyaṃ dadau mudā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*ardhyaṃ ca pradadau tatra dūrvāpuṣpajalānvitam \|*  
*madhuparkaṃ ca surabhiṃ sarvāṅge gandhayandanam \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. Some of the people call you as the form of lustre and eternal while others call you as the supreme soul which is reflected in a human being.

## \|\| 107.94 \|\|

*yatpradattaṃ mahendreṇa śubhakarmaṇi yautukam \|*  
*pārijātasya mālyaṃ ca jāmātuśca gale dadau \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The people of ordinary wisdom conceived you as the one having polity and Prakritika Jiva. The person with great wisdom conceive you as the one having the eternal body.

## \|\| 107.95 \|\|

*kubereṇa ca yadattamamūlyaratnabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*cakāra varaṇaṃ tasya sa rājā bhaktipūrvakam \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Some of the people conceive you as the internal light, eternal and having an ever-lasting body. Because without the visible lord the lustre cannot emerged.

## \|\| 107.96 \|\|

*kahniśuddhāṃśukayugaṃ yaddattaṃ vāhninā purā \|*  
*dadau tadeva kṛṣṇāya paripūrṇatamāya ca \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The two garments sanctified by fire which was given by Agni to the king in earlier times were offer to lord Krishna.

## \|\| 107.97 \|\|

*jvalitaṃ ratnamukuṭaṃ yaddattaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*dadau tanmastake rājā kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The shining gem-studded crown which was offered by Vishvakarma, to the king was given by him to lord Krishna, adorning his forehead.

## \|\| 107.98-101 \|\|

*dhūpaṃ ratnapradīpaṃ ca naivedyaṃ sumanoharam \|*  
*nānāprakārapuṣpaṃ ca ratnasihāsanaṃ dadau \|\| 98 \|\|*

*saptatīrthodakaṃ caiva punarācamanīyakam \|*  
*tāmbūlaṃ ca varaṃ ramyaṃ karpūrādisuvāsitam \|\| 99 \|\|*

*śayyāṃ ratikarī ramyāṃ pānārthaṃ vāsitaṃ jalam \|*  
*kṛtvā ca varaṇaṃ rājā parihāraṃ cakāratam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*kṛtāñjalipuṭo rājā tasmai puṣpāñjalīṃ dadau \|\| 101 \|\|*

98-101. The incense, the lamps of gems, tasteful naivedya and several types of flowers besides gem-studded lion throne were also offered to him. The water of seven holy places was given to the lord for sipping and a betel with camphor was also given to him. He was also given a charming bed which was quite appropriate for love-sport and the fragrant water was offered for drinking. Thus selecting Krishna as the groom, the prayer was offered. The king then offered the bunch of flowers to Krishna.

## Chapter 108

## \|\| 108.1-5 \|\|

*athāṣṭādhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyāṇa uvāca etasminnantare devī mahālakṣmīśca rukmiṇī \|*  
*ājagāma sabhāmadhye munidevādibhiryute \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ratnasiṃhāsanasthā ca ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitā \|*  
*vahniśuddhāśukādhānā kabarībhārabhūṣitā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paśyantī sasmitā sādhvīhyamūlyaratnadarpaṇam \|*  
*kastūrībindubhiryuktā snigdhacandanacarcitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sidhūrabidunā śaśvadbhālamadhyasthalojjvalā \|*  
*taptakāñcanavarṇabhā śatacandrasamaprabhā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*candanokṣitamarvāṅgā mālatīmālyaśobhitā \|*  
*saptabhirnṛpaputraiścasamānītā ca bālakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Narayana said – In the meantime Rukmini the form of Maha-Lakshmi arrived in the court of the king together with the gods and the sages, she was seated on the gem-studded lion-throne. She was adorned with gem-studded ornaments and clad in the garments sanctified by fire. Her hair-do was looking quite charming; the chaste lady, wearing a smile on her face was looking at the invaluable gem-studded mirror. She had the spot of kasturl over her forehead and her limbs were plastered with sandal-paste; the forehead was decorated with the spot of vermilion. She had the lustre of molten gold and she was shining like the lustre of the hundreds of moons. All her limbs were plastered with sandal-paste and she wore the garland of jasmine flowers. The seven princesses brought her in the court.

## \|\| 108.6 \|\|

*devendrāśca munīndrāśca siddhendrā nṛpapuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*dadṛśū rukmiṇīṃ devīṃ mahālakṣmīṃ pativratām \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All the yogis, the gods, the sages, the siddhas and the kings had a glance of the chaste Rukmini who was the form of Lakshmi.

## \|\| 108.7-8 \|\|

*saptapradakṣiṇāḥkṛtvā praṇamya svapatiṃsatī \|*  
*siṣeca śītatoyena snigdhacandanapallavaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tāṃ siṣeca jagatkāntaḥ kāntā śāntāṃ ca sasmitām \|*  
*dadarśa kāntaḥ kāntāṃ ca kāntaṃ kāntā śubhe kṣaṇe \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The chaste Rukmini took seven rounds and bowed before her husband, she sprinkled cool water with the tender leaves, soaked in sandal-paste. Thereafter Krishna also sprinkled water on his beloved who was smiling. At the auspicious time both the husband and the wife looked at each other.

## \|\| 108.9 \|\|

*atha devī pituḥ kroḍe samuvāsa śubhānanā \|*  
*lajjayā namravadanā jvalantī ca svatejasā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Rukmini with the serene and smiling face was shining with her lustre and keeping her head downwards sat in the lap in her father.

## \|\| 108.10 \|\|

*rājā deveśvarīṃ tasmai paribūrṇatamāya ca \|*  
*pradadau saṃpradānena vedamantreṇa nārada \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О Narada, the king with the reciting of the hymns from the Vedas handed over in marriage, his daughter to Krishna.

## \|\| 108.11 \|\|

*vasudevājñayā kṛṣṇaḥ svastītyuktvā sthito mudā \|*  
*jagrāha devīṃ devaśca bhavānīṃ ca bhavo yathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Krishna accepted the hand of Rukmini with the permission of Vasudeva reciting the words Svasti. Lord Krishna accepted Rukmini in the same way and Shiva had accepted Parvati.

## \|\| 108.12 \|\|

*suvarṇānāṃ pañcalakṣaṃ kṛṣṇāya paramātmane \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ tāṃ dadau rājā paripūrṇatamāya ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The king gave away to the lord Krishna five lakhs of gold coins in Daksina.

## \|\| 108.13 \|\|

*śubhakarmaṇi niṣpanne kṛtvā kanyāṃ ca vakṣasi \|*  
*ruroda rājā mohena munidevendrasaṃsadi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. After the performing of the marriage, the king embraced the daughter and started sobbing in presence of the gods and the sages.

## \|\| 108.14 \|\|

*parihāreṇa vacasā kutvā tasmai samarpaṇam \|*  
*siṣeca kanyāṃ dhanyāṃ ca netrayugmajalena ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Then begging forgiveness the king gave away his daughter to lord Krishna who was soaked in tears flowing from the eyes of the king.

## Chapter 109

## \|\| 109.1-3 \|\|

*atha navādhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ nārāyaṇa uvāca etasminnantare rājñī rukmiṇījananī śabhā \|*  
*patiputravatībhiśca sādhvībhiḥ sahitā mudā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*āgatya maṅgalaṃ kṛtvā tatra nirmañchanādikam \|*  
*daṃpatī veśayāmāsa ratnanirmāṇamandiram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nānācitravicitrāḍhyaṃ hīrahāreṇa bhūṣitam \|*  
*muktāmāṇikyaratnena mudīptaṃ darpaṇena ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Narayana said – In the meantime the queen mother of Rukmini arrived with other chaste woman whose husbands and sons were alive to complete the welfare ceremonies. Both the bride and the groom were made to enter the palace made of gems. The palace was decorated with several types of diamonds, the garland of gems as well as the paintings. The sapphire emeralds and others gems besides the mirrors were shining.

## \|\| 109.4-8 \|\|

*dadarśa kṛṣṇastatraiva durgāṃ durgatināśinīm \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ ca sāvitrīṃ ratiṃ ca rohiṇīṃ satīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

*devapatnīṃ rājapatnīṃ munipatnīṃ pativratām \|*  
*ratnamihānasthāṃ ca ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 5 \|\|*

*uttasthurārāddṛṣṭvā ca śrīkṛṣṇaṃ jagatīpatim \|*  
*ratnasihāsane ramye vārayāmāsa tāṃ mudā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*stutiṃ cakruśca devāśca munipatnyaśca mādhavam \|*  
*puṭāñjaliyutāstatra trameṇa ca pṛdhakpṛthak \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhojayāmāsa rājñī ca vareṇa saha kanyakām \|*  
*sakarpūraṃ satāmbūlaṃ pradadau vāsitaṃ jalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

4-8. Krishna found that Durga, the remover of misfortune, Sarasvati, Savitri, Rati, Rohini, Sati, wives of the gods, Indra, the queen and the chaste wives of the sages were seated on the gem-studded lion thrones. All of them were adorned with gem-studded ornaments. At the entry of Shri Krishna into the palace, all the people stood up in reverence and made him sit on the charming lion throne. All the wives of the sages and the gods praised him individually. The queen served food to both the newlyweds and offered fragrant water and the betels with camphor.

## \|\| 109.9-12 \|\|

*durgā kṛṣṇāya pradadau tatra maṅgalapatrikām \|*  
*sarvāsāmājñayā devī paṭheti tamuvāca sā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*papāṭha patrikāṃ kṛṣṇo devīsaṃsadi sasmitaḥ \|*  
*lakṣmī sarasvatī durgā sāvitrī rādhikā satī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tulasī pṛthivī gaṅgā'rundhati yamunā'ditiḥ \|*  
*śatarūpā ca sītā ca devahūtiśca menakā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*daivyaścaitāśca daṃpatyoḥ kurvantu param \|*  
*papāṭha ceti kṛṣṇaśca śuśruvurjahasuśca tāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

9-12. Durga handed over to Krishna the letter of welfare and with the permission of all, she asked him to read it out. In the courtyard of the goddess, Krishna smiling read it. It said Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Durga, Savitri, Sati, Radhika, Tulasi, PrthvI, Gangs, Arundhatl, Yamuna, Aditi, SatarQpa, Sita, Devahtiti and Menaka bestow welfare upon the newly wedded couple. When Krishna read it all the goddesses present there laughed aloud.

## \|\| 109.13 \|\|

*pārvatyuvācarukmiṇīṃ rukmiṇīkānta tvāṃ paśyantīṃ ca sasmitām \|*  
*paśya prauḍhāṃ rupavatīṃ sundarīṃ navayauvanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Parvati said – "O beloved of Rukmini, I look at you with a smiling face you look at the young, beautiful damsel named Rukmini".

## \|\| 109.14 \|\|

*śacyuvāca tava yogyā ca yuvatī ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*tvāṃ prārthayantī suciramavamanyānyamīśvaram \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. IndranI said – The one who had been desirous of you since long insulting other gods, this Rukminl who is. adorned with all the gem-studded ornaments is quite suitable for you.".

## \|\| 109.15 \|\|

*sāvitryuvāca yathā varastathā kanyā vidhinā yojitā purā \|*  
*vidagdhāyā vidagdhena sarvatra saṃgamaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Savitri said – "Both the bride and the groom are equal and they were made for each other by the lord earlier. The union of the equals is always auspicious.".

## \|\| 109.16 \|\|

*ratyuvāca īśvareṇa parīhāsaṃ kā vā kartuṃ kṣamā bhuvi \|*  
*dhyānāsādhyo durārādhyaścāvamanyānyamīśvaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Rati said – "Who else is competent enough to cut jokes at the lord disregarding the other gods"?

## \|\| 109.17 \|\|

*gāyatryuvāca yathā varastathā kanyā ca kṣubdhe bhaiṣmake gṛhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Gayatri said – "In the house of Bhlsmaka, with so much of hustle and bustle, the bride is equal to the groom".

## \|\| 109.18 \|\|

*rohiṇyuvāca satyaṃ brūhi jagannātha kāminīnāṃ ca saṃsadi \|*  
*kīdṛśī rādhikā ramyā rukmiṇī cāpi kīdṛśī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Rohini said – "O lord of the universe, you speak out the truth in the assembly of the damsels as to how did you like Radhika in comparison to Rukminl".

## \|\| 109.19 \|\|

*sarasvatyuvāca rādhāyāṃ yādṛśī prītī rukmiṇyāṃ naiva tādṛśī \|*  
*sā saṅginī pūrvakāle sarvakrīḍāsu vardhinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sarasvati said – The love he had for Radha, cannot be had in Rukmini. In the earlier times, she was always with him in all his sports and increased interested in sports.

## \|\| 109.20-22 \|\|

*prāṇādhiṣṭhātudevī sā pañcaprāṇādhikā satī \|*  
*rukmiṇī kamalā sākṣātsaṃpadāmadhidevatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarvaśaktisvarūpā ca kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ \|*  
*buddherapyadhidevī ca durgā nārāyaṇī parā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*devādhiṣṭhātṛdevī tvaṃ sāvitrī vedamātṛkā \|*  
*vidyādhidevatā'haṃ ca tato'nyāśca kalākalāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. She happens to be the goddess of his life, she is dearer to him than all the five pranas. Rukminl happens to be an incarnation of Lakshmi and the bestower of all the riches, Radha on the other hand happens to represents the entire prowess of lord Krishna besides being the goddess of wisdom. Durga, NarayanI, Parvati the great goddess of the gods, Savitri the mother of the Vedas, Sarasvati the goddess of learning and all other goddesses are only the rays of Radha.

## \|\| 109.23-26 \|\|

*na brahmaṇi śive śeṣe gaṇeśe ca dineśvare \|*  
*na bhakteṣu ca padmāyāṃ na śivāyāṃ ca mayyapi \|\| 23 \|\|*

*prasādo yādṛśastasyāmanyeṣu ca na tādṛśaḥ \|*  
*trailokye pṛthivī dhanyā supuṇyaṃ bhārataṃ yataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatra vṛndāvanaṃ dhanyaṃ rādhāpādābjacihnitam \|*  
*sarvāsāmapi devīnāṃ rādhā puṇyavatī satī \|\| 25 \|\|*

*rādhāpādābjanakhare dadau snigdhamalaktakam \|*  
*ayamevamiti śrutvā jahasuḥ sarvayoṣitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Brahma, Shesha, Ananta, Ganesha, Surya, devotees, Lakshmi, Parvati and myself do not enjoy the same grace of Krishna was has been enjoyed by Radha. The earth is graceful of all the three lokas on which the land of Bharata is located. Out of the land of Bharata, VmdSvana is graceful, having the impression of the lotus-like feet of the Radha. Radha happens to be the most virtuous and auspicious of all the chaste ladies. "He is the one who painted the toes of Radha with paint." On hearing this all these damsels started laughing.

## \|\| 109.27 \|\|

*dhyāyante dūrtaḥ sarvā rādhā vakṣaḥsthalasthitā \|*  
*tasmādrādhāṃ namaskṛtya tulanāṃ manyate kila \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The one who is adored by all the ladies from a distance, the heart of the same lord adores Radha who always remains present there. A comparison should thus be made keeping Radha in view.

## \|\| 109.28 \|\|

*sarasvatīvacaḥ śrutvā sāvitrī pārvatī satī \|*  
*anyāśca yoṣitaḥ sarvāḥ sādhvityūcuśca saṃsadi \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. On hearing these words of Sarasvati, Savitri, Sati, Parvati and all other damsels spoke out in the assembly, "You have spoken out the truth".

## \|\| 109.29 \|\|

*lopāmudrā'nasūyā cāpyahalyā'rundhatī tathā \|*  
*sarvāstā munipatnyaśca rabhasaṃ cakrurīśvaram \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Lopamudra, AnusQya, Ahalya, Arundhatl and all the wives of the sages, felicitated lord Krishna.

## \|\| 109.30 \|\|

*atha devāṃśca bhūpāṃśca munīdrāṃścāpi bhīṣmakaḥ \|*  
*pūjayāmāsa vidhinā bhojayāmāsa sādaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thereafter the king Bhismaka properly adored all the kings, the gods and the sages serving them food at the same time.

## \|\| 109.31 \|\|

*khādyatāṃ lokā dīyatāṃ dīyatāmiti \|*  
*śabdo babhūva nagare vādyasaṃgītamaṅgalaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The sound of welfare music besides, "Eat more and give more", echoed in the sky.

## \|\| 109.32 \|\|

*atha prabhāte brahmeśaseṣāstridaśāstathā \|*  
*yānamārohaṇaṃ bhūpāścakrire ca tvarānvitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. After this, in the early morning Brahma, Shiva, Ananta and the gods besides Vasudeva were mounted on the vehicles.

## \|\| 109.33 \|\|

*rājā mahograsenaśca vasudevastvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*kārayāmāsa yātrāṃ ca śrīkṛṣṇaṃ rukmiṇīṃ satīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The king Ugrasena and Vasudeva made Krishna and Rukmini to move on the journey.

## \|\| 109.34 \|\|

*subhadrā rukmiṇīmātā kanyāṃ kṛtvā svavakṣasi \|*  
*rurodoccaistatsakhībhirbāndhavairityuvāca sā \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Subhadra the mother of Rukmini embraced her daughter and then started crying in presence of her relatives and female friends.

## \|\| 109.35 \|\|

*subhadrovāca kva yāsi māṃ parityajya vatse mātaramīśvarīm \|*  
*kathaṃ jīvāmi tvāṃ tyaktvā kathaṃ tvaṃ vā'pi jīvasi \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Subhadra said – О daughter, where are you going leaving alone the queen mother? How can I disown you? And how can you disown me?

## \|\| 109.36 \|\|

*mahālakṣmīrmama gṛhātkanyārūpā ca māyayā \|*  
*vasudevālayaṃ yāsi vāsudevapriyā satīḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. You had been born as my daughter with the illusion of Maha-Lakshmi and you are leaving for the house of lord Krishna, becoming his chaste wife, leaving from my house, go to the Vasudeva.

## \|\| 109.37-38 \|\|

*ityuktvā kanyakāṃ śokātsiṣeva netrajairjalaiḥ \|*  
*bhīṣmakaḥ sāśrunetraśca kanyāṃ kṛṣṇe samarpya ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*taṃ ca kṛtvā parīhāraṃ rurodoccairatīva saḥ \|*  
*ruroda rukmiṇī devī śrīkṛṣṇaścāpi māyayā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Thus speaking with her mind filled with grief, the mother soaked her daughters body with her tears. Bhismaka on the other hand with his eyes filled with tears entrusted her daughter to Krishna, begging forgiveness for any short coming, crying aloud at the same time. Rukmini also started sobbing while Krishna too also followed suit.

## \|\| 109.39-44 \|\|

*rathamāropayāmāsa vasudevaḥ sutaṃ vadhūm \|*  
*etasminnantare rājā jāmātre yautukaṃ dadau \|\| 39 \|\|*

*gacendrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ ca ṣaṅguṇaṃ ca turaṃgamam \|*  
*dāsīnāṃ ca sahasraṃ ca kiṃkarāṇāṃ śataṃ śatam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ratnānāṃ ca sahasraṃ caivāmulyaratnabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*svarṇānāṃ pariśuddhānāṃ pañcalakṣaṃ ca sādarama \|\| 41 \|\|*

*toyabhojanapātrāṇi kutāni viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*sauvarṇāni ca ramyāṇi surabhīḥ pradadau mudā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dugdhavatīnāṃ dhenunāṃ savatsānāṃ sahasrakam \|*  
*amūlyāni ca ramyāṇi vahniśuddhāṃśukāni ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vasudevaścograseno devaiśca munībhiḥ saha \|*  
*prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śīghraṃ dvārakābhisukhaṃ yayau \|\| 44 \|\|*

39-44. Vasudeva made the son and the daughter-in-law to mount the chariot. In the meantime the king gave away the dowry to his son-in-law which included a thousand elephants six time more the horses, a thousand slave girls, a hundred servants, a thousand gems, invaluable gem-studded ornaments, gracefully, beside five lakhs of coins of pure gold, the gold vases made by Vishvakarma for taking food and a large number of cows delightfully. The number of calves of those cows was one thousand. He gave away beautiful costumes which were shining like the fire and were invaluable. Both Vasudeva and Ugrasena accompanied by the sages and the gods delightfully moved towards Dvaraka.

## \|\| 109.45-47 \|\|

*praviśya svapurīṃ ramyā kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|*  
*vādyaṃ ca vādayāmāsa sundaraṃ sumanoharam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*devakī rohiṇī ramyā yaśodā nandagehinī \|*  
*aditiśca ditiścaiva tathā ca varakāminī \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śrīkṛṣṇaṃ rukmiṇīṃ ramyāṃ vilokya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*gṛhaṃ praveśayāmāsa kārayāmāsa maṅgalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Entering the city of Dvaraka the welfare ceremonies were performed and the musical instrument were played upon.
